docs.title: Introduction and goals
docs.text:
The Technisch Ontwerp (TO) is the technical design of Gemeenschappelijke Bronontsluiting (GBO). It describes the GBO facilities (voorzieningen) and interfaces (koppelvlakken). The TO goes one level deeper than the Globaal Ontwerp (GO) and stays within the frameworks of the Projectstartarchitectuur (PSA).

The TO uses the arc42 template. It records how the GBO components are built. For why GBO exists and what it must do, see the PSA introduction and the GO solution direction.

docs.title: Baseline: the demo at v0.9.0
docs.text:
The reference implementation gbo-demo is the ground truth for the behavior of GBO. This version of the TO is pinned to demo tag v0.9.0 (November 2, 2026). Every statement about behavior links to code or a test at that tag. Each divergence between the design and the implementation has a record in one of these places:

  • an architecture decision,
  • a finding,
  • an entry in Risks and technical debt.

docs.title: Earlier work in the TO
docs.text:
The TO is the standalone reference for the technical design of GBO. It absorbs two earlier bodies of work:

  • The reference architecture v0.6.2 (archived and unpublished). The ADR log holds its decisions. This includes the decisions that the implementation superseded later.
  • The traceability work that ran next to the demo. The TO holds its requirements, findings, open questions, demo increments, and design-to-demo matrix. How to trace explains how the IDs link.

The IDs did not change (REQ-NN, RL-NN, AV-NN, BSNK-NN, F-NN, Q-NN, SL-NN). A reader who knows an old ID finds it under the same number.

docs.title: How this document is organized
docs.text:
The TO has three parts:

Part Content arc42 sections 1 to 12 The design: constraints, context, strategy, building blocks, runtime scenarios, deployment, crosscutting concepts, decisions, quality, risks, and glossary. Requirements Testable demands on what GBO builds and on its interfaces (REQ), guidelines for bronhouders (RL), candidate connection conditions (AV), and BSNk preconditions (BSNK). Traceability The chain from design to demo: the matrix, demo increments (SL), findings (F), open questions (Q), and feedback to standards bodies (E1 to E10).

Each arc42 page and each ADR ends with a "Traceability" section. This section lists the requirements, findings, open questions, and demo increments that the page explains or depends on.

docs.title: Routes
docs.text:
GBO gives bronhouders one technical backbone for several data flows. A bronhouder is a government organization that holds an authentic source. A bronhouder exposes a GraphQL API behind an FSC Inway. Every request passes the same chain: the FSC Inway as PEP, the PDP of the source, the source gateway, and the source API. The routes differ at the consumer edge and in the evidence that a request carries. The evidence selects the authorization regime (ADR-0031).

gbo-demo v0.9.0 implements three routes end to end:

  • DvTP (Delen van gegevens via Toestemming met Private dienstverleners). A citizen gives consent, and a private consumer requests source data under that consent. The consumer never holds a citizen identifier. An integrator can call on behalf of the consumer under FSC delegation (ADR-0034). A second consumer pilot runs on the same chain: the Installatie Register asks the LVG source about ownership (rule LVG0001). See DvTP query.
  • EUDI issuance (PuB-EAA route). A citizen discloses a PID from the EUDI wallet and gets an attestation from a government source. The bronhouder is the PuB-EAA provider. GBO operates the technical issuance facility (ADR-0028). The demo proves this route, but the PSA treats wallet support (P-06) as a hook outside version 1. See EUDI issuance.
  • ASI verification (eIDAS Article 45e). A QTSP verifies or retrieves attributes at the Authentic Source Interface, as specified in ETSI TS 119 478 clause 6.1. The QTSP is an OAuth client and does not take part in FSC. The ASI provider calls the source over FSC (ADR-0037). The route is demo grade: it uses a stub register, development certificates, and a DigiD mock. See ASI verification.

Three routes exist at design level only (design-level scenarios):

  • Gov-to-Gov: exchange between government parties on a legal basis. The legal-basis regime needs its own positive evidence. No rule set exists for this regime.
  • SDG-OOTS: cross-border evidence exchange through an AS4 bridge (ADR-0020).
  • Relying-party presentation: the citizen presents a wallet attestation to a relying party. This route has no GBO runtime.

For the interaction patterns (interactiepatronen) behind these routes, see the GO.

docs.title: Quality goals
docs.text:
The technical design has five main quality goals, in order of priority. Quality requirements refines them into testable scenarios. Each goal has the following effect on the design:

Priority Quality goal What it means for the design 1 Data minimization The query of the consumer is the authorization object. The PDP decides on each requested field. It denies a field that no rule of the active regime covers (REQ-17, REQ-48). See P-02. 2 Privacy (BSN-free) In DvTP, the consumer gets no BSN and no other citizen identifier. The query names the subject with a placeholder. As a result, the PDP input and the decision logs hold no identity (REQ-20, REQ-79). EUDI and ASI are an exception: the plain BSN is in the PDP input and in both decision logs (REQ-60 not met). ADR-0043 (proposed) records the fix. See P-04. 3 Verifiable authorization A policy engine decides every data request. Application code does not make this decision. Each decision is allow or deny with a reason code. The consumer and the decision record get a coarse code. The operator gets the rule code per field (REQ-06, ADR-0036). See S05. 4 Traceability One W3C trace ID links the processing records of all controllers. Next to it, the records hold the FSC transaction ID, which links the transport records (REQ-55, ADR-0035). In demo v0.9.0, the link to the decision record behind the FSC Inway is missing (risk R23). See P-12. 5 Bronhouder autonomy Sources own their schema, their service description, their decryption keys, and their policy. PAP and PDP are at the bronhouder (ADR-0021). GBO keeps no copy of source data (REQ-11). See P-10.

docs.title: Stakeholders
docs.text:
For the parties involved and the impact of GBO on them, see GO chapter 6. The TO has three primary audiences:

  • Engineers who build or integrate GBO components.
  • Bronhouder teams that connect a source.
  • Reviewers who check that the implementation stays within the PSA frameworks.

docs.text:

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text:
Four sources set the constraints for this design: the PSA, the law, the GDI standards, and the functional requirements for DvTP. Each constraint links to its normative text, and the TO does not restate that text. If a design element conflicts with a constraint, one of these records the conflict:

  • an entry in Risks and technical debt,
  • a finding,
  • an architecture decision.

docs.title: Architecture principles (PSA)
docs.text:
The 16 architecture principles of the PSA bind this design. The PSA page has no anchor per principle. For this reason, each link opens the principles page. The following principles constrain the technical design most directly:

ID Principle Bearing on the TO P-01 Legal basis before exchange Before data flows, the PDP judges every request under a regime. The evidence in the request selects the regime (ADR-0031). P-02 Minimal data processing The PDP decides on each field of the GraphQL query (REQ-17). P-04 BSN-free for private consumers In DvTP, the consumer holds no citizen identifier. After the allow decision, the source decrypts its own value (ADR-0033). See Pseudonymization. P-06 Support for the EUDI wallet The PSA treats this principle as a hook outside version 1. The demo still proves EUDI issuance and ASI verification. P-07 Trust through recognized admission and trust anchors (until September 2026: "trust framework based on PKI") Every FSC connection uses mTLS with PKI certificates. Admission comes from a register (REQ-61). The legal identity comes from the certificate (REQ-67). See Identity and trust. P-09 Open standards and vendor independence The design uses FSC, AuthZEN, OpenID4VCI and OpenID4VP, GraphQL, OPA, LDV, W3C Trace Context, and OAuth 2.0. P-10 Data sovereignty: the bronhouder keeps control Sources own their schema, service description, decryption keys, and policy. PAP and PDP are at the bronhouder (ADR-0021). P-12 Logging and non-repudiation The design has three authoritative records, one per Logius standard. The ADL holds the authorization decisions (ADR-0036). The LDV logbook of each controller holds the processings (ADR-0026). FSC-Logging holds the transport. The W3C trace ID joins the three records, and the FSC transaction ID is recorded next to it (ADR-0035). See Logging, audit and traceability. P-13 Transparency and access for the citizen The citizen views and revokes consents (REQ-38). Each controller can answer an access request from its LDV logbook. P-14 Separation of generic and specific functions GBO has one generic chain. Route-specific adapters are at the edge (REQ-44).

For the full list (P-01 to P-16) and the status of each principle in the demo, see the matrix.

docs.title: Design principles (PSA)
docs.text:
The 14 design principles govern how the GBO components are built. Each link opens the design principles page. The following design principles constrain the TO most directly:

ID Principle Bearing on the TO D-01 Decentral where possible, central where necessary Each bronhouder has its own PDP and PAP. Each provider issues its own tokens. GBO has central components only where they are necessary: the consent facility (toestemmingsvoorziening) and the admission register. D-03 Use national generic facilities (GDI) unless GBO reuses FSC, FTV, BSNk PP, DigiD, and PKIoverheid and does not rebuild them. The demo mocks DigiD, BSNk, and MijnOverheid. D-07 Open source unless All GBO components and the demo are open source (EUPL). D-08 Comply or explain: mandatory open standards A deviation from a mandated standard is an explicit ADR or risk. D-09 API-first All interfaces (koppelvlakken) are specified APIs. See Context and scope. D-11 Least privilege Authorization is closed-world: without a rule, there is no access. Only the FSC Inway reaches the source gateway (REQ-81). D-13 Standardize where possible, make exceptions explicit Exceptions to a standard are visible in the data and in the ADR log. An example is the file metadata transport (AV-08).

For the full list (D-01 to D-14), see the matrix.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
The requirements state testable demands on what GBO builds and on the interfaces between GBO and other parties. Each requirement names its source. The source is a passage in the GO, the PSA, or FR-DvTP, or a principle for which a demo finding showed the need. The arc42 sections explain how the design meets the requirements. The status of each requirement is one of these words: draft, ready for review, approved, covered, or withdrawn.

The requirements page also lists the guidelines for bronhouders (RL-01 to RL-05). A guideline is a recommendation for bronhouders. It puts no demand on GBO.

docs.title: Connection conditions (candidates)
docs.text:
Some demands fall on the parties that connect to GBO, and GBO itself does not carry them. The TO collects these demands as candidate connection conditions (AV-01 to AV-15). They are input for the management organization, which sets the real connection conditions (PSA S04).

The candidates apply to three types of party:

Party Candidates Consumer AV-01 trace context, AV-02 LDV, AV-03 consent facility and BSNk PP, AV-04 own FSC peer. AV-05 proof sent unchanged, AV-14 contact details for GDPR rights, AV-15 equivalent alternative. Integrator AV-06 admitted separately, acts as processor Bronhouder AV-07 to AV-13: service description, consent to a taken-over description, old decryption keys, LDV for relation attestations, and validity and revocation policy

docs.title: BSNk preconditions
docs.text:
BSNk PP sets preconditions that the DvTP design must respect (BSNK-01 to BSNK-11). These preconditions are facts about an external facility. They are not requirements on GBO. Three of them shape the design most:

  • Transformation is possible only while the citizen is logged in (BSNK-04). As a result, the consent facility makes all values at consent time, and the proof freezes at consent (F-78).
  • Only a recognized party can activate and transform (BSNK-01). It is open whether the consent facility can be such a party (Q-26, Q-49).
  • The interfaces are SOAP with PKIoverheid (BSNK-11). The demo mock offers the same operations as JSON.

How the register finds a returning citizen is an open design choice. The working assumption is route D (ADR-0040, proposed).

docs.title: Functional requirements DvTP (FR-DvTP v0.9)
docs.text:
FR-DvTP v0.9 contains the functional requirements FR-01 to FR-39 for the DvTP route. The document is not public. For this reason, the TO names a criterion without a link, for example "FR-34, criterion 1". The matrix gives the demo status per FR.

FR-DvTP v0.9 has known contradictions. If the text and a decision conflict, the requirements follow the decision. The known contradictions are:

  • FR-22 to FR-24 name the same consent statuses with different words. The rationale of FR-23 contradicts its criteria (F-97).
  • FR-39 puts policy at a central authority, and FR-26 puts it at a central authorization component. FR-25 ties the GDPR pointer to "revocation no longer possible". FR-35 describes a register content that the design does not use (F-98).

docs.title: Legal and regulatory constraints
docs.text:
The PSA groups its principles by legal framework. The following frameworks constrain this design:

Constraint Source Bearing on the TO AVG (GDPR) PSA architecture principles, framework 1 Data minimization, purpose limitation (doelbinding), and legal basis (grondslag). Each controller (Verantwoordelijke) logs its own processing (ADR-0026). Digital Government Act (Wdo) and PKIoverheid PSA framework 3 Organization identity through PKI certificates and the OIN. eIDAS2 and ARF PSA framework 4 EUDI wallet support. Article 45e: the Authentic Source Interface (ADR-0037). eIDAS implementing regulations of 2026 (ASI) CIR (EU) 2025/1569 art. 9, CIR (EU) 2026/1735 Annex IV Art. 9 applies from August 19, 2026. From January 1, 2027, the verify interface follows ETSI TS 119 478 clause 6.1.1, clause 6.2.3, or both. From that date, every result is sealed. The authorization part stays a national choice (F-80). eIDAS implementing regulations of 2026 (PuB-EAA) CIR (EU) 2026/1735 (ETSI TS 119 471), CIR (EU) 2026/1731 (ETSI TS 119 412-6, TS 119 472-3), CIR (EU) 2026/1730, and CIR (EU) 2025/848 PuB-EAA issuance falls under the same standard as QEAA issuance. The issuer needs designation and a registration with entitlement PUB_EAA_Provider. It also needs an access certificate, a registration certificate, and a qualified seal certificate with its own profile (F-81, Q-28). BSN legislation (Wabb) PSA framework 6 Private parties must not process the BSN. This rule drives pseudonymization and the BSN exception for the QTSP (F-86). Single Digital Gateway Regulation (EU 2018/1724) GO interaction patterns The OOTS connection over AS4 is an obligation under EU law, and GBO has no choice in it (ADR-0020).

docs.title: Standards
docs.text:
The capabilities chapter of the PSA lists the agreements, standards, and facilities (voorzieningen) per capability, with their gaps. See capabilities S01 to S11. The design builds directly on the following standards:

  • Connectivity and authorization: OpenFSC, OpenFTV with OpenID AuthZEN 1.0 and the FTV GraphQL profile, OPA/Rego, GraphQL, and PKIoverheid.
  • Pseudonymization: BSNk PP.
  • EUDI issuance: OpenID4VCI, OpenID4VP, and SD-JWT VC.
  • ASI verification: ETSI TS 119 478, OAuth 2.0 with PKCE, DPoP (RFC 9449), and JWT access tokens (RFC 9068). ASI verification also uses dynamic client registration (RFC 7591), authorization server metadata (RFC 8414), resource indicators (RFC 8707), rich authorization requests (RFC 9396), and problem details (RFC 9457).
  • Logging and traceability: LDV 1.0.0 (Logboek Dataverwerkingen), ADL (Authorization Decision Log), FSC-Logging (draft), W3C Trace Context, and OpenTelemetry.

If the demo deviates from a standard that the PSA names, a risk entry records the deviation. For example, the demo uses Rego instead of ODRL as policy language (R16).

docs.title: Context and scope
docs.text: The GBO technical system connects to external actors and systems. This chapter lists every interface (koppelvlak) on the system boundary and between GBO components. It covers the technical context only. The GO solution direction and the PSA solution direction give the business context: which parties exchange which data, and why.

docs.title: Technical context
docs.text:
GBO has the same shape as in the Globaal Ontwerp: external parties use one of the channels, and every channel reaches the source through GBO Basis. The following figure shows who is on the other side of each interface in gbo-demo v0.9.0. Dashed blocks are designed but not built. Click a block to zoom in.

Figure 2: The interfaces between GBO components.

The interface inventory lists every interface with its protocol and code. The building block view zooms in per channel.

Four points in these diagrams are easy to misread:

  • Only the portal backend calls BSNk, at consent time. Neither the PDP nor the source gateway calls BSNk. The source reads its own value with its own decryption component (ADR-0033).
  • The PDP gets the consent status over FSC: from its own Outway (peer …0800) to the register's Inway (peer …0700). Only the public keys come directly from the register (ADR-0032).
  • The QTSP is not an FSC participant. It is an OAuth client of the ASI authorization server and calls the ASIP over HTTPS. The ASIP is the FSC participant toward the source (F-87, ADR-0037).
  • The ASI has four roles. GBO provides the ASIP and the authorization server. The Discover Interface and the QTSP are external. For these two roles, the demo has a stub and a reference client. It is open who operates the ASIP and the authorization server (Q-37).

docs.title: Interface inventory
docs.text: Every interface has a row in one of the tables in the following sections. A row gives the standard that the interface follows and its implementation in gbo-demo. Rows marked designed are not built in demo v0.9.0. Paths in the last column are relative to gbo-demo v0.9.0.

docs.title: DvTP consent
docs.text:
The DvTP consent chain uses these interfaces:

Interface Between Protocol and standard Implemented in Consent initiation Consumer → consent portal (toestemmingsportaal), and back HTTPS redirect with consumer, scopes, purpose, and return URL. The return carries the consent proof in the URL fragment, or status=denied (REQ-37, REQ-119). toestemmingsportaal-frontend Citizen login Citizen ↔ consent portal DigiD (mock): the citizen types a test BSN, and the backend signs a portal token with the BSN in sub. Real DigiD gives the identity in an assertion (REQ-24). portalhttp Consent registration Portal backend ↔ consent register (toestemmingsregister) REST: POST /consents, GET /consents?subject_ref=…, GET and DELETE /consents/{id}, GET and PUT /subjects/{ref}/polymorphic. No BSN crosses this interface (REQ-23, REQ-39). consent-register/main.go BSNk PP Portal backend → BSNk /v2/activate, /v2/transform, and /v2/bsn-authorisation-list. The mock follows the BSNk interface as JSON and does not encrypt. Production BSNk uses SOAP with PKIoverheid (BSNK-11). bsnk-mock Consent proof Consumer → Inway → PDP and source gateway Signed JWT gbo-consent+jwt (ES256) in the X-GBO-Consent-Token header, with encrypted_subject per source. The query names the subject with the placeholder consent:identity or consent:pseudonym (REQ-79, AV-05). consent_token.go Consent keys PDP → consent register GET /.well-known/jwks.json, cached for 300 s consent.rego Consent status PDP Outway (…0800) → register Inway (…0700) FSC service consent-status: GET /consents/{id}/status on a status-only listener, with no cache and a 2 s timeout. The register refuses a call without an FSC peer (REQ-76). status.go, Makefile

docs.title: Authorization and FSC
docs.text:
The authorization chain and the FSC group use these interfaces:

Interface Between Protocol and standard Implemented in Data request Consumer Outway ↔ bronhouder Inway FSC (OpenFSC v2.4.0): mTLS, access token, and grant hash. Grants carry no properties. fsc-infra Delegated data request Integrator Outway ↔ bronhouder Inway FSC DelegatedServiceConnectionGrant, signed by the integrator, the represented consumer, and the provider (REQ-106) seed-bri-delegation-int.sh Authorization Inway (PEP) ↔ PDP OpenID AuthZEN 1.0, POST /authzen/v1/evaluation over HTTPS. The Inway passes the raw body, and the PDP maps it per the FTV GraphQL profile (REQ-42). openftv-pdp Contract decision Provider Manager → PDP AuthZEN autosign request for each submitted contract (REQ-62) autosign.rego Participant admission PDP ← admission register OpenFTV PIP pull, GET /internal/openftv/participants, every 5 s, on a network that only the PDP shares (REQ-61) dvtp-onboarding.yaml

docs.title: Bronhouder
docs.text:
The bronhouder uses these interfaces:

Interface Between Protocol and standard Implemented in GraphQL source API Source gateway ↔ source GraphQL over HTTP, POST /graphql. Only the Inway can reach the gateway (REQ-81). graphql-server, brp-graphql-server, lvg-graphql-server Source decryption Source gateway → decryption component of the source POST /signed-encrypted-identity and POST /signed-encrypted-pseudonym. The component calls no other service (REQ-21). decryption.go Source metadata Reconciler ← source GET /.well-known/gbo over a separate FSC metadata service, per gbo-source-metadata 1.0 or 1.1 (REQ-64) schema, source_metadata.go

docs.title: EUDI issuance
docs.text:
EUDI issuance uses these interfaces:

A DigiD mock is the second means (REQ-102). asi-wallet-verifier, digidmock ASI token Authorization server → QTSP → ASIP RFC 9068 JWT (ES256), DPoP (RFC 9449), private_key_jwt (REQ-86, REQ-87) accesstoken ASI verify and retrieve QTSP ↔ ASIP ETSI TS 119 478 clauses 6.1.1 and 6.1.2 at /<ds>/authsrc-api/verify and /retrieve. docs.text:
Two interfaces are designed but not built in demo v0.9.0:

Interface Between Protocol and standard Implemented in OOTS evidence exchange EU access points ↔ OOTS adapter AS4/eDelivery and OOTS-EDM. This interface is designed. For more information, see ADR-0020 and Q-79. — Government data request Government consumer ↔ bronhouder Inway FSC with its own positive evidence. This interface is designed. For more information, see design-level scenarios. —

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
The demo implements three routes end to end, at demo grade:

  1. The DvTP query under consent, with an integrator variant and the LVG pilot as a second consumer and source.
  2. EUDI issuance of PuB-EAA attestations.
  3. ASI verification and retrieval for QTSPs (ETSI TS 119 478 clause 6.1).

Two routes are design-level: SDG-OOTS and Gov-to-Gov. The runtime view has a scenario for each.

This design covers the following parts of the system:

  • the authorization chain: PEP, PDP, PIPs, policies, and contract decisions
  • the consent chain: portal, register, consent proof, and status service
  • pseudonymization at consent time and decryption at the source
  • the FSC group configuration and the admission register
  • EUDI issuance, source onboarding, and the source registry
  • the Authentic Source Interface: ASIP, authorization server, and discovery records
  • logging, audit, and observability

The following parts are out of scope:

  • the internal architecture of bronhouder systems behind the GraphQL API
  • the EUDI wallet, DigiD, and BSNk themselves
  • the QTSP, the Discover Interface, and the national register of relying parties
  • the relying-party side of wallet presentations, which touches no GBO infrastructure
  • the EU OOTS common services

The developer tooling of the demo is scaffolding: the developer portal, the consumer mocks, keyper-mock, and the reference QTSP. This tooling is outside the target architecture. The deployment view marks each unit as target architecture or scaffolding.

docs.title: Deployment view
docs.text: The GBO deployment in this chapter follows the infrastructure configuration of gbo-demo v0.9.0: docker-compose.yml, fsc-infra/docker-compose.yml, the Makefile, and the Helm chart. The demo is a reference deployment. It is not a production topology. The availability model lists what changes for production.

docs.title: Environments
docs.text:
The demo runs in two environments:

Environment Platform Purpose Local Two Docker Compose projects: the main stack and fsc-infra. Make targets start them: demo-minimal, demo-dvtp (the default make demo), demo-eudi, demo-full, demo-manager, demo-integrator, and demo-asi. Development and demonstration Simulation Kubernetes with the generic gbo-app Helm chart. Each application is one release with a Deployment or a Job, a Service, and a Gateway API HTTPRoute. It runs in two tenants: MinEZK (Ministry of Economic Affairs and Climate Policy) and MinBZK (Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations). Public demo at gbo.simulatie.datastelsel.nl

Compose profiles switch on optional parts. The base (no profile) runs the PDP and its databases, the admission register (toelatingsregister), and the consent register (toestemmingsregister). It also runs the BD and BRP sources with their gateways, the BSNk mock, the decryption component, the LDV logbooks, the developer portal, and observability. Each profile adds parts to the base:

Profile Adds Make target dvtp Consent portal (toestemmingsportaal), consumer backends and frontends (Hypotheek-BV, Installatie Register with keyper-mock), and the LVG source and gateway demo-dvtp eudi Issuance chain: postgres-eudi, source registry bootstrap and migrations, issuance migrations, configuration materializer, issuance server, and EUDI adapter demo-eudi onboarding Source reconciler as the registry writer, with postgres-eudi and the registry jobs onboard-demo-sources full dvtp and eudi together demo-full integrator Integrator backend and the int-* peer in fsc-infra demo-integrator (after demo-dvtp or demo-full) asi ASIP, ASI authorization server, wallet verifier, discovery stub, reference QTSP, and the asip-* peer in fsc-infra demo-asi (after demo-eudi or demo-full) manager OpenFTV Manager, its UI, and Keycloak demo-manager

In demo v0.9.0, the ASI route runs only locally. The chart has no values for the ASI services. Issue #594 covers the deployment to the simulation environment. The simulation uses its own Peer IDs, for example 0000009961MINEZK0000 for the issuance peer.

docs.title: Deployment units and network zones
docs.text:
The local stack separates traffic with Docker networks. The isolation of the source gateway is a security control. The gateway acts on the consent token after the PDP allows the request. It does not verify the token again (REQ-81, ADR-0033). The local stack has these networks:

Network Members Purpose frontend Browser-facing UIs UI traffic backend Most services Service traffic dvtp-onboarding PDP and admission register only Keeps admission data away from other services eudi Issuance chain, postgres-eudi, reconciler, ASIP, and reference QTSP Source registry and issuance source-gateways Source Inways (bd-inway, brp-inway) and source gateways The only path to a gateway. fsc-infra owns this network. sources Source gateways, source APIs, decryption component, source logbooks, and OTel collector Traffic of the components that serve the sources. No consumer is on this network. fsc-infra FSC components and the services they reach FSC transport

The source gateways publish no port and are only on source-gateways and sources (docker-compose.yml). Two limits apply to this isolation:

  • The source APIs are also on backend and fsc-infra. The FSC metadata services of BD and RvIG point at them directly. In the demo, a container on those networks can reach a source API without the PDP. Production must limit a source API to its gateway and its metadata path.
  • The chart has no NetworkPolicy. A Kubernetes deployment needs one, or an equivalent control (F-79).

The consent register also relies on network placement. Its portal API must serve only the portal backend (REQ-39). The API does not authenticate the caller. It is open whether it must (Q-58).

The status listener of the register answers only with the FSC peer that cr-inway forwards (REQ-76). In the demo, the listener is also reachable on the compose networks. Production does not accept that exposure.

docs.title: FSC peers
docs.text:
The FSC group fsc-demo runs OpenFSC v2.4.0. Each organization has its own FSC components, a txlog API, and a Peer ID. A self-hosted directory peer and certificate portal serve the group. The group has these peers:

Organization Peer ID Units Role Directory peer …0000 directory-manager, directory-inway, directory-controller, directory-txlog-api, directory-ui Group registry. It signs service publications automatically. It signs nothing else. EDI issuer (GBO) …0100 edi-manager, edi-outway, edi-controller, edi-txlog-api Consumer for EUDI issuance (bri, brp) and for the metadata services. The EUDI rules list it as a designated issuer. Belastingdienst mock …0200 bd-manager, bd-inway, bd-controller, bd-txlog-api Provider of bri, brp (RvIG), lvg, gbo-metadata-bd, and gbo-metadata-rvig. Its Manager decides contracts through the PDP. Its Inway is the PEP. Mortgage lender mock (Hypotheek-BV) …0300 hv-manager, hv-outway, hv-controller, hv-txlog-api DvTP consumer of bri BRP/RvIG mock …0400 brp-manager, brp-inway, brp-controller, brp-txlog-api Provider peer with its own PEP and contract decision. The default demo publishes RvIG on …0200 instead. make fsc-seed-brp publishes brp here. Consent register (GBO) …0700 cr-manager, cr-inway, cr-controller, cr-txlog-api Provider of consent-status. The Inway has no AuthZEN hook. The Manager decides contracts through the PDP. The admission register lists it as a system participant.

One FSC peer can host more than one logical source. In the default demo, the RvIG and LVG sources use the Belastingdienst peer …0200 and its OIN. Each source still has its own service, gateway, metadata document, and certificate set. This shared peer is a demo shortcut. The demo therefore does not show one OIN per bronhouder (REQ-67).

Unit Host port (container) Networks Notes asi-provider 9424 (4020) backend, fsc-infra, eudi Reads the source registry with the reader role. Uses asip-outway. asi-authorization-server 9425 (4021) backend Keeps clients, codes, and transactions in memory asi-wallet-verifier 9428 (8001), internal API 8002 backend Needs the nl-wallet sources. docs.title: One-shot jobs
docs.text:
The chart renders a task as a Job (job.enabled: true). The source registry bootstrap, the source registry migrations, and the issuance migrations are Jobs. A database lock or one transaction stops a second copy of a Job from running at the same time. The issuance configuration materializer is an init container. It writes issuance_server.toml into an emptyDir for each pod. postgres-eudi is a Deployment with Recreate and a ReadWriteOnce volume.

The rollout order is bootstrap, then migrations, then the reconciler, the adapter, and the issuance server (chart README).

docs.title: Certificates and PKI
docs.text:
FSC traffic is mTLS inside a self-generated PKI. cfssl serves a root CA and an intermediate CA, with a certificate portal for CSRs. Each organization gets a group certificate with its OIN in serialNumber and its name in O. It also gets internal mTLS certificates (fsc-infra/pki). The legal identity of an organization comes from its certificate (REQ-67).

Private keys are not in Git. Each checkout generates them again.

The EUDI and ASI material comes from two pre-provisioned development CAs: an issuer CA and a reader CA. The Makefile refuses to generate them. A separate privileged command mints leaf certificates under them. The runtime gets leaves and public CA certificates. It never gets a CA private key. The demo has the following certificate and key material:

Material Minted by (demo) Held at runtime by Production FSC group and internal certificates, per organization fsc-infra/pki bootstrap scripts (cfssl) The FSC components of that organization PKIoverheid (REQ-46) PDP AuthZEN TLS certificate generate-pdp-cert.sh PDP. Inways and Managers pin it as CA. Platform TLS (Helm: Secret openftv-pdp-tls) Consent proof signing key Consent register at start, or a mounted file (CONSENT_SIGNING_KEY_PATH, required with a persistent store) Consent register Managed key. Key rotation is an open question (Q-55). Source decryption keys Demo keys in the gateway image, for the shared demo OIN Source gateway and decryption component. A deployment mounts its own keys (SUBJECT_KEYS_DIR). BSNk key delivery per source (BSNK-09). Old key versions stay available as long as consent proofs that use them are valid (AV-09). EUDI certificate set per source: issuer, reader, status list make provision-development-certificates Issuance server (private keys through the init step) and reconciler (public leaves only) Qualified seal certificate in a QSCD, access and registration certificates, and a status-list certificate. Key custody is an open question (Q-17). Reference QTSP issuance set: reader, issuer, status list, callback TLS make provision-qtsp-issuance-certificates Issuance server, reference QTSP Outside GBO. The QTSP holds its own set. ASIP seal certificate make provision-asip-seal-certificate (issuer CA) ASIP Qualified seal certificate. It is open who holds it (Q-28, ADR-0041). QTSP client certificate make provision-asip-qtsp-certificate (reader CA) Reference QTSP Wallet-relying-party access certificate (Q-35) Wallet verifier reader certificates (asi-login, qtsp-login) make provision-asi-wallet-verifier (reader CA) Wallet verifier Access certificate ASI authorization server signing key If AZSP_SIGNING_KEY_FILE is not set, the server makes an ephemeral key at start. Authorization server Managed key

Missing or incomplete EUDI material blocks only that source (REQ-58). The issuance server trusts the pre-production NL PID issuer CA. Its PID trust list also holds the development issuer CA and the issuer CA of every source. This list is too broad (REQ-45). The ASI wallet verifier trusts a fixed list: the pre-production PID issuer and the development issuer CA. Neither list is the EU Trusted List.

Production needs separate certificate roles per bronhouder for EUDI: access, registration, qualified seal, and status list. It is open which trust list anchors PuB-EAA providers (Q-30). Identity and trust and ADR-0023 explain the roles.

Readers use the SELECT-only role adl_reader. Logins and pending statements of the reference QTSP. Jaeger, Loki Volumes, seven-day retention Debug traces and logs, including the engine's console decision log

docs.title: Observability and audit stores
docs.text:
The stores fall into two groups with different duties (logging):

  • Audit stores hold the authoritative records: the ADL for decisions, the LDV logbooks for processings, and the FSC txlogs for transport (REQ-32). Each peer has its own txlog API. This includes the GBO peers cr, pdp, and asip.
  • Observability stores are for debugging. An OpenTelemetry collector receives OTLP from all services. It exports to Jaeger and to the developer portal's live event stream. Promtail ships container logs to Loki, including the engine's console decision log. Grafana shows dashboards. These stores are never the record of a decision.

One W3C trace ID per request joins the records. The FSC transaction ID is recorded next to it (ADR-0035). On the simulation platform, one observability stack runs in MinEZK, and MinBZK shares it (OBSERVABILITY.md). In demo v0.9.0, no audit store has a retention policy, an access model, or tamper evidence (Q-08).

docs.title: Availability model
docs.text:
The demo is built for inspection. Availability is not one of its goals. The demo-grade choices in the following lists must change for production. Risks and technical debt tracks them.

Authorization and consent have these demo-grade choices:

  • One PDP serves all providers. The target is a PDP per bronhouder (ADR-0004). The PDP does not start without its ADL database, so postgres-ftv runs in every profile.
  • Every DvTP decision needs the consent status, live, over FSC. By default, the register keeps its data in memory. Production needs a replicated store and an availability target for this role (REQ-75).
  • The PDP pulls the admission register every 5 s. If the register is missing, the PDP denies contracts with ADMISSION_REGISTER_UNAVAILABLE. It denies delegated calls with INTEGRATOR_REGISTER_UNAVAILABLE.
  • The LDV logbooks are off the critical path. If a logbook is down, the outbox delays the record. The request still completes.

EUDI issuance has these demo-grade choices:

  • The issuance server reads its configuration at start. After a change of the active release, the server needs a controlled restart (state rollout_required).
  • If one source is outside its stale grace period, it blocks new releases for all sources. Then the offer catalog answers 503 for all sources (REQ-66).
  • The adapter callback must be reachable over public HTTPS. It needs caller authentication (REQ-45).

The ASI chain has these demo-grade choices:

  • The authorization server keeps registrations in memory. After a restart, every QTSP registers again. Without AZSP_SIGNING_KEY_FILE, issued tokens also stop working after a restart.
  • If the register is unreachable at a re-check, the client stays active (Q-34).
  • If the current source description or the keys of the authorization server are missing, the ASIP fails closed (503).

In production, the mocked services become external dependencies with their own availability: BSNk, DigiD, and the register of relying parties.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
The TO is written in English. Each concept has one English term. On its first use on a page, the term gets the Dutch name of the Globaal Ontwerp in parentheses, for example "consent register (toestemmingsregister)". After that, the page uses the English term only. Proper names stay as they are: Gemeenschappelijke Bronontsluiting, Delen van gegevens via Toestemming met Private dienstverleners, Globaal Ontwerp, Projectstartarchitectuur, Technisch Ontwerp, MijnOverheid, DigiD, Logius, BSN, Autorisatielijst BSN, Basisinrichting OOTS, Logboek Dataverwerkingen. One Dutch government term also stays as it is, without a translation: bronhouder.

The following tables give each term, the Dutch name, its meaning, and the words that the TO does not use for the same concept. The style linter (scripts/style_lint.py) reports every word from a "Do not use" column in running text. A Dutch name directly inside parentheses is allowed. Code names, quotes from sources, and IDs are exempt. For the full begrippenlijst of the GBO stelsel, see the GO begrippenlijst.

docs.title: Building blocks and channels
docs.text:
These terms follow the building block view:

Term Dutch (GO) Meaning Do not use GBO Basis GBO Basis The part of GBO at every bronhouder: FSC, the PEP and the PDP, the source gateway, source configuration, and the records. It feeds every channel (GBO Basis). — Channel kanaal A way in which GBO serves one kind of consumer. The three channels are DvTP, EUDI wallet, and OOTS. trajectory Route — One end-to-end flow through a channel: the DvTP route, the PuB-EAA route, the ASI route, the SDG-OOTS route, and the Gov-to-Gov route. trajectory Facility voorziening A shared function that GBO or another party provides, for example the consent facility. voorziening Consent facility toestemmingsvoorziening The GBO facility of the DvTP channel where the citizen gives, views, and revokes consent. It consists of the consent portal and the consent register (Consent facility). toestemmingsvoorziening, consent service Consent portal toestemmingsportaal The citizen-facing application of the consent facility (PSA S02). It has a frontend and a backend. The short form "portal backend" is allowed. toestemmingsportaal Consent register toestemmingsregister The register of consents (PSA S01). It signs the consent proof and answers the consent status. toestemmingsregister Pseudonymization facility pseudonimiseervoorziening BSNk PP: the Logius facility that the DvTP channel uses at consent time. pseudonimiseervoorziening PuB-EAA provider PubEAA-voorziening The GBO block of the EUDI wallet channel that issues an attestation from source data to the wallet (PuB-EAA provider). Legally, the bronhouder is the provider. PubEAA Issuance facility — The technical part of the PuB-EAA provider that GBO runs: the issuance server and the EUDI adapter (ADR-0028). — ASI — Authentic Source Interface: the interface of ETSI TS 119 478 through which a QTSP verifies or retrieves attributes at an authentic source (eIDAS article 45e). — ASI provider ASI-provider The GBO block of the EUDI wallet channel that offers the ASI. It consists of the ASIP and the ASI authorization server (ASI provider). — OOTS adapter OOTS-adapter The GBO block of the OOTS channel that answers EU evidence requests. Design only (OOTS channel). — Source gateway — The component in front of a source API (code name bron-sidecar). After the allow decision, it decrypts the value for its own OIN (ADR-0033). sidecar Decryption component — The component of a source that reads the VI or VP for that source with its own keys. The source gateway calls it after the allow decision. — Admission register toelatingsregister The register of admitted participants and integrator mandates. The PDP pulls it as a PIP (code name dvtp-onboarding-register). onboarding register Source registry — The store of source descriptions: candidates, immutable releases, and the active release. — Source metadata — The description that a source publishes of its own services, at /.well-known/gbo (Source configuration). — EUDI adapter — The component between the issuance server and the FSC chain. In the demo, its FSC peer is called "EDI issuer" (edi-…). — Wallet verifier — The nl-wallet verification server that the ASI authorization server uses for a login with the NL Wallet. — Integrator integrator A software party that calls a source on behalf of a consumer, under an FSC delegated grant and a registered mandate (ADR-0034). —

docs.title: Domain terms
docs.text: Term Dutch (GO) Meaning Do not use Bronhouder bronhouder The government organization responsible for an authentic register and the access to it. The TO keeps this Dutch government term, also in English text, without translation. source holder Source bron A system of a bronhouder that answers queries. — Source access bronontsluiting The provision of register data through a standard interface. bronontsluiting Citizen burger The data subject in GBO flows. — Consent toestemming The informed agreement of the citizen to a specific data exchange. — Consumer afnemer An organization that asks a bronhouder for data, in any channel. afnemer Service provider dienstverlener The private party that is the consumer in the DvTP channel. dienstverlener Controller Verantwoordelijke The party that decides on a processing (AVG). Under LDV, each controller keeps its own logbook. — Data subject Betrokkene The person whom a processing is about (AVG and LDV term). — Data set gegevensset A named group of fields that a consent covers as a whole (REQ-10). gegevensset Service catalog dienstencatalogus The legally anchored register of the maximum scope that a consumer can ask for per use case. See ADR-0008. dienstencatalogus Purpose limitation doelbinding Processing of data is allowed only for the stated purpose. — Legal basis grondslag The legal ground for a processing or a provision of data. A legal basis set directly by law is a statutory basis (wettelijke grondslag). grondslag Interface koppelvlak A specified technical interface between parties or components. koppelvlak Interaction pattern interactiepatroon One of the patterns of the GO: A (EUDI wallet), B (OOTS), C (DvTP). interactiepatronen Processing verwerking Any operation on personal data (AVG term). —

docs.title: Consent, identity, and pseudonyms
docs.text: Term Meaning Do not use Consent proof The signed gbo-consent+jwt that the toestemmingsregister issues. It carries an encrypted value per source (encrypted_subject), the scopes, and the consumer (ADR-0032). — Consent token The same JWT as it travels in X-GBO-Consent-Token, before the PDP verified it. The evidence that selects the consent regime is a consent token. — Placeholder The value that a dienstverlener puts in the query in place of the citizen: consent:identity or consent:pseudonym. The source gateway replaces it after the allow decision (REQ-79). — Regime The basis on which the PDP judges a request. The evidence in the request selects it (ADR-0031). With a consent token, the consent regime applies. Without one, the PID regime applies. — Designated issuer An FSC peer on the actor list of the EUDI rules. Only a designated issuer can ask for source data under the PID regime. — Mandate (acts_for) The registration in the admission register that an integrator acts for a consumer and a rule. The PDP reads it at request time. — BSN authorization list The BSNk list (Autorisatielijst BSN) of the parties that are allowed to receive the BSN. A source on the list gets a VI in the consent proof. Other sources get only a VP. — PI Polymorphic identity. A BSNk value made for the requester (the toestemmingsportaal) from the BSN. The toestemmingsregister stores it under the subject_ref. Recipients get a VI made from it. — PP Polymorphic pseudonym. Like the PI, but for pseudonyms. Recipients get a VP made from it. — VI Encrypted identity. A BSN that BSNk encrypted for one recipient OIN and one key version. Only that recipient can read it. — VP Encrypted pseudonym. A pseudonym that BSNk encrypted for one recipient OIN and one key version. The BSNk specification calls it EP. — subject_ref The reference under which the toestemmingsvoorziening knows a citizen: a keyed HMAC of the BSN (route D). It is not a BSNk value. — Peer ID The identifier of an FSC peer. It is different from the OIN of the organization (REQ-67). —

docs.title: Records and tracing
docs.text: Term Meaning Do not use Decision record One ADL record: the authoritative record of a PDP decision (ADR-0036). — Console decision log The log of the policy engine that goes to Loki. It holds the detail per field, but it is observability, not audit. — LDV logbook The logbook of one controller, with one record per processing (ADR-0026). — FSC txlog The transaction log of an FSC peer (FSC-Logging): the authoritative record of transport. — W3C Trace Context The traceparent and tracestate headers. The trace ID in traceparent is the correlation key of the chain (ADR-0035). —

docs.title: Abbreviations
docs.text: Term Meaning ADL Authorization Decision Log. The Logius standard for the record of an authorization decision. In GBO, the ADL is the authoritative record of every PDP decision. ASIP Authentic Source Interface Provider. The GBO service that offers verify and retrieve as specified in ETSI TS 119 478 clause 6.1. It calls the source over FSC (ADR-0037). AuthZEN The OpenID standard for the evaluation interface from PEP to PDP. AVG Algemene verordening gegevensbescherming (GDPR). AZSP The ASI authorization server. It registers QTSPs, lets the citizen approve by logging in, and issues DPoP-bound access tokens. BSN Burgerservicenummer. The citizen identification number, restricted to authorized parties. BSNk PP BSN-koppelregister polymorphic pseudonymization. The Logius facility that turns a BSN into encrypted values per recipient. GBO uses it only at consent time (ADR-0005). DIP Discover Interface Provider. The party that publishes the data service records of ASIPs. The demo has a stub. DPoP Demonstrating Proof of Possession (RFC 9449). It binds an access token to a key of the client. DvTP Delen van gegevens via Toestemming met Private dienstverleners. The consent-based channel. EUDI wallet European Digital Identity wallet (eIDAS2). FSC Federated Service Connectivity. The connectivity standard, with Inway, Outway, Manager, directory, and contracts. FSC Manager The FSC component of each peer that negotiates contracts and signs access tokens. It is different from the OpenFTV Manager. FTV, OpenFTV Federatieve Toegangsverlening. The authorization framework that hosts the PDP. GBO Gemeenschappelijke Bronontsluiting. Gov-to-Gov The route in which a government consumer gets data on a legal basis, without consent. Design only. LDV Logboek Dataverwerkingen. The Logius standard (v1.0.0) that records each processing in the logbook of its controller. OIN Organisatie-identificatienummer. The organization identifier, bound to PKI certificates. OOTS Once-Only Technical System. The EU cross-border evidence exchange under the SDG-verordening. OpenFTV Manager The policy administration component of OpenFTV. It stores policies and serves bundles to the PDP. It is different from the FSC Manager. OpenID4VCI, OpenID4VP Protocols for credential issuance and presentation. PAP Policy Administration Point. It authors and distributes policies. PBAC Policy-based access control. PDP Policy Decision Point. It evaluates authorization requests. PEP Policy Enforcement Point. It enforces PDP decisions. In this design, the FSC Inway is the PEP. PID Person Identification Data. The identity attestation in the EUDI wallet. PIP Policy Information Point. It supplies data to the PDP: the consent status and the admission register. PuB-EAA Public Body Electronic Attestation of Attributes. QEAA Qualified Electronic Attestation of Attributes. QTSP Qualified Trust Service Provider. In the ASI route, the QTSP is an OAuth client of the AZSP, not an FSC participant. QEAA_Provider The entitlement in the national register of relying parties that a QTSP needs to become an ASI client. SD-JWT VC The selective-disclosure JWT verifiable credential format (dc+sd-jwt). VCT Verifiable credential type identifier. It is published with vct#integrity over immutable Type Metadata.

docs.title: Traceability terms
docs.text: Term Meaning BSNk precondition (BSNK-NN) A fact about BSNk PP that the design must respect. It is not a requirement on GBO (BSNk preconditions). Connection condition (AV-NN) A demand on a party that connects to GBO, not on GBO. The TO holds candidates for the management organization (connection conditions). Demo increment (SL-NN) A bounded piece of demo work with its result (increments). The ID keeps the old prefix SL. Finding (F-NN) An observation from building the demo: a design gap, an exposed design choice, an implicit requirement, or an erratum (findings). Guideline (RL-NN) A recommendation to bronhouders, for example on policy management. Not a demand on GBO (policy management). Open question (Q-NN) A question that the demo cannot answer, with the forum that must answer it and the working assumption until then (open questions). Quality scenario (QS-NN) A testable scenario for a quality goal (quality requirements). Requirement (REQ-NN) A testable demand on what GBO builds or on its interfaces (requirements).

docs.text:

docs.title: Quality requirements
docs.text:
The scenarios on this page refine the quality goals and make them testable. The scenarios use the IDs QS-01 to QS-52. The Q-NN IDs belong to the open questions.

The column "Pinned by" links the test in gbo-demo v0.9.0 that holds the scenario. "Not pinned" means that no automated test holds the scenario. In that case, the scenario is an acceptance criterion for future work, or it fails in demo v0.9.0. If a scenario fails in demo v0.9.0, its expected outcome says so.

Reason codes have two layers (Reason codes). The consumer and the ADL get a client code, for example FIELD_NOT_PERMITTED. The operator gets the rule code per field in the console decision log, for example YEAR_NOT_COVERED. Each scenario names the code at the layer where the test checks it.

docs.title: Data minimization and authorization
docs.text:
The following scenarios test data minimization and authorization:

# Scenario Expected outcome Pinned by QS-01 A consumer asks for a field that no rule covers, for example box2Inkomen next to permitted income fields Deny. Rule code NO_APPLICABLE_RULE for that field. No data leaves the source. engine_test.rego#L210 QS-02 A query asks for a year that the citizen did not give consent for Deny. Rule code YEAR_NOT_COVERED. dvt0001_test.rego#L167 QS-03 A query has no year filter Deny (fail closed). dvt0001_test.rego#L172 QS-04 The mapper cannot prove the field list because of a parse error, an exceeded limit (depth 64, 100 fragments, 1 MiB body), or an unknown schema Deny. Client code COVERAGE_UNVERIFIABLE with a subcode. A mutation or subscription gives OPERATION_NOT_SUPPORTED. engine_test.rego#L117 QS-05 A request carries a consent proof, or carries none With a consent proof, only consent-regime rules judge the request. Without one, only PID-regime rules judge it (REQ-74). engine_test.rego#L227, #L234 QS-06 The actor list of a PID rule contains a consent consumer The test fails. The lists stay disjoint. The test knows only the local consumers (F-70, R21). engine_test.rego#L371 (local consumers only) QS-07 A rule for service brp meets a request on service bri The rule does not bind, and the field gets NO_APPLICABLE_RULE. Every rule names its services (REQ-97). engine_test.rego#L397, #L497 QS-08 The PDP gets a schema for a service whose digest the bundle does not pin Deny. engine_test.rego#L108 QS-09 A consumer gets a deny The consumer sees only the client code. This code names no field and no rule code (REQ-06). engine_test.rego#L29

docs.title: Consent integrity
docs.text:
The following scenarios test the integrity of consent:

# Scenario Expected outcome Pinned by QS-10 The citizen revokes a consent between grant and use The PDP denies the next request. Rule code CONSENT_WITHDRAWN (REQ-14). consent_test.rego#L202 QS-11 A forged or tampered consent token reaches the PDP Deny. Rule code CONSENT_SIGNATURE_INVALID. consent_test.rego#L318, #L324 QS-12 A consumer other than the one in the consent presents a valid consent proof Deny. Rule code CONSENT_ACTOR_MISMATCH. dvt0001_test.rego#L84 QS-13 The status service of the register does not answer Deny (fail closed). Rule code CONSENT_STATUS_UNAVAILABLE, and the consumer sees ACCESS_DENIED. consent_test.rego#L303 QS-14 A consumer puts a literal BSN in the query under a valid consent Deny. Rule code CONSTRAINT_MISMATCH (REQ-79). dvt0001_test.rego#L131 QS-15 A request carries two consent proofs Deny. The PDP picks neither proof. Rule code CONSENT_CONTEXT_INVALID. consent_test.rego#L438 QS-16 A citizen revokes an expired or already revoked consent The backend refuses the revocation with CONSENT_NOT_REVOCABLE (REQ-109). Fails in demo v0.9.0: the backend answers 200 (#600, R31). Not pinned

docs.title: Admission and integrators
docs.text:
The following scenarios test admission and integrators:

# Scenario Expected outcome Pinned by QS-17 A suspended participant submits an FSC contract The contract stays proposed. Reason PARTY_NOT_ACTIVE. autosign_test.rego#L138 QS-18 A participant asks for a source outside its allowed_source_peer_ids The contract stays proposed. Reason SOURCE_NOT_ALLOWED. autosign_test.rego#L109 QS-19 The admission register is missing from the PDP data The contract stays proposed. Reason ADMISSION_REGISTER_UNAVAILABLE. The reason is not "party unknown". autosign_test.rego#L86 QS-20 An integrator proposes a delegated contract for a provider for which it has no registered integration The contract stays proposed. Reason DELEGATION_NOT_REGISTERED. autosign_test.rego#L176 QS-21 An integrator calls for a provider without a mandate, or the register is unavailable Deny. Rule code INTEGRATOR_NOT_REGISTERED, or INTEGRATOR_REGISTER_UNAVAILABLE (REQ-106). engine_test.rego#L621, #L631 QS-22 A suspended consumer with an existing contract sends a query under a valid consent Deny (REQ-110). Fails in demo v0.9.0: the request passes until the contract is revoked. Not pinned

docs.title: Privacy
docs.text:
The following scenarios test privacy:

# Scenario Expected outcome Pinned by QS-23 A DvTP consumer asks for income data under a consent The consumer request names the subject with the placeholder consent:identity. The request, the PDP input, and the ADL hold no citizen identifier (REQ-20). consumer_test.go#L86 QS-24 The proof carries a value made for another OIN The source gateway refuses the value and does not forward the request (REQ-80). substitution_test.go#L112 QS-25 A consumer tries to reach a source gateway or a source API directly Unreachable (REQ-81). Partly met in demo v0.9.0: Docker Compose isolates the gateways, but the source APIs share networks with consumers (R25). Not pinned (manual check of the gateways, October 5, 2026) QS-26 A consent record is read from the register The record holds no BSN and no per-party value. The register keeps PI and PP under the subject_ref of the portal, and no consent answer carries them (REQ-69). polymorphic_test.go#L39, #L85 QS-27 Two sources get values for the same citizen The values differ per recipient and cannot be linked. Not demonstrated in demo v0.9.0: the BSNk mock does not encrypt, and the demo sources share one OIN. Not pinned QS-28 An EUDI or ASI request reaches the PDP The PDP input and both decision logs hold no BSN (REQ-60). Fails in demo v0.9.0 (#368, R22). Not pinned QS-29 A component writes an LDV record that contains a valid BSN anywhere The logbook refuses the record. validate_test.go#L94

docs.title: Traceability and audit
docs.text:
The following scenarios test traceability and audit:

# Scenario Expected outcome Pinned by QS-30 A caller sends both traceparent and Fsc-Transaction-Id The component takes the trace ID from traceparent. The transaction ID is recorded next to it (REQ-55). tracecontext_test.go#L100 QS-31 An auditor reads all processing records of one request Each logbook returns the records of that trace (REQ-72). logbook_test.go#L180 QS-32 The logbook is unavailable while a request runs The request is served. Later, the outbox delivers the record once (REQ-72). outbox_test.go#L86, #L119 QS-33 An auditor holds a transaction ID and looks for the ADL record The ADL record carries the trace ID and the transaction ID (REQ-71). Partly met in demo v0.9.0: behind the FSC Inway, the record has neither. The reader finds the record through the stored request header (#369, R23). Not pinned (code: adl.go#L49-L66) QS-34 An auditor asks which policy version made the decision The ADL record names the policy version (REQ-59). Fails in demo v0.9.0. Not pinned QS-35 A citizen asks which parties processed data under one consent The answer is available per consent. Partly met in demo v0.9.0: each controller can answer from its logbook, but the citizen view per consent is not built (R19). Not pinned

docs.title: EUDI issuance
docs.text:
The following scenarios test EUDI issuance:

# Scenario Expected outcome Pinned by QS-36 A caller outside the designated issuers asks for an attestation Deny. Rule code ACTOR_NOT_ALLOWED. eud0001_test.rego#L65 QS-37 A caller posts a BSN to the adapter callback without the issuance server Refused (REQ-45). Fails in demo v0.9.0: the callback is unauthenticated (#133, R5). Not pinned QS-38 A source has no certificate set Only that source is blocked. Other sources keep working (REQ-58). service_test.go#L130 QS-39 The source metadata endpoint is unavailable The last candidate stays in use within the stale grace (REQ-66). service_test.go#L213 QS-40 A published Type Metadata version is fetched twice The responses are byte-identical, and vct#integrity matches. type_metadata_test.go#L17

docs.title: Authentic Source Interface
docs.text:
The following scenarios test the Authentic Source Interface:

# Scenario Expected outcome Pinned by QS-41 A QTSP uses a token issued for another data service 401. A token is valid for one data service only (REQ-95). dataservices_test.go#L16 QS-42 A request has no DPoP proof, or replays one 401. token_test.go#L158, #L200 QS-43 A request asks for an attribute outside the approved authorization_details 401 insufficient_scope (REQ-103). token_test.go#L217 QS-44 A verify or retrieve succeeds The body is sealed with a detached JWS in X-JWS-Signature. Errors are not sealed (REQ-83). handler_test.go#L238 QS-45 A verify gives Match The response carries no value from the source (REQ-85). handler_test.go#L108 QS-46 The source holds no value, or the chain fails No value gives Unknown. A failed chain gives an error, never Unknown (REQ-84, REQ-93). handler_test.go#L140, source_test.go#L141 QS-47 A retrieve asks for an attribute for which the source has no value 404. No partial result (REQ-101). handler_test.go#L291 QS-48 A QTSP reads the discovery records of the ASIP Each record leads to the data service endpoint, its contract, and the authorization server metadata (REQ-99, REQ-100). discovery_test.go#L66, #L105 QS-49 A QTSP without QEAA_Provider in the register registers, or loses the entitlement later Registration refused (unapproved_software_statement). After a withdrawal, the next re-check deactivates the client (REQ-88, REQ-89). If the register is unreachable, the client stays active (R27). registration_test.go#L152, #L276, #L306 QS-50 The wallet returns on the same device but in another browser Refused before the verifier is asked. wallet_test.go#L123 QS-51 An FSC peer other than the ASIP asks for BRP personal data under the PID regime Deny. Rule code ACTOR_NOT_ALLOWED. ASI0001 judges service brp only. asi0001_test.rego#L29, #L56 QS-52 The QTSP holds the access token The QTSP cannot read the BSN (F-86). Fails in demo v0.9.0 (#595, R26). Not pinned

The ETSI conformance matrix etsi-ts-119478.yaml gives each ETSI TS 119 478 requirement a status and the tests that hold it. The CI check fails in each of these cases:

  • A requirement ID has no entry.
  • A status lacks what it requires.
  • A named test does not exist.

One entry has the status failing: fuzzy matching against a response without a value (R30).

docs.title: Open quality targets
docs.text:
Availability, capacity, and performance targets have no scenarios in this version of the TO. By design, the demo runs one instance of each component. For more information, see the availability model. Two targets are open:

  • The volumes that the chain must handle (Q-47).
  • The propagation time, availability, and latency of the consent status (REQ-75). The register is a dependency of every DvTP decision (R10).
