docs.title: Risks and technical debt
docs.text: The design and gbo-demo v0.9.0 have known risks and technical debt. The risk list carries forward the gap analysis of the archived reference architecture v0.6.2, with updates from the demo findings. Every entry names its follow-up: a decision, a hardening action, a demo issue, or an open question. Each entry links the findings (F), open questions (Q), requirements (REQ), and decisions (ADR) that it rests on.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Each risk belongs to one group:

ID Risk Group R1 The ASI exists at demo grade only Routes R2 The SDG-OOTS bridge is design-level only Routes R3 No Gov-to-Gov regime and no positive evidence for it Routes R4 The consent proof is a bearer token Security R5 The EUDI adapter accepts unauthenticated issuance callbacks Security R6 No rate limiting or quota Security R7 Data-chain responses are not sealed Security R8 Contract acceptance sees the parties but not the service Security R9 Demo-grade shared services Production readiness R10 The consent register (toestemmingsregister) is a dependency of every DvTP decision Production readiness R11 The demo runs one PDP for all providers Production readiness R12 Policy distribution has no integrity chain and no visible fallback Production readiness R13 The PDP mapper is a patch on OpenFTV Production readiness R14 New sources need a restart of the issuance server Production readiness R15 The legal ceiling of the service catalog (dienstencatalogus) has no technical counterpart Governance R16 Rego instead of ODRL Governance R17 GraphQL is not a recognized data service (datadienst) type of the Federatief Datastelsel (FDS) Governance R18 Integrator mandates have no validity and no governance Governance R19 LDV gaps: citizen view, activity register, ASIP Governance R20 Onboarding cost for small bronhouders Governance R21 The absence of a consent proof selects the PID regime Security R22 BSN in the decision logs of the EUDI and ASI routes Privacy R23 The ADL record is incomplete behind the FSC Inway Audit R24 The consent proof freezes at consent DvTP R25 Source isolation is incomplete Security R26 The QTSP can read the BSN in the ASI token Privacy R27 No national register for QTSP admission ASI R28 No link between the QTSP login and the source login ASI R29 The NL PID has no place of birth ASI R30 Fuzzy matching without returning a value ASI R31 The backend revokes a revoked consent again DvTP R32 Only the network protects the register listener Security R33 A suspended consumer keeps access DvTP R34 Any connected peer can read any consent status Security R35 The consumer sets the consent validity DvTP R36 Attestations are valid 365 days without a change feed EUDI R37 BSNk recognition of the consent facility (toestemmingsvoorziening) is not settled DvTP

docs.title: R1: The ASI exists at demo grade only
docs.text:
• Risk: The Authentic Source Interface is built (ADR-0037), but only as a local demo stack. From January 1, 2027, the interface of CIR 2026/1735 Annex IV and the seal obligation apply (F-80).
  • Impact: Production needs these parts, which the demo does not have:
    • a qualified seal certificate and its holder (Q-17, Q-28, Q-32)
    • the national register of relying parties and access certificates (R27)
    • real identification means: the DigiD route is a mock, and the wallet verifier also trusts the development issuer CA (Q-36)
    • a decision on the role of GBO (Q-37) and on catalog registration (Q-31, Q-67)
    • a simulation deployment (#594)
  • Follow-up: Three items track this risk:
    • the proposed ADRs 0041 and 0042
    • the ASI risks R26 to R30
    • the standards feedback E1 to E10, which is not sent.
  • Related: F-80, F-84, F-87, REQ-112, SL-28.

docs.title: R2: The SDG-OOTS bridge is design-level only
docs.text:
• Risk: The AS4 bridge for SDG-OOTS has no implementation.
  • Impact: Until the bridge is built, the EU obligation is not met.
  • Follow-up: ADR-0020, ADR-0024. It is open who builds the adapter (Q-79).
  • Related: SDG-OOTS scenario.

docs.title: R3: No Gov-to-Gov regime and no positive evidence for it
docs.text:
• Risk: The PDP knows two regimes: consent and PID. No legal-basis regime, rule set, or legal basis (grondslag) data exists. A request without a consent proof falls in the PID regime (ADR-0031).
  • Impact: The two-path access-basis model of ADR-0004 is only half proven. A Gov-to-Gov regime cannot reuse "absence of a token" as its evidence, because the PID regime already uses it (R21).
  • Follow-up: Define the positive evidence for a legal basis. Then add a regime and a rule set.
  • Related: REQ-74, Gov-to-Gov scenario.

docs.title: R4: The consent proof is a bearer token
docs.text:
• Risk: The actor binding stops another consumer from using a proof. It does not stop replay by the same consumer within the validity period.
  • Impact: A stolen proof gives data access for its remaining life.
  • Follow-up: Make the validity period shorter. Bind the proof to the FSC identity with proof of possession (ADR-0032).
  • Related: REQ-68, Bearer token.

docs.title: R5: The EUDI adapter accepts unauthenticated issuance callbacks
docs.text:
• Risk: The issuance server verifies the PID disclosure. The gap is behind it: the adapter route POST /attestations/{source}/{type} has no caller authentication (source_release_runtime.go#L69-L81, plain ListenAndServe at main.go#L700). The developer portal shows the gap: its playground posts a typed BSN straight to the adapter through /eudi-api/ (EudiQrPanel.tsx#L36-L51, nginx.conf#L36-L42).
  • Impact: Any caller that reaches the adapter can post an arbitrary BSN. The adapter calls the source over FSC as the designated issuer. As a result, the PDP allows the request, and the adapter returns the claims without any wallet. Two more gaps add to this risk:
    • nothing binds the BSN in the source query to the verified disclosure
    • the PID trust list of the issuance server also holds non-PID anchors, including the GBO development issuer CA.
  • Follow-up: Authenticate the callback (mTLS or a signed request from the issuance server), or let the adapter verify the SD-JWT itself. Bind the disclosure to the request. Restrict the PID trust list to PID issuers (REQ-45, #133). The QTSP callback already uses a secret path and CA-pinned TLS.
  • Related: F-70, Q-18, ADR-0018, SL-25 (dropped), the callback gap.

docs.title: R6: No rate limiting or quota
docs.text:
• Risk: Authorization concern ⑤ exists only as structural checks: parse, depth, size, and coverage. Rate limiting and quota are not built.
  • Impact: Only the FSC contracts limit enumeration and abuse.
  • Follow-up: Define limits per grant. Enforce them at the Inway or the PDP (ADR-0004).
  • Related: REQ-17.

docs.title: R7: Data-chain responses are not sealed
docs.text:
• Risk: DvTP and EUDI source responses carry no qualified electronic seal. ASI verification results carry a seal: a detached JWS (ES256, x5c) over the exact body. The ASI certificate is a development certificate and is not qualified (REQ-83).
  • Impact: Non-repudiation of a data-chain response rests on the FSC transaction log and the ADL. No seal supports it.
  • Follow-up: Decide whether every source response gets one seal, whatever the channel (Q-75). The ASI seal format waits for Q-32 (ADR-0041). The BSN in the decision logs is a separate risk (R22).
  • Related: F-80, E4.

docs.title: R8: Contract acceptance sees the parties but not the service
docs.text:
• Risk: The autosign input carries peer IDs and grant types only.
  • Impact: At contract time, the policy cannot enforce admission per service.
  • Follow-up: An upstream FSC change. Until that change, request-time rules compensate (ADR-0015).
  • Related: F-56 (closed), REQ-62.

docs.title: R21: The absence of a consent proof selects the PID regime
docs.text:
• Risk: A request without a consent proof is in the PID regime (engine.rego#L168-L181). The only control is the list of designated issuers per EUDI rule. A consumer on that list can skip consent: it leaves out the consent proof.
  • Impact: The PID regime rests on an identifier whose origin no one in the chain checks. A test keeps the issuer list disjoint from the DvTP consumers, but the test knows only the local consumers. For the simulation consumer, only an inspection shows that it is disjoint.
  • Follow-up: Make positive PID evidence at the point where the wallet presentation is verified. Bind this evidence to the subject of the query (REQ-45, #133, #381). Until then, test the disjointness per environment.
  • Related: F-70, REQ-74, Q-18, Q-22, ADR-0031.

docs.title: R25: Source isolation is incomplete
docs.text:
• Risk: The rule "Decrypt only after the allow" depends on one condition: only the FSC Inway reaches the source gateway (REQ-81). In Docker Compose, the gateways publish no port and are only on source-gateways and sources. However, the source APIs (graphql-server, brp-graphql-server, lvg-graphql-server) are also on backend and fsc-infra (docker-compose.yml#L631-L636), together with the consumer backend (#L1080-L1082).
  • Impact: A party on those networks can reach a source API without the Inway, the PDP, and the gateway. The Helm chart has no NetworkPolicy. The decrypted value is not bound to one consent (no nonce).
  • Follow-up: Take the source APIs off the shared networks. Outside Compose, add a NetworkPolicy or an equal control. Add the nonce as a second safeguard (BSNk preconditions).
  • Related: F-79, REQ-21, ADR-0033, network isolation.

docs.title: R32: Only the network protects the register listener
docs.text:
• Risk: The register listener for create, list, read, and revoke has no caller authentication. The consent portal (toestemmingsportaal) backend is its only intended caller (REQ-39). In Compose, the register is on backend (docker-compose.yml#L737-L740).
  • Impact: Any party that reaches the register directly can create or revoke consents for every citizen.
  • Follow-up: Decide between authentication of the backend and network isolation (Q-58). Isolation alone works only under one condition: the register and the backend run at one participant (Q-49).
  • Related: REQ-76 (the status listener goes over FSC).

docs.title: R34: Any connected peer can read any consent status
docs.text:
• Risk: The status service over FSC answers every peer that has a contract for it. It does not check that the caller is the PDP of a source in the consent.
  • Impact: A connected peer with a consent_id learns its status.
  • Follow-up: Restrict the status answer to the PDPs of the sources in the consent (REQ-76, #382).
  • Related: ADR-0032.

docs.title: R22: BSN in the decision logs of the EUDI and ASI routes
docs.text:
• Risk: In the EUDI and ASI routes, the query names the citizen with the plain BSN. The PDP input, the ADL, and the console decision log hold it. Nothing masks the BSN, and the mapper stopped pseudonymizing it.
  • Impact: REQ-60 is not met for these routes. Masking alone also does not meet the requirement.
  • Follow-up: Keep identifiers out of the PDP input (ADR-0043, proposed). The decision is made in #368.
  • Related: F-54, SL-29 (reversed by PR #370), the BSN exception.

docs.title: R23: The ADL record is incomplete behind the FSC Inway
docs.text:
• Risk: The ADL is the authoritative decision record (ADR-0036). Three parts are missing:
    • Behind the FSC Inway, the record has its own random trace and no transaction ID. The Inway passes neither to the PDP (#369).
    • The record does not name the policy version (REQ-59).
    • The record holds only the allow and the reason. It does not hold the consent status answer (F-72).
  • Impact: An auditor finds the record only through the stored request header. The auditor cannot replay the decision against a known policy.
  • Follow-up: Fix the trace headers upstream in open-fsc (ADR-0035). Record the bundle revision in the ADL.
  • Related: F-41, REQ-71, Q-25.

docs.title: R26: The QTSP can read the BSN in the ASI token
docs.text:
• Risk: ETSI requires the identification data in the access token. In the demo, a token claim holds the BSN in readable form (tokens.go#L29).
  • Impact: The QTSP holds the token. It can read a BSN that it is not allowed to process (P-04).
  • Follow-up: Encrypt the identification data for the ASIP (#595). Send the gap to ETSI (E7).
  • Related: F-86, REQ-86, Q-36.

docs.title: R27: No national register for QTSP admission
docs.text:
• Risk: The authorization server admits a QTSP on the entitlement QEAA_Provider in the national register of relying parties. That register and its API do not exist. It is not fixed which identifier links the QTSP certificate to its entry. The demo uses a stub register file.
  • Impact: QTSPs cannot be admitted in production. If the register is unreachable during a re-check, the demo keeps the client active (fail-open). Issued tokens stay valid up to 10 minutes after a withdrawal.
  • Follow-up: Q-34 (outage behavior), Q-35 (identifier), Q-41 (tokens after withdrawal).
  • Related: F-85, REQ-88, REQ-89, E10.

docs.title: R28: No link between the QTSP login and the source login
docs.text:
• Risk: The QTSP identifies the citizen, and the ASI authorization server identifies the citizen again. Nothing links the two. The QR route can be completed on another phone.
  • Impact: A QTSP can attest the data of person B to person A.
  • Follow-up: Add a check under CIR 2025/1569 art. 9(5). In this check, the QTSP sends its identification data for verification. As an alternative, the QTSP gives this data to the authorization server as a hint (Q-40). Send the gap to ETSI (E6).
  • Related: F-93, REQ-90, REQ-102.

docs.title: R29: The NL PID has no place of birth
docs.text:
• Risk: CIR 2024/2977 makes the place of birth a mandatory PID attribute. The NL PID type metadata has no place of birth. As a result, the authorization server asks for four of the five mandatory attributes.
  • Impact: If the Netherlands reads "identification data" as the mandatory PID attributes, a token from the NL Wallet cannot meet that reading. DigiD gives a BSN only (F-88).
  • Follow-up: Ask the NL Wallet team. Fix the minimum identification data in the PSA (Q-36).
  • Related: F-94, REQ-86.

docs.title: R30: Fuzzy matching without returning a value
docs.text:
• Risk: The ASIP gives MatchWithVariation and never returns the stored value. Annex IV of CIR 2026/1735 makes the value optional but keeps the fuzzy-matching requirement. The conformance matrix marks that requirement failing.
  • Impact: In a literal reading of the annex, the ASIP does not conform.
  • Follow-up: Decide whether the ASIP returns the value on a match (Q-29). Send the gap to ETSI (E2).
  • Related: F-92, REQ-85, REQ-113.

docs.title: R24: The consent proof freezes at consent
docs.text:
• Risk: BSNk transforms only while the citizen is logged in (BSNK-04). As a result, the proof fixes the parties, the key versions, the BSN authorization, and the proof form for its whole validity period. The proof has no version.
  • Impact: A new source needs a new consent. A re-keyed source must keep its old keys (AV-09). A new proof form makes all outstanding proofs fail with CONSENT_CONTEXT_INVALID.
  • Follow-up: Give the proof a version. Extend the service catalog with OIN, key version, and BSN authorization per party (REQ-82, Q-77).
  • Related: F-78, ADR-0032, the proof freezes at consent.

docs.title: R31: The backend revokes a revoked consent again
docs.text:
• Risk: A direct revoke of an expired or already revoked consent returns HTTP 200, sets REVOKED again, and writes a new LDV record (main.go#L282-L299).
  • Impact: The status history and the logbook get false entries.
  • Follow-up: Refuse the revoke with CONSENT_NOT_REVOCABLE (REQ-109, #600).
  • Related: F-97.

docs.title: R33: A suspended consumer keeps access
docs.text:
• Risk: The request policy does not read the admission status of a direct consumer. A suspended consumer with an existing contract can still send queries under a valid consent.
  • Impact: Suspension takes effect only at the revocation of the contract.
  • Follow-up: REQ-110. Q-53 covers the time until the suspension takes effect.
  • Related: ADR-0015.

docs.title: R35: The consumer sets the consent validity
docs.text:
• Risk: The consumer sends the validity period. The default is one year, with no upper limit. The citizen cannot change it.
  • Impact: A proof can live longer than the purpose needs. This makes R4 and R24 worse.
  • Follow-up: Decide who sets the validity period (Q-13, Q-76).
  • Related: F-11, REQ-19.

docs.title: R37: BSNk recognition of the consent facility is not settled
docs.text:
• Risk: Only a recognized party can activate and transform (BSNK-01). It is open whether the consent facility can be that party, and in which role. The demo assumes route D: the backend derives and activates, and the register stores PI and PP.
  • Impact: Route D works only under one condition: the backend and the register are one BSNk participant. The rotation of the reference key (Q-56) and the protection of stored PI and PP (Q-57) are open.
  • Follow-up: Q-26, Q-49, and ADR-0040 (proposed).
  • Related: F-75, REQ-69.

docs.title: R36: Attestations are valid 365 days without a change feed
docs.text:
• Risk: Every attestation type gets a fixed validity of 365 days. GBO only queries sources and has no change feed.
  • Impact: If the source data changes, an issuer must revoke an attestation that is valid for 24 hours or more. GBO cannot do that.
  • Follow-up: Per type, choose short-lived attestations or a change feed with revocation (REQ-77).
  • Related: F-82, AV-12, AV-13, ADR-0028.

docs.title: R9: Demo-grade shared services
docs.text:
• Risk: The shared services are demo grade: the consent register runs in memory by default, DigiD is a mock, and the PKI is self-generated. The BSNk mock follows the BSNk interface (as JSON), but it encrypts nothing. The three demo sources share one OIN and one decryption component.
  • Impact: None of these services carries production trust or availability. The demo does not demonstrate unlinkability per source.
  • Follow-up: ADR-0023, ADR-0005, a replicated register store (SL-12), and a DigiD connection.
  • Related: Q-54, demo mock and production BSNk.

docs.title: R10: The consent register is a dependency of every DvTP decision
docs.text:
• Risk: For every request, the policy asks for the consent status online, without a cache.
  • Impact: A register outage stops all consent-based traffic (fail closed).
  • Follow-up: Set the availability, latency, and propagation targets (REQ-75, Q-47). Replicate the register.
  • Related: F-61, ADR-0032.

docs.title: R11: The demo runs one PDP for all providers
docs.text:
• Risk: The target model has a PAP and a PDP at each bronhouder (ADR-0021). The demo runs one shared PDP.
  • Impact: The demo does not show policy separation between bronhouders.
  • Follow-up: Run a PDP per provider in the simulation deployment.
  • Related: Q-21 (answered).

docs.title: R12: Policy distribution has no integrity chain and no visible fallback
docs.text:
• Risk: By default, the PDP loads policies from a bind mount. Bundle distribution through the OpenFTV Manager is opt-in. Bundles are not signed. Signing is not planned while bundles stay inside one organization (#426). The policy store is cumulative, and one broken module stops every decision.
  • Impact: There is no integrity chain from author to runtime. There is no visible fallback to the last valid policy set.
  • Follow-up: Guidelines RL-01 and RL-05. If a bundle crosses an organization boundary, signing becomes a requirement.
  • Related: F-09, F-51, F-52, Q-21.

docs.title: R13: The PDP mapper is a patch on OpenFTV
docs.text:
• Risk: The PDP is built from OpenFTV tag v0.1.0, with the FTV GraphQL mapper patched in.
  • Impact: Upstream changes can break the build. The patch steps fail loudly, but the maintenance cost stays.
  • Follow-up: Contribute the mapper extension point to OpenFTV upstream (ADR-0013).
  • Related: REQ-42.

docs.title: R14: New sources need a restart of the issuance server
docs.text:
• Risk: The issuance server reads its configuration at startup.
  • Impact: Source activation needs a controlled restart.
  • Follow-up: Accepted in demo v0.9.0 (ADR-0016). If the issuance server supports reload, revisit this decision.
  • Related: REQ-64.

docs.title: R15: The legal ceiling of the service catalog has no technical counterpart
docs.text:
• Risk: Rule coverage replaced the catalog artifact. The legally anchored ceiling and its governance (the Bureau DvTP process) are not defined.
  • Impact: The legal ceiling of what a consumer can ask for is not inspectable on its own.
  • Follow-up: A legal anchoring decision (ADR-0008, ADR-0009). The data-set description is one input (REQ-121).
  • Related: F-74.

docs.title: R16: Rego instead of ODRL
docs.text:
• Risk: The PSA lists ODRL for S06. The design uses Rego, and Cedar inside the OpenFTV Manager.
  • Impact: The comply-or-explain duty is open.
  • Follow-up: Bring the deviation to the standards bodies, in line with D-13. For more information, see Policy lifecycle and Q-78.

docs.title: R17: GraphQL is not a recognized FDS data service type
docs.text:
• Risk: The data access pillar rests on a deviation that no standard covers.
  • Follow-up: ADR-0025.

docs.title: R18: Integrator mandates have no validity and no governance
docs.text:
• Risk: Three points of the integrator route are open. A mandate has no validity period, and the integrator is not in the proof (Q-46). The upstream act.sub deviates from RFC 8693. The route itself is built (opt-in) and has three parts (ADR-0034):
    • an FSC delegated grant
    • a mandate per integrator, provider, and rule in the admission register
    • a consent that binds the represented party.
  • Impact: A mandate stays valid until someone removes it. It is not set who admits integrators and on which terms (AV-06).
  • Follow-up: Three items are open: mandate validity, the governance of admission (Q-74), and a change log for admissions (REQ-123).
  • Related: F-73 (closed), REQ-106, Q-12.

docs.title: R19: LDV gaps: citizen view, activity register, ASIP
docs.text:
• Risk: LDV is built: each controller logs its own processings in its own logbook (ADR-0026). These gaps remain:
    • the citizen view of processings per consent is not built (P-13)
    • the register of processing activities is a stand-in (Q-08)
    • the local dpl.gbo.* extension is not agreed (Q-72)
    • the ASIP writes no LDV records
    • no pointer leads from the ADL to the consent logbook (Q-25)
    • no retention, access model, or tamper evidence exists for the ADL the logbooks, and the FSC transaction logs (REQ-32).
  • Impact: A citizen cannot see QTSP verifications. A chain read stops at a party that does not log under LDV (F-68).
  • Follow-up: The open points of ADR-0026, and the consumer obligation (AV-02).
  • Related: REQ-72, F-64, SL-50.

docs.title: R20: Onboarding cost for small bronhouders
docs.text:
• Risk: The cost to connect a source stays high for small organizations.
  • Impact: There is an adoption risk for municipalities and small sources.
  • Follow-up: ADR-0027.

docs.title: Accepted technical debt
docs.text:
The design accepts the following technical debt on purpose:

  • Monetary amounts in attestations are integers, because the pinned wallet stack cannot represent non-integral values (ADR-0017).
  • Attestations have no nested claims (REQ-78).
  • The unsecured source transport exists for local development. The mount policy excludes it from deployments. The code does not exclude it.
  • The demo works around OpenFTV upstream quirks and documents them: the policy language flag, the missing policy-data APIs, and the broken policy DELETE (the demo retires a policy instead).

docs.title: Traceability
docs.text:
• Requirements: REQ-39, REQ-45, REQ-59, REQ-60, REQ-71, REQ-74, REQ-75, REQ-76, REQ-77, REQ-81, REQ-83, REQ-86, REQ-88, REQ-106, REQ-109, REQ-110
  • Findings: F-52 (open), F-54 (open), F-70 (open), F-72 (open), F-78 (open), F-79 (open), F-80 (open), F-85 (open), F-86 (open), F-92 (open), F-93 (open), F-94 (open)
  • Open questions: Q-08, Q-13, Q-21 (answered), Q-29, Q-34, Q-36, Q-40, Q-49, Q-58, Q-75 (all open unless marked)
  • Demo increments: SL-12 (planned), SL-25 (dropped), SL-28 (done), SL-29 (done, reversed by PR #370), SL-50 (done), SL-51 (done)

docs.title: Solution strategy
docs.text: The design rests on the pillars in the following tables. Each pillar links to the decisions that record its rationale and to the page that gives the details. The pillars realize the capabilities of the PSA within the solution shape of the GO. gbo-demo v0.9.0 implements every pillar that is marked "built".

docs.title: The generic chain
docs.text: Pillar Approach Decisions Detail Data access Each bronhouder has one GraphQL API. The query is the authorization object. ADR-0001, ADR-0025 Building blocks Connectivity All domestic traffic uses FSC. Protocol adapters at the edge handle all other traffic. ADR-0003 Deployment view Authorization The FSC Inway is the PEP. OPA/Rego in OpenFTV is the PDP, behind AuthZEN with the FTV GraphQL profile. Authorization has five separable concerns and one PDP per bronhouder. There is no central authorization server. Rules are plain Rego, bound by regime, FSC service, and field. ADR-0002, ADR-0004, ADR-0009, ADR-0013 Authorization Regime from evidence The evidence that a request carries selects the regime. A consent proof gives the consent regime. Without a consent proof, the PID regime applies. Grants carry no properties. ADR-0031 Regime selection Admission A register admits parties. The decision policy does not admit parties. A separate policy decides on FSC contracts. An integrator connects under FSC delegation with a registered mandate. ADR-0015, ADR-0034 Admission and activation Policy management Each bronhouder manages and distributes its own policy. GBO supplies a reference policy set and guidelines (RL-01 to RL-05). GBO does not supply a central PAP. ADR-0021 Policy lifecycle Source onboarding Sources publish their own service description. A reconciler validates the description, and an operator activates it. A valid contract alone does not activate a source. ADR-0016 Source onboarding

docs.title: Consent and pseudonymization (DvTP)
docs.text: Pillar Approach Decisions Detail Consent proof A signed consent proof carries an encrypted value per source. The consumer names the subject with a placeholder. For every request, the policy verifies the proof and asks for the status online over FSC. ADR-0032 Consent, DvTP query Pseudonymization The design uses BSNk PP only at consent time. After the allow decision, the source gateway decrypts the value for its own OIN. Only the FSC Inway reaches the gateway. The consent facility (toestemmingsvoorziening) recognizes the citizen by its own keyed reference (route D, proposed). ADR-0005, ADR-0033, ADR-0040 Pseudonymization

docs.title: EUDI routes
docs.text: Pillar Approach Decisions Detail EUDI issuance Issuance is disclosure-based OpenID4VCI on the nl-wallet stack. Sources feed it over FSC under the PID regime. The bronhouder is the PuB-EAA provider, and GBO operates the facility. Built. The PSA treats wallet support (P-06) as a hook outside version 1. ADR-0018, ADR-0017, ADR-0028 EUDI issuance ASI verification An OAuth front door as specified in ETSI TS 119 478 clause 6.1 (verify, retrieve, authorization server). The QTSP is an OAuth client and does not take part in FSC. The design has one data service per authentic source and one token per data service. The source describes its ASI attributes. Built, demo grade. ADR-0037, ADR-0038, ADR-0039 ASI verification

docs.title: Audit and traceability
docs.text: Pillar Approach Decisions Detail Audit The design has three authoritative records: the ADL for authorization decisions, the LDV logbook of each controller for processings, and FSC-Logging for transport. Observability tools are not audit records. ADR-0036, ADR-0026 Logging, audit and traceability Traceability W3C Trace Context is the correlation key. Each component records the FSC transaction ID next to the trace ID. ADR-0035 Correlation

docs.title: Design-level and proposed elements
docs.text:
Two strategy elements exist at design level only. Both reuse the generic chain:

  • The AS4 bridge for SDG-OOTS (ADR-0020) is a protocol adapter in front of the same FSC and authorization chain.
  • Gov-to-Gov needs its own positive evidence for the legal-basis regime (ADR-0031). No rule set exists for this regime (R3).

Four decisions have the status proposed. Each one waits for an open question or a demo issue:

  • ADR-0040, citizen recognition, waits for Q-49.
  • ADR-0041, seal format of ASI results, waits for Q-32.
  • ADR-0042, per-attribute token binding, waits for Q-33.
  • ADR-0043, identifiers out of the PDP input, waits for demo issue #368.

docs.title: Traceability
docs.text:
• Requirements: REQ-17, REQ-21, REQ-55, REQ-61, REQ-64, REQ-68, REQ-71, REQ-72, REQ-74, REQ-80, REQ-97, REQ-106, REQ-112
  • Findings: F-70 (open), F-79 (open), F-87 (open), F-89 (open)
  • Open questions: Q-21 (answered), Q-32 (open), Q-33 (open), Q-38 (partly answered), Q-49 (open)
  • Demo increments: SL-28 (done), SL-45 (done), SL-46 (done), SL-47 (done), SL-48 (done), SL-50 (done), SL-51 (done)

docs.title: Building block view
docs.text:
GBO has one base and three channels. GBO Basis sits at every bronhouder and opens the source in one standard way. The DvTP, EUDI and OOTS channels each serve a different kind of consumer, and GBO Basis feeds all three. This picture is the overview of the Globaal Ontwerp, with the state of gbo-demo v0.9.0 added.

Each block with a thick border is clickable and zooms in one level. The levels go from this overview, to one page per block, to the component catalog with the code.

docs.title: The blocks
docs.text:
The overview has seven GBO blocks. Five of them run in the demo:

Block What it does In demo v0.9.0 Zoom in Generic source access Opens a source over FSC with GraphQL. The PDP of the source decides on every request, field by field. Built GBO Basis Source configuration The source describes its own services. GBO validates the description and activates it as a release. Built Source configuration GBO tools Help a bronhouder that cannot offer GraphQL, through a translation layer. Design only ADR-0027 Consent facility (toestemmingsvoorziening) The citizen gives, views and revokes consent. The register signs a consent proof for the consumer. Built, with a DigiD mock DvTP channel PuB-EAA provider Issues an attestation from source data to the wallet of the citizen. Built on the nl-wallet stack PuB-EAA provider ASI provider Lets a QTSP verify or retrieve an attribute at the source (eIDAS article 45e). Built, demo grade ASI provider OOTS adapter Answers an EU evidence request with source data. Design only OOTS channel

The pseudonymization facility BSNk PP (pseudonimiseervoorziening) and the QTSP are not GBO components. GBO uses them. The demo runs a mock of BSNk PP.

docs.title: How GBO Basis feeds every channel
docs.text:
Every channel reaches the source in the same way. A channel component calls the source through its own FSC Outway. At the source, GBO Basis decides and only then asks the source:

flowchart LR subgraph ch["Channel (one of three)"] direction TB c1("Consumer backend<br/>DvTP") c2("EUDI adapter<br/>PuB-EAA") c3("ASIP<br/>ASI") end out["Outway of the caller"] subgraph gb["GBO Basis at the source"] direction LR pep("FSC Inway<br/>PEP") pdp("PDP<br/>policy per field") gw("Source gateway") end api[("Source API")] subgraph rec["Records"] direction TB adl[("ADL<br/>decision")] ldv[("LDV<br/>processing")] txl[("FSC txlog<br/>transport")] end c1 & c2 & c3 --> out out -- "1 · mTLS + FSC token" --> pep pep -- "2 · AuthZEN question" --> pdp pdp -- "3 · allow or deny" --> pep pep -- "4 · only after allow" --> gw gw -- "5 · query" --> api pdp -.-> adl api -.-> ldv pep -.-> txl %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class c1 ext class c2,c3 eudi class out,pep,pdp,gw basis class api source class adl,ldv,txl store class pep,pdp,gw zoom style gb fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#16A34A click pep "gbo-basis/" "GBO Basis" click pdp "gbo-basis/authorization/" "Authorization" click gw "gbo-basis/source-access/" "Source access"

Figure 2: One path to the source for all channels. Dotted lines: the three audit records.

The channels differ in the evidence that a request carries. The evidence selects the rules that the PDP applies, and it decides how the source learns who the citizen is:

Channel Evidence in the request Rules How the source gets the citizen DvTP A consent proof, signed by the consent register (toestemmingsregister) DVT0001, LVG0001 The source decrypts its own value from the proof PuB-EAA issuance No consent proof: PID regime EUD0001, EUD0002 The adapter puts the BSN from the PID of the wallet in the query ASI No consent proof: PID regime ASI0001 The ASIP puts the BSN from its access token in the query

For the regime rule, see ADR-0031. For the five rules, see Authorization.

docs.text:
This catalog is the lowest zoom level of the building block view. It lists every component of gbo-demo v0.9.0 with its responsibility and a link to its code. Each block is either part of the target architecture or demo scaffolding. Demo scaffolding makes the demo usable or observable.

To read the design from the top down, start at the overview. It shows GBO Basis and the channels that GBO Basis feeds, and each block there zooms in to this catalog.

The demo implements three routes end to end: the DvTP query under consent, EUDI issuance, and ASI verification for QTSPs. The SDG-OOTS adapter has no implementation and is not in this view (ADR-0020). The QTSP and the Discover Interface are external roles. The context view shows them.

docs.title: Level 2: authorization chain
docs.text:
The authorization chain has the following components:

Component Responsibility Implementation OpenFTV PDP Decides every data request and every FSC contract submission. The build uses OpenFTV tag v0.1.0 and patches in the GBO FTV GraphQL mapper. If a patch step changes nothing, the build fails. The PDP offers AuthZEN 1.0 at POST /authzen/v1/evaluation over HTTPS. It writes one ADL record per evaluation. It does not start without the ADL database. services/openftv-pdp, Dockerfile FTV GraphQL mapper Implements the mapping function of the FTV GraphQL profile (ftv-graphql/0.1). It parses the raw body and resolves parent types from the bundled schema of the FSC service in the access token. It returns the field list with arguments as the source executes them, or COVERAGE_UNVERIFIABLE with a subcode. It accepts only queries. For any other operation it returns OPERATION_NOT_SUPPORTED. It applies fixed limits: body 1 MiB, depth 64, and 1000 field records. It verifies no token, reads no flow, and calls no external service. services/ftv-graphql-mapper, limits, OpenFTV adapter Bundled schemas and pins One directive-free schema per FSC service (bri, brp, lvg). The policy bundle pins the digest of each schema. The policy denies an evaluation against another schema (SCHEMA_MISMATCH). A CI job compares the bundled schemas with the source schemas. schemas/pdp-mirror, graphql_schemas.rego, check-schema-drift.sh Policy entrypoint Allows the source-metadata fetch for two known peers, on the two metadata services only. It sends every other request to the rule engine. It passes only allow and the consumer's reason code to OpenFTV. policies/authz.rego Rule engine Selects the regime from the evidence. If the request carries a consent token, the regime is consent. Without a token, the regime is PID. The engine binds a field to the rules of that regime that serve the FSC service and name the field key. It denies a field that no rule covers (NO_APPLICABLE_RULE). The first bound rule without a reason grants the field. The engine checks the integrator mandate on every delegated call. It returns a coarse reason code to the consumer and keeps the per-field codes for the operator. policies/gbo/engine.rego Request reader Reads the field list, the arguments, the caller, the represented party, and the time from the input. It does no checks. policies/gbo/lib.rego Consent PIP Verifies the consent token in policy: ES256 signature, issuer, audience, type, validity with 30 s skew, and required claims. It fetches the JWKS directly from the register and caches it for 300 s. It fetches the status for each evaluation over FSC, through the PDP's Outway. The status fetch has no cache and a 2 s timeout. Every failure has its own reason code. The engine copies the resolved consent into its response. policies/gbo/consent.rego Authorization rules Five plain-Rego rules, listed in the next table. Each rule names its regime, its FSC services, and its fields. It also states its own reasons to deny. policies/gbo/rules Contract acceptance policy Decides whether a provider's FSC Manager signs a submitted contract. It accepts grant types service connection and delegated service connection. It applies eight ordered refusal codes, from NOT_AN_AUTOSIGN_REQUEST to DELEGATION_NOT_REGISTERED. It keeps a missing register (ADMISSION_REGISTER_UNAVAILABLE) apart from a missing entry (PARTY_NOT_IN_REGISTRY). policies/fsc/autosign.rego Admission register (toelatingsregister) Holds the admitted participants: bronhouders, GBO system participants (EDI issuer, PDP, ASIP), and consumers. Each entry has active and allowed_source_peer_ids. The register also holds integrator mandates (integrations) and serves them as acts_for. OpenFTV pulls it every 5 s over a network that only the PDP shares. The register deactivates an entry and never deletes it. It keeps no change log (REQ-123). It is a SQLite database with an admin UI. services/dvtp-onboarding-register, PIP pull

The PID regime has no positive evidence of its own. A request without a consent token enters it (F-70). For this reason, the PID rules admit only named actors. These actor lists must stay apart from the consent consumers. The five rules grant these fields:

Rule Regime Services What it grants Own deny reasons File DVT0001 consent bri Income declaration fields under consent consent codes, SCOPE_NOT_ALLOWED, CONSTRAINT_MISMATCH, YEAR_NOT_COVERED dvt0001.rego LVG0001 consent lvg Ownership check at LVG, scope lvg:vbo:eigendom consent codes, SCOPE_NOT_ALLOWED, CONSTRAINT_MISMATCH lvg0001.rego EUD0001 pid bri Income statement (inkomensverklaring) to the wallet, years 2024 and 2025 PID_NOT_PRESENT, ACTOR_NOT_ALLOWED, YEAR_NOT_ALLOWED eud0001.rego EUD0002 pid brp Death certificate ("akte van overlijden") to the wallet PID_NOT_PRESENT, ACTOR_NOT_ALLOWED eud0002.rego ASI0001 pid brp Fields of the Personal Records Database (BRP) behind the ASI attributes, for the ASIP peer …1200 only PID_NOT_PRESENT, ACTOR_NOT_ALLOWED asi0001.rego

The EUDI rules share one actor list, designated_issuers (eudi_helper.rego). The consent rules share the consent checks in dvtp_helper.rego.

docs.title: Rule shape
docs.text:
A rule is plain Rego. It declares what it covers and states its reasons to deny. If a rule has no deny reason for a field, it grants that field. box2Inkomen and box3Inkomen are not in covers_fields, so the engine denies them under consent. This excerpt from DVT0001 shows the shape of a rule:

rule_id := "DVT0001"
regime := "consent"
services := {"bri"}

covers_types := {"Bedrag"}
covers_fields := {
    "Query.ingeschrevenPersoon",
    "IngeschrevenPersoon.heeftBelastingjaarAangifte",
    "AangifteIH.verzamelinkomen",
    "AangifteIH.box1Inkomen",
    # ... scalar fields of the declaration
}

deny contains helper.consent_invalid_reason if not helper.consent_verified
deny contains "CONSENT_WITHDRAWN" if not helper.consent_active
deny contains "CONSENT_ACTOR_MISMATCH" if not helper.consent_given_to_caller
deny contains "SCOPE_NOT_ALLOWED" if not income_scope_granted

# The subject must be the identity placeholder, not a literal BSN.
deny_field[i] contains "CONSTRAINT_MISMATCH" if {
    some i, f in lib.fields
    lib.key(f) == "Query.ingeschrevenPersoon"
    not helper.names_consent_citizen(f, "bsn", {lib.identity_placeholder})
}

Authorization explains regime selection, rule binding, and the two layers of reason codes. The decisions are in ADR-0002, ADR-0009, ADR-0013, ADR-0015, and ADR-0031.

docs.title: Level 2: consent chain
docs.text:
The consent chain has the following components:

Component Responsibility Implementation Consent portal (toestemmingsportaal) frontend The citizen UI. It has a DigiD login (mock), one toggle per data set, a consent overview, and revocation. It shows only the requested data sets and refuses a data set that it cannot describe. It checks the return origin against an allowlist. It returns the consent proof in the URL fragment, or status=denied. toestemmingsportaal-frontend Consent portal backend Keeps the BSN away from the register and the consumer. The type system enforces this boundary, and the backend never sends a BSN to the register. It derives subject_ref as a keyed HMAC of the BSN, with a key version. It activates a citizen at BSNk once and stores PI and PP in the register. At each consent, it reads the BSN authorization list and has BSNk transform the values. Every configured source gets a VP. Only a source on the list also gets a VI. services/consent-portal-backend, portal.go, subjectref.go Consent register (toestemmingsregister) Stores consent records: subject_ref, consumer, scopes, scope entries per source, purpose (use_case), validity, and status. It also stores the portal's PI and PP per subject_ref (route D, ADR-0040). It stores no BSN, no VI, and no VP. It signs the consent proof and serves the JWKS. A separate listener serves only the status, published as the FSC service consent-status. By default, the register keeps its data in memory. If it uses Postgres, it requires a persistent signing key. services/consent-register, status.go, polymorphic.go Consent proof ES256 JWT, type gbo-consent+jwt. Claims: consent_id, encrypted_subject, scopes, scope_entries, dienstverlener_oin, valid_until (equal to exp), iss, aud, iat, nbf, jti. encrypted_subject holds a pseudonym per source OIN. For a source on the BSN authorization list, it also holds an identity. Each value has a key_set_version. dienstverlener_oin holds the consumer's FSC Peer ID (Q-68). The PDP denies a token in the old form with pi. consent_token.go

The consumer holds no citizen identifier. Its query names the subject with the placeholder consent:identity or consent:pseudonym. The source gateway replaces the placeholder after the allow decision (see the next section). Consent explains the record and its lifecycle. Pseudonymization explains the values. The decision is ADR-0032.

docs.title: Level 2: bronhouder
docs.text:
The bronhouder runs the following components:

Component Responsibility Implementation GraphQL source API The query endpoint of the source. Sources identify a citizen by BSN. The demo has three sources. Service bri is a Belastingdienst profile with income declarations per year. Service brp is a BRP profile with the personal record (persoonslijst) and the death certificate view. Service lvg is an LVG mock for the LVG pilot (vbo(bsn, vboId) { vboId }). graphql-server, brp-graphql-server, lvg-graphql-server Source gateway (bron-sidecar) Source-owned gateway between the Inway and the API, one instance per source. Its behavior depends on the presence of a consent token. With a token, it takes the value for its own OIN from encrypted_subject and has the decryption component read it. It checks that the value names its own OIN. Then it replaces the placeholder. It refuses a literal subject under a token. Without a token, it passes the request through. It accepts only the transport shape the PDP judged: POST, one path, no query string. services/bron-sidecar, substitution, transport.go Decryption component Reads a VI or VP with the source's own keys. It calls no other service, so there is no BSNk call at query time. The demo uses the bsnk-mock image with only the decryption endpoints. The three demo sources share one instance and one OIN. Production needs one instance per source. decryption.go, bsnk-mock README Source metadata endpoint Serves the source-owned description at /.well-known/gbo over a separate FSC metadata service. source_metadata.go, BD document

Only the source Inways can reach the source gateway. Because of this network isolation, every request at the gateway comes after a PDP decision. For this reason, the gateway does not verify the token again (ADR-0033, F-79). The deployment view shows the networks.

docs.title: Source metadata document
docs.text:
A source describes its own products in one JSON document. It serves the document at /.well-known/gbo. For a source without an endpoint, an operator supplies it through the file transport. GBO validates the document against gbo-source-metadata-v1 (urn:gov:nl:gbo:schema:gbo-source-metadata:1).

GBO holds no catalog of sources, years, or schemas. This document is the catalog, and the source owns it (ADR-0016). The document format is a proposal for the open PSA decision on S10.

The document has the following fields:

Field Content schema_version 1.0 or 1.1. Version 1.1 adds capabilities.asi. source_oin, version, issued_at, expires_at Envelope. source_oin must match the OIN in the certificate set. version must increase. GBO refuses a validity of less than one hour. capabilities.eudi version and attestations[], one entry per attestation type. type_id, type_version Identity of the attestation type. With the source ID they form the VCT path /types/{source-id}/{type-id}/v{n}. offers[] Products a wallet can request: id, label, description and fixed parameters (for example {"jaar": 2025}). graphql The source-owned query plan: service_reference (the FSC data service), endpoint, document (exactly one read operation), subject_variable, typed parameters, and result_pointer (RFC 6901). mapping_profile gbo-simple-v1 (ADR-0017). It applies to the eudi capability only. display Per language: name, description, a summary with {{claim}} placeholders, and rendering. claims Per claim: source (one gbo-simple-v1 rule: pointer, datatype, optional optional), label, optional description, and sd (always by default, allowed or never). The claim order is the display order in the wallet. capabilities.asi version, authentic_source (legal_name, country), a graphql block with one ...Selected fragment, and attributes[]. Each attribute has an identifier, an optional type condition on, and fields built with pointer, join, const or each (ADR-0039).

GBO generates the SD-JWT VC Type Metadata from display and claims. It publishes the Type Metadata immutably per version, with vct#integrity. A change to claims or display therefore needs a new type_version. The schema has no unit. The reconciler refuses reserved claim names (vct, iss, status, cnf) and nested objects (REQ-78).

The adapter puts the BSN from the PID into $bsn and the year of the offer into $jaar. It reads the result at result_pointer and copies each source.pointer into its claim. This shortened excerpt from the Belastingdienst document (version 2.4.0) shows how the query plan and the claims relate:

{
  "type_id": "inkomensverklaring",
  "type_version": "2.4",
  "offers": [
    {"id": "inkomensverklaring_2025", "label": "Inkomensverklaring 2025",
     "description": "Inkomensverklaring over belastingjaar 2025",
     "parameters": {"jaar": 2025}}
  ],
  "graphql": {
    "service_reference": "bri",
    "endpoint": "/graphql",
    "document": "query Inkomensverklaring($bsn: BSN!, $jaar: Int!) { ... }",
    "subject_variable": "bsn",
    "parameters": {"jaar": {"type": "integer", "required": true}},
    "result_pointer": "/data/ingeschrevenPersoon/heeftBelastingjaarAangifte"
  },
  "mapping_profile": "gbo-simple-v1",
  "display": {
    "nl-NL": {"name": "Inkomensverklaring",
              "summary": "€{{verzamelinkomen}} ({{belastingjaar}})"}
  },
  "claims": {
    "belastingjaar": {"source": {"pointer": "/belastingjaar", "datatype": "gYear"},
                      "label": {"nl-NL": "Belastingjaar"}},
    "verzamelinkomen": {"source": {"pointer": "/verzamelinkomen/waarde", "datatype": "integer"},
                        "label": {"nl-NL": "Verzamelinkomen"}}
  }
}

The BRP document (version 2.6.0, schema 1.1) also publishes the asi capability. This excerpt shows two of its attributes:

{
  "version": "1.0",
  "authentic_source": {"legal_name": "Basisregistratie Personen (mock)", "country": "NL"},
  "graphql": {
    "service_reference": "brp",
    "endpoint": "/graphql",
    "document": "query Asi($bsn: BSN!) { ingeschrevenPersoon(bsn: $bsn) { ...Selected } }",
    "subject_variable": "bsn",
    "result_pointer": "/data/ingeschrevenPersoon"
  },
  "attributes": [
    {"identifier": "https://gbo.example/attributes/family_name/1",
     "fields": {"family_name": {"join": ["/voorvoegsel", "/geslachtsnaam"], "separator": " "}}},
    {"identifier": "https://gbo.example/attributes/nationality/1",
     "fields": {"nationalities": {"each": "/heeftNationaliteit", "pointer": "/nationaliteit"}}}
  ]
}

By design, the document leaves out three things:

  • The GraphQL schema. The PDP keeps its own bundled copy. It authorizes the source's query plan field by field, like any other query.
  • Access decisions. The EUD and ASI rules decide which fields a channel can receive. The mapping of the source has no part in that decision.
  • The value_schema of an ASI attribute. GBO keeps it per attribute identifier in schemas/asi-attributes.json until an EU catalog of attributes exists.

Provenance rests on the authenticated FSC transport and the OIN in the certificate set. The source does not sign the document. The document also has no reference to an LDV read API or a DCAT-AP-NL entry (F-57, AV-07).

docs.title: Source configuration on the GBO side
docs.text:
The GBO configuration per source is small: one YAML file, named after the source_id. The file names where the description comes from and how GBO reaches the data. This is sources/configured/belastingdienst.yaml:

metadata_endpoint:
  transport: fsc
  provider_peer_id: "99999999900000000200"
  service_reference: gbo-metadata-bd

An optional data_access block (transport, provider_peer_id) gives the data leg a different transport than the metadata leg. The file transport is an exception for a source without its own endpoint. In that case, the operator takes over the description. GBO does not record the agreement of the bronhouder (F-71, AV-08).

The legal identity of the source comes from the certificate set with the same source_id. The OIN comes from the certificate's serialNumber, and the name comes from its O. GBO refuses a configured value that differs (REQ-67). The configuration holds the FSC Peer ID apart from the OIN. The data service and the grant hash come from the source document and the FSC contracts in force. They never come from this file.

A valid FSC contract activates nothing. A source becomes active only after three steps: it is configured, its candidate is valid, and an operator promotes a release (REQ-65). If a precondition is missing, the reconciler reports METADATA_CONTRACT_NOT_FOUND, DATA_CONTRACT_NOT_FOUND, or FSC_MANAGER_UNAVAILABLE. Source onboarding and admission and activation explain the lifecycle.

In demo v0.9.0, the RvIG source (rvig.yaml) uses the Belastingdienst peer …0200 and the OIN of the Belastingdienst. This is a demo shortcut. The demo therefore does not show one OIN per bronhouder.

docs.title: Source schema and the PDP copy
docs.text:
The source owns its schema. The PDP holds a directive-free copy per FSC service to resolve parent types. The year selector is in the query, so the PDP can enforce consent per year. This excerpt from the BD copy shows the DvTP part:

type IngeschrevenPersoon {
  bsn: BSN!
  heeftBelastingjaarAangifte(belastingjaren: [Int!]): [BelastingjaarAangifte!]
}

type Query {
  ingeschrevenPersoon(bsn: BSN!): IngeschrevenPersoon
}

The BRP source adds a flat view for the death certificate. The selection of the deceased partner from the marriage history is a security-sensitive invariant. The source holds this selection and its tests. The policy does not contain it (REQ-57, F-47). For the view, see the BRP copy and EUD0002:

type Query {
  ingeschrevenPersoon(bsn: BSN!): IngeschrevenPersoon
  akteVanOverlijden(bsn: BSN!): [AkteVanOverlijden!]!
}

docs.title: Level 2: FSC group
docs.text:
The FSC group fsc-demo runs OpenFSC v2.4.0. The deployment view lists the peers. The group has the following components:

Component Responsibility Implementation Directory The registry of the group. It signs service publications automatically. It signs nothing else. fsc-infra/docker-compose.yml Manager (per organization) Issues access tokens for contracted connections. The token carries the signed service_name, which binds the PDP rules to a service. The provider Managers of BD, BRP, and the consent register decide contract acceptance through the PDP (AuthZEN autosign). bd-manager Inway (per provider) bd-inway and brp-inway are the PEP. Their AuthZEN plugin sends every request with its body to the PDP before the request reaches the source gateway. cr-inway has no AuthZEN hook. Behind cr-inway, the contract authorizes consent-status, and the register reads the calling peer from the Fsc-Authorization token. bd-inway, cr-inway Outway (per consumer) Opens mTLS connections to Inways under a grant hash. Grant links give each contracted service a path: /bri, /brp, /lvg, /consent-status. seed-bri-contract.sh Grants Service-connection grants carry no properties. The demo removed flow in PR #363 and subject_id_type in #473. The regime follows from the evidence on the request (ADR-0031). seed-bri-contract.sh Delegated grants An integrator connects under a DelegatedServiceConnectionGrant. The integrator, the represented consumer and the provider sign it. The provider's Manager admits it only for a registered integration (ADR-0034). seed-bri-delegation-int.sh Consent-status service The register peer …0700 publishes consent-status. The PDP peer …0800 connects to it with grant link /consent-status. The register's Manager signs the connection only for peers in the admission register. fsc-seed-consent-status ASIP peer The ASIP peer …1200 has an Outway only. It holds a contract for brp on …0200 with grant link /brp. fsc-seed-asip Txlog API (per peer) Records each transport transaction (FSC-Logging). It is the authoritative transport record. The ADL records the decisions, and the LDV logbooks record the processings. fsc-infra/docker-compose.yml

docs.title: Level 2: EUDI chain
docs.text:
The EUDI chain has the following components:

Component Responsibility Implementation EUDI adapter The bridge between the issuance server and the FSC chain. The issuance server calls POST /attestations/{sourceID}/{typeID}. The adapter takes the BSN from the disclosed PID and builds the query from the source's published graphql block. It calls the source through the EDI Outway with Fsc-Grant-Hash and traceparent. It projects the answer into claims through gbo-simple-v1. It writes two LDV records per issuance: one for the BSN read and one for the assembly of the attestation. It fetches source data per request and stores none (REQ-11). services/eudi-adapter, routes, ldv_issuance.go Adapter callback and public endpoints The callback route has no caller authentication (REQ-45, #133). The same listener serves GET /eudi-offers.json (the offer catalog for the frontends) and GET /types/... (Type Metadata). source_release_runtime.go Issuance error contract The adapter returns 400 for offer parameters outside the offer, or for a PID without a BSN. It returns 404 if there is no result. If a result does not fit the claims, it returns 502 with GBO_SIMPLE_PATH_MISSING, GBO_SIMPLE_TYPE_MISMATCH, GBO_SIMPLE_RESULT_TYPE, or GBO_SIMPLE_RESULT_AMBIGUOUS. It never issues a partial attestation (REQ-116). internal/gbosimplev1 Issuance server The nl-wallet issuance server (v0.5.0). It does OpenID4VP disclosure and OpenID4VCI issuance (dc+sd-jwt). It verifies the PID disclosure against issuer_trust_anchors. That list also holds non-PID anchors: the development issuer CA and the issuer CA of every source. An attestation is valid for 365 days. Each type has one status list (REQ-77). A second use case, qtsp-attestation, issues the reference QTSP's test statement. An init step writes the server configuration from the active release. services/eudi-issuance-server, issuance_config.go, qtsp_issuance.go Source reconciler Reconciles the configured sources to a desired state. It discovers the FSC contracts. It fetches the source document over FSC, or reads the file for the file transport. It validates the document, and it validates the asi capability against the attribute catalog. Then it writes candidates and statuses. Promotion creates an immutable release and activates it. The --auto-promote flag is for the demo only. reconcile_command.go, source_configuration.go Source registry A shared Go module with a PostgreSQL store. The store holds candidates, statuses, immutable releases (content-addressed by SHA-256), and one active-release pointer. It has a writer role and a read-only role. The readers are the adapter, the issuance init step, and the ASIP. The states are pending, active, stale, blocked, and rollout_required. A source is fresh for 15 min and then has a stale grace period of 1 h (REQ-66). services/source-registry, source_metadata_cache.go Release runtime Polls the active-release pointer in the adapter. If the release changes, it rebuilds the attestation bindings. If an error occurs, it keeps the previous snapshot. source_release_runtime.go gbo-simple-v1 profile A minimal mapping profile that fails closed. It maps one source object to flat claims through RFC 6901 pointers. It allows only scalar data types, with no conversions or expressions. profile, docs/gbo-simple-v1.md Certificate set (per source) Issuer, reader, and status-list leaf certificates per source. Sources never share them. A separate privileged command mints the leaves under pre-provisioned CAs. It never mints a CA. Missing or incomplete material blocks only that source (CERTIFICATE_SET_NOT_FOUND, CERTIFICATE_SET_INVALID) (REQ-58). development_ca_provider.go

The issuance route runs under the PID regime: it carries no consent token. The BSN from the PID is in the PDP input and in both decision logs (REQ-60, ADR-0043). The decision is ADR-0018.

docs.title: Level 2: ASI chain
docs.text:
The ASI chain implements the Authentic Source Interface of ETSI TS 119 478, clause 6.1 (ADR-0037). The chain is demo grade. It uses a stub register, development certificates, and a DigiD mock. It has the following components:

Component Responsibility Implementation ASIP Offers clause 6.1.1 verify and 6.1.2 retrieve per data service at /<ds>/authsrc-api. It first verifies the DPoP-bound token. It takes the BSN only from the token (REQ-87). It derives one GraphQL query per request from the source's asi description and sends it through its own Outway (REQ-92). For each attribute, it answers Match, NoMatch, MatchWithVariation, or Unknown. It never returns a source value (REQ-85). It seals every 200 response with a detached JWS in X-JWS-Signature (REQ-83). services/asi-provider, seal.go Data services One per authentic source, each with its own base URL, contract, discovery records and token audience (ADR-0038). The demo has one: brp, source rvig. config/dataservices.json Source description (asi capability) The source maps its fields onto GBO attribute identifiers. The ASIP reads the active release every 5 s with the reader role. If no current description is available, the data service answers 503. services/asi-mapping, services/source-registry, schemas/asi-attributes.json Authorization server Clause 6.1.3. It registers a QTSP with RFC 7591 and a software statement sealed by the QTSP certificate. It verifies the chain and the entitlement QEAA_Provider in the register (REQ-88). It checks the entitlement again every hour (REQ-89). It runs the code flow with PKCE S256 and private_key_jwt. It issues DPoP-bound RFC 9068 tokens (10 min) for exactly one resource (REQ-95). The request page shows who asks for which data at which source (REQ-91). The login is the approval (REQ-90). The token carries the BSN and acr/amr (REQ-86). services/asi-authorization-server Register stub Stands in for the national register of relying parties. The server reads it at every lookup. testdata/register.json Wallet verifier The nl-wallet verification_server (v0.5.0). It runs the OpenID4VP PID disclosure for the authorization server (use case asi-login, BSN required, REQ-102). As a demo shortcut it also serves the reference QTSP (qtsp-login, no BSN). services/asi-wallet-verifier DigiD mock (ASI) A stub means of identification. It accepts nine digits and returns only a BSN. internal/digidmock Rule ASI0001 Grants the ASIP peer the BRP fields behind the attributes, on brp only. It does not verify the token or the QTSP. asi0001.rego Discover Interface (stub) External role. It answers retrieve from the ASIP's dataService records (REQ-99). For search, it returns 501. services/asi-discovery-stub Reference QTSP External role, demo scaffolding. It discovers, registers, gets a token, verifies or retrieves, and accepts a result only with a valid seal. Then it issues a test statement, marked "not qualified", to the wallet. services/qtsp-reference Conformance matrix Gives each ETSI requirement ID a status and named tests. If an ID or a test is missing, a CI job fails. conformance

docs.title: Trust boundary
docs.text:
The QTSP is not an FSC participant (F-87). It is an OAuth client of the authorization server. Its certificate and its register entitlement admit it. It has no FSC contract.

The ASIP is an FSC consumer peer of its own. For the PDP, the actor is the ASIP, never the QTSP or the citizen. The ASIP passes nothing about the QTSP into the chain. In demo v0.9.0, the ASIP writes no LDV records.

ASI verification shows the flow. The ASI requirements give the profile per ETSI clause.

docs.title: Level 2: logging and audit
docs.text:
GBO keeps three authoritative records, one per Logius standard (ADR-0036, ADR-0026). One W3C trace ID joins them. The records store the FSC transaction ID next to it (ADR-0035). Logging explains the model. The logging and audit chain has the following components:

Component Responsibility Implementation Authorization Decision Log (ADL) The authoritative record of each PDP decision, contract decisions included. OpenFTV writes it to Postgres ftv_adl. Readers get a SELECT-only role. It holds the request and {allow, reason}. It has no policy version (REQ-59) and no consent-status answer (F-72). For decisions behind the Inway, it has no trace ID and no transaction ID (#369). docker-compose.yml, adl-reader.sql LDV logbook Demo stand-in for the logbook of each controller (Verantwoordelijke), one instance per controller. It accepts one record per processing (POST /logboek/records) and serves the read extension (POST /data-processing-operations). It keeps a versioned stand-in register of processing activities. It refuses any record with a run of nine digits that passes the BSN check digit test (elfproef). It uses SQLite with synchronous = FULL. Write and read take separate tokens. services/ldv-logboek LDV client A shared Go module. In production, GBO ships this module to chain participants. It does not ship the logbook. The client takes the trace from traceparent. It writes records and waits for the logbook to acknowledge them. It derives the subject in the controller's own pseudonym space. It sets nextLogbookId on outbound calls. A local durable outbox stores each record before delivery. As a result, a logbook outage delays records but does not fail requests. services/ldv-client, outbox.go FSC txlog Authoritative transport record per peer (see FSC group). fsc-infra/docker-compose.yml Observability stack OpenTelemetry collector, Jaeger, Promtail, Loki and Grafana. The engine's console decision log goes to Loki. These stores are for debugging only. They have no audit function. otel/collector-config.yaml, OBSERVABILITY.md

The demo runs seven logbooks. Each controller logs its own processings (REQ-72):

Logbook Controller Writers logboek-bd Belastingdienst graphql-server, bron-sidecar logboek-brp RvIG brp-graphql-server, brp-sidecar logboek-lvg LVG lvg-graphql-server, lvg-sidecar logboek-toestemming GBO consent facility (toestemmingsvoorziening) consent-register, consent-portal-backend logboek-eudi-adapter GBO issuance facility eudi-adapter logboek-afnemer Hypotheek-BV (consumer) dienstverlener-backend, integrator-backend logboek-ir Installatie Register (consumer) ir-backend

The register logs each status lookup with the verified FSC peer of the PDP as processor (REQ-76). The ASIP writes no records. The consumer logbooks follow candidate condition AV-02.

docs.title: Level 2: shared services and mocks
docs.text:
The demo has the following shared services and mocks:

Component Responsibility Implementation BSNk PP mock Follows the BSNk interface as JSON instead of SOAP: /v2/activate, /v2/transform, /v2/provide-dv-keys, /v2/bsn-authorisation-list, and /v2/scheme-keys. It enforces the rules of BSNk. A PI or PP belongs to its requester. A transformation has at most four parties. Only a party on the BSN authorization list gets an identity. It does not encrypt: anyone who holds a value can read it. Only the portal backend calls it, at consent time. services/bsnk-mock, README DigiD mocks The consent portal has a DigiD login page. The user types a test BSN, and the portal backend signs a portal token with it. The ASI authorization server has its own stub (see the ASI chain). Demo scaffolding. DigiDAuth.tsx, portalhttp Consumer backend and frontend Mock consumer Hypotheek-BV (peer …0300). It starts the consent flow, receives the proof and sends the DvTP query with the placeholder. QUERY_KIND selects the source (bd or lvg) and its placeholder. It writes its own LDV records. Demo scaffolding. services/dienstverlener-backend, dienstverlener-mock Installatie Register (LVG pilot) keyper-mock is the IR/Keyper frontend. It has the installer request, the owner approval, and the installer data. ir-backend is the consumer backend with QUERY_KIND=lvg on its own peer …1000. Under one consent, IR calls LVG again at each installer access. IR holds the second consent (citizen to installer). GBO does not hold it. Demo scaffolding. keyper-mock, docs/lvg-ir.md Integrator backend Consumer backend on the integrator peer …1100. It calls bri for Hypotheek-BV under a delegated grant. It is opt-in: run make demo-integrator. Demo scaffolding. docs/integrator.md Developer portal and backend A cockpit for engineers. It shows the live flow from the trace event stream and a scenario library. It shows the ADL decision next to the engine detail, the LDV chain, the FSC txlogs, and an ASI tab. Rule metadata comes from a generated rules.json. Demo scaffolding. developer-portal, services/dev-portal-backend OpenFTV Manager, UI, Keycloak Opt-in policy administration point. It keeps the policies in Postgres and makes a tagged bundle that the PDP pulls. For more information, see policy lifecycle. services/openftv-manager, services/openftv-manager-ui Landing page Public explainer with links to the demo UIs. Demo scaffolding. landing-page

The demo removed the old sector PIP (#378). Admission runs through the admission register and the contract decision. The decision in ADR-0022 is deferred.

docs.title: OOTS channel
docs.text:
In the OOTS channel, a public authority in another EU member state gets evidence from a Dutch source. The authority needs the evidence for a procedure under the Single Digital Gateway Regulation. The Basisinrichting OOTS handles the European transport and the interaction with the citizen. GBO adds an OOTS adapter in front of GBO Basis, so the bronhouder sees a normal FSC request. This is interaction pattern B of the Globaal Ontwerp. The channel is design only: it is not built in demo v0.9.0.

Overview › OOTS channel

docs.title: Inside the channel
docs.text:

"preview" .- oov %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class burger,api source class ca,cs,ap,oov ext class pa,map planned class pdp,gw basis class pa,map,pdp,gw zoom style eu fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#D1D5DB style bi fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#D1D5DB style oa fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#EA580C,stroke-dasharray:6 4 style basis fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#16A34A click pa "../../runtime/design-level/#sdg-oots" "SDG-OOTS scenario" click map "../../decisions/0024-canonical-semantic-models/" "Canonical semantic models" click pdp "../gbo-basis/authorization/" "Authorization" click gw "../gbo-basis/source-access/" "Generic source access"

Figure 1: The OOTS channel. Dashed: design only (not built in demo v0.9.0). Grey: parties outside GBO.

The channel has these parts:

Part Role Zoom in Basisinrichting OOTS Delivered by RINIS for the Ministry of the Interior (BZK) and the Ministry of Economic Affairs (EZK). Its part OOTS-V receives evidence requests and has the citizen authenticate again. It checks for a mix-up of identities, fetches the data, and shows them to the citizen before it sends them. Not a GBO component GO pattern B Protocol adapter Translates the OOTS request into a GraphQL query over FSC and passes it on. It decides nothing about source data (REQ-44) ADR-0020 Semantic mapping Maps the source format to the SDG Evidence Data Model, if the bronhouder configures a mapping. Optional for the bronhouder ADR-0024 GBO Basis Decides at the source, field by field, and only then asks the source. The same chain as for every other channel GBO Basis

docs.title: One evidence request
docs.text:
The Globaal Ontwerp describes the request in this order. The OOTS process steps stay with the Basisinrichting OOTS:

sequenceDiagram autonumber actor B as Citizen box rgb(241,239,232) Outside GBO participant EU as EU authority participant OV as Basisinrichting OOTS end box rgb(255,237,213) GBO OOTS adapter (design only) participant OA as OOTS adapter end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis at the source participant PDP as PEP + PDP participant GW as Source gateway end box rgb(221,235,247) Source participant API as Source API end B->>EU: request a service EU->>OV: evidence request (eDelivery AS4) OV->>OA: request (GraphQL) Note over OA: optional: evidence type<br/>to source query OA->>PDP: GraphQL query over FSC Note over PDP: regime and evidence<br/>for OOTS not designed PDP->>GW: allow GW->>API: query API-->>OA: only the selected fields Note over OA: optional: source format<br/>to SDG-EDM OA-->>OV: evidence response OV->>B: show the data to share B->>OV: choose what to share OV->>EU: evidence response (eDelivery AS4)

Figure 2: One OOTS evidence request, after GO pattern B. The runtime page Design-level scenarios has every hop.

OOTS-V sends the data only after the citizen agrees. The member states use eDelivery, AS4, ebMS and RegRep. OOTS-EDM specifies the request and response messages, and SDG-EDM describes the evidence. The bronhouder applies none of these standards itself.

docs.title: Two designs for the edge
docs.text:
The Globaal Ontwerp and the design decision of this TO put the AS4 edge in different places:

flowchart LR subgraph go["Globaal Ontwerp, pattern B"] direction LR g1["Basisinrichting OOTS<br/>access point + protocol<br/>translator to GraphQL"] g2("GBO facility<br/>optional semantic mapping") g3("GBO Basis") g1 -- "GraphQL" --> g2 -- "FSC" --> g3 end subgraph adr["ADR-0020"] direction LR a1("GBO OOTS adapter<br/>Domibus access point,<br/>OOTS-EDM adapter,<br/>FSC translator") a3("GBO Basis") a1 -- "FSC" --> a3 end as4(["AS4 from<br/>a member state"]) as4 --> g1 as4 --> a1 %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class as4,g1 ext class g2,a1 planned class g3,a3 basis style go fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#D1D5DB style adr fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#D1D5DB

Figure 3: Where the AS4 edge sits in the two designs.

In both designs, AS4 exists only at the edge, and the bronhouder sees a normal FSC request through the standard PEP and PDP chain. The difference is who builds the protocol translation. It is open whether GBO builds the adapter, or the OOTS-V operator extends its facility with the GBO interface (Q-79, PSA B-12).

docs.title: What the adapter reuses from GBO Basis
docs.text:
The adapter is a protocol adapter in front of GBO Basis. It reuses every part of GBO Basis and adds no decision of its own:

Part of GBO Basis Use for OOTS State FSC connection and admission The adapter calls the source as an FSC consumer, with a contract after admission (REQ-46) Design PDP and policy The PDP of the source decides on every field. OOTS needs a regime, evidence and a rule of its own Not designed Source gateway Without a consent proof, the gateway passes the query on unchanged Built for other channels Source configuration The Globaal Ontwerp takes the mapping configuration from the bronhouder. The source document has no OOTS capability Not designed Records ADL, LDV and the FSC txlog record the request like any other request Built for other channels

A channel adapter that GBO delivers does only protocol translation (REQ-44). It does not decide which data a party gets. It does not fetch decision information such as consent or admission. It carries no knowledge of a source in code. It uses the source access that the source offers for all interaction patterns, and never an interface (koppelvlak) for one channel.

The mapping depends on a canonical model per source. The proposed decision makes the GraphQL schema of the source profile that canonical model (ADR-0024, proposed). GBO then derives the OOTS-EDM evidence-type mappings from it. No central canonical model exists. Bronhouders and domains own their models (Q-11).

docs.title: What demo v0.9.0 does
docs.text:
The demo does not touch OOTS. It has no adapter, no access point and no rule for OOTS. The following figure shows what happens if a peer sends an OOTS-like request today:

flowchart LR r(["Request from an<br/>adapter peer"]) q{"Consent proof<br/>in the request?"} p["PID regime<br/>EUD0001 · EUD0002 · ASI0001"] a{"Caller on a<br/>PID actor list?"} d(["Deny<br/>actor check fails"]) r --> q q -- "no" --> p --> a a -- "no" --> d %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class r planned class q,a basis class p eudi class d dvtp class a zoom click a "../gbo-basis/authorization/#regime-from-evidence" "Regime from evidence"

Figure 4: An OOTS request in demo v0.9.0 ends in a deny.

The request carries no consent proof, so it enters the PID regime. The PID rules admit only named callers, and an OOTS adapter is not one of them. The regime follows from the evidence in the request (REQ-74). Without evidence of its own, an OOTS request cannot get an allow. Risk R2 tracks the missing bridge.

docs.title: Compared with the Globaal Ontwerp
docs.text:
The TO design follows pattern B in the main line. It differs in the edge, and the demo has no part of it:

Topic Globaal Ontwerp TO design Demo v0.9.0 AS4 access point In the Basisinrichting OOTS Domibus at the GBO edge (ADR-0020) None Protocol translation to GraphQL A translator in the Basisinrichting OOTS. OOTS-V must also support GraphQL The FSC translator of the GBO adapter None Semantic mapping An optional GBO facility, configured by the bronhouder An OOTS-EDM adapter, based on the canonical model per source (ADR-0024) None Basis for the request Policy checks a basis other than consent A legal-basis path in the Gov-to-Gov style, needed and not built No rule: the PDP denies

docs.title: Open points
docs.text:
The main open points in the OOTS channel are these:

  • Who builds the adapter, and where the boundary between OOTS-V and the mapping function is (Q-79).
  • The regime and the evidence for an OOTS request. A request without evidence of its own enters the PID regime (F-70).
  • Whether the service description of the source must refer to a managed schema and concept framework, as PSA S10 asks (Q-11).
  • The mapping to SDG-EDM needs traceable versions, as REQ-124 asks for issuance. The requirements register has no OOTS requirement (Q-79).

docs.title: DvTP channel
docs.text:
In the DvTP channel, a private service provider (dienstverlener) gets source data about a citizen, with the consent of that citizen. The channel adds two things to GBO Basis. In the consent facility (toestemmingsvoorziening), the citizen gives and revokes consent. The pseudonymization facility (pseudonimiseervoorziening) of BSNk makes sure that the service provider never gets a BSN. This is interaction pattern C of the Globaal Ontwerp.

Overview › DvTP channel

docs.title: Inside the channel
docs.text:
