Figure 1: The DvTP channel. Pink: GBO components of the channel. Green: GBO Basis at the source.

The channel has these parts:

Part Role Zoom in Consent facility The citizen sees the request, logs in, and gives or refuses consent. Later the citizen views and revokes consents. The register signs a consent proof and answers the status of a consent. Consent facility Pseudonymization facility BSNk PP turns the BSN into values that only one party can read. The channel calls it only when a citizen gives consent. Pseudonymization Service provider Starts the request, keeps the proof, and sends it with every query. It never gets a BSN or another number for the citizen. DvTP query Integrator A software party that calls the source for a service provider, under an FSC delegation and a registered mandate. ADR-0034 GBO Basis Checks the proof and the consent status for every request, and fills in the citizen only after an allow. GBO Basis

docs.title: Two phases
docs.text:
The channel works in two phases, as in the Globaal Ontwerp. In phase 1, the citizen gives consent. In phase 2, the service provider queries a source under that consent, as often as the consent allows:

sequenceDiagram autonumber actor B as Citizen box rgb(241,239,232) Consumer participant DV as Service provider end box rgb(254,220,216) Consent facility participant P as Portal participant TR as Register end box rgb(241,239,232) External participant BK as BSNk PP end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis at the source participant PDP as PEP + PDP participant GW as Source gateway end box rgb(221,235,247) Source participant S as Source API end rect rgb(255,248,246) Note over B,BK: Phase 1: consent B->>DV: start a service DV->>P: redirect with consumer, service, data sets B->>P: log in (DigiD) and give consent P->>BK: make a value per source BK-->>P: encrypted values (VI, VP) P->>TR: store the consent TR-->>P: signed consent proof P-->>DV: redirect back with the proof end rect rgb(246,252,248) Note over DV,S: Phase 2: query, again for every use DV->>PDP: query with a placeholder + the proof PDP->>TR: status of this consent (over FSC) TR-->>PDP: active Note over PDP: check proof, fields,<br/>years, caller PDP->>GW: allow Note over GW: decrypt own value,<br/>replace the placeholder GW->>S: query with the BSN S-->>DV: only the selected fields end

Figure 2: The two phases of DvTP. Every step names the essence only. The runtime pages have every hop.

For every hop, with the data and the error paths, see DvTP consent and DvTP query. Viewing and revoking a consent is a third flow: DvTP citizen access.

docs.title: Who sees which identifier
docs.text:
The channel is built so that the BSN appears in as few places as possible. The service provider holds no identifier for the citizen at all:

flowchart LR subgraph bsn["Sees the BSN"] direction TB pb("Portal backend<br/>at login and consent") bk["BSNk PP"] gw("Source gateway<br/>after the allow") api[("Source API")] end subgraph pseudo["Sees only pseudonymous values"] direction TB tr[("Register<br/>PI, PP under its<br/>own reference")] pdp("PDP<br/>checks the proof,<br/>not the person") end subgraph none["Sees no identifier"] direction TB dv["Service provider<br/>proof + placeholder"] int["Integrator"] end %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class pb,tr dvtp class bk,dv,int ext class gw,pdp basis class api source style bsn fill:#FFF1F0,stroke:#E28F80 style pseudo fill:#FFF7ED,stroke:#EA580C style none fill:#F0FDF4,stroke:#16A34A

Figure 3: Where the BSN can appear in the DvTP channel.

The consent proof carries one encrypted value per source. Only that source can decrypt its value. The value becomes the own pseudonym of the source, or the BSN if the source has the right to process the BSN (ADR-0032, ADR-0033). In its query, the service provider names the citizen with a fixed placeholder.

This has a cost. The service provider cannot recognize the same citizen across two consents, and it logs under the consent, not under the person (F-76).

docs.title: Compared with the Globaal Ontwerp
docs.text:
The demo follows pattern C of the Globaal Ontwerp. It differs in the form of three steps:

Step Globaal Ontwerp Demo v0.9.0 What the service provider gets A consent ID and an encrypted identity A signed consent proof that holds the consent ID and an encrypted value per source What the register stores The encrypted identity, scope, purpose, validity The consent, plus the polymorphic values of the citizen under its own reference. No encrypted values per source Who checks the consent The bronhouder asks the register The PDP of the source checks the proof itself, then asks the register for the status over FSC

The design choice behind these differences is in ADR-0032. Whether the register and the portal backend are one system, and which of them talks to BSNk, is open (Q-49, ADR-0040).

docs.title: Open points
docs.text:
The main open points in the DvTP channel are these:

  • Whether a private service provider without a public task can connect to BSNk PP at all (Q-01).
  • Who sets the validity period of a consent (Q-13).
  • Whether the proof must also name the integrator (Q-46).
  • The values in the proof are fixed at consent: a source that joins later needs a new consent (F-78).

docs.title: Traceability
docs.text:
• Requirements: REQ-12, REQ-20, REQ-21, REQ-37, REQ-68, REQ-79, REQ-106
  • Findings: F-76 (open), F-78 (open)
  • Open questions: Q-01 (partly answered), Q-13 (open), Q-46 (open), Q-49 (open)
  • Demo increments: SL-06a (done), SL-47 (done), SL-51 (done)

docs.title: Consent facility
docs.text:
The consent facility (toestemmingsvoorziening) is where the citizen gives, views and revokes consent. It also tells every source, at every request, whether a consent still holds. It has three components: the consent portal (toestemmingsportaal) frontend and backend (PSA capability S02) and the consent register (toestemmingsregister) (S01). The Consent concept page has the detail and the links to the code.

Overview › DvTP channel › Consent facility

docs.title: Components and interfaces
docs.text:
flowchart LR burger(["Citizen<br/>browser"]) dv["Service provider"] subgraph tv["Consent facility"] direction TB pf("Portal frontend<br/>request, login, choice,<br/>overview, revoke") pb("Portal backend<br/>keeps the BSN away<br/>from the register") subgraph tr["Consent register"] direction TB api("Portal API<br/>create, list, revoke") st("Status listener<br/>status only") jw("JWKS<br/>public keys") db[("Consents,<br/>PI + PP per citizen")] end end digid["DigiD<br/><i>mock</i>"] bsnk["BSNk PP<br/><i>mock</i>"] inw("Register Inway<br/>FSC service consent-status") pdp("PDP of a source") log[("LDV logbook<br/>consent facility")] dv -- "redirect: consumer, service,<br/>data sets, return address" --> pf burger --> pf pf -- "login" --> digid pf --> pb pb -- "activate once,<br/>transform per consent" --> bsnk pb -- "only the backend" --> api api --- db st --- db pf -- "proof in the URL fragment" --> dv pdp -- "over FSC" --> inw --> st pdp -. "keys, cached 5 min" .-> jw api -.-> log st -.-> log %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class burger source class dv,digid,bsnk ext class pf,pb,api,st,jw dvtp class db,log store class inw,pdp basis class pdp,bsnk zoom style tv fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#E28F80 style tr fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#E28F80 click pdp "../../gbo-basis/authorization/" "Authorization" click bsnk "../../../concepts/pseudonymization/" "Pseudonymization"

Figure 1: The components of the consent facility and their interfaces.

Each component has one job:

Component Job Never does Portal frontend Shows the request in plain language, one choice per data set. Shows the consents of the citizen and lets the citizen revoke one. Picks fields inside a data set (REQ-10) Portal backend Recognizes the citizen with a keyed hash of the BSN. Asks BSNk for the values per source. Talks to the register. Sends a BSN to the register (REQ-23) Register: portal API Creates, lists and revokes consents. Signs the consent proof. Only the portal backend can call it. Serves the status to a source Register: status listener Answers one question per request: is this consent active? It is reachable only over FSC. Serves anything else Register: JWKS Publishes the public keys that the PDP uses to check a proof. —

docs.title: The consent proof
docs.text:
The register signs a consent proof when the citizen gives consent. The service provider (dienstverlener) keeps it and sends it unchanged with every query:

flowchart LR subgraph jwt["Consent proof: ES256 JWT, type gbo-consent+jwt"] direction TB h["Header<br/>algorithm, type, key ID"] subgraph claims["Claims"] direction TB id["consent_id · jti"] sc["scopes · scope_entries<br/>data sets per source"] who["dienstverlener_oin<br/>the party it is for"] t["valid_until = exp<br/>iss · aud · iat · nbf"] subgraph es["encrypted_subject: one entry per source OIN"] direction LR vp["pseudonym (VP)<br/>for every source"] vi["identity (VI)<br/>only for a source that<br/>may process the BSN"] end end end sig["Signature of<br/>the register"] jwt --- sig %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class h,id,sc,who,t dvtp class vp,vi store class sig ext style jwt fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#E28F80 style claims fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#D1D5DB style es fill:#F5F3FF,stroke:#7C3AED

Figure 2: The parts of the consent proof.

The proof holds no BSN. The service provider can read which data sets it can ask for. It cannot read who the citizen is: each value in encrypted_subject can be decrypted only by the source it was made for (REQ-80). The decision for this form is ADR-0032.

The proof works as a bearer token. The binding to the service provider stops use by another party, but not replay by the same party within the validity (R4).

docs.title: Life of a consent
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2 direction LR [*] --> Active: citizen gives consent,<br/>register signs the proof Active --> Active: service provider queries<br/>(as often as needed) Active --> Revoked: citizen revokes Active --> Expired: valid_until passes Revoked --> [*] Expired --> [*] classDef active fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef stop fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B class Active active class Revoked,Expired stop

Figure 3: The states of a consent.

The register stores ACTIVE or REVOKED. Expired follows from the date in the proof. A consent can be used again within its validity: the design does not require single use (Q-04). A revocation takes effect on the next request, because the PDP asks the status every time (REQ-14).

docs.title: Why the status stays online
docs.text:
The proof carries the content of the consent, and the register keeps the status. Each part has its own freshness:

What How fresh Why Content: data sets, party, validity Fixed at consent, checked locally The register signed it. The PDP needs no call for it. Public keys At most five minutes old Keys change rarely. An unknown key ID triggers a fetch at once. Status Live at every request A revocation must stop the next request.

The price is a hard dependency: if the register does not answer, the PDP denies every DvTP request (REQ-75). The target values for availability and delay are open (Q-47).

docs.title: Open points
docs.text:
The main open points in the consent facility are these:

  • Whether the register and the portal backend are one system, and which one is the BSNk participant (Q-49).
  • Who sets the validity period, and whether the citizen can change it (Q-13).
  • When a consent counts as "retrieved", and how the register learns that (Q-42).
  • Where the signing key lives and how it rotates (Q-55).
  • Whether the register must authenticate the portal backend, or whether network isolation is enough (Q-58).

docs.title: Traceability
docs.text:
• Requirements: REQ-10, REQ-14, REQ-23, REQ-68, REQ-75, REQ-76, REQ-80
  • Findings: F-61 (closed), F-78 (open)
  • Open questions: Q-04 (answered), Q-13 (open), Q-42 (open), Q-47 (open), Q-49 (open), Q-55 (open), Q-58 (open)
  • Demo increments: SL-11 (done), SL-47 (done), SL-51 (done)

docs.title: EUDI wallet channel
docs.text:
In the EUDI wallet channel, a citizen gets data from a government source in the EUDI wallet. Interaction pattern (interactiepatroon) A of the Globaal Ontwerp has two flows. In flow A, the source issues an attestation itself, as a PuB-EAA. In flow B, a QTSP verifies or retrieves the data at the source and issues a QEAA. GBO delivers one component for each flow, and both components reach the source through GBO Basis.

Overview › EUDI wallet channel

docs.title: Inside the channel
docs.text:
flowchart LR burger(["Citizen"]) subgraph extp["External parties"] direction TB wallet["NL Wallet<br/>PID, attestations"] qtsp["QTSP<br/><i>reference QTSP in the demo</i>"] end subgraph pub["PuB-EAA provider: flow A"] direction TB is("Issuance server<br/>nl-wallet") ad("EUDI adapter") end subgraph asi["ASI provider: flow B"] direction TB az("Authorization server<br/>login, tokens") asip("ASIP<br/>verify, retrieve") end reg[("Source registry<br/>active release")] subgraph basis["GBO Basis, at each source"] direction LR pdp("PEP + PDP<br/>PID regime") --> gw("Source<br/>gateway") --> api[("Source<br/>BD · BRP")] end burger --- wallet burger -- "B · asks for a statement" --> qtsp wallet -- "A · PID, then<br/>attestation" --> is is -- "callback<br/>with the PID" --> ad wallet -. "B · login with the PID" .-> az qtsp -- "token" --> az qtsp -- "verify, retrieve" --> asip ad -- "query + BSN<br/>over FSC" --> pdp asip -- "query + BSN<br/>over FSC" --> pdp reg -. "eudi" .-> ad reg -. "asi" .-> asip %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class burger,api source class wallet,qtsp ext class is,ad,az,asip eudi class pdp,gw basis class reg store class is,ad,az,asip,pdp,gw,reg zoom style pub fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#EA580C style asi fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#EA580C style basis fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#16A34A style extp fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#D1D5DB click is "pubeaa/" "PuB-EAA provider" click ad "pubeaa/" "PuB-EAA provider" click az "asi/" "ASI provider" click asip "asi/" "ASI provider" click pdp "../gbo-basis/" "GBO Basis" click gw "../gbo-basis/#the-request-path" "Request path" click reg "../../concepts/source-onboarding/" "Source onboarding"

Figure 1: The EUDI wallet channel. Orange: the GBO components of the channel, with GBO Basis in green. Thick border: click to zoom in.

The channel has these parts:

Part Role Zoom in PuB-EAA provider (PubEAA-voorziening) The technical issuance facility. The issuance server asks the wallet for the PID. The EUDI adapter gets the source data and turns it into claims. The bronhouder stays the PuB-EAA provider (ADR-0028, proposed). PuB-EAA provider ASI provider Lets a QTSP verify or retrieve attributes at the source (eIDAS article 45e). It has its own OAuth authorization server. The QTSP is an OAuth client there, and not an FSC participant (F-87). ASI provider Source registry Holds the active release of every source description. The source describes its attestations (eudi) and its attributes (asi) itself. Source onboarding GBO Basis Decides every request of the channel under the PID regime, with the rules EUD0001, EUD0002 and ASI0001. GBO Basis NL Wallet and QTSP External parties. The wallet holds the PID of the citizen. The demo runs a reference QTSP, which is not a real QTSP. ASI verification

docs.title: Flow A: the source issues a PuB-EAA
docs.text:
In flow A, the citizen shares the PID with the issuance facility and gets an attestation back. The attestation carries the name of the source as the issuer:

sequenceDiagram autonumber actor B as Citizen box rgb(241,239,232) External participant W as NL Wallet end box rgb(255,237,213) PuB-EAA provider participant IS as Issuance server participant AD as EUDI adapter end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis at the source participant PDP as PEP + PDP end box rgb(221,235,247) Source participant S as Source API end B->>W: scan the QR code of an offer W->>IS: fetch the request IS-->>W: ask for the PID claim bsn, in the name of the source B->>W: share the PID W->>IS: PID as SD-JWT VC Note over IS: check the PID<br/>against the trust anchors IS->>AD: callback with the disclosed PID Note over AD: BSN from the PID,<br/>query from the release AD->>PDP: query with the BSN, over FSC Note over PDP: no consent token,<br/>so PID regime, EUD0001 PDP->>S: allow, query through the gateway S-->>AD: source data Note over AD: claims with gbo-simple-v1 AD-->>IS: claims and type IS-->>W: attestation, signed for the source W-->>B: accept the attestation

Figure 2: Flow A, at essence level. The runtime page has every hop.

The facility signs with the certificate set of the source. The wallet shows the source as the issuer. GBO plays no part when the citizen later presents the attestation to a service provider (dienstverlener). For every hop, with the data and the error paths, see EUDI issuance.

docs.title: Flow B: a QTSP verifies at the source
docs.text:
In flow B, the QTSP asks the ASI provider to verify or retrieve attributes at the source. The citizen approves the request by logging in at the authorization server:

sequenceDiagram autonumber actor B as Citizen box rgb(241,239,232) External participant Q as QTSP participant W as NL Wallet end box rgb(255,237,213) ASI provider participant AS as Authorization server participant ASIP as ASIP end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis at the source participant PDP as PEP + PDP end box rgb(221,235,247) Source participant S as BRP end B->>Q: ask for a statement Q-->>B: redirect to the authorization server B->>AS: see who asks what at which source W->>AS: log in with the PID (or the DigiD mock) AS-->>Q: code, then a token with the BSN Q->>ASIP: verify or retrieve, with the token Note over ASIP: check the token,<br/>BSN from the token ASIP->>PDP: query with the BSN, over FSC Note over PDP: PID regime, ASI0001 PDP->>S: allow, query through the gateway S-->>ASIP: fields of the person ASIP-->>Q: sealed result per attribute Q->>W: test statement, not a QEAA

Figure 3: Flow B, at essence level. Discovery and registration of the QTSP happen once, before the first request.

A token is valid for one data service, and each data service serves one source. The QTSP issues the QEAA itself. In the demo, the reference QTSP issues a test statement through the issuance server of flow A. For every hop, see ASI verification.

docs.title: Who sees which identifier
docs.text:
The channel does not use BSNk. The BSN goes into the source query as a plain value:

flowchart LR subgraph need["Needs the BSN"] direction TB wallet["NL Wallet<br/>PID of the citizen"] is("Issuance server<br/>checks the PID") ad("EUDI adapter<br/>BSN from the PID") az("Authorization server<br/>BSN from the login") asip("ASIP<br/>BSN from the token") api[("Source<br/>after the allow")] end subgraph extra["Holds the BSN without a need"] direction TB qtsp["QTSP<br/>reads the token"] pdp("PDP input") adl[("ADL and console<br/>decision log")] end subgraph none["Holds no BSN"] direction TB ldv[("LDV records<br/>logbook pseudonym")] logs[("ASIP logs<br/>and traces")] stmt["QTSP login and<br/>test statement"] end %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class wallet,qtsp,stmt ext class is,ad,az,asip eudi class api source class pdp basis class adl,ldv,logs store style need fill:#FFF7ED,stroke:#EA580C style extra fill:#FFF1F0,stroke:#E28F80 style none fill:#F0FDF4,stroke:#16A34A

Figure 4: Where the BSN can appear in the EUDI wallet channel. Red: the BSN is there without a need.

In flow A, the EUDI adapter takes the BSN from the disclosed PID. In flow B, the ASIP takes it from the access token. Both components put the BSN in the query variables. As a result, the BSN is in two kinds of places that do not need it:

  • The PDP input, and with it the ADL and the console decision log. This is a known violation of REQ-60. The proposed fix keeps identifiers out of the PDP input (ADR-0043, proposed).
  • The access token of flow B. ETSI requires the identification data in the token, and the QTSP can read the BSN (F-86).

The LDV records hold no BSN, because the logbook refuses one. For the detail, see Exception: the BSN in the EUDI and ASI routes.

docs.title: The PID regime
docs.text:
Neither flow carries a consent proof. The evidence in the request selects the regime, so both flows land in the PID regime (ADR-0031):

flowchart LR q{"Consent token<br/>in the request?"} c["Consent regime<br/>DvTP"] p["PID regime<br/>EUD0001 · EUD0002 · ASI0001"] a{"Caller on the<br/>actor list?"} s{"BSN in the<br/>root argument?"} f{"Fields and limits<br/>of the rule?"} ok(["Allow"]) no(["Deny"]) ev("Verified PID as<br/>positive evidence<br/><i>design only</i>") q -- "one" --> c q -- "none" --> p p --> a a -- "yes" --> s s -- "yes" --> f f -- "yes" --> ok a -. "ACTOR_NOT_ALLOWED" .-> no s -. "PID_NOT_PRESENT" .-> no f -. "FIELD_NOT_PERMITTED" .-> no ev -. Figure 5: The PID regime. Dashed: the positive evidence that the design asks for. Demo v0.9.0 does not build it.

Each PID rule admits only named callers: the FSC peer of the EUDI adapter, or the ASIP peer. Only consent is positive evidence. A request enters the PID regime because it carries no token (F-70). For that reason, the actor lists of the PID rules must stay disjoint from the consent consumers. The fix in the design is a verified PID disclosure, bound to the subject of the query (REQ-45).

In demo v0.9.0, the callback that carries the PID is not authenticated. The callback gap shows what that allows.

docs.title: Approval in the wallet is no legal basis
docs.text: In flow A, the citizen chooses in the wallet to share the PID. In flow B, the citizen approves one request by logging in (REQ-90). The ARF says that approval in the wallet is never a legal basis for the relying party (F-83). The approval of flow B is also not stored, and the citizen cannot revoke it. A DvTP consent and a wallet approval cannot replace each other. For the detail, see Wallet approval is not a legal basis.

docs.title: Compared with the Globaal Ontwerp
docs.text:
The demo follows the two flows of pattern A. It differs in six steps:

Step Globaal Ontwerp Demo v0.9.0 Start of flow A The wallet sends a credential request to the PuB-EAA provider. The citizen scans a QR code. The issuance server first asks for the PID (disclosure-based issuance, ADR-0018). Authorization in flow A An authorization facility (autorisatievoorziening) asks the wallet for the PID and authorizes the PuB-EAA provider. No separate service. The nl-wallet issuance server checks the PID and calls the adapter. The adapter does not authenticate that call. Authorization in flow B The verify and retrieve service uses the same authorization facility of GBO. The ASI provider has its own OAuth authorization server, with a wallet verifier and a DigiD mock (ADR-0037). Approval by the citizen The wallet shows the request and asks for consent. Flow A: the citizen shares the PID. Flow B: the citizen logs in. Neither is a stored consent. Format of the attestation SD-JWT VC or mdoc SD-JWT VC (dc+sd-jwt) only Result of flow B The QTSP issues a QEAA. The reference QTSP issues a test statement, marked as not qualified.

The GO also says that a request over ISO 15000 needs no authorization. The demo offers clause 6.1 of ETSI TS 119 478 only (REQ-112). In both the GO and the demo, GBO itself is not a PuB-EAA provider.

docs.title: Open points
docs.text:
The main open points in the EUDI wallet channel are these:

  • Nothing binds the BSN in the source query of flow A to a checked PID disclosure (REQ-45, Q-18).
  • The BSN is in the PDP input and in both decision logs (F-54).
  • The QTSP can read the BSN in the access token (F-86).
  • Nothing links the citizen who logs in at the QTSP to the citizen who logs in at the authorization server (F-93).
  • The regulatory frame for PuB-EAA issuance and the designation of the issuer (F-81, Q-28).

docs.text:

  • Findings: F-54 (open), F-70 (open), F-81 (open), F-83 (open), F-86 (open), F-87 (open), F-93 (open)
  • Open questions: Q-18 (open), Q-28 (open)
  • Demo increments: SL-19 (done), SL-26 (done), SL-28 (done)

docs.title: ASI provider
docs.text:
The ASI provider lets a qualified trust service provider (QTSP) verify or retrieve attributes of a citizen at the authentic source. The exchange follows eIDAS article 45e and ETSI TS 119 478, clause 6.1. It is flow B of interaction pattern (interactiepatroon) A in the Globaal Ontwerp. GBO offers it as an OAuth front door with two services: the Authentic Source Interface Provider (ASIP) and its own authorization server (ADR-0037). The ASI verification runtime page has every hop and the links to the code.

Overview › EUDI wallet channel › ASI provider

docs.text:

Figure 1: The components of the ASI provider and their interfaces. Grey dashed: stubs and the reference QTSP. Thick border: click to zoom in.

Each component has one job:

Component Job In demo v0.9.0 ASIP Offers verify and retrieve per data service at /<ds>/authsrc-api. Checks the DPoP-bound token first and takes the BSN only from the token (REQ-87). Seals every 200 response. Real Authorization server Registers a QTSP, shows the request page, runs the login, and issues a DPoP-bound token of 10 minutes for one data service. Real. It keeps the registered clients in memory. Wallet verifier The nl-wallet verification server. It runs the PID disclosure for the login and asks for the BSN (REQ-102). Real. It also serves the login of the reference QTSP, as a demo shortcut. DigiD mock A second means to log in. Stub. It checks for nine digits and gives only a BSN (F-88). Register of relying parties Holds the entitlement QEAA_Provider of each QTSP. Stub: a file Discover Interface An external role. Tells a QTSP which data service offers an attribute, from the records of the ASIP. Stub Reference QTSP An external role. Discovers, registers, gets a token, verifies, and checks the seal. Real client behavior. It is not a real QTSP.

docs.title: Trust boundary
docs.text:
The QTSP and the source belong to two trust domains. The ASIP is the only part that acts in both:

flowchart LR subgraph oauth["OAuth trust, outside FSC"] direction TB qtsp["QTSP<br/>OAuth client"] cert["QTSP certificate<br/>organizationIdentifier"] ent[("Register entry<br/>QEAA_Provider")] as("Authorization server") end asip("ASIP<br/>FSC peer …1200") subgraph fsc["FSC trust, inside the GBO chain"] direction TB inw("PEP + PDP<br/>rule ASI0001") src[("BRP mock")] end qtsp -- "software statement" --> as as -. "chain to a trust anchor" .-> cert as -. "lookup, every hour" .-> ent qtsp -- "DPoP token" --> asip asip -- "actor is the ASIP peer,<br/>nothing about the QTSP" --> inw inw --> src %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class qtsp,ent mock class cert ext class as,asip eudi class inw basis class src source class inw zoom style oauth fill:#FFF7ED,stroke:#EA580C style fsc fill:#F0FDF4,stroke:#16A34A click inw "../../gbo-basis/authorization/" "Authorization"

Figure 2: The trust boundary of the ASI route (F-87).

The QTSP is an OAuth client of the authorization server. It has no FSC peer, no OIN and no PKIoverheid certificate. The reference architecture placed the interface in front of the FSC chain. The demo showed that this placement does not fit a QTSP, so the QTSP trust ends before FSC (ADR-0037).

The admission of a QTSP has two parts (REQ-88):

  • The QTSP registers with a software statement, sealed with its certificate. The authorization server checks the chain and the organizationIdentifier.
  • The register entry must carry QEAA_Provider and the same organizationIdentifier. The server checks the entry again every hour (REQ-89). If the register does not answer, the client stays active (Q-34).

The ASIP is an FSC consumer peer of its own, with a contract for the service brp at the source. For the PDP, the actor is always the ASIP. Rule ASI0001 grants the ASIP peer the fields of the Personal Records Database (BRP) behind the attributes, on brp only. The rule does not check the token or the QTSP. The PDP input and the ADL hold the BSN (REQ-60).

docs.title: The verify and retrieve flow
docs.text:
A verification runs through discovery, registration, authorization with a login, the token, the query through GBO Basis, and the seal:

sequenceDiagram autonumber actor B as Citizen box rgb(241,239,232) External participant Q as QTSP participant D as Discover Interface participant W as NL Wallet end box rgb(255,237,213) ASI provider participant AS as Authorization server participant ASIP as ASIP end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis at the source participant PDP as PEP + PDP end box rgb(221,235,247) Source participant S as BRP mock end rect rgb(255,250,245) Note over Q,AS: Once per QTSP Q->>D: which data service offers these attributes? D-->>Q: dataService records of the ASIP Q->>AS: register with a sealed software statement AS-->>Q: client_id, after the register check end rect rgb(246,252,248) Note over B,S: For every request B->>Q: ask for a statement, with values to check Q-->>B: redirect with resource, scope, attributes B->>AS: request page, who asks what at which source W->>AS: PID with the BSN (or the DigiD mock) AS-->>Q: code, through the browser Q->>AS: token request with PKCE, client assertion, DPoP AS-->>Q: access token for one data service, with the BSN Q->>ASIP: verify, with the token and the values Note over ASIP: check the token,<br/>BSN from the token,<br/>one query from the description ASIP->>PDP: query with the BSN, over FSC Note over PDP: PID regime, ASI0001 PDP->>S: allow, query through the gateway S-->>ASIP: fields of the person ASIP-->>Q: sealed result per attribute Note over Q: no valid seal,<br/>no accepted result end

Figure 3: Verify through the ASI provider, at essence level.

The login is the approval (REQ-90). Before the login, the request page shows the legal name of the QTSP, the operation, the source, and the attributes (REQ-91). If the citizen refuses, no login takes place and the source gets no request.

Retrieve runs the same way, with the scope retrieve. The request names attribute identifiers without values, and the sealed answer carries the values. If the source holds no value for one attribute, the answer is 404, without a partial result (REQ-101).

After an accepted result, the reference QTSP issues a test statement to the wallet. It uses the issuance server of the PuB-EAA provider. The statement has a test marking and is not a QEAA.

docs.title: One data service per source
docs.text:
An ASIP that serves several sources offers one data service per source (ADR-0038). Each data service has its own base URL, contract, discovery records and token audience:

flowchart LR qtsp["QTSP"] subgraph asip["ASIP"] direction TB ds1("Data service brp<br/>/brp/authsrc-api") ds2("Data service of<br/>a second source<br/><i>unit tests only</i>") end s1[("RvIG<br/>BRP mock")] s2[("Second source")] qtsp -- "token 1, audience brp" --> ds1 qtsp -. "token 2, second login" .-> ds2 ds1 --> s1 ds2 -.-> s2 %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class qtsp mock class ds1 eudi class ds2,s2 planned class s1 source style asip fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#EA580C

Figure 4: One data service and one token per source. Dashed: only in unit tests in demo v0.9.0.

ETSI lets a response name one authentic source. Article 9(4) requires that the result names the responsible body (F-89, REQ-94). An authorization request names exactly one data service as resource, or the answer is invalid_target. The ASIP refuses a token for another data service with 401 (REQ-95). A QTSP that needs attributes of two sources authorizes twice, and the citizen logs in twice.

By default, a token binds per operation, as ETSI specifies. A QTSP can also bind the token to the attributes with authorization_details. The ASIP then refuses any other attribute (ADR-0042, proposed, Q-33).

docs.title: Attributes described by the source
docs.text:
The source describes the attributes that it offers, in the asi capability of its source document (ADR-0039). The ASIP has no source knowledge in its code:

flowchart LR subgraph doc["Source document: capabilities.asi"] direction TB au["authentic_source<br/>legal name, country"] gq["graphql<br/>query that ends in ...Selected"] at["attributes<br/>identifier and fields"] end ops["pointer · join · const · each"] cat[("GBO attribute catalog<br/>value_schema per identifier")] rec("Reconciler<br/>validates, promotes") rel[("Active release")] asip("ASIP<br/>one query per request,<br/>only the needed fields") au --> rec gq --> rec at --> rec at --- ops cat -.-> rec rec --> rel rel -- "every 5 s" --> asip %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class au,gq,at,ops source class cat,rel store class rec basis class asip eudi class rec zoom style doc fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#6F94B8,stroke-dasharray:4 3 click rec "../../../concepts/source-onboarding/#the-asi-capability-schema-11" "The asi capability"

Figure 5: From the asi capability to one query per request.

Each attribute has an identifier from the GBO catalog and the source fields per member of the value. Four operations build a value: pointer, join, const and each. A house number, for example, is three BRP fields. For each request, the ASIP replaces ...Selected with the fields of the requested attributes only (REQ-92).

The identifiers and their value schemas are provisional until the EU catalog of attributes exists (Q-31). If the asi part has an error, the reconciler refuses the whole source, with its EUDI issuance. In demo v0.9.0, the authorization server takes its list of data services from configuration (AZSP_RESOURCES). The source descriptions do not feed that list (Q-38).

docs.title: Results and the seal
docs.text:
The ASIP builds each value from the source fields and compares it with the value that the QTSP sent. Each attribute gets one of four results:

flowchart LR q("Query over FSC") f[("Fields from<br/>the source")] b("Build the value<br/>from the description") c{"Compare with the<br/>value of the QTSP"} m(["Match"]) mv(["MatchWithVariation<br/>free text only"]) nm(["NoMatch"]) u(["Unknown<br/>the source has no value"]) e(["503 or 500<br/>never Unknown"]) s("Seal: detached JWS<br/>ES256, x5c") r["200 with<br/>X-JWS-Signature"] q --> f q -. "no answer, or a deny" .-> e f --> b --> c c --> m c --> mv c --> nm f -. "no value" .-> u m & mv & nm & u --> s s --> r %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class q basis class f source class b,c,m,mv,nm,u,s eudi class e dvtp class r ext

Figure 6: The result per attribute, and the seal on the response. Red: an error, never a result.

Three rules apply to the results:

  • Unknown means only that the source holds no value (REQ-84). A chain that does not answer gives 503 (REQ-93). A PDP deny or GraphQL errors give 500.
  • A verify response holds no source value (REQ-85). MatchWithVariation also returns no value. The conformance matrix records that row as failing (F-92).
  • Fuzzy matching applies only to strings without a format (REQ-113).

From January 1, 2027, every verification result must be sealed (REQ-83). The ASIP seals the exact body of every 200 response with a detached JWS in X-JWS-Signature (ADR-0041, proposed). It does not seal errors. The QTSP refuses a result without a valid seal. ETSI defines no seal format, so the format waits for a decision (Q-32). The demo seals with a development certificate, and it is open who holds the qualified seal certificate in production (Q-28).

docs.title: Compared with the Globaal Ontwerp
docs.text:
The demo follows flow B of pattern A. It differs in four steps:

Step Globaal Ontwerp Demo v0.9.0 Authorization The verify and retrieve service uses the authorization facility (autorisatievoorziening) of GBO. The ASI provider has its own OAuth authorization server, as ETSI clause 6.1.3 describes (ADR-0037). Approval The wallet shows the request and asks for consent. The citizen logs in with the NL Wallet or the DigiD mock. The demo stores no approval (REQ-90). ISO 15000 A request over ISO 15000 needs no authorization. Clause 6.2 is not offered (REQ-112). After an accepted result The QTSP issues a QEAA. The reference QTSP issues a test statement that is not qualified.

docs.title: Open points
docs.text:
The main open points in the ASI provider are these:

  • The QTSP can read the BSN in the access token (F-86, #595).
  • The register of relying parties and the certificate profile for QTSPs do not exist (F-85).
  • Nothing links the citizen who logs in at the QTSP to the citizen who logs in at the authorization server (F-93, Q-40).
  • The NL PID has no place of birth, and the DigiD mock gives only the BSN (F-94, F-88).
  • Who decides the seal format for all Dutch ASIPs (Q-32).

docs.text:

  • Findings: F-85 (open), F-86 (open), F-87 (open), F-88 (open), F-89 (open), F-92 (open), F-93 (open), F-94 (open)
  • Open questions: Q-28 (open), Q-31 (open), Q-32 (open), Q-33 (open), Q-34 (open), Q-38 (partly answered), Q-40 (open)
  • Demo increments: SL-28 (done)

docs.title: PuB-EAA provider
docs.text:
The PuB-EAA provider (PubEAA-voorziening) issues an attestation with source data to the EUDI wallet of the citizen. It is flow A of interaction pattern A in the Globaal Ontwerp. GBO operates the technical issuance facility, and each bronhouder stays the PuB-EAA provider of its own attestations (ADR-0028, proposed). The facility runs on the nl-wallet issuance server (ADR-0018). The EUDI issuance runtime page has every hop and the links to the code.

Overview › EUDI wallet channel › PuB-EAA provider

Figure 1: The components of the PuB-EAA provider and their interfaces. Thick border: click to zoom in.

Each component has one job:

Component Job Never does Issuance server Asks the wallet for the PID over OpenID4VP and checks it against its PID trust anchors. Issues the attestation over OpenID4VCI, signed with the issuer certificate of the source. Calls the source EUDI adapter Takes the BSN from the PID. Builds the query from the active release and calls the source through its own FSC Outway. Turns the answer into claims and writes two LDV records. Keeps source data, or has a query or mapping of its own (REQ-44) Release runtime Polls the active release and rebuilds the bindings of the adapter. If an error occurs, it keeps the previous snapshot. Fetches source metadata itself Source reconciler and registry The reconciler fetches and validates the source document. Promotion writes an immutable release and sets the active pointer. Activates a source because of a valid FSC contract (REQ-65) Certificate set Issuer, reader and status-list certificates of one source. The wallet shows the issuer and the purpose from these certificates. Serves another source (REQ-58) Issuance init Writes the configuration of the issuance server from the active release. The server reads it only at startup, so a new release needs a controlled restart. —

docs.title: The issuance flow
docs.text:
One issuance of the income statement (inkomensverklaring) for 2024 takes these steps:

sequenceDiagram autonumber actor B as Citizen box rgb(241,239,232) Wallet and demo portal participant P as Developer portal participant W as NL Wallet end box rgb(255,237,213) PuB-EAA provider participant IS as Issuance server participant AD as EUDI adapter end box rgb(237,233,254) Records participant LB as Adapter logbook end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis at the source participant PDP as PEP + PDP participant GW as Source gateway end box rgb(221,235,247) Source participant S as Source API end P->>AD: GET /eudi-offers.json AD-->>P: offers of the active release B->>W: scan the QR code of an offer W->>IS: fetch the disclosure request IS-->>W: ask for the PID claim bsn, with the reader certificate of the source W->>IS: PID as SD-JWT VC, after the citizen approves Note over IS: check the PID against<br/>issuer_trust_anchors IS->>AD: POST /attestations/belastingdienst/inkomensverklaring?jaar=2024 Note over AD: type in the release, BSN from<br/>the PID, parameters in an offer AD->>LB: record pid-bsn-extractie AD->>PDP: query with the BSN, over FSC Note over PDP: PID regime, EUD0001 PDP->>GW: allow GW->>S: query, unchanged S-->>AD: income data, back through FSC Note over AD: claims with gbo-simple-v1 AD->>LB: record attestatie-samenstellen AD-->>IS: claims, VCT, format dc+sd-jwt IS-->>W: attestation over OpenID4VCI W-->>B: accept the attestation

Figure 2: One issuance, at essence level.

Three properties of this flow matter for the design:

  • The issuance server checks the PID. The adapter trusts the callback without a check of the caller (The callback gap).
  • The adapter writes an LDV record before it calls the source. If the logbook does not acknowledge the record, the adapter does not call the source. Neither record holds the BSN (REQ-72).
  • The offer and the policy are separate limits. The source offers 2024 and 2025, and EUD0001 allows the same years. Publication by the source does not authorize the data (F-74).

For every hop, with the data and the code, see EUDI issuance.

docs.title: From source description to claims
docs.text:
The source describes each attestation once, in the eudi capability of its source document. GBO derives the rest:

flowchart LR subgraph doc["Source document: capabilities.eudi"] direction TB off["offers<br/>for example year 2024"] gq["graphql<br/>query, subject variable,<br/>result_pointer"] disp["display<br/>name, summary per language"] cl["claims<br/>pointer, datatype, label, sd"] end subgraph gen["Generated by GBO"] direction TB cfg("Issuance configuration<br/>offers, disclosure") tm("Type Metadata<br/>VCT with an integrity hash") prof("gbo-simple-v1<br/>projection rules") end subgraph run["For each issuance"] direction TB ans[("Answer of<br/>the source")] flat("Flat scalar claims") att["Attestation<br/>SD-JWT VC"] end off --> cfg disp --> tm cl --> tm cl --> prof gq --> ans ans --> prof prof --> flat flat --> att tm -. "type" .-> att %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class off,gq,disp,cl,ans source class cfg,tm,prof,flat eudi class att ext class tm zoom style doc fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#6F94B8,stroke-dasharray:4 3 style gen fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#EA580C style run fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#D1D5DB click tm "../../../concepts/source-onboarding/#the-eudi-capability-claims-once-type-metadata-generated" "The eudi capability"

Figure 3: From the eudi capability to an attestation.

A claim has a pointer into the answer, a datatype, a label and a setting for selective disclosure. GBO derives the projection from the claims. It also generates the SD-JWT VC Type Metadata from display and claims (ADR-0017, REQ-64). As a result, the schema in the Type Metadata always matches what the projection fills.

The URL of the Type Metadata is the VCT of the type version. A change to the claims or the display changes the bytes behind that URL, so the change needs a new type_version. The profile gbo-simple-v1 allows only scalar claims. Nested claims are not built (REQ-78).

The demo has two attestation types:

Type Source and service Rule Offers Subject of the data Income statement Belastingdienst, bri EUD0001 jaar (year) 2024 and 2025 The PID holder Death certificate (akte van overlijden) RvIG, brp EUD0002 One, without parameters The deceased partner of the PID holder

docs.title: Error contract
docs.text:
The adapter checks a callback in a fixed order. The first failed check decides the HTTP status:

flowchart LR in(["Callback"]) c1{"Release<br/>loaded?"} c2{"Type in the<br/>release?"} c3{"Source metadata<br/>fresh or in grace?"} c4{"PID with<br/>a BSN?"} c5{"Parameters<br/>in an offer?"} c6{"Source answer<br/>without errors?"} c7{"One result that<br/>fits the claims?"} ok(["200<br/>claims"]) e503(["503"]) e404(["404"]) e400(["400"]) e502(["502"]) in --> c1 --> c2 --> c3 --> c4 --> c5 --> c6 --> c7 c7 -- "yes" --> ok c1 & c3 -. "no" .-> e503 c2 -. "no" .-> e404 c4 & c5 -. "no" .-> e400 c6 -. "no, or a PDP deny" .-> e502 c7 -. "no result" .-> e404 c7 -. "more, or no fit" .-> e502 %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class in ext class c1,c2,c3,c4,c5,c6,c7,ok eudi class e503,e404,e400,e502 dvtp

Figure 4: The checks of the adapter, in order. Red: the HTTP status that the issuance server gets.

The issuance server gets only the HTTP status. The reason is in the adapter log (stage), and for a PDP deny also in the ADL. The FSC Inway removes the reason of a deny on the way back. These rules hold for every error path:

  • No attestation reaches the wallet, and a partial attestation does not exist (REQ-116).
  • A PDP deny (ACTOR_NOT_ALLOWED, PID_NOT_PRESENT, YEAR_NOT_ALLOWED, FIELD_NOT_PERMITTED) gives 502, the same status as a chain that does not answer.
  • If the logbook does not acknowledge an LDV record, the adapter answers 500 and does not continue.
  • A missing or incomplete certificate set blocks only that source (REQ-58).

The offer list is an exception to the isolation per source. If one source is past its grace period, /eudi-offers.json answers 503 for every source (#606). For all triggers, see Error paths.

docs.title: The callback gap
docs.text:
The issuance server checks the PID. The adapter does not know that a callback comes from the issuance server:

flowchart LR wallet["NL Wallet"] x["Any caller that<br/>reaches the adapter"] is("Issuance server<br/>checks the PID") cb("Adapter callback<br/>no caller authentication") pdp("PDP<br/>checks the caller peer<br/>and a BSN in the query") src[("Source")] f1("Adapter checks<br/>the SD-JWT itself") f2("Authenticated callback<br/>with signed evidence") wallet -- "PID" --> is is -- "BSN from the PID" --> cb x -- "any BSN" --> cb cb -- "as the designated issuer" --> pdp pdp --> src f1 -.-> cb f2 -.-> cb %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class wallet ext class x mock class is,cb eudi class pdp basis class src source class f1,f2 planned

Figure 5: The callback gap. Dashed: the two fixes that REQ-45 names. Demo v0.9.0 builds neither.

No mechanism binds the BSN in the callback to a checked disclosure (REQ-45, Q-18, #133). The PDP sees the designated issuer peer and a BSN, so it allows. The list of designated issuers is the only gate of the PID regime (F-70). The demo uses the gap itself: a playground in the developer portal posts a typed BSN to the adapter.

The demo dropped a PID check in the adapter, because the issuance server checks the signature (SL-25). The PID trust list of the issuance server is also too broad. Next to the PID provider, it trusts the GBO development CA and the issuer CA of every source. Both fixes of REQ-45 need a binding of the disclosure to the request.

docs.title: Related-person attestation
docs.text:
The death certificate holds data about the deceased partner of the citizen who shares the PID. The subject of the claims differs from the person who discloses the PID (F-47, REQ-57):

flowchart LR holder(["PID holder"]) ad("EUDI adapter<br/>BSN of the holder") pdp("PDP, rule EUD0002<br/>sees only the flat output") brp[("BRP source<br/>resolves the relation")] rel["Marriage ended by<br/>the death of the partner"] att["Death certificate<br/>claims about the partner"] holder -- "PID" --> ad ad -- "akteVanOverlijden(bsn)" --> pdp pdp --> brp brp --- rel brp -. "fields of the<br/>deceased partner" .-> att %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class holder,brp,rel source class ad eudi class pdp basis class att ext

Figure 6: A related-person attestation. The source, and not GBO, knows the relation.

The source selects the marriage that ended by the death of the partner. If the partner died on another date than the dissolution, the source returns nothing, and the adapter answers 404. The PDP does not see the relation. The deceased is not a data subject under the GDPR, so the source logs the requester and the living parents (AV-10).

The preferred design puts the relation in filter arguments of the published schema. The policy then requires these arguments with fixed values (#425, Q-14). In demo v0.9.0, a caller can ask for the death certificate of any BSN, because of the callback gap.

docs.title: Trust roles and the PuB-EAA provider
docs.text:
Each bronhouder needs its own certificate per role, and one certificate never fills two roles. The following figure shows the roles around one bronhouder:

flowchart LR subgraph legal["Legal role"] bh["Bronhouder<br/>PuB-EAA provider"] end subgraph tech["Technical role"] fac("GBO issuance facility<br/>probably the EEAIssuer") end subgraph certs["Certificate set of one bronhouder"] direction TB iss[("Issuer certificate<br/>production: qualified seal<br/>in a QSCD")] rdr[("Reader certificate<br/>production: access certificate")] stl[("Status-list certificate")] regc("Registration certificate<br/><i>not in the demo</i>") end subgraph open["Open decisions"] direction TB q28("Designation and<br/>supervision: Q-28") q30("Trust list for<br/>PuB-EAA providers: Q-30") q17("Custody of the seal and<br/>status-list keys: Q-17") end bh -- "instructs: validity,<br/>revocation" --> fac fac -- "signs with" --> iss fac --- rdr fac --- stl certs ~~~ open %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class bh source class fac eudi class iss,rdr,stl store class regc,q28,q30,q17 planned class fac zoom style legal fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#6F94B8,stroke-dasharray:4 3 style tech fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#EA580C style certs fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#7C3AED style open fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,stroke-dasharray:6 4 click fac "../../../concepts/identity-trust/#eudi-trust-roles" "EUDI trust roles"

Figure 7: Trust roles in PuB-EAA issuance. Dashed: not built or not decided.

ADR-0028 (proposed) divides the roles. The bronhouder is the PuB-EAA provider and stays legally responsible for content, validity and revocation. GBO operates the technical issuance facility and is probably the EEAIssuer in the notification of each bronhouder. The facility is optional: a bronhouder can run its own credential issuer.

Since August 2026, PuB-EAA issuance falls under the same standard as QEAA issuance (F-81). That frame asks for these parts:

  • Designation of the issuer.
  • A registration certificate.
  • A qualified seal in a QSCD.
  • Conformity with ETSI TS 119 471 and TS 119 472-3.

Demo v0.9.0 is not checked against this frame. One development CA fills all roles. Three decisions are open: who designates the issuer (Q-28), on which trust list the providers appear (Q-30), and who holds the keys (Q-17). For the certificate roles, see EUDI trust roles.

docs.title: Compared with the Globaal Ontwerp
docs.text:
The demo follows flow A of pattern A. It differs in three points:

Point Globaal Ontwerp Demo v0.9.0 Role of GBO A technical, central and optional facility. GBO is not a PuB-EAA provider. The same. The bronhouder is the provider (ADR-0028, proposed). Authorization An authorization facility (autorisatievoorziening) authorizes the PuB-EAA facility after a PID login. The issuance server checks the PID itself. No separate authorization service exists. Semantic mapping A shared GBO facility translates the format of the source. The source maps its own fields to claims with gbo-simple-v1. No translation layer exists.

docs.title: Open points
docs.text:
The main open points in the PuB-EAA provider are these:

  • The callback gap: nothing binds the disclosure to the source query (REQ-45, Q-18).
  • The regulatory frame for PuB-EAA issuance, and who designates the issuer (F-81, Q-28).
  • The trust list for PuB-EAA providers (Q-30).
  • Every attestation is valid for 365 days. GBO gets no change signal from the source, so it cannot revoke on a change (F-82, REQ-77).
  • The source description does not mark the relation behind a related-person attestation (F-47).
  • Issuance with the authorization code flow, which HAIP 1.0 requires: which authorization server identifies the citizen and records consent (Q-83).

docs.title: GBO Basis
docs.text:
GBO Basis opens a government source in one standard way, for every channel. It runs at the bronhouder: each source has its own FSC Inway, its own PDP and its own source gateway. No central server decides for all sources (ADR-0004). GBO delivers the components, and the bronhouder runs them (P-10).

Overview › GBO Basis

docs.title: Inside GBO Basis
docs.text:
The Globaal Ontwerp names four parts: a standard interface, generic source access, configurable authorization, and GBO tools. The following figure shows the components that make up these parts in gbo-demo v0.9.0:

flowchart LR caller["Caller<br/>(any channel)"] subgraph bh["Bronhouder"] direction LR subgraph fsc["Standard interface: FSC"] direction TB inway("FSC Inway<br/>= PEP") mgr("FSC Manager<br/>contracts, tokens") end subgraph authz["Configurable authorization"] direction TB pdp("PDP<br/>OpenFTV + OPA/Rego") pol("Policy set<br/>engine + 5 rules") end subgraph access["Generic source access"] direction TB gw("Source gateway") dec("Decryption<br/>component") api[("Source API<br/>GraphQL")] meta[("Source metadata<br/>/.well-known/gbo")] end rec[("Records<br/>ADL · LDV · txlog")] end subgraph shared["Shared GBO facilities"] direction TB adm[("Admission register")] reg[("Source registry")] tools("GBO tools<br/><i>design only</i>") end tr[("Consent register")] caller -- "FSC request" --> inway caller -. "contract proposal" .-> mgr inway -- "AuthZEN" --> pdp mgr -- "AuthZEN autosign" --> pdp pdp --- pol adm -. "PIP pull" .-> pdp pdp -. "status (DvTP only)" .-> tr inway -- "after allow" --> gw gw --> dec gw --> api meta -. "fetched over FSC" .-> reg pdp -.-> rec api -.-> rec %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class caller ext class inway,mgr,pdp,pol,gw,dec basis class api,meta source class adm,reg,rec store class tools planned class tr dvtp class pdp,pol,gw,mgr,meta,reg,rec zoom style bh fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#6F94B8,stroke-dasharray:4 3 style fsc fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#16A34A style authz fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#16A34A style access fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#16A34A style shared fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#D1D5DB click pdp "authorization/" "Authorization" click pol "policy/" "Policy rules" click mgr "authorization/#admission-of-parties" "Admission" click gw "source-access/" "Source access" click meta "source-configuration/" "Source configuration" click reg "source-configuration/" "Source configuration" click rec "records/" "Records"

Figure 1: The parts of GBO Basis. Thick border: click to zoom in.

The parts have the following roles:

Part Components Role Zoom in Standard interface FSC Inway, FSC Manager, FSC Outway of the caller Every connection to a source runs over FSC, with mTLS and a contract (ADR-0003). The Inway is the PEP. FSC group Configurable authorization PDP, policy set, admission register The PDP decides on every request and on every contract proposal. Policy is configuration, not code. Authorization Generic source access Source gateway, decryption component, source API The source answers one GraphQL query. Under consent, the gateway first puts the citizen in the query. Source access Policy rules Policy set, its tests and its distribution The rules are data for the PDP. Each bronhouder manages its own set. Policy rules Records ADL, LDV logbooks, FSC txlog Every decision, processing and transport leaves a record, linked by one trace ID. Records Source configuration Source metadata, source registry The source describes its own services. GBO validates and activates that description. Source configuration GBO tools Translation layer, onboarding toolkit Help a bronhouder without a GraphQL API. Not built. ADR-0027

docs.title: The request path
docs.text:
A request through GBO Basis has the same steps in every channel. The PDP decides before anything reaches the source. The source gateway does its work only after an allow:

sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(241,239,232) Channel participant C as Caller end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis at the bronhouder participant IN as FSC Inway (PEP) participant PDP as PDP participant GW as Source gateway end box rgb(221,235,247) Source participant API as Source API end box rgb(237,233,254) Records participant R as ADL, LDV end C->>IN: GraphQL query over FSC (mTLS, token) IN->>PDP: AuthZEN question with the raw body Note over PDP: field list, regime,<br/>rules per field PDP->>R: decision record (ADL) PDP-->>IN: allow or deny alt deny IN-->>C: deny, nothing reaches the source else allow IN->>GW: the judged request opt consent proof present Note over GW: decrypt own value,<br/>replace the placeholder end GW->>API: query API->>R: processing record (LDV) API-->>C: only the selected fields end

Figure 2: One request through GBO Basis.

The steps work as follows:

  1. The caller sends a GraphQL query through its FSC Outway. The Inway checks the certificate and the contract of the caller.
  2. The Inway sends the request, with its raw body, to the PDP as an AuthZEN question. The Inway does not read the query (REQ-42).
  3. The PDP turns the query into a list of fields, selects the regime from the evidence, and decides each field. Authorization shows how.
  4. The PDP writes the decision to the ADL, the audit record of decisions (ADR-0036).
  5. On a deny, the source sees nothing. By design, the caller gets a coarse reason code. The FSC Inway of demo v0.9.0 drops that code on the way back.
  6. On an allow, the Inway passes the request to the source gateway. Only the Inway can reach the gateway (ADR-0033).
  7. Under consent, the gateway decrypts the value that the consent proof holds for this source. It puts the BSN or the source pseudonym in the place of the placeholder. Without a consent proof, it passes the query unchanged.
  8. The source runs the query and returns only the selected fields (REQ-08). It logs the processing in its own LDV logbook.

docs.title: What the bronhouder runs
docs.text:
GBO delivers the components as reference components. The bronhouder chooses to run them, or a working equivalent that meets the same interfaces. The following figure shows who owns what at one source:

flowchart TB subgraph own["Owned by the bronhouder"] direction LR api[("Source API<br/>and schema")] meta[("Service description")] keys[("Decryption keys")] log[("LDV logbook")] pol("Policy set<br/>and its management") end subgraph deliv["Delivered by GBO, run by the bronhouder"] direction LR inway("FSC Inway") pdp("PDP") gw("Source gateway") ldvc("LDV client") end subgraph run["Run by GBO for all sources"] direction LR adm[("Admission register")] reg[("Source registry")] tr[("Consent register")] end own ~~~ deliv ~~~ run %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class api,meta,keys,log source class pol,inway,pdp,gw,ldvc basis class adm,reg store class tr dvtp style own fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#6F94B8,stroke-dasharray:4 3 style deliv fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#16A34A style run fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#D1D5DB

Figure 3: Ownership at one source.

The PEP, the PDP, policy management and source access are decentral, at the bronhouder. The consent facility (toestemmingsvoorziening) is central and mandatory for DvTP (Q-10, ADR-0021). The PSA has not decided who operates the central facilities (open decisions B-06 and B-17). The demo runs everything in one stack and shares one PDP between the sources. That is a demo shortcut.

docs.title: Open points
docs.text:
The main open points in GBO Basis are these:

  • The PID regime has no positive evidence of its own. A request without a consent proof enters it (F-70).
  • The rule "only after the decision" depends on the network. Only the Inway can be allowed to reach the source gateway (F-79).
  • The ADL record holds only what the consumer also sees (F-72).
  • A broken policy module stops every decision, without a visible fallback (F-52).

docs.text:
