  • Demo increments: SL-42 (done), SL-45 (done), SL-51 (done)

docs.title: Authorization in GBO Basis
docs.text:
The Globaal Ontwerp calls this part "configurable authorization". Each source has a PDP that decides on every request, field by field, with rules written as policy. The FSC Inway of the source enforces the decision. This page shows the parts, the order of the checks, and the admission of parties. The Authorization concept page has the detail and the links to the code.

Overview › GBO Basis › Authorization

docs.title: Five questions, five places
docs.text:
Authorization answers five separate questions. Each question has its own place in the chain:

flowchart LR req(["Request"]) subgraph s1["① Organization"] direction TB a1("Is this a known<br/>organization?") b1["FSC connection<br/>mTLS + PKI certificate"] a1 --- b1 end subgraph s2["② Permission"] direction TB a2("Can it use<br/>this service?") b2["FSC Manager<br/>contract after admission"] a2 --- b2 end subgraph s5["⑤ Validity"] direction TB a5("Is the request complete<br/>and well formed?") b5["Request mapper<br/>field list, limits, pins"] a5 --- b5 end subgraph s3["③ Basis"] direction TB a3("Consent<br/>or PID?") b3["Policy<br/>regime from evidence"] a3 --- b3 end subgraph s4["④ Scope"] direction TB a4("Which fields, whose<br/>data, which years?") b4["Policy<br/>rules per field"] a4 --- b4 end src[("Source")] req --> s1 --> s2 --> s5 --> s3 --> s4 --> src %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class req ext class src source class a1,a2,a5,a3,a4 basis class b1,b2,b5,b3,b4 ext class a2,a5,a3,a4 zoom style s1 fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#D1D5DB style s2 fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#D1D5DB style s5 fill:#F0FDF4,stroke:#16A34A style s3 fill:#F0FDF4,stroke:#16A34A style s4 fill:#F0FDF4,stroke:#16A34A click a2 "#admission-of-parties" "Admission" click a3 "#regime-from-evidence" "Regime" click a4 "#the-rules" "The rules" click a5 "#from-query-to-decision" "Decision pipeline"

Figure 1: The five authorization questions and where each one is answered. Grey: FSC, once per connection. Green: the PDP of the source, for every request.

Questions ① and ② belong to FSC and hold for the whole connection. The PDP answers ③ to ⑤ again for every request (ADR-0004). No central authorization server exists.

docs.title: The parts
docs.text:
The PEP, the PDP and two PIPs work together as follows:

flowchart LR out["Outway of<br/>the caller"] subgraph src["At the bronhouder"] direction LR pep("FSC Inway<br/>PEP") subgraph pdp["PDP: OpenFTV v0.1.0"] direction TB map("FTV GraphQL mapper<br/>query → field list") eng("Rego policy<br/>engine + rules") end pout("Outway<br/>of the PDP") gw("Source gateway") end adm[("PIP: admission register<br/>parties, mandates")] tr[("PIP: consent register<br/>keys, consent status")] adl[("ADL")] out -- "request + raw body" --> pep pep -- "AuthZEN" --> map map --> eng eng -- "status, over FSC" --> pout --> tr tr -. "keys (JWKS), cached 5 min" .-> eng adm -. "pulled every 5 s" .-> eng eng --> adl pep -- "only after allow" --> gw %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class out ext class pep,map,eng,pout,gw basis class adm,adl store class tr dvtp class eng,map,tr,adm zoom style src fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#6F94B8,stroke-dasharray:4 3 style pdp fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#16A34A click map "#from-query-to-decision" "Decision pipeline" click eng "#the-rules" "The rules" click tr "../../dvtp/consent-service/" "Consent facility" click adm "#admission-of-parties" "Admission"

Figure 2: PEP, PDP and PIPs at one source.

The parts have these roles:

Part Role PEP The FSC Inway. Its AuthZEN plugin sends every request with the raw body to the PDP and forwards the request only on an allow. There is no separate PEP service (ADR-0002). Request mapper Turns the GraphQL body into a list of fields with their arguments, following the FTV GraphQL profile. It does nothing else (ADR-0013). Policy Rego code that selects the regime, checks the consent proof and decides each field. The policy is data for the PDP, so a bronhouder changes it without a new build. PIP: consent register (toestemmingsregister) Gives the status of a consent for every request, over FSC. Gives the keys to check the proof. DvTP only. PIP: admission register Lists the admitted parties and the mandates of integrators. OpenFTV pulls it every five seconds.

docs.title: From query to decision
docs.text:
The PDP takes a fixed series of steps for each request. The first step that fails decides the outcome:

flowchart TB in(["AuthZEN question<br/>with raw GraphQL body"]) m{"Mapper: complete<br/>field list?"} r{"Regime: how many<br/>consent tokens?"} cv{"Consent proof:<br/>signature, claims, status OK?"} b["Bind rules to each field:<br/>same regime · same FSC service ·<br/>rule names the field"] f{"Every field granted<br/>by a rule?"} allow(["ALLOW<br/>query goes to the source"]) d1(["DENY<br/>COVERAGE_UNVERIFIABLE"]) d2(["DENY<br/>two tokens"]) d3(["DENY<br/>consent reason"]) d4(["DENY<br/>FIELD_NOT_PERMITTED"]) in --> m m -- "no" --> d1 m -- "yes" --> r r -- "two" --> d2 r -- "one: consent regime" --> cv r -- "none: PID regime" --> b cv -- "no" --> d3 cv -- "yes" --> b b --> f f -- "yes" --> allow f -- "no, or no rule at all" --> d4 %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class in ext class m,r,cv,f,b basis class allow basis class d1,d2,d3,d4 dvtp class cv zoom click cv "../../dvtp/consent-service/#the-consent-proof" "Consent proof"

Figure 3: The decision pipeline of the PDP. Red: deny.

Three properties of this pipeline matter for the design:

  • Closed world. A field that no rule names is denied (NO_APPLICABLE_RULE). There is no separate catalog of allowed fields: the rules are the catalog (ADR-0009).
  • All or nothing. The PDP allows the request only if it allows every field. It never removes fields from a query.
  • Two layers of reasons. The consumer gets one coarse code, so it cannot learn the schema by trying field names. The administrator of the source sees the reason per field (REQ-06).

docs.title: Regime from evidence
docs.text:
The evidence in the request selects the regime. A declared regime or a contract property plays no part (ADR-0031):

flowchart LR q{"X-GBO-Consent-Token<br/>in the request?"} c["Consent regime<br/>DVT0001 · LVG0001"] p["PID regime<br/>EUD0001 · EUD0002 · ASI0001"] x(["Deny"]) q -- "one" --> c q -- "none" --> p q -- "two" --> x %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class q basis class c dvtp class p eudi class x dvtp

Figure 4: Regime selection.

The regime only selects which rules apply. Each rule still checks its own basis: DVT0001 denies without a verified consent, and the PID rules deny if a consent token is present.

Only consent is positive evidence. A request enters the PID regime because it carries no token (F-70). For that reason, the PID rules admit only named callers: the EUDI adapter and the ASIP. These lists must never contain a DvTP consumer. The fix in the design is a verified PID as positive evidence (REQ-45).

docs.title: The rules
docs.text:
Demo v0.9.0 has five rules. Each rule names its regime, the FSC services it serves, and the fields it can grant:

Rule Regime Service Grants DVT0001 consent bri Income declaration fields, per consented year LVG0001 consent lvg The ownership check of the LVG pilot EUD0001 PID bri Income statement (inkomensverklaring) to the wallet, years 2024 and 2025 EUD0002 PID brp Death certificate (akte van overlijden) to the wallet ASI0001 PID brp The BRP fields behind the ASI attributes, for the ASIP only

A rule binds to a field only on its own services. A field name such as Query.ingeschrevenPersoon exists in several schemas. Without this binding, a rule for one source grants the same field at another source (REQ-97, F-90).

Under consent, two checks look inside the query. The citizen must be the placeholder consent:identity, never a real number. Every requested year must have a consented scope, and a query without a year filter is denied. The PDP checks that the citizen comes from the proof. It never learns who the citizen is (F-77).

docs.title: Admission of parties
docs.text:
Before a party can send requests, it needs an FSC contract. The FSC Manager of the source asks the same PDP whether to sign it. The contract policy reads the admission register and stops at the first failed check:

flowchart LR p(["Contract proposal"]) c1{"Well-formed<br/>request?"} c2{"Grant type 2 or 3?"} c3{"Has a<br/>counterparty?"} c4{"Register<br/>available?"} c5{"Party in<br/>the register?"} c6{"Party<br/>active?"} c7{"Admitted for<br/>this source?"} c8{"Delegation<br/>registered?"} ok(["Manager signs"]) no(["Stays proposed<br/>with a reason code"]) p --> c1 --> c2 --> c3 --> c4 --> c5 --> c6 --> c7 --> c8 --> ok c1 & c2 & c3 & c4 & c5 & c6 & c7 & c8 -. "no" .-> no %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class p ext class c1,c2,c3,c4,c5,c6,c7,c8 basis class ok basis class no dvtp

Figure 5: The eight checks for a contract, in order (ADR-0015).

Admission is data in a register, not a rule in the policy (REQ-61). An operator admits, pauses or widens a party without a policy change. A refused contract stays proposed, so the party can try again after admission (REQ-63). The contract decides who can connect. The request rules decide what each request can get (REQ-62).

docs.title: Open points
docs.text:
The main open points in authorization are these:

  • The PID regime needs positive evidence of its own (F-70, REQ-45).
  • The ADL record does not hold the consent status that the PDP used, so a decision cannot be replayed from the record (F-72).
  • The FSC Inway of demo v0.9.0 loses the reason code on the way back to the consumer (detail).
  • How to model fields, recursion and arguments for future sources (Q-14).

docs.title: Policy rules and their management
docs.text:
The Globaal Ontwerp names policy rules ("Beleidsregels") as a block of GBO Basis: policy rules decide who can get which data. Each bronhouder owns, writes and publishes the policy that its own PDP evaluates. GBO supplies a reference policy set, the engine choice, and five guidelines, but no central policy service (ADR-0021). The Policy lifecycle concept page and the Policy distribution runtime page have the detail and the links to the code.

Overview › GBO Basis › Policy rules

docs.title: The policy set
docs.text:
flowchart LR pep("FSC Inway<br/>PEP") mgr("FSC Manager<br/>of the source") subgraph set["Policy set: policies/"] direction LR entry("authz.rego<br/>entrypoint") subgraph eng["Engine and readers"] direction TB e("engine.rego<br/>regime, binding,<br/>closed world") con("consent.rego<br/>consent PIP") pins("graphql_schemas.rego<br/>schema pins") end subgraph rules["Rules"] direction TB r1("rules/dvtp<br/>DVT0001 · LVG0001") r2("rules/eudi<br/>EUD0001 · EUD0002") r3("rules/asi<br/>ASI0001") end auto("fsc/autosign.rego<br/>contract policy") end tr[("Consent<br/>register")] pep -- "AuthZEN" --> entry --> e e --> r1 & r2 & r3 e --- con e --- pins con -. "status over FSC" .-> tr mgr -- "AuthZEN autosign" --> auto %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class pep,mgr,entry,e,con,pins,r1,r2,r3,auto basis class tr dvtp class r1,r2,r3,auto,con,pins zoom style set fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#16A34A style eng fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#16A34A style rules fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#16A34A click r1 "../authorization/#the-rules" "The rules" click r2 "../authorization/#the-rules" "The rules" click r3 "../authorization/#the-rules" "The rules" click auto "../authorization/#admission-of-parties" "Admission" click con "../../dvtp/consent-service/#the-consent-proof" "Consent proof" click pins "../source-access/#the-pdp-copy-of-the-schema" "Schema copy"

Figure 1: The policy set of demo v0.9.0. Thick border: click to zoom in.

All policy is Rego in version control, with tests next to the rules. The set has four parts:

Part Files Role Entrypoint authz.rego The package that OpenFTV evaluates. It passes only allow and the coarse reason to OpenFTV. It allows the source-metadata fetch for two known peers on the two metadata services Engine and readers gbo/engine.rego, gbo/lib.rego, gbo/consent.rego, gbo/graphql_schemas.rego Generic machinery: regime and service binding, the closed world, reason codes, the consent proof, and the schema pins Rules gbo/rules/dvtp/, gbo/rules/eudi/, gbo/rules/asi/ One package per access verdict: DVT0001, LVG0001, EUD0001, EUD0002, ASI0001 Contract policy fsc/autosign.rego Decides for the FSC Manager of the source whether to sign a contract (ADR-0015)

A new access verdict is a new rule file with tests. The engine does not change. The policy is data for the PDP, so a bronhouder changes it without a new build. The contract policy is a separate rule set from the request policy, in the same bundle (REQ-62).

Rules use data with four lifecycles. Some data is in the rule itself, for example the years of EUD0001 and the actor lists of the PID rules. The schema digests are in the bundle. The admission register is a PIP that the PDP pulls every five seconds. The consent proof and its status arrive with each request.

docs.title: Ownership
docs.text:
The policy belongs to the source (P-10). The question who can manage and publish the policy of a bronhouder has an answer: the bronhouder itself (Q-21, October 28, 2026). Each party has a fixed role:

Party Does Never does Bronhouder Writes, approves and publishes its own policy. Runs its own PAP and PDP. Hands its policy to a central PAP GBO Supplies the reference policy set, the engine choice and the guidelines RL-01 to RL-05. Sets requirements on the policy installation of another party Another organization that builds or hosts bundles Signs the bundles. The PDP verifies them. Publishes without a signature across the organization boundary

PSA S06 sets the norm for publication control. The norm asks for an owner, an approver, an effective date, a change history, tests before publication, and an emergency and rollback procedure. Authority over policy is with competent public parties, so the management practices are guidelines. A guideline becomes a requirement only if GBO delivers the management setup itself.

docs.title: From version control to the PDP
docs.text:
A policy change goes through a fixed series of checks before the PDP uses it:

flowchart LR a(["Author edits<br/>a .rego file"]) g[("policies/<br/>with tests")] c["make policy-check<br/>Rego only, unique names,<br/>opa check"] t["make policy-test<br/>opa fmt, opa test"] ci["CI<br/>same checks, generated<br/>files up to date"] d["Distribution<br/>mount or bundle"] p("PDP compiles<br/>the whole set") ok(["Decides,<br/>writes ADL records"]) stop(["PDP does not start"]) br(["Every decision fails<br/>no visible fallback"]) a --> g --> c --> t --> ci --> d --> p p -- "compiles" --> ok c -- "fails" --> stop p -- "one bad module" --> br %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class a ext class g store class c,t,ci ext class d,p,ok basis class stop,br dvtp class d zoom click d "#two-distribution-modes" "Distribution modes"

Figure 2: From version control to the PDP. Red: failure.

The PDP compiles the policy set as a whole. One bad module does not give a deny. It breaks every decision (F-52). The demo had this fault several times:

  • A stale policy declared the same package as an existing rule. Every request got HTTP 500.
  • A non-Rego file under policies/ removed every policy after it in walk order.
  • A second file with the same name replaced the first, because the loader keys policies by file name.
  • At hot reload, the PDP reports a module that does not compile as loaded, while the old policy keeps deciding (#151).

make policy-check is the local safety net. It refuses non-Rego files and duplicate file names, and then it runs opa check. Every make target that starts the PDP depends on it. make policy-test adds opa fmt --diff and opa test. CI repeats these steps. CI also checks that two generated files are up to date: the schema pins and the rule list of the developer portal.

The contract policy is in the same set. One broken module therefore also stops the admission of new parties. Its package name is fixed (doelbinding.auto_sign_contract). If someone renames it, every contract stays pending without a signal.

docs.title: Two distribution modes
docs.text:
The demo gets the policy set to the PDP in one of two modes:

flowchart LR git[("policies/<br/>version control")] subgraph mount["Mount mode: default"] direction TB bm["Bind mount<br/>./policies"] pdp1("PDP<br/>hot reload") bm --> pdp1 end subgraph bundle["Bundle mode: opt-in"] direction TB seed["seed-openftv-manager.py<br/>deployment identity"] kc["Keycloak<br/>realm gbo"] mgr("OpenFTV Manager<br/>PAP, Cedar on its API") pg[("postgres-ftv<br/>policy + audit trail")] pdp2("PDP<br/>pulls at start") seed -- "short-lived token" --> kc seed -- "write, retire" --> mgr mgr --> pg pdp2 -- "GET /v1/bundle/gbo-pdp" --> mgr end git --> bm git --> seed %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class git store class bm,seed mock class kc ext class mgr,pdp1,pdp2 basis class pg store class pdp1,mgr zoom style mount fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#16A34A style bundle fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#16A34A click pdp1 "../../../runtime/policy-distribution/#mount-mode" "Mount mode" click mgr "../../../runtime/policy-distribution/#bundle-mode" "Bundle mode"

Figure 3: The two distribution modes. Version control is the source of the content in both.

The two modes differ as follows:

Mount mode Bundle mode How the PDP gets the policy The image carries policies/, and compose bind-mounts ./policies over it The PDP pulls bundle gbo-pdp from the OpenFTV Manager, because PDP_BUNDLE_MANAGER is set When a change takes effect At each edit, by hot reload At the next PDP start. make manager-seed restarts the PDP Started by Every make demo* target make demo-manager, then make manager-seed Version None The bundle has an ID and a version

Bundle mode has these properties:

  • The PDP pulls, and nothing pushes. The PDP guards its own management endpoints with the decision policy, which denies every request that is not a data request. A push therefore gets HTTP 403 (F-51).
  • The seed script retires policy and does not delete it. It gives every policy that left version control the tag gbo-retired. A delete fails upstream on a foreign key to the audit trail.
  • Cedar policies authorize the API of the OpenFTV Manager, apart from the Rego decision policy. The PDP shows no identity, so pdp-bundle.cedar allows only GET on the one bundle path.
  • The Manager seeds its Cedar policies only into an empty store. An existing volume does not pick up a changed Cedar file.
  • The realm has the roles admin, author and auditor. Publication uses a non-personal deployment identity with a token of 30 minutes. In demo v0.9.0, no Cedar policy grants author an action, so only admin writes and publishes.
  • The bundle has no signature. Inside one organization, signing is not planned (#426). If a bronhouder lets another organization build or host its bundles, signing and verification become a requirement (F-09).

Two components have the name Manager. The OpenFTV Manager manages policy. The FSC Manager manages contracts and issues access tokens.

docs.title: Guidelines for bronhouders
docs.text:
GBO gives five guidelines for policy management. Each guideline has a status in demo v0.9.0:

Guideline Demo status RL-01 Deliver policy as a versioned bundle. Do not bake it into the PDP Opt-in only. The default mounts the policies. No signature RL-02 Authorize the management API with its own policy set. Deny on an empty store Built for the OpenFTV Manager (Cedar). The PDP itself does not follow it (F-51) RL-03 Separate writing from publishing. Publish with a non-personal, short-lived identity Deployment identity built. The author role grants no action RL-04 Withdraw policy, and do not delete it. Reconcile with version control Built: retire_stale at every seed RL-05 Validate a bundle before activation. Fall back visibly to the last valid set Local check built (make policy-check). Visible fallback not built

Source metadata has the lifecycle that RL-05 asks for: validation before activation, atomic promotion, and rollback (F-59, Source configuration). For policy, this lifecycle is a backlog item.

docs.title: Compared with the Globaal Ontwerp
docs.text:
The demo follows the Globaal Ontwerp in the PEP, PDP and PIP chain with AuthZEN and Rego. It differs in the management of the policy:

Topic Globaal Ontwerp Demo v0.9.0 Place of the PAP A PAP manages the policies and distributes them to the PDPs of the bronhouders A PAP and a PDP at each bronhouder. No central PAP (ADR-0021) Bundles Signed policy bundles A bundle with an ID and a version, without a signature. Signing only across an organization boundary Policy language ODRL in the PAP Rego for every decision, and Cedar for the API of the OpenFTV Manager (Q-78)

docs.title: Open points
docs.text:
The main open points in policy management are these:

  • The PDP guards its own management endpoints with the decision policy (F-51).
  • One broken module stops every decision and the admission of new parties, without a visible fallback (F-52).
  • The decision record does not name the policy version that decided (REQ-59, Records).
  • The actor lists of the PID rules are policy data. They must stay apart from the consent consumers in every environment (F-70).
  • How the reference policy shows that it is not tied to one language or engine (Q-78).

docs.title: Records: decisions, processing, transport
docs.text:
Every data exchange through GBO must be reconstructable afterwards. A reader must see who asked for what, under which basis, with which decision, and who processed which personal data (P-12). GBO keeps three authoritative records, one per Logius standard. One W3C trace ID joins them, and each record stores the FSC transaction ID next to it. This is capability S09 of the Globaal Ontwerp. The Logging, audit and traceability concept page has the detail and the links to the code.

Overview › GBO Basis › Records

docs.title: Three records
docs.text:
flowchart LR subgraph dec["Decision"] direction TB pdp("PDP<br/>OpenFTV") adl[("ADL<br/>ftv_adl")] pdp --> adl end subgraph proc["Processing"] direction TB comp("Gateway, source API,<br/>register, consumer,<br/>EUDI adapter") ldv[("LDV logbook<br/>per controller")] comp --> ldv end subgraph tra["Transport"] direction TB fsc("FSC Inway<br/>and Outway") tx[("FSC txlog<br/>per peer")] fsc --> tx end subgraph obs["Observability, not audit"] direction TB all("All services") jg[("Traces<br/>Jaeger, 7 days")] lk[("Logs<br/>Loki, 7 days")] all --> jg all --> lk end dec ~~~ proc ~~~ tra ~~~ obs %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class pdp,comp,fsc basis class adl,ldv,tx store class all ext class jg,lk mock class adl,ldv,tx zoom style dec fill:#F5F3FF,stroke:#7C3AED style proc fill:#F5F3FF,stroke:#7C3AED style tra fill:#F5F3FF,stroke:#7C3AED style obs fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#D1D5DB,stroke-dasharray:4 3 click adl "../../../concepts/logging/#decision-records-adl" "Decision records" click ldv "../../../concepts/logging/#processing-records-ldv" "Processing records" click tx "../../components/#level-2-fsc-group" "FSC group"

Figure 1: The three authoritative records and the observability stores. Thick border: click to zoom in.

Each record answers one question:

Record Standard Question it answers Writer Store in the demo Decision Authorization Decision Log (ADL) Which decision did the PDP take on this request or contract? The PDP Postgres database ftv_adl Processing Logboek Dataverwerkingen (LDV) 1.0.0 Which organization processed which personal data, for which activity? Each component, in the logbook of its own controller One logbook per controller Transport FSC-Logging (draft) Which FSC transaction took place between which peers? FSC Inway and Outway Transaction log per FSC peer

A PDP decision is not a processing, so it gets no LDV record. On the DvTP path, the LDV records are at three processings:

  • The consent status lookup at the register.
  • The decryption at the source gateway.
  • The query at the source.

Traces and logs are for debugging. They are sampled or best effort, and nobody cites them as evidence (REQ-32). The console decision log of the policy engine goes to Loki. It holds the rule per field and the step trace. The developer portal shows it as detail next to the ADL record. The portal sets the color of the PDP from the ADL record alone (ADR-0036).

docs.title: One request leaving its trail
docs.text:
For one DvTP query, every component on the path writes its own record. The following figure shows which identifier lands in which record:

sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(241,239,232) Consumer participant C as Consumer backend participant OW as Consumer Outway end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis at the source participant IN as FSC Inway (PEP) participant PDP as PDP participant GW as Source gateway end box rgb(254,220,216) DvTP participant CR as Consent register end box rgb(237,233,254) Records participant TX as FSC txlogs participant ADL as ADL participant LDV as LDV logbooks end C->>OW: query, traceparent T, Fsc-Transaction-Id X1 OW->>TX: transaction X1 OW->>IN: mTLS, T, X1 IN->>TX: transaction X1 IN->>PDP: AuthZEN on a fresh context (no T, no X1) PDP->>CR: status lookup with T and X1 CR->>LDV: consent logbook: lookup, trace T PDP->>ADL: decision, random trace, request headers stored PDP-->>IN: allow IN->>GW: the judged request, T GW->>LDV: source logbook: decryption, trace T Note over GW: the source API logs<br/>the query under T as well GW-->>C: only the selected fields C->>LDV: consumer logbook: under consent ID, trace T

Figure 2: The trail of one DvTP query. The runtime page DvTP query has every hop.

Two identifiers link the records (REQ-55, ADR-0035):

W3C trace ID Fsc-Transaction-Id Made by The application that starts the processing The FSC Outway, or the entry component Count per processing One One per FSC transaction Recorded in LDV trace_id, ADL trace_id, spans, logs FSC txlog, ADL adl.fsc.transaction_id, span attribute gbo.fsc.transaction_id

Every component takes the trace ID unchanged from the incoming traceparent and sends it on every outbound call. The transaction ID never replaces an incoming trace. The earlier rule "trace ID equals transaction ID" broke for a caller with its own trace, for one processing over several sources, and at every extra FSC hop (F-67).

The Inway copies the headers of the request into the AuthZEN context. From there, the policy sends T and X1 on the status lookup. As a result, the record of the register lands in the trace of the request.

docs.title: Decision records (ADL)
docs.text:
The PDP writes one ADL record for each evaluation, contract decisions included (REQ-71). The PDP does not start without the database ftv_adl, so the ADL runs in every deployment profile. A reader gets the SELECT-only role adl_reader.

The record holds the AuthZEN request and the answer {allow, reason}. By design, the Inway returns that reason to the consumer, so per-field detail cannot go into the answer. The record therefore holds only what the consumer can also see. The FSC Inway of demo v0.9.0 drops the reason on the way back (F-72).

docs.title: Records per controller (LDV)
docs.text:
Every GBO-delivered component that processes personal data writes one LDV record per processing and per data subject. It writes to the logbook of its own controller (REQ-72, ADR-0026). Only trace metadata crosses an organization boundary, so the demo runs one logbook image as seven logbooks:

Logbook Controller Writers logboek-bd Belastingdienst bron-sidecar, graphql-server logboek-brp RvIG brp-sidecar, brp-graphql-server logboek-lvg LVG lvg-sidecar, lvg-graphql-server logboek-toestemming GBO consent facility (toestemmingsvoorziening) consent-register, consent-portal-backend logboek-eudi-adapter GBO issuance facility eudi-adapter logboek-afnemer Hypotheek-BV (demo consumer) dienstverlener-backend, integrator-backend logboek-ir Installatie Register (demo consumer) ir-backend

In production, each controller runs its own logbook, and GBO ships the LDV client. Each record carries the trace context, a versioned processing activity, and the data subject in the own pseudonym space of the controller. If the component calls another party, the record also points to the read API of that party in dpl.read.nextLogbookId.

Three properties make the records reliable:

  • Durable first, delivered after. A component stores the record in a local outbox, with an fsync, before its response leaves. It delivers the record afterwards with retries. A logbook outage delays records and does not fail requests. If the component cannot store the record locally, it refuses the processing.
  • No BSN. The logbook scans every write for a nine-digit run that passes the BSN check digit test (elfproef), and refuses a match. The check is word-bounded, so a 20-digit OIN passes.
  • Separate tokens. A component that can write cannot read with that token.

In demo v0.9.0, the ASIP writes no LDV records, although it processes personal data.

docs.title: How to read a chain
docs.text:
A read starts at the application that started the processing. From there, a reader follows nextLogbookId. The LDV read extension selects records by trace ID, processing activity, or data subject:

sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(241,239,232) Reader participant R as Reader end box rgb(237,233,254) Records participant LA as Consumer logbook participant LS as Source logbook participant TX as FSC txlogs participant ADL as ADL participant LT as Consent logbook end R->>LA: read trace ID T LA-->>R: record with nextLogbookId = source and X1 R->>LS: read trace ID T LS-->>R: gateway and source records R->>TX: read transaction X1 TX-->>R: transport records R->>ADL: SELECT on X1 in the stored request headers ADL-->>R: decision record Note over R,LT: no record points here (Q-25) R->>LT: read trace ID T LT-->>R: status lookup record

Figure 3: Reading the chain of one DvTP query.

Two gaps limit this route (F-68):

  • The chain starts at a party that LDV does not bind. In DvTP, a private consumer starts the processing. Without its records, nobody knows which sources one processing touched. The consumer logs under the consent ID, because it has no citizen identifier (Q-27).
  • No pointer leads from the decision to the consent logbook. The ADL has no field like nextLogbookId. The demo applies option 3 of Q-25: a reader calls the consent logbook by trace ID.

The register records form a second index over the chain. Every source call leads to a status lookup, and the register logs it with trace ID and consent ID.

docs.title: Gaps in demo v0.9.0
docs.text:
The records have these known gaps:

Gap Effect Link ADL behind the Inway is not correlated The Inway sends neither traceparent nor Fsc-Transaction-Id to the PDP. The record gets a random trace and no transaction ID. A reader finds it through the stored request headers. The fix is upstream in open-fsc #369 No policy version The records carry policies: 0. A reader cannot see which policy decided REQ-59 Only {allow, reason} The record lacks the consent status answer and the configuration. Nobody can replay a decision from it F-72 BSN in the decision logs In the EUDI and ASI routes, the ADL and the console log hold the plain BSN. Neither masks it REQ-60, ADR-0043 (proposed) A chain reads forward only The read starts at the consumer, and no pointer leads to the consent logbook F-68

No record type has tamper evidence or a retention period in demo v0.9.0. Who can read which records, and how long they are kept, is open (Q-08).

docs.title: Compared with the Globaal Ontwerp
docs.text:
The Globaal Ontwerp names the three standards and leaves their use in GBO open. The demo fills it in as follows:

Topic Globaal Ontwerp Demo v0.9.0 Standards FSC-Logging, LDV and ADL are available. The GBO use is open One authoritative record per standard (ADR-0036, ADR-0026) Chain-wide traceability Agreements still to make The W3C trace ID is the join key, with the transaction ID next to it (ADR-0035) Link with the authorization chain Still to make The PDP writes the ADL. The record is not correlated behind the Inway, and it has no pointer to the consent logbook

docs.title: Open points
docs.text:
The main open points in the records are these:

  • The decision record holds only what the consumer also sees, so a decision cannot be replayed (F-72).
  • A chain read goes forward only and starts at a party that LDV does not bind (F-68).
  • Masking in the policy engine has no effect, and the BSN is in the decision logs of the EUDI and ASI routes (F-54).
  • How a reader finds the step from the decision to the consent logbook (Q-25).
  • Read access and retention of the records (Q-08).

docs.title: Traceability
docs.text:
• Requirements: REQ-32, REQ-55, REQ-59, REQ-60, REQ-71, REQ-72
  • Findings: F-54 (open), F-67 (resolved in demo), F-68 (open), F-72 (open)
  • Open questions: Q-08 (open), Q-25 (open), Q-27 (open)
  • Demo increments: SL-38 (done), SL-50 (done), SL-51 (done)

docs.title: Generic source access
docs.text:
The Globaal Ontwerp calls this part "generieke bronontsluiting", which means generic source access. It is the path behind the PEP: after the PDP allows a request, the source gateway passes it to the source API. Under consent, the gateway first puts the citizen into the query. The source answers one GraphQL query and returns only the fields that the query selects. The Pseudonymization and Authorization concept pages have the detail and the links to the code.

Overview › GBO Basis › Generic source access

docs.title: Components behind the PEP
docs.text:
flowchart LR out["Outway of<br/>the caller"] subgraph bh["At the bronhouder"] direction LR pep("FSC Inway<br/>PEP") subgraph pdpg["PDP"] direction TB pdp("Mapper + policy") copy[("Schema copy<br/>and pins")] end subgraph acc["Generic source access"] direction TB gw("Source gateway<br/>bron-sidecar") dec("Decryption<br/>component") end api[("Source API<br/>GraphQL")] log[("LDV logbook<br/>of the source")] end out -- "request + raw body" --> pep pep -- "AuthZEN" --> pdp pdp --- copy pep -- "only after allow" --> gw gw -- "own value" --> dec gw -- "judged query" --> api gw -.-> log api -.-> log %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class out ext class pep,pdp,gw,dec basis class copy,log store class api source class pdp,copy,gw,dec zoom style bh fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#6F94B8,stroke-dasharray:4 3 style pdpg fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#16A34A style acc fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#16A34A click pdp "../authorization/" "Authorization" click copy "#the-pdp-copy-of-the-schema" "Schema copy" click gw "#placeholder-substitution-under-consent" "Substitution" click dec "../../../concepts/pseudonymization/#where-the-boundary-is-enforced" "Pseudonymization"

Figure 1: The components of generic source access at one source. Thick border: click to zoom in.

Each component has one job:

Component Job Never does Source gateway Accepts only the request shape that the PDP judged. Under consent, it replaces the placeholder with the own value of the source. Without consent, it passes the query on unchanged. Verifies the consent proof again, or forwards a literal subject under a consent proof Decryption component Reads a VI or a VP with the keys of the source. Calls BSNk or another service at query time (REQ-21) Source API Runs the GraphQL query and logs the processing in the LDV logbook of its controller. Returns a field that the query did not select (REQ-08) Schema copy and pins One copy of the source schema per FSC service, so the PDP can resolve each field. The policy bundle pins its digest. Changes without a new policy bundle

The source gateway belongs to the source, and each source has its own instance. It sits between the Inway and the API (ADR-0033). The gateway writes two LDV records: one for the decryption and one for the query that it forwards. The answer goes back to the caller through the Inway. A GBO-delivered channel component calls the source again for each request and does not store the answer (REQ-11).

docs.title: The transport subset
docs.text:
The PDP judges one form of request. The source gateway accepts only that form, so a request that the PDP never judged cannot run. In demo v0.9.0, the gateway refuses a request in these cases:

Request Answer of the gateway Path other than /graphql 404 Method other than POST 405 A query string 400 A Content-Type that the mapper does not accept 415 An Upgrade or Content-Encoding header 400

The path check compares the raw request target byte for byte. It does not clean or decode the path (transport.go). The PDP refuses the same forms. The second check at the gateway covers a request that reaches the gateway by another route.

docs.title: Placeholder substitution under consent
docs.text:
Under consent, the consumer does not know who the citizen is. Its query names the citizen with a fixed placeholder. The gateway fills in the citizen after the allow:

sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(241,239,232) Consumer participant DV as Service provider end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis at the source participant IN as FSC Inway (PEP) participant PDP as PDP participant GW as Source gateway participant DEC as Decryption component end box rgb(221,235,247) Source participant API as Source API end box rgb(237,233,254) Records participant L as LDV logbook end DV->>IN: query with consent:identity + consent proof IN->>PDP: AuthZEN question with the raw body Note over PDP: proof valid, subject is<br/>the placeholder, fields allowed PDP-->>IN: allow IN->>GW: the judged request Note over GW: transport subset,<br/>take encrypted_subject[own OIN] GW->>DEC: VI (identity) or VP (pseudonym) DEC-->>GW: BSN or own pseudonym, with the recipient alt recipient is not the own OIN, value missing, or literal subject GW-->>DV: refused, nothing reaches the source else recipient matches Note over GW: replace the placeholder<br/>in the query variables GW->>L: record: decryption GW->>API: query with the BSN API->>L: record: query API-->>DV: only the selected fields end

Figure 2: Substitution of the placeholder after the allow. The runtime page DvTP query has every hop.

The query names the form that the source API takes. Each placeholder maps to one value in the consent proof:

Placeholder Value in the proof Becomes Who gets the value consent:identity VI, encrypted_subject[<OIN>].identity The BSN Only a source on the BSN authorization list consent:pseudonym VP, encrypted_subject[<OIN>].pseudonym The own pseudonym of the source Every source

Under a consent, the subject comes only from the proof (REQ-79). The gateway takes only the value for its own OIN. It accepts the result only if the decrypted value names that OIN as the recipient (REQ-80). The key in the proof is not evidence. The value that BSNk made is the evidence.

The gateway refuses the request in three cases, and the request goes no further:

  • The proof has no value in the requested form, for example no VI for a source that is not on the BSN authorization list.
  • The decrypted value names another recipient.
  • The query names the subject with a literal value under a consent proof.

Substitution works only on query variables. If the query text holds a literal placeholder, the PDP allows it, the gateway leaves it, and the query finds nobody. In demo v0.9.0, no rule accepts consent:pseudonym, and no source API answers on a pseudonym (#474).

docs.title: Pass-through without consent
docs.text:
The evidence decides what the gateway does, as it decides the regime at the PDP. The gateway reads no grant property:

Evidence in the request Regime at the PDP Gateway Consent proof, subject is a placeholder Consent Decrypts its own value and replaces the placeholder Consent proof, subject is a literal value Consent Refuses: the PDP denies this, so it arrives only by another route No consent proof PID Passes the query on unchanged

The EUDI adapter and the ASIP send no consent proof. They put the BSN from the PID or from the access token in the query variables themselves. As a result, the BSN is in the PDP input and in both decision logs (REQ-60). The proposed fix keeps identifiers out of the PDP input (ADR-0043).

docs.title: Network isolation is the control
docs.text:
The gateway does not verify the consent proof again. The PDP verified it on the same request, and a consumer holds real proofs. So the rule "only after the decision" depends on one thing: nothing but the Inway reaches the gateway (REQ-81):

flowchart LR out["Outway of<br/>a consumer"] subgraph sg["Network source-gateways"] direction TB pep("FSC Inway<br/>PEP") gw("Source gateway<br/>no published port") end subgraph src["Network sources"] direction TB dec("Decryption<br/>component") api[("Source API")] log[("Source logbook")] end subgraph other["Networks backend and fsc-infra"] direction TB meta("FSC metadata<br/>service") any["Other<br/>containers"] end out -- "mTLS" --> pep pep -- "after allow" --> gw gw --> dec gw --> api gw -.-> log meta -. "direct, demo limit" .-> api any -. "can reach the API,<br/>demo limit" .-> api %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class out,any ext class pep,gw,dec,meta basis class api source class log store class gw zoom style sg fill:#F0FDF4,stroke:#16A34A style src fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#6F94B8 style other fill:#FFF1F0,stroke:#E28F80,stroke-dasharray:4 3 click gw "../../../deployment/#deployment-units-and-network-zones" "Network zones"

Figure 3: Network zones around the source gateway in demo v0.9.0. Red: the limits of the isolation.

In the demo, the gateways publish no port. They are on two Docker networks only. The source Inways share source-gateways with them. The source APIs, the decryption component, and the source logbooks share sources. No consumer is on either network.

The isolation has three limits (F-79):

  • The source APIs are also on backend and fsc-infra, because the FSC metadata services point at them directly. A container on those networks can reach a source API without the PDP.
  • The Helm chart has no NetworkPolicy. A Kubernetes deployment needs one, or an equivalent control.
  • A nonce that binds a value to one consent, as a second line, is not built.

docs.title: The PDP copy of the schema
docs.text:
The source owns its GraphQL schema. The PDP needs the schema to give each field its parent type. So the PDP keeps its own copy, and three controls keep the judged request equal to the executed request:

flowchart LR subgraph srcs["Source"] s[("Source schema<br/>owned by the source")] end subgraph bundle["Policy bundle"] direction TB m[("PDP copy<br/>one per FSC service")] p[("Schema pins<br/>graphql_schemas.rego")] end subgraph pdpg["PDP"] direction TB map("Mapper<br/>parent types") eng("Engine<br/>pin check") end no(["Deny<br/>SCHEMA_MISMATCH"]) s -- "CI drift check<br/>check-schema-drift.sh" --- m m -- "gen-graphql-pins.sh" --> p m -- "resolve fields" --> map p -- "pinned digests" --> eng map --> eng eng -- "schema not pinned" --> no %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class s source class m,p store class map,eng basis class no dvtp class map zoom style bundle fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#16A34A style pdpg fill:#F4F5F7,stroke:#16A34A style srcs fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#6F94B8,stroke-dasharray:4 3 click map "../../../concepts/authorization/#query-mapping-ftv-graphql-profile" "Query mapping"

Figure 4: The PDP copy of the schema, the pins, and the drift check.

The three controls work as follows:

Control What it does Where Schema pins The policy bundle pins the digest of each copy. An evaluation against a schema that is not pinned gets CONFIG_ERROR SCHEMA_MISMATCH. graphql_schemas.rego Drift check A CI job compares each copy with the schema that the source runs. check-schema-drift.sh Transport subset The gateway runs only the request form that the PDP judged. The transport subset

The copy has no directives. In demo v0.9.0, the copies are bd.graphql for bri, eudi/brp.graphql for brp, and lvg.graphql for lvg. The year selector is an argument in the schema. As a result, the PDP can check consent per year. A change to a source schema needs a new copy, new pins, and a new policy bundle.

docs.title: Invariants that stay at the source
docs.text:
Some rules depend on data that only the source sees. The PDP cannot check them, so the source holds them and their tests.

The death certificate (akte van overlijden) is the example in the demo. A surviving partner discloses her own PID and gets an attestation about her deceased partner. The BRP source offers the flat view akteVanOverlijden(bsn). The source picks the marriage and the deceased partner. The PDP sees only the output fields of the view (F-47).

REQ-57 asks for more. The source records the relation in its service description, and the reference policy denies another entry point. A filter that the schema cannot express stays a tested invariant of the source. The test for the death certificate is not built (#425).

docs.title: Three demo sources
docs.text:
Demo v0.9.0 has three sources. Each source has its own API, its own gateway, and its own logbook:

FSC service Source Offers Rules Logbook bri Belastingdienst profile (graphql-server, bron-sidecar) Income declarations per year DVT0001, EUD0001 logboek-bd brp BRP profile of RvIG (brp-graphql-server, brp-sidecar) Personal record (persoonslijst) and the death certificate view EUD0002, ASI0001 logboek-brp lvg LVG mock (lvg-graphql-server, lvg-sidecar) The ownership check vbo(bsn, vboId) { vboId } LVG0001 logboek-lvg

The demo takes two shortcuts in this part:

  • The three sources share one decryption component.
  • The three sources share one OIN.

Production needs one decryption component per source, each with its own OIN. Because of the shortcuts, the demo cannot show that the values of two sources are not linkable.

docs.title: Compared with the Globaal Ontwerp
docs.text:
The demo follows the Globaal Ontwerp in the use of GraphQL for selective queries. It differs in three places:

Topic Globaal Ontwerp Demo v0.9.0 Allowed queries A service catalog (dienstencatalogus) lists the allowed queries per application The rules are the catalog: a field that no rule names is denied (ADR-0009) Source without GraphQL A GBO translation layer turns an existing API into a GraphQL source Not built. All three sources run GraphQL (ADR-0027, proposed) From proof to BSN BSNk PP keeps the BSN away from the private service provider (dienstverlener) The same, and the source gateway converts its own value after the allow. BSNk is not in the query path

docs.title: Open points
docs.text:
The main open points in generic source access are these:

  • The isolation of the gateway outside Docker Compose, and a nonce as a second line (F-79).
  • The PDP checks that the subject comes from the proof. It does not check who the subject is (F-77).
  • A relation to another person stays an invariant of the source that the policy cannot check (F-47).
  • In the PID regime, the BSN is in the PDP input and in both decision logs (F-54).
  • How the PDP models fields, recursion, and arguments for future sources (Q-14).

docs.text:
• Requirements: REQ-08, REQ-11, REQ-21, REQ-57, REQ-60, REQ-79, REQ-80, REQ-81

  • Open questions: Q-14 (open)

docs.title: Source configuration
docs.text:
The Globaal Ontwerp gives each bronhouder a decentral configuration component ("decentraal configuratiecomponent"): the source configures what the central GBO facilities offer for it. In the demo, the source describes its own services in one document. GBO validates that description and activates it as an immutable release. The EUDI adapter, the issuance server and the ASIP read only the active release. The Source onboarding concept page has the detail and the links to the code.

Each component has one job:

The nl-wallet issuance server reads its configuration only at start. A new release therefore needs a controlled restart of that server.

docs.title: Who owns what
docs.text:
Four parties own a part of the description of one source. GBO never adds to the part of the bronhouder (REQ-64):

Figure 2: The owners of the parts that describe one source.

The source file is small. This is the file for the Belastingdienst in demo v0.9.0:

metadata_endpoint:
  transport: fsc
  provider_peer_id: "99999999900000000200"
  service_reference: gbo-metadata-bd

The file name is the stable source_id. The legal identity comes from the certificate set under the same key: the OIN from serialNumber and the name from O. GBO refuses a configured value that differs (REQ-67). The data service and the grant hash come from the document and from the FSC contracts in force.

A source has a metadata leg and a data leg. Each leg selects one of three transports:

Transport Metadata leg Data leg Use fsc Fixed path /.well-known/gbo, through a separate FSC metadata service The data service in the document, under its contract The intended form file A document in the metadata directory of the operator Not possible: a file cannot answer a query A source without its own endpoint, as a temporary exception that needs the agreement of the bronhouder (AV-08) unsecured An absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL, without FSC headers or redirects An absolute URL Local demonstrations only

The reconciler refuses fsc metadata with unsecured data. The registry reports one authentication flag per leg. With one flag for both legs, an FSC data call can hide that its description came over an unauthenticated channel.

docs.title: Lifecycle of a source
docs.text:
Every reconcile run takes each configured source through the same states. A source fails or ages on its own, without effect on the other sources:

stateDiagram-v2 direction LR [*] --> pending: run starts,<br/>certificate set found pending --> active: candidate equals<br/>the active release pending --> rollout_required: new valid candidate rollout_required --> active: operator promotes,<br/>immutable release pending --> stale: refresh fails,<br/>previous candidate in grace pending --> blocked: no usable candidate,<br/>or grace over [*] --> blocked: certificate set<br/>missing or invalid classDef ok fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef wait fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef stop fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B class active ok class pending,rollout_required,stale wait class blocked stop

Figure 3: The states of a source per reconcile run. The next run starts again at pending.

The run has these steps:

  1. The reconciler loads the certificate set of the source. Without a valid set, the source is blocked before any network call.
  2. For the fsc transport, the reconciler finds the metadata contract and the data contract of the configured peer in the FSC Manager.
  3. It fetches the document with ETag and If-None-Match. A 304 only extends the freshness. It validates every 200 in full.
  4. A valid result becomes a complete candidate. If the candidate differs from the active release, the state is rollout_required.
  5. Promotion writes one release from the complete candidate set. The SHA-256 of the content identifies the release, and the release never changes.
  6. In the same database transaction, promotion sets the singleton active_release_id. If promotion fails, the previous release stays active.
  7. The readers poll the active pointer and swap the new release in memory.

In the demo, the reconciler promotes by itself (--auto-promote). Automatic promotion is off by default. Compose and the Helm example turn it on, and then the source file is the management action.

docs.title: A contract is not activation
docs.text:
A valid FSC contract does not take a source into use. It also does not put the offer of the source in the wallet (REQ-65, F-58). Transport and mandate are two decisions with two owners. Each situation has a fixed result:

Situation Result Valid metadata contract, no source file Nothing happens Source file, no metadata contract blocked: METADATA_CONTRACT_NOT_FOUND Source file, no contract for the data service blocked: DATA_CONTRACT_NOT_FOUND FSC Manager unreachable FSC_MANAGER_UNAVAILABLE. The candidate stays within grace Valid candidate without promotion Not active

Demo v0.9.0 does not build two things. No control decides who can add a source file. No record keeps the admission decision (REQ-123, PSA B-09 in the decision register).

docs.title: Freshness, versions and rollback
docs.text:
Source metadata fails closed for each source, ages within fixed bounds, and can be rolled back (REQ-66). The bounds in demo v0.9.0 are these:

Bound Value Fresh after a successful check 15 minutes at most Stale grace after that One hour at most Validity left at acceptance At least one hour Answer for a source past its grace HTTP 503, for that source only

The issuance route shows X-GBO-Metadata-Cache: fresh or stale. The versioning rules are these:

  • Activation refuses a lower version than the last validated candidate. It also refuses the same version with other content. This rule has no test (#610).
  • A change to claims or display needs a new type_version, because vct#integrity covers the exact bytes of the Type Metadata. GBO never deletes a published type version automatically.
  • An operator rolls back with activate-source-release --release-id. The command refuses a release that the adapter cannot load. An auto-promoter keeps the rollback until new content arrives.

Demo v0.9.0 has two deviations from the isolation rule (#606). Promotion needs a valid version of every configured source, so one broken source freezes new releases for all sources. The offer list /eudi-offers.json takes the shortest grace of all sources, so it fails for all sources at the same time.

Policy bundles do not have this lifecycle of validation, bounded staleness, atomic promotion and rollback (F-59). For the policy side, see Policy rules and their management.

docs.title: A certificate set per source
docs.text:
Every source has its own certificate set for issuance: an issuer, a reader and a status-list certificate. GBO never shares a set between sources and never substitutes one (REQ-58). The wallet shows the issuer name and the purpose from these certificates. A fallback to the set of another source made the wallet show the wrong issuer (F-50).

Missing material fails for that source only. Without a set, the source is blocked with CERTIFICATE_SET_NOT_FOUND. A set without an OIN or an organization name gives CERTIFICATE_SET_INVALID. The reconciler gets only public certificates. Only the issuance init container gets the private keys.

docs.title: The source document
docs.text:
The document is closed JSON, validated against gbo-source-metadata-v1. Validation refuses unknown fields:

"derives" .-> gen %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class doc,env,e,a,t,o,q,c,as,aq,at source class gen eudi

Figure 4: The structure of the source document.

A new attestation type, offer or tax year is a change in the document. It needs no change in GBO code, because the adapter takes its parameters from the source (Q-19).

The eudi capability defines each claim once. GBO derives the mapping and generates the SD-JWT VC Type Metadata from display and claims. As a result, the schema of an attestation cannot differ from what the mapping fills. The VCT of a type version is /types/{source-id}/{type-id}/v{type-version}.

The asi capability describes the attributes that the ASIP can verify (ADR-0039). Each identifier must exist in the attribute catalog of GBO. If asi has an error, onboarding refuses the whole source, also when eudi is valid. How many sources the ASIP must connect, and how fast, is open (Q-38).

The document does not hold the GraphQL schema: the PDP keeps its own copy. It also holds no access decision: the rules decide which fields a channel gets. The source does not sign the document. Its origin rests on the authenticated FSC transport and the OIN in the certificate set.

docs.title: Compared with the Globaal Ontwerp
docs.text:
The demo follows the idea of the Globaal Ontwerp: the bronhouder configures, and the central facilities read that configuration. It differs in three places:

Topic Globaal Ontwerp Demo v0.9.0 Form of the configuration A decentral configuration component at the bronhouder One closed JSON document per source at /.well-known/gbo, a proposal for PSA S10 (ADR-0016) Findability A service catalog (dienstencatalogus) with a shared profile and central findability, based on DCAT-AP-NL No central findability and no DCAT-AP-NL reference (F-57) Channels Every channel reads the configuration EUDI and ASI read it. DvTP does not: the GBO rules hold the DvTP offer (F-74)

docs.title: Open points
docs.text:
The main open points in source configuration are these:

  • The description lacks the read API of the logbook of the source, a DCAT-AP-NL reference and central findability (F-57).
  • The file transport has no recorded agreement of the bronhouder (F-71).
  • DvTP scope comes from the demand side and EUDI scope from the supply side (F-74).
  • The central issuance server holds the private keys of every source (Q-17).
  • The ASI attribute identifiers are placeholders until the EU catalog of attributes exists (Q-31).

docs.title: Traceability
docs.text:
• Requirements: REQ-58, REQ-64, REQ-65, REQ-66, REQ-67, REQ-123, AV-08
  • Findings: F-50 (closed), F-57 (open), F-58 (closed), F-59 (closed), F-71 (open), F-74 (open)
  • Open questions: Q-17 (open), Q-19 (answered), Q-31 (open), Q-38 (partly answered)
  • Demo increments: SL-32 (done), SL-46 (done), SL-49 (done)

docs.title: Authorization
docs.text:
GBO authorizes every data request with policy-based access control. A policy engine decides, and the FSC Inway of the source enforces the decision. The authorization model on this page is the model that gbo-demo v0.9.0 builds. The model realizes capability S05.

The model follows from seven architecture decisions:

  • ADR-0002: OPA/Rego in OpenFTV, the FSC Inway as PEP, and AuthZEN with the FTV GraphQL profile.
  • ADR-0004: five concerns, federated evaluation, and no central authorization server.
  • ADR-0009: closed-world rules, bound by regime and service.
  • ADR-0013: the request mapper only maps.
  • ADR-0015: FSC contract acceptance by policy.
  • ADR-0031: the regime follows from the evidence.
  • ADR-0032: the policy verifies the consent proof.

For the consent proof, see Consent. For how the source fills in the citizen after the decision, see Pseudonymization. For how policy gets to the PDP, see Policy lifecycle.

docs.title: Five concerns
docs.text:
Authorization answers five separate questions. Each question has its own decision maker, protocol, and moment. Each concern has its own enforcement point:

# Concern Question Enforced by ① Organization identity Is this a legitimate organization? mTLS with PKIoverheid certificates at every FSC connection (Identity and trust) ② Organization permission Can this organization use this service? FSC contract and access token, issued by the FSC Manager of the provider. Contract acceptance is a policy decision on the admission register (Admission and contract acceptance) ③ Access basis Is there a consent, or a verified PID of the citizen? PDP policy: the regime follows from the evidence (Regime selection). The policy verifies the consent proof and gets the status online (Consent verification in policy). The design has a Gov-to-Gov regime on a legal basis. Demo v0.9.0 does not build it ④ Data scope Which fields, records, and years can the source return? PDP policy: per-field rules, the subject placeholder, and the year filter (Rule model) ⑤ Request validity Is the request well-formed and complete? Request mapper: FTV GraphQL profile, limits, and schema pins (Query mapping). The source gateway accepts only the judged request shape. Demo v0.9.0 does not build rate limiting (Risks)

No central authorization server exists. Concerns ① and ② are in the FSC layer, federated per organization. The PDP of the source evaluates concerns ③ to ⑤ for each request. With the integrator path, concern ② also has a part at request time: the mandate check (ADR-0034).

docs.text:
