A private consumer SHOULD record its processing according to LDV, with dpl.read.nextLogbookId for each call to a source.

  • Status: candidate
Source, evidence and notes
  • Obliged party: private consumer
  • Channel: DvTP
  • Source: the LDV read extension (the chain starts at the application that started the processing), F-68, and Q-24 option 3. The demo does this (PR #366).
  • Related: REQ-72, REQ-75
  • Notes: LDV does not bind private parties itself. The chain-wide starting point can also come from the records of the register (REQ-75).

docs.title: AV-03: Consumer uses the consent facility and BSNk PP
docs.text:
A private consumer that takes part in DvTP SHOULD use the central consent function and BSNk PP.

  • Status: candidate, already in the GO
Source, evidence and notes
  • Obliged party: private consumer
  • Channel: DvTP
  • Source: the table of facilities in the GO (section 5). A participating private service provider (dienstverlener) must use the consent facility (toestemmingsvoorziening) and BSNk PP, and must meet the connection conditions: "Een private dienstverlener die deelneemt, moet de toestemmingsvoorziening en BSNk PP gebruiken en aan de aansluitvoorwaarden voldoen."

docs.title: AV-04: Consumer has its own FSC peer with PKIoverheid certificate and OIN
docs.text:
A private consumer SHOULD connect with its own FSC peer, with a PKIoverheid certificate, and SHOULD use the OIN as its legal identity.

  • Status: candidate
Source, evidence and notes
  • Obliged party: private consumer
  • Channel: DvTP
  • Source: FR-33 and FR-34 (v0.9), the GO (S04 building blocks PKIoverheid and OIN), Q-06, and Q-07.
  • Related: REQ-67
  • Notes: FR-33 (v0.9) allows an OIN or a KvK number. The link between identifiers is an open decision in S04.

docs.title: AV-05: Consumer sends the consent proof unchanged
docs.text:
A private consumer SHOULD send the consent proof unchanged, including the identifier of the citizen as it is in the proof.

  • Status: candidate, depends on the outcome of #377
Source, evidence and notes
  • Obliged party: private consumer
  • Channel: DvTP
  • Source: REQ-68 (the policy binds the query subject to the proof). With a real BSNk, a PI is randomized. So only the exact value binds (ICTU/GBO-demo#377, consequence 1).
  • Related: REQ-68, REQ-80
  • Notes: from demo increment SL-51 on, the proof carries an encrypted value for each source (REQ-80). The query names the subject only with a placeholder.

docs.title: AV-06: Integrator is admitted separately and acts as processor
docs.text:
An integrator SHOULD be admitted separately, with its own organization identity means. It SHOULD have a processing agreement with the service provider, and SHOULD NOT store personal data persistently. It SHOULD have a registration for each service provider and use case.

  • Status: candidate
Source, evidence and notes
  • Obliged party: integrator
  • Channel: DvTP
  • Source:
    • FR-18 and FR-37 (v0.9).
    • PSA S04 and PSA S05, B-19.
    • F-73.
    • ICTU/GBO-demo#379.
  • Related: REQ-106 (the technical side: binding and mandate), REQ-61, ADR 0034

docs.title: AV-07: Bronhouder publishes a machine-readable description for each data service
docs.text:
A bronhouder SHOULD publish a machine-readable and versionable description at the fixed location. It SHOULD publish one for each data service and for every data flow in which it offers that service. The description contains the schema and its version, a reference to the concept framework, the error messages, and the availability properties. It also contains quality properties and provenance information. It also holds the mappings that the bronhouder fixes for that flow, and the URL of the LDV read API of its logbook. Where possible, the description SHOULD refer to managed objects (the service in the catalog, the schema, the mapping) instead of repeating them.

  • Status: candidate
Source, evidence and notes
  • Obliged party: bronhouder
  • Channel: all channels
  • Source:
    • PSA S07 (published information describes schemas, versions, error messages, and availability properties: "gepubliceerde informatie beschrijft schema's, versies, foutmeldingen en beschikbaarheidskenmerken").
    • PSA S10 (a reference to a managed schema and concept framework, a machine-readable and versionable form, quality properties and provenance information, and references to managed objects where possible: "verwijst naar een beheerd schema en begrippenkader", "machineleesbaar en versieerbaar", "kwaliteitskenmerken en herkomstinformatie", "verwijst waar mogelijk naar beheerde objecten").
    • F-68.
  • Related: REQ-64
  • Notes: the candidate applies to every data flow: DvTP, EUDI issuance, ASI, and OOTS.

docs.title: AV-08: Bronhouder without its own endpoint provably agrees with a taken-over description
docs.text:
A bronhouder that publishes no metadata endpoint of its own SHOULD provably agree with the service description that the operator keeps on its behalf.

  • Status: candidate
Source, evidence and notes
  • Obliged party: bronhouder
  • Channel: EUDI
  • Source: F-71 and the exception in REQ-64.
  • Related: REQ-64

docs.title: AV-09: Bronhouder keeps decryption keys of an older version while proofs for that version are valid
docs.text:
A bronhouder SHOULD keep the keys with which it decrypts the values in a consent proof. It SHOULD keep a key version as long as valid proofs made with that key version exist.

  • Status: candidate
Source, evidence and notes
  • Obliged party: bronhouder
  • Channel: DvTP
  • Source: REQ-82 and BSNK-08 (an encrypted value belongs to one key version).
  • Related: REQ-82, F-78

docs.title: AV-10: Bronhouder logs every living data subject of a relation attestation
docs.text:
An attestation can hold data about someone other than the requester. For such an attestation, a bronhouder SHOULD record in its processing log every living data subject whose data it supplies. A record of the requester alone is not enough.

  • Status: candidate
Source, evidence and notes
  • Obliged party: bronhouder
  • Channel: EUDI
  • Source: REQ-57 and REQ-72.
  • Related: REQ-57, REQ-72

docs.title: AV-11: Bronhouder tests its view for relation attestations
docs.text:
A bronhouder can supply a relation (for example a marriage) through a view of its own. It SHOULD then prove with tests that this view returns only the relation of the identified citizen.

  • Status: candidate
Source, evidence and notes
  • Obliged party: bronhouder
  • Channel: EUDI
  • Source: REQ-57.
  • Related: REQ-57

docs.title: AV-12: Bronhouder as provider has a public validity and revocation policy
docs.text:
A bronhouder that has attestations issued SHOULD have a written and public policy for validity and revocation. It SHOULD publish the validity period for each attestation type in its configuration.

  • Status: candidate
Source, evidence and notes
  • Obliged party: bronhouder
  • Channel: EUDI
  • Source: Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1569, article 4(1), REQ-77, and REQ-64.
  • Related: REQ-77, REQ-64

docs.title: AV-13: Bronhouder gives the instruction to revoke an attestation
docs.text:
If the data in an issued attestation is no longer correct, a bronhouder SHOULD tell the issuance function that the attestation must be revoked.

  • Status: candidate
Source, evidence and notes
  • Obliged party: bronhouder
  • Channel: EUDI
  • Source: Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1569, article 4(2) and 4(3), and REQ-77.
  • Related: REQ-77, F-82
  • Notes: it is open who detects a change in the source: Q-17.

docs.title: AV-14: Consumer has registered contact details for GDPR rights
docs.text:
A private consumer SHOULD have contact details registered at its admission, where the citizen can exercise their GDPR rights. A consumer without those details SHOULD NOT be admitted.

  • Status: candidate
Source, evidence and notes
  • Obliged party: private consumer
  • Channel: DvTP
  • Source:
    • FR-25 criterion 2 (contact details recorded during onboarding or configuration: "vastgelegd tijdens onboarding/configuratie").
    • REQ-120 (the portal shows them with every consent and after a revocation).
    • Q-62 sub-question 2.
  • Related: REQ-120, REQ-61

docs.title: AV-15: Consumer declares an equivalent alternative at admission
docs.text:
At its admission, a private consumer SHOULD declare provably that it offers an equivalent alternative next to the digital consent route. It SHOULD also declare that a refusal of consent gives the citizen no disadvantage. It SHOULD describe that alternative so that the consent screen can name it.

  • Status: candidate
Source, evidence and notes
  • Obliged party: private consumer
  • Channel: DvTP
  • Source:
    • FR-36 criteria 1 and 2.
    • PSA S02 (the setup offers an equivalent alternative if law or policy requires it: "de inrichting biedt een gelijkwaardig alternatief als wetgeving of beleid dat vereist").
    • REQ-117 (the screen names the alternative).
    • Q-62 sub-question 3.
  • Related: REQ-117

docs.title: Authentic Source Interface requirements
docs.text:
In the Authentic Source Interface (ASI) route, a qualified trust service provider (QTSP) verifies or retrieves attributes of a citizen at an authentic source. The QTSP does this at the request of that citizen. eIDAS article 45e gives the QTSP this right. The Authentic Source Interface Provider (ASIP) offers the interface. Its authorization server admits QTSPs and lets the citizen approve each request.

The interface follows ETSI TS 119 478 V1.1.1, clause 6.1. Article 9 of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1569 and Annex IV of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1735 make clause 6.1.1 the legal interface for verification. Annex IV and the seal obligation of article 9(4) apply from January 1, 2027.

The requirements on the ASIP and its authorization server cover these topics:

  • the verify and retrieve interface
  • the seal
  • the authorization server
  • the admission of QTSPs
  • the request page with citizen identification
  • the chain behind the ASIP, with one data service per source
  • discovery

F-80 describes the legal frame. F-84 to F-89 describe the open design choices.

Evidence links to gbo-demo point at two versions. A link at v0.9.0 shows the code of demo v0.9.0. A link at commit 819f3eb shows the code at the time of the review of the requirement. Use that link as historical evidence, because the file changed or moved after that commit.

docs.title: GBO profile on ETSI TS 119 478
docs.text:
The specification for a Dutch ASIP is ETSI TS 119 478 V1.1.1, as Annex IV of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1735 adapts it (Implementing Regulation 2025/1569, article 9(2a)). The profile does not repeat that text. For each clause, the profile records two things:

  • what GBO chooses, adds, or interprets on top of ETSI
  • where that choice is recorded: in a requirement on this page, an open question, or a finding

A requirement that the profile does not name follows ETSI unchanged.

The profile is for the build of the ASIP and its authorization server. That build does not reuse the code of the demo ASIP. The content for each requirement comes from two documents of the demo: the conformance matrix (etsi-ts-119478.yaml) and the documentation of the ASI route (asi-route.md). If nobody decided on a choice of the demo, the profile records it as an open question and does not make it a requirement.

  • Source: design. The source is the line on ETSI TS 119 478 in the section on agreements and standards ("Afspraken en standaarden") of PSA S11. The profile fills the open point on PuB-EAA and ASI profiles ("PubEAA-/ASI-profielen") from the summary of S11. Matters about the ASI provider and its conditions belong to PSA open decision B-14.

docs.title: Categories
docs.text:
The profile puts each GBO choice in one of eight categories:

Code Meaning K a choice where ETSI leaves room N not applicable because of a GBO choice R requirements on a role outside the ASIP and its authorization server (DIP, TSP) A an addition: GBO requires something that ETSI does not specify I an interpretation, or a conflict in the text X applies, but depends on an external facility O applies to the operator and not to the software open no decision

docs.title: Per clause
docs.text:
For each ETSI clause, the profile gives the ETSI requirements, the category, the GBO choice, and where the choice is recorded:

Clause ETSI requirements Cat. GBO choice Recorded in 4.3 REQ-ASIP-4.3-04 K only the interface of clause 6.1 (HTTP, OAuth) REQ-112, Q-64 4.4, 6.2, Annex C REQ-AZP-4.4-02, REQ-ASIP-6.2.*, REQ-ASIP-C-01 N follows from REQ-112 REQ-112 4.3 REQ-ASIP-4.3-03 X a legitimate user and an entitled QTSP depend on the identification means and the register of relying parties REQ-88, REQ-102, Q-36 4.2 — A the ASIP queries the source through the chain, with one query per request, and the source judges that query REQ-92, Q-38 5 REQ-DIP-*, REQ-TSP-5.4-* R these requirements are for the common OOTS services of the Commission. How Dutch data services get there is open. Q-67 5.3 — A the ASIP publishes a dataService record for each attribute and data service REQ-99 5.3 — I the contract names the metadata of the authorization server. ETSI gives no field for it. REQ-100, Q-39, F-91 6.1.1.1 REQ-ASIP-6.1.1.1-06-01, -06-02-01 X attribute IDs and value schemas come from the EU catalogue of attributes. Until that catalogue exists, the source describes them. Q-38 6.1.1.1 REQ-ASIP-6.1.1.1-09 K the ASIP supports attribute fragments REQ-115 6.1.1.1 REQ-ASIP-6.1.1.1-10 K fuzzy matching only on text values, with published rules REQ-113, Q-70 6.1.1.1 REQ-ASIP-6.1.1.1-10-01 I conflicts with Annex IV, which makes the value optional REQ-85, Q-29, E2 6.1.1, 6.1.2 REQ-ASIP-6.1.1.1-11 to -13, -6.1.1.2-10, -11, -6.1.2.1-04, -6.1.2.2-05, -05-01 K a request on behalf of another person (mandate) gets 501 REQ-114, Q-65 6.1.1.2 REQ-ASIP-6.1.1.2-04 I Unknown means that the source has no value, or no complete value. ETSI takes precedence over the ARF. REQ-84 6.1.1.2 REQ-ASIP-6.1.1.2-04-01 to -03, -06-03, -06-04-* K no value in the response REQ-85, Q-29 6.1.1.2 REQ-ASIP-6.1.1.2-08, -6.1.2.2-04 I one authentic source per response, so one data service per source REQ-94, F-89 6.1.2.2 REQ-ASIP-6.1.2.2-02-01 I a retrieve without a value in the source gets 404 and no partial result REQ-101 6.1 — open synchronous processing only. ETSI has deferred responses only in clause 6.2. Q-64 6.1 — A a chain that does not answer gives 500 or 503 and never Unknown REQ-93 6.1 — A + X the ASIP seals every successful response (Implementing Regulation 2025/1569, article 9(4)). The format is open. The qualified seal certificate is external. REQ-83, Q-32, Q-17 6.1.3.1 REQ-AZSP-6.1.3.1-02, -03 X identification with the EUDI wallet. Other means are open. REQ-90, REQ-102, Q-36 6.1.3.1 REQ-AZSP-6.1.3.1-05, -06 open client authentication (mTLS, or private_key_jwt, or both) and token binding (mTLS or DPoP) Q-66, F-84 6.1.3.1 REQ-AZSP-6.1.3.1-08 I the identification data in the token. The NL PID has no place of birth. REQ-86, F-86, F-94 6.1.3.1 — A resource is mandatory, with one token for one data service REQ-95 6.1.3.1 — A optional binding of the token to the attributes (authorization_details) REQ-103 6.1.3.1 — A the citizen sees the QTSP, the source, and the operation before he logs in REQ-90, REQ-91 (absorbs the former REQ-96) 6.1.3.2 REQ-AZSP-6.1.3.2-01, -02 A + X registration with a software statement of the QTSP. The entitlement is in the register. Access certificates are external. REQ-88, F-85 6.1.3.2 — A + open a periodic re-check of the entitlement. The behavior when the register is unreachable is open. REQ-89, Q-34 6.1.3.4 REQ-AZSP-6.1.3.4-01 I + open GBO weighs each security consideration. The security profile, iss, and tokens after withdrawal are open. Q-66, F-96, Q-41 6.1.3.4 REQ-AZSP-6.1.3.4-02 O follows ETSI (an ISMS) and applies to the operator. Who the operator is stays open. Q-37 6.1.3 REQ-TSP-6.1.3.* R requirements on the QTSP — — — R the QTSP identifies the citizen itself, and issues only to that citizen. This is a duty of the QTSP under ETSI and eIDAS. GBO only checks that the QTSP is on the trusted list as qualified. REQ-88

docs.title: External dependencies
docs.text:
Some parts are a stub in the demo. For the build, each of these parts is a facility that must come from outside. They are not requirements on the ASIP. The profile needs these external facilities to apply in full:

  • the register of relying parties, and the API to look up the entitlement of a QTSP (F-85)
  • access certificates for QTSPs according to ETSI TS 119 411-8 (Q-35)
  • a qualified seal certificate for the ASIP (Q-17)
  • DigiD or another identification means next to the EUDI wallet (Q-36)
  • the EU catalogue of attributes, with IDs and value schemas (Q-38)

docs.title: REQ-83: Every ASIP verification result is sealed
docs.text:
The ASIP MUST seal every successful response to verify and to retrieve. With only the received response and the trusted lists, the QTSP can then establish that the response comes unchanged from this ASIP. The seal MUST cover the response exactly and carry the certificate chain. The seal MUST be at least an advanced electronic seal. This seal MUST be based on a qualified seal certificate of the responsible public sector body or of the designated intermediary.

Case Outcome verify, 200 sealed (code) retrieve, 200 sealed (code) error response (400, 401, 404, 500, 501, 503) not sealed (code, design choice)
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design for verify, and derived for retrieve. The requirement has these sources:
    • Article 9(4) of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1569. Article 1(3)(b) of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1735 replaces it from January 1, 2027 ("the verification result shall be signed or sealed … using at least … an advanced electronic seal based on a qualified certificate").
    • PSA S11, on ETSI profiles for qualified seals ("ETSI-profielen voor gekwalificeerde zegels").
    • For retrieve, the requirement serves PSA S11. A QTSP can put a retrieved value in a qualified attestation. It must then show in the same way that the value comes from the source.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the ASIP. Interface agreement: the form of the seal, for every ASIP.
  • Evidence: ICTU/GBO-demo#498, PR #499. Code and tests:
    • The seal is in seal.go#L18-L57.
    • Only a successful response gets the seal, in handler.go#L393-L408. Errors get no seal, in #L410-L420.
    • The header is an addition to the contract, in completions.json#L25-L33.
    • The tests are in handler_test.go#L240-L254, #L310-L312, and contract_test.go#L120-L121.
    • Code at v0.9.0: handler.go#L402-L417, tested in handler_test.go#L238-L252.
  • Related: REQ-94, REQ-112, F-80, Q-17, Q-28, Q-32, ADR 0041.
  • Notes:
    • The seal format is a design choice. It is a detached JWS (RFC 7515, Annex F) over the exact body, in the header X-JWS-Signature. It uses ES256 and carries the chain in x5c.
    • The body stays plain JSON, as the ETSI OpenAPI prescribes.
    • ETSI TS 119 478 defines no seal on the response. The format must be the same for all ASIPs (Q-32, E4).
    • An error response is not a verification result, so it gets no seal.
    • The demo seals with a development certificate. Who holds the qualified seal certificate is Q-17. Who the intermediary is, is Q-28.

docs.title: REQ-84: Unknown only means the source has no (complete) value
docs.text:
If the source has no value, or no complete value, for this citizen, the ASIP MUST answer an attribute or fragment with Unknown. It MUST NOT give NoMatch in that case. An attribute that the data service does not deliver MUST get 404 (REQ-94) and MUST NOT get Unknown. A source that does not answer MUST NOT get Unknown either (REQ-93).

Case Outcome The source has an equal value Match (code) The source has a different value NoMatch (code) The source does not know the BSN Unknown (code) The source has no value for this citizen, for example no residential address because he is not a resident Unknown (code) The source has an incomplete value: an address without street, house number, postal code, or town Unknown (code) An attribute that this data service does not deliver 404, and the ASIP does not ask the source (code) The source is unreachable, or the chain refuses 503 or 500, see REQ-93 (code)
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
    • ETSI TS 119 478 REQ-ASIP-6.1.1.2-04, item 4 ("no authentic source data was available to determine a match for the attribute for the user").
    • Annex IV of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1735, which designates clause 6.1.1.

    Source: design:

    The ARF (QTSPAS_02) calls this case no match. GBO follows ETSI, because the regulation designates ETSI and the ARF does not bind. GBO interprets an incomplete value as no value.

  • Addressee: interface agreement: every ASIP. GBO-delivered component: the ASIP and its source connection.

    • No value gives Unknown in service.go#L169-L206.
    • The source gives no value in source.go#L74-L108 and #L147-L161.
    • An attribute of another source is not in the catalogue (catalogue.go#L8-L10).
    • The tests are in handler_test.go#L144-L165, token_test.go#L252-L258, source_test.go#L98-L120, #L219-L226, service_test.go#L66-L80, and #L133-L148.

    Evidence: PR #499, PR #527, PR #529. Historical code and tests:

    Code at v0.9.0: steps 1 to 5 of ICTU/GBO-demo#592 removed the BRP code adapter (PR #611, PR #613, PR #620, PR #622, PR #623, PR #624). The ASIP builds each attribute from the asi description that the source publishes. An attribute without a value gets Unknown in service.go#L166-L179. An attribute that the description does not name gets 404 in #L238-L251. The test is in handler_test.go#L140-L161.

  • Related: REQ-93, REQ-94, REQ-101, REQ-113, F-80, Q-38.

  • Notes: the value schema of the attribute defines what a complete value is. Until the EU catalogue of attributes exists, the source describes it (Q-38, ICTU/GBO-demo#592). Unknown also tells something about the person, for example that he has no Dutch residential address. The citizen approved the request himself (REQ-90).

docs.title: REQ-85: The verify response contains no value from the source
docs.text:
On Match and MatchWithVariation, the ASIP MUST NOT return an attributeValue, and for fragments no fragmentValue. The QTSP only learns whether its value is correct.

  • Status: draft
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: derived. The requirement serves P-02 (minimal data processing). If the response carries the value on MatchWithVariation, the QTSP learns the value from the source. The QTSP does not need that value for the verification. The legal frame is as follows:
    • Annex IV of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1735 makes the value optional (REQ-ASIP-6.1.1.2-04-01 and -06-04-01).
    • Unchanged ETSI TS 119 478 requires the value.
  • Addressee: interface agreement: every ASIP. GBO-delivered component: the ASIP.
  • Evidence: ICTU/GBO-demo#498, PR #499. Code and tests:
    • The response has no value field (handler.go#L177-L192, service.go#L100-L103).
    • The test is in handler_test.go#L112-L136, with #L418-L425.
    • The conformance matrix has the rows etsi-ts-119478.yaml#L173-L181 and #L132-L135.
    • Code at v0.9.0: handler.go#L186-L201.
  • Related: REQ-113, F-80, F-92, Q-29.
  • Notes: sub-questions 2 and 3 of Q-29 are open.
    • REQ-ASIP-6.1.1.1-10-01 still requires the source value from an ASIP that supports fuzzy matching. Annex IV does not adapt that requirement.
    • Read literally, the ASIP does not meet REQ-ASIP-6.1.1.1-10-01 (E2). The conformance matrix marks the row failing.
    • On Match, the value is equal to the value of the QTSP. Only on MatchWithVariation does the omission of the value share less data. For that reason, on MatchWithVariation the QTSP records its own value.

docs.title: REQ-86: The access token carries the citizen's identification data and the means used to identify him
docs.text:
The authorization server MUST issue access tokens as a JWT according to RFC 9068. Each token MUST be bound to a key of the QTSP and MUST carry the scope for each operation (verify, retrieve). The token MUST carry the identification data of the citizen as the identification means delivers them. It MUST always carry the BSN. Of the mandatory PID attributes, it MUST carry only those that the means delivers.

The token MUST name the means in acr and amr. The authorization server MUST establish that means itself, and MUST NOT copy what the means declares. An identification without a BSN MUST NOT lead to a token. The BSN in the token MUST be readable only for the ASIP. A QTSP without BSN authority that holds the token MUST NOT be able to read it.

Case Outcome Logged in with DigiD (mock) the BSN, with acr and amr set to digid-mock, and no PID attributes (code) A QTSP without BSN authority reads the token no readable BSN. This is a proposal. In the demo, the BSN in the token is readable. Logged in with the NL Wallet the BSN, family_name, given_name, birthdate, and nationalities, with acr and amr set to nl-wallet. No place of birth (F-94) (code). The means delivers no BSN no authorization code. The citizen sees the request page again, and the transaction stays (code).
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • ETSI TS 119 478 REQ-AZSP-6.1.3.1-06 (token binding), -08 (JWT according to RFC 9068 "which shall contain the required identification data of the user"), and clause 6.1.3.2 (the scopes).
    • Article 9(3) of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1569 ("the verification request shall set out the attributes and the identification data of the subject"). NOTE 6 of -08 refers to this article.
    • PSA S11. Implementing Regulation 2026/1735 does not designate clause 6.1.3. S11 names TS 119 478 as a whole.
    • For a BSN that only the ASIP can read: PSA S03 and P-04. Under S03, a private consumer without a statutory BSN authority gets a party-specific identity or pseudonym ("een private afnemer zonder wettelijke BSN-bevoegdheid ontvangt een partijspecifieke identiteit of pseudoniem").
    • For the means in the token, the requirement is derived. It serves P-05: the ASIP and the audit must see with which means, and so at which level, the citizen was identified.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the authorization server. Interface agreement: the content of the token between the authorization server and the ASIP.
  • Evidence: ICTU/GBO-demo#605 is not built in demo v0.9.0. A BSN that only the ASIP can read is not built either: ICTU/GBO-demo#595 (open). The built parts come from ICTU/GBO-demo#503, #544, #546, PR #504, PR #524, PR #545, and PR #552 (with a run with the real NL Wallet). Code and tests:
    • The issuance is in tokens.go#L53-L85.
    • The DPoP binding at the token request is in service.go#L326.
    • The core establishes the means, and allows no identification without a BSN, in identification.go#L45-L51 and #L358-L363.
    • The tests are in handler_test.go#L62-L122 (DigiD), wallet_test.go#L243-L268 (NL Wallet), and handler_test.go#L138-L149 (sub).
    • The conformance claim is in etsi-ts-119478.yaml#L371-L377.
  • Related: REQ-87, REQ-95, REQ-102, REQ-103, F-84, F-86, F-88, F-94, Q-33, Q-36, Q-66.
    • The binding is DPoP (RFC 9449) and not mTLS (Q-66).
    • The token has a lifetime of ten minutes.
    • The sub differs for each token.
    • The PID attributes use the names of the IANA JWT Claims Registry. The SD-JWT VC encoding of the PID also uses these names.
    • The BSN has a provisional claim name.

    Notes: design choices:

    GBO interprets -08 so that the token with DigiD carries only the BSN (F-88, Q-36). How the claims become readable only for the ASIP is a design choice, for example encryption for the ASIP (RFC 9068 §6). See ICTU/GBO-demo#595 and F-86. With the NL Wallet, the demo puts place_of_birth as an empty object in the token (tokens.go#L73-L78). The requirement asks to leave it out.

docs.title: REQ-87: The ASIP takes the citizen only from a valid token bound to the QTSP that covers the operation
docs.text:
On every verify and retrieve request, before any other check, the ASIP MUST validate the access token according to RFC 9068 §4 (signature with a key of the authorization server, issuer, audience, validity). It MUST validate the binding to the key of the QTSP with a valid DPoP proof for this request according to RFC 9449. It MUST check that the scope covers the operation. The identification data of the citizen MUST come from that token, never from the request. Every authentication or authorization error MUST be 401, with a WWW-Authenticate challenge. If the keys of the authorization server are not available, the ASIP MUST give 503.

Case Outcome No token 401, challenge without an error code (code) Signature, issuer, audience, expiry, or typ is wrong, or the token has no cnf or no BSN 401 invalid_token (code) No proof 401 invalid_request (code) Proof invalid, reused, or with another key than cnf.jkt 401 invalid_dpop_proof (code) The scope does not cover the operation 401 insufficient_scope, with the scope in the challenge (code) The token names attributes and the request asks another attribute 401 insufficient_scope (REQ-103) (code) An invalid token and an invalid request 401: the token comes first (code) Keys of the authorization server not available 503 (code)
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • ETSI TS 119 478 REQ-ASIP-6.1.1.2-12 (401 "due to an authentication or authorization error"). Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1735 designates clause 6.1.1.
    • ETSI REQ-ASIP-4.3-03 ("access controls … to determine that the requester is a trust service provider and is acting at the request of a legitimate user").
    • RFC 9068 §4, and RFC 9449 §4.3 and §7.
    • PSA S11. Under S11, issuance, verification, and retrieval use appropriate authentication, authorization, and logging ("uitgifte, verificatie en retrieval gebruiken passende authenticatie, autorisatie en logging").
    • For the 503, the requirement is derived. It serves PSA S11: a 401 blames the QTSP for a failure on the side of the ASIP.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the ASIP. Interface agreement: every ASIP.
  • Evidence: ICTU/GBO-demo#503, PR #504. Code and tests:
    • The check is in accesstoken.go#L112-L175 and dpop.go#L35-L80.
    • The citizen from the token, the 401, and the 503 are in handler.go#L211-L249.
    • The 503 is an addition to the contract, in completions.json#L86-L95.
    • The tests are in token_test.go#L34-L109, #L158-L231, #L233-L250, and #L260-L296.
    • Code at v0.9.0: handler.go#L220-L258.
  • Related: REQ-86, REQ-95, REQ-103, F-84, Q-41, Q-66.
  • Notes: GBO interprets ETSI so that insufficient_scope is also 401. RFC 6750 §3.1 gives 403 for this case. The ASIP accepts RS256, because RFC 9068 §2.1 requires it. The authorization server signs with ES256. The ASIP gets the keys from the metadata of the authorization server. If the entitlement of a QTSP is withdrawn, its token stays valid until it expires (Q-41).

docs.title: REQ-88: Only a QTSP with the QEAA_Provider right in the register becomes a client
docs.text:
The authorization server MUST register a client only with a software statement that the QTSP signed or sealed with the key of its certificate. That certificate MUST have a chain to a trusted anchor. The statement refers to an entry in the register of relying parties (registryURI). That entry MUST carry the entitlement QEAA_Provider and MUST name the organization of the certificate.

After registration, the client MUST be able to authenticate only with the key of that certificate. If the register cannot be consulted, the authorization server MUST refuse the registration. It MUST register only a QTSP that is on the trusted list as a qualified provider, and MUST NOT know clients outside this registration.

Case Outcome Valid statement, and an entry with QEAA_Provider and the organization of the certificate client registered, private_key_jwt with the certificate key (code) No statement, alg none, signed with another key, or no x5c invalid_software_statement (code) The chain reaches no trusted anchor, or the certificate is expired, has no organizationIdentifier, or has no digitalSignature invalid_software_statement (code) The statement is expired, has iat in the future, or has no iss, iat, exp or registryURI invalid_software_statement (code) registryURI unknown in the register unapproved_software_statement (code) Entry without QEAA_Provider unapproved_software_statement (code) The organization of the certificate is not in the entry unapproved_software_statement (code) The registration names jwks or jwks_uri invalid_client_metadata (code) The register cannot be consulted 503 temporarily_unavailable (code)
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • Article 9(5) of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1569. The member state can impose access controls "to determine that the requester is a qualified trust service provider".
    • eIDAS article 45e. The verification is for QTSPs that issue qualified electronic attestations of attributes.
    • Annex I item 12 of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/848, which defines the entitlement QEAA_Provider.
    • ETSI TS 119 478 REQ-AZSP-6.1.3.2-01, -02, and figure 2 (informative).
    • P-07.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the authorization server.
  • Evidence: ICTU/GBO-demo#607 is not built in demo v0.9.0. The built parts come from ICTU/GBO-demo#503 and PR #522. Code and tests:
    • Registration and approval are in registration.go#L154-L215.
    • The statement and the certificate are in #L253-L303.
    • The client has no key of its own, in #L345-L354.
    • The tests are in registration_test.go#L41-L83, #L105-L169, #L173-L220, and #L323-L329.
  • Related: REQ-89, REQ-91, F-85, Q-07, Q-35.
  • Notes:
    • The register with its API does not exist. The access certificates according to ETSI TS 119 411-8 do not exist either. The demo uses a file and certificates of the development CA (F-85).
    • Which identifier links the certificate and the entry is Q-35. The demo uses organizationIdentifier.
    • What the QTSP must deliver (REQ-TSP-6.1.3.2-01 to -03) is a requirement on the QTSP. It belongs in a candidate connection condition.
    • A client from the configuration file of the demo (AZSP_CLIENTS_FILE) bypasses this admission. A production setup does not have that entry point.
    • The demo keeps registrations in memory only.

docs.title: REQ-89: The right of a registered client is re-checked periodically
docs.text:
The authorization server MUST periodically re-check the entitlement of every registered client in the register. A client can lose the entitlement: its entry no longer carries QEAA_Provider, or no longer names the organization of the certificate. The authorization server MUST then deactivate the client. A deactivated client gets no more authorizations and no more tokens.

Case Outcome Entitlement unchanged the client stays active, and the authorization server takes over the name from the entry (REQ-91) (code) Entitlement withdrawn client deactivated. A token request gets invalid_client. An authorization request gets an error page without redirect (code). The register cannot be consulted the client stays active until the next check (code, demo choice, Q-34)
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • ETSI TS 119 478 clause 6.1.3.2, figure 2, step 2 ("verified again in regular intervals determined by the applicable policy"). This figure is informative.
    • Article 9(5) of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1569.
    • The requirement is also derived. It serves P-07: a QTSP whose entitlement is withdrawn must not continue to verify because it registered earlier.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the authorization server.
  • Evidence: PR #522. Code and tests:
    • The re-check is in registration.go#L222-L244.
    • The interval is in main.go#L101-L104 and #L155-L169.
    • The tests are in registration_test.go#L224-L242, #L273-L304 (through the stub register), and #L306-L321.
  • Related: REQ-88, REQ-91, F-85, Q-34, Q-41.
  • Notes: the interval is policy. The operator can configure it with AZSP_ENTITLEMENT_RECHECK_INTERVAL, and the default is one hour. What happens when the register is unreachable, and how often to check, is Q-34. Tokens issued before the deactivation stay valid until they expire, at most ten minutes (Q-41). The stub register of the demo reads its file on every lookup, so a withdrawal works without a restart.

docs.title: REQ-90: The citizen approves the request by logging in, or refuses
docs.text:
The authorization server MUST show every valid authorization request to the citizen before it issues an authorization code. The citizen MUST be able to refuse, or to log in with an identification means. The approval MUST become fixed only after the means identifies the citizen. A refusal MUST give access_denied and MAY happen without a login.

The pending request MUST be single-use, short-lived, and bound to the browser in which it started. A session with a means MUST be bound to that request. If a decision does not belong to a valid pending request of that browser, the authorization server MUST NOT send it back to the client. If the login fails or the means is unreachable, the request MUST stay open for a new attempt or another means.

Case Outcome The citizen refuses, before or instead of a login access_denied to the QTSP, without a login (code) The citizen logs in and the means identifies him authorization code to the QTSP (code) The means does not identify him: DigiD (mock) gets no BSN of nine digits, or the wallet gives no usable PID the page again, with the reason. The transaction stays (code). Refused in the wallet, or the session expired the request page again, with the reason. The transaction stays (code). The means is unreachable. This includes the case where the shared attributes cannot be fetched after a completed session. error page (503). The transaction stays for another means (code). A decision without a transaction cookie, with the cookie of another transaction, or for an unknown, used, or expired transaction error page (400), no redirect (code) A wallet session of another transaction, or a session token from the browser no identification (code)
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • eIDAS article 45e(1) ("at the request of the user").
    • Article 9(5) of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1569 ("acting at the request of a legitimate user").
    • ETSI TS 119 478 REQ-AZSP-6.1.3.1-02 ("shall identify the user"), and clause 6.1.3.3, steps 7 to 11. These steps are informative ("the authorization of the later resource request by the user").
    • RFC 6749 §3.1, and RFC 9700 §2.1.1 and §4.11. ETSI refers to RFC 9700.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the authorization server.
  • Evidence: ICTU/GBO-demo#523, #544, #546, #548, PR #524, PR #545, PR #552, PR #573. Code and tests:
    • The transaction is in service.go#L210-L231 and identification.go#L107-L120. It is single-use and bound to the browser in #L195-L207.
    • Refuse and log in are in #L275-L317 and #L358-L371.
    • The decision and the wallet are in handler.go#L81-L116 and #L158-L190.
    • The page and the cookie are in pages.go#L206-L229.
    • The tests are in login_test.go#L60-L188, wallet_test.go#L148-L173, and #L270-L354.
    • The trade-off is in security-considerations.md#L21 and #L77-L79.
  • Related: REQ-86, REQ-91, REQ-102, Q-36, Q-40.
    • The transaction is valid for five minutes.
    • The cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict, with path /authorize.
    • The pages are not cached and not shown in a frame.

    Notes: design choices:

    The choice of a means starts the approval. Approval and identification are one step, as in ETSI figure 3 step 9. DigiD (mock) is a stub that only checks the form of the BSN. Which means a Dutch ASI accepts is Q-36. Q-40 asks whether the citizen who logs in here is the same as the citizen who logged in at the QTSP.

docs.title: REQ-91: The citizen sees who asks what at which source before logging in
docs.text:
For every authorization, the authorization server MUST show the citizen these facts before he logs in:

  • The QTSP that makes the request. The page MUST use the name from the entry of the QTSP in the register of relying parties. A technical client identifier alone is not enough.
  • The requested operation. This is verify, retrieve, or both.
  • The authentic source. The page MUST name the source for which the token is valid.

If the request names attributes (REQ-103), the page MUST show them too. If the request names no attributes, the page MUST NOT name any.

Case Outcome Registered QTSP the legal name from the entry. A changed name shows after the next re-check (code). Client from the configuration without a name the client_id (code, demo glue) Data service without a source name in the configuration the authorization server does not start (code) Request with authorization_details the attributes, and what the QTSP gets to see (code) Request without authorization_details no attributes and no promise about them (code)
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • eIDAS article 45e(1) ("at the request of the user"), with ETSI TS 119 478 clause 6.1.3.3, step 7 (informative).
    • The FAPI 2.0 Security Profile, to which ETSI clause 6.1.3.1 NOTE 3 refers. The profile asks for an informed decision of the end user. Its recommendation is to "provide end-users with all necessary information …, including the identity of the client and the scope of the authorization".
    • The requirement is also derived. It serves P-13: without the name of the QTSP and of the source, the citizen does not know what he approves. If he does not see the source, a token for one source (REQ-95) does not help him.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the authorization server.
  • Evidence: ICTU/GBO-demo#525, #544, #547, PR #529, PR #545, PR #559, PR #591. Code and tests:
    • The request page is in pages.go#L94-L123.
    • The name from the entry is in registration.go#L185, and at the re-check in #L228-L244.
    • The name and the source in the transaction are in service.go#L225-L229 and #L286-L293.
    • The source name is mandatory in main.go#L190-L210.
    • The tests are in login_test.go#L17-L58, style_test.go#L105-L163, registration_test.go#L67-L83, #L244-L271, and main_test.go#L5-L17.
  • Related: REQ-88, REQ-89, REQ-90, REQ-95, REQ-102, REQ-103, Q-36.
  • Notes:
    • The page has other texts: why, what the QTSP learns, only this request, and where the citizen logs in. These texts are a text choice of the demo and are not a requirement.
    • The NL Wallet shows the authorization server and not the QTSP, because a fixed reader certificate cannot carry a name for each QTSP. The page and the purpose in that certificate explain the relation (provision.go#L109, REQ-102).
    • The chosen safeguard is that the server does not start without a source name. In v0.9.0, the authorization server takes its data services and source names from AZSP_RESOURCES and not from the source descriptions. ICTU/GBO-demo#592 stays open.
    • This requirement absorbs the former REQ-96.

docs.title: REQ-92: The ASIP asks the source only for the fields of the requested attributes
docs.text:
An ASIP that queries a source through the chain MUST ask the source only for the fields that the requested attributes need. This applies to each verify or retrieve request, for the citizen from the access token. The ASIP MUST refuse a request with an attribute that the data service does not deliver, before it asks the source anything.

Case Outcome Verify with three attributes and a fragment one query to the source, with the fields of each attribute once (code) An attribute outside the catalogue next to a valid attribute 404, and the ASIP does not ask the source (code) An attribute for which the ASIP knows no fields error, and the ASIP does not ask the source (code)
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: derived. The requirement serves P-02 and D-09 (selective data request). The ASIP is a consumer of the source. If it asks more fields than the QTSP needs, it processes data without a purpose. ETSI TS 119 478 clause 4.3 leaves open how an ASIP that is "an intermediary acting on its behalf" queries its source.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the ASIP.
    • The fields for each attribute, and the one query, are in source.go#L37-L46 and #L74-L108.
    • The check against the catalogue comes first, in service.go#L110-L118.
    • The tests are in service_test.go#L150-L199, source_test.go#L122-L146, #L186-L217, and trace_test.go#L45-L81.

    Evidence: ICTU/GBO-demo#525, PR #527, PR #530. Historical code and tests:

    Code at v0.9.0: since steps 1 to 5 of ICTU/GBO-demo#592 (up to PR #624), the ASIP derives one query from the asi description of the source. It does this in two steps:

    1. The ASIP checks that the description names every attribute (service.go#L238-L251).
    2. The ASIP makes one plan for all requested attributes (#L253-L268, plan.go#L22-L35), with the BSN as a variable (source.go#L94).

    The tests are in source_test.go#L102 and trace_test.go#L59.

  • Related: REQ-08, REQ-55, REQ-60, REQ-64, REQ-94, Q-38, ADR 0039.

  • Notes:
    • The design uses one query per request. As a result, there is one FSC transaction and one decision of the PDP. The BSN is a variable and is not in the query text. The source enforces the limit itself with its own rule (asi0001.rego).
    • In v0.9.0, the source describes which fields belong to an attribute. It does this in the asi capability of its source metadata. GBO validates the description against its attribute catalogue (schemas/asi-attributes.json). The open points of that direction are in Q-38 and ICTU/GBO-demo#592.

docs.title: REQ-93: A chain that does not answer is an error, not Unknown
docs.text:
If the ASIP cannot reach the source, or the chain gives a server error, the ASIP MUST return 503. If the chain refuses the query, the ASIP MUST return 500. An example is a refusal by the PDP of the source. If the ASIP cannot read the answer of the source, it MUST also return 500. In all these cases, the ASIP MUST NOT return a verification result. This also excludes Unknown.

Case Outcome Outway not reachable 503 (code) Outway answers with a 5xx (for example 502, source unreachable) 503 (code) The PDP of the source refuses (the Inway gives 401) 500 (code) The source answers with GraphQL errors, or with something other than JSON 500 (code)
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: derived. For verify, the requirement serves PSA S11. Unknown says that the source has no data (ETSI TS 119 478 REQ-ASIP-6.1.1.2-04). If the ASIP reports a failure as Unknown, the QTSP gets a wrong verification result. The QTSP can then refuse the citizen, or let him fill in the value himself. Annex B has no 500 and no 503, so these codes are an addition.
  • Addressee: interface agreement: every ASIP. GBO-delivered component: the ASIP.
    • The status codes are in handler.go#L353-L375.
    • Unreachable or refused is in source.go#L211-L240.
    • The addition to the contract is in completions.json#L76-L95.
    • The tests are in source_test.go#L74-L97, brpsource/source_test.go#L148-L177, and service_test.go#L201-L217.

    Evidence: ICTU/GBO-demo#525, PR #527. Historical code and tests:

    Code at v0.9.0: the status codes are in handler.go#L362-L384. Unreachable or refused is in source.go#L107-L138. The tests are in source_test.go#L141 and graphqlsource/source_test.go#L157.

  • Related: REQ-60, REQ-84, REQ-101.

  • Notes: only unit tests show the 500 on a refusal by the PDP. The stack does not show it. A refusal by the chain is a fault in the setup and not a property of the citizen. Error messages name the Fsc-Transaction-Id and not the BSN (REQ-60). In v0.9.0, if the source has no up-to-date asi description, the ASIP also gives 503 (source.go#L60-L68).

docs.title: REQ-94: Every ASI response names the one authentic source responsible for it
docs.text:
Every verify and retrieve response of the ASIP MUST name the ASIP (provider). If the ASIP is not itself the authentic source, the response MUST also name the responsible authentic source (authenticSource). It MUST name exactly one source. For that reason, an ASIP that serves several sources MUST limit each request to one source. An attribute of another source MUST give 404, and the ASIP MUST NOT ask any source anything.

Case Outcome Data service with an authentic source behind the ASIP provider and authenticSource in every response (code) Data service of which the ASIP is itself the source provider, no authenticSource. This is historical code, in unit tests only. In v0.9.0, the ASIP always takes authenticSource from the source description. Attribute of another data service 404, and the ASIP asks no source (code)
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • Article 9(4) of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1569, as Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1735 replaces it. The result "shall … specify the public sector body responsible for the authentic source". Where applicable, the result specifies instead "the public sector body designated to act on behalf of the authentic source".
    • ETSI TS 119 478 REQ-ASIP-6.1.1.2-07, -08, and REQ-ASIP-6.1.2.2-04 (one authenticSource).
    • PSA S11. Under S11, the bronhouder stays responsible for the law and for the content ("de bronhouder blijft juridisch en inhoudelijk verantwoordelijk").
    • P-10.
  • Addressee: interface agreement: every ASIP. GBO-delivered component: the ASIP.
    • The data services come from the configuration in dataservice.go#L52-L106 and main.go#L86-L105.
    • Each data service has a base URL, a contract, and records in handler.go#L89-L113.
    • The source in the response is in #L37-L53 and #L187-L192.
    • The tests are in dataservices_test.go#L32-L48, handler_test.go#L153-L159, #L329-L349, and service_test.go#L133-L148.

    Evidence: ICTU/GBO-demo#525, PR #529. Historical code and tests:

    Code at v0.9.0: the data services are in dataservices.json and main.go#L115-L125. The ASIP takes authenticSource from the source description in handler.go#L304 and #L339. The tests are in dataservices_test.go#L35 and handler_test.go#L151-L155.

  • Related: REQ-83, REQ-84, REQ-95, REQ-99, F-89, Q-37, Q-38, E3, ADR 0038.

  • Notes: the design has one data service per source (ADR 0038). Each data service has its own base URL, contract, catalogue, and token audience. The demo has one data service (brp, source rvig). A second data service exists only in unit tests. Whether an ASIP for several sources makes GBO an intermediary is Q-37.

docs.title: REQ-95: An access token is valid only for the source the citizen saw
docs.text:
An access token MUST be valid only for the authentic source that the citizen saw at the authorization (REQ-91). An authorization request or a token request can name no data service, more than one, or an unknown one. The authorization server MUST then refuse it with invalid_target. The ASIP MUST refuse a token for another data service.

Case Outcome One known resource token with its base URL as aud (code) No resource, two, or an unknown one invalid_target (code) Token request with another resource than the one of the code invalid_target (code) Token for data service A at data service B 401 invalid_token (code)
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: derived. The requirement serves eIDAS article 45e(1) ("at the request of the user") and P-13. If a token is also valid for another source, the QTSP verifies data at a source that the citizen did not see. ETSI TS 119 478 does not specify the reach of a token for each data service.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the authorization server and the ASIP.
  • Evidence: ICTU/GBO-demo#525, PR #529. Code and tests:
    • The authorization server is in service.go#L201-L204, #L255-L276, and #L341-L343.
    • The audience at the ASIP is in accesstoken.go#L148, and for each data service in main.go#L102.
    • The tests are in handler_test.go#L151-L182 and dataservices_test.go#L15-L30.
    • Code at v0.9.0: the audience for each data service is in main.go#L121, tested in dataservices_test.go#L16.
  • Related: REQ-86, REQ-87, REQ-91, REQ-94, REQ-99, REQ-103, F-89, ADR 0038.
  • Notes: the design allows exactly one resource for each authorization (ADR 0038). As a result, a QTSP that needs attributes of two sources authorizes twice, with two interactions of the citizen. RFC 8707 §2.2 allows more resources in one authorization, with a token for each resource.

docs.title: REQ-99: The ASIP provides a discovery record for each attribute and data service, with a path to endpoint, contract, and authorization server
docs.text:
For every data service, the ASIP MUST provide a dataService record according to ETSI TS 119 478 clause 5.3.3. It MUST provide one record for each attribute that the data service delivers. The record holds these items: the identifier of the attribute (attributeIdentifier), the endpoint of the data service (endpointURI), its contract (endpointDescription), and the provider (provider). The contract MUST name the same endpoint as server. The contract MUST also name the metadata of the authorization server (REQ-100). From the record, a QTSP can then verify or retrieve without prior knowledge of the addresses of the ASIP.

Case Outcome Data service brp with three attributes three records, each with endpoint, contract, provider, and country. The records conform to the ETSI schema (code). Record → contract servers is the endpoint of the record. The contract names the metadata of the authorization server (code). Unknown data service no records, 404 (code)
  • Status: draft
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • ETSI TS 119 478 clause 5.3.3, REQ-DIP-5.3.3-03 (the content of the record). ETSI puts this requirement on the DIP.
    • ETSI figure 3, steps 2 to 5. In these steps, the QTSP finds the data service through the Discover Interface.
    • The requirement is also derived. It serves PSA S11 and P-11: without a record, a QTSP finds no Dutch data service for an attribute. S11 asks for the connection to relevant trusted lists and catalogues ("aansluiting op relevante vertrouwenslijsten en catalogi").
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the ASIP. Interface agreement: the record and the contract.
  • Evidence: ICTU/GBO-demo#533, PR #534, PR #535. Code and tests:
    • The records for each data service are in handler.go#L104-L111 and #L138-L156.
    • A test checks the records against the ETSI schema (discovery_test.go#L62). Another test follows the path from record to contract (discovery_test.go#L101).
    • The stub of the DIP checks the records (directory.go#L101-L134) and finds them for each attribute (handler_test.go#L97).
    • The reference QTSP follows the record, the contract, and the metadata (qtsp.go#L119-L202).
    • Code at v0.9.0: the records follow the up-to-date description of the source. Without an up-to-date description, the ASIP gives 503 (handler.go#L131-L165). The tests are in discovery_test.go#L66, #L105, and #L169.
  • Related: REQ-94, REQ-95, REQ-100, F-89, Q-67.
  • Notes:
    • How the records get into the Data Service Directory of OOTS, and who registers them, is open (Q-67).
    • The demo offers the records for each data service at /<dataservice>/dataservices. A stub of the DIP fetches them.
    • In demo v0.9.0, the provider carries no identifiers. REQ-DIP-5.3.3-03-04-04 is only a recommendation, and there is no EU identifier type for an OIN.
    • The search of a QTSP through the Discover Interface is behavior of the QTSP itself (clause 5) and is no requirement on GBO.
    • The reference QTSP refuses a request with attributes of two data services before it contacts the authorization server. The reason is that a token is valid for one data service (REQ-95).

docs.title: REQ-100: A data service contract names its authorization-server metadata at the location RFC 8414 prescribes
docs.text:
The contract of a data service MUST name the URL of the metadata of its authorization server. That URL MUST be the location that RFC 8414 §3.1 prescribes for the issuer: the suffix /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server between host and path of the issuer.

Case Outcome Issuer https://host https://host/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server (code) Issuer with path https://host/issuer1 https://host/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/issuer1 (code)
  • Status: draft
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • ETSI TS 119 478 REQ-DIP-5.3.3-03-02-01. The contract "shall specify the corresponding metadata of the OAuth 2.0 based authorization server".
    • RFC 8414 §3.1 and §3.3.
    • PSA S11, which names ETSI TS 119 478 V1.1.1 for the setup of the ASI provider ("ETSI TS 119 478 V1.1.1 voor de inrichting van de ASI-provider").
  • Addressee: interface agreement: the contract of every ASIP. GBO-delivered component: the ASIP.
  • Evidence: PR #534, PR #537. Code and tests:
    • The contract is in contract.go#L102-L110.
    • The URL is in asmetadata.go#L45-L53.
    • The tests are in asmetadata_test.go#L84, #L103 (issuer with a path), and discovery_test.go#L101.
  • Related: REQ-99, F-91, Q-39, Q-67, E1.
  • Notes: the extension x-oauth-authorization-server in the oauth2 security scheme is a design choice. GBO chose this name itself, because ETSI gives no field (E1). Until Q-39 has a decision, each ASIP chooses for itself. RFC 8414 §3.3 already requires the client to check the issuer in the metadata against the URL. The reference QTSP does exactly this (qtsp.go#L196-L200).

docs.title: REQ-101: A retrieve for which the source lacks a requested attribute is not found and gives no partial result
docs.text:
If the source has no value for a requested attribute, the ASIP MUST answer a retrieve request with 404, with the attribute in the reason. A retrieve MUST NOT give a partial result: a 200 MUST contain every requested attribute. Verify still gives Unknown (REQ-84).

Case Outcome The source has a value for every requested attribute 200 with every attribute, sealed (code) The source has no value for one attribute, also next to an attribute with a value 404 without a seal. The reason names the attribute (code). Attribute not in the catalogue of the data service 404 (REQ-94) (code) Verify, the source has no value Unknown (REQ-84) (code)
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design. The source is ETSI TS 119 478 REQ-ASIP-6.1.2.2-06 ("404 … at least one of the requested attributes … was not found") and -02-01 ("one or more attribute objects"). GBO reads these requirements so that no value in the source also counts as not found.
  • Addressee: interface agreement: every ASIP. GBO-delivered component: the ASIP.
  • Evidence: PR #541, PR #542. Code and tests:
    • Historical code: service.go#L152-L158 and handler.go#L366-L367. The test for one and two attributes is in handler_test.go#L291-L319.
    • Code at v0.9.0: service.go#L198-L236 and handler.go#L375-L376. The test is in handler_test.go#L291-L315.
  • Related: REQ-84, REQ-90, REQ-93, REQ-94.
  • Notes: a missing value also tells something about the person, for example that he has no Dutch address. The citizen authorized the request himself (REQ-90).

docs.title: REQ-102: The authorization server identifies the citizen with the EUDI wallet through OpenID4VP and asks only the PID attributes in its registration
docs.text:
The authorization server of the ASI MUST be able to identify the citizen with the EUDI wallet through OpenID4VP. It MUST act as a registered wallet relying party of its own, and ask only the PID attributes that are in its registration. The PID MUST come from a trusted PID issuer and contain a BSN. A presentation of another type, or without a BSN, MUST NOT lead to an identification.

Case Outcome PID urn:eudi:pid:nl:1 with BSN, from a trusted issuer identified. The BSN and the PID attributes go into the token (REQ-86) (code). PID without BSN, another type, another query ID, or no presentation not identified (code) Return on the same device with the session of another browser, or without a valid nonce not identified (code) Verifier not reachable means not available. The transaction stays (REQ-90) (code).
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • ETSI TS 119 478 REQ-AZSP-6.1.3.1-02 and -03 ("with the EUDI-Wallet using the OpenID4VP protocol"), and clause 6.1.3.3, steps 8 to 10.
    • eIDAS article 5b(1) to (3). The relying party is registered and asks no other data than the registered data.
    • Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/848 article 8.
    • PSA S11, which names OpenID4VP for presentation or verification where relevant ("OpenID4VP voor presentatie of verificatie waar relevant").
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the authorization server of the ASI.
  • Evidence: ICTU/GBO-demo#546, PR #550, PR #552, PR #573. Code and tests:
    • The request for the PID is in client.go#L39-L48 and provision.go#L36-L40.
    • The registration with only those attributes is in provision.go#L106-L112 and #L189-L195, tested in provision_test.go#L115-L117.
    • The trusted issuers are in provision.go#L139-L150.
    • The code accepts only a PID of the right type with a BSN, in client.go#L157-L175, tested in client_test.go#L174-L192.
    • Return on the same device works only for the session of this transaction and browser, in identification.go#L318-L341. The tests are in wallet_test.go#L88, #L123, #L177, and #L205.
    • PR #552 records a run with the real NL Wallet (cross-device).
  • Related: REQ-86, REQ-90, REQ-91, F-93, F-94, Q-36.
  • Notes:
    • The choice of verifier is a design choice of the demo. The verifier is the verification_server of nl-wallet v0.5.0. It checks the signature of the issuer and the binding to the wallet. Another verifier is allowed.
    • The reader certificate of the NL Wallet carries the registration (purpose and allowed attributes). In the demo, this certificate comes from a development CA and is not a registered access certificate.
    • The NL PID has no place of birth (F-94).
    • The wallet shows the authorization server and not the QTSP. The purpose in the registration explains the relation (REQ-91).
    • The same-device route runs only in tests. A real run needs the ASI route on https in the simulation environment (ICTU/GBO-demo#594, ICTU/GBO-demo#596).
    • Which means come next to the wallet is Q-36.
    • The verifier accepts a PID whose revocation status cannot be established (config.go#L45). A sub-question of Q-36 asks whether a PID with an unknown revocation status, or a revoked PID, can lead to an identification.

docs.title: REQ-103: An authorization can be bound to the requested attributes, and the ASIP then processes only those attributes
docs.text:
An authorization request can name the attributes that the QTSP wants to verify or retrieve. The authorization server of the ASI MUST then check that these attributes belong to exactly the data service and the operations of the request. It MUST refuse an invalid list, show the attributes to the citizen, and put them unchanged in the access token. If the token carries such a list, the ASIP MUST refuse a request that names an attribute outside the list.

A policy under article 9(5) of Implementing Regulation 2025/1569 can make the list mandatory (Q-33). Without such a policy, the authorization server MUST treat a request without a list as an authorization per operation according to ETSI TS 119 478. The catalogue of the data service is then the limit.

Case Outcome No list authorization per operation, a page without attributes, and a token without a list. The ASIP allows every attribute from the catalogue (code). No list, list made mandatory invalid_request (code) The list is empty, of an unknown type, or for another data service. Or the list has other operations than the scope, no attributes, or invalid or duplicate attributes. invalid_request (code) Valid list attributes on the page and unchanged in the token (code) Token with a list, and the request names another attribute 401 insufficient_scope. The reason names the attribute (code).
  • Status: draft
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1569 article 9(5). A member state can impose access control.
    • ETSI TS 119 478 clause 6.1.3.2 binds only for each operation (F-95).
    • The requirement is also derived. It serves PSA S11 and P-02. Under S11, issuance, verification, and retrieval use appropriate authentication, authorization, and logging ("uitgifte, verificatie en retrieval gebruiken passende authenticatie, autorisatie en logging"). Without a binding, the QTSP can ask every attribute from the catalogue with the same token, also when the citizen approved something else.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the authorization server and the ASIP. Interface agreement: with the QTSP.
  • Evidence: PR #559, ICTU/GBO-demo#571, PR #572. Code and tests:
    • The check at the authorization server is in authorization_details.go#L31-L79 and service.go#L205-L209.
    • The page shows the attributes in pages.go#L109-L111.
    • The token is in tokens.go#L70-L72.
    • The configuration that makes the list mandatory is in main.go#L109.
    • The check at the ASIP is in accesstoken.go#L177-L197 and handler.go#L337-L347.
    • The tests are in service_test.go#L85-L125, #L151-L160, handler_test.go#L62, #L124, style_test.go#L145, token_test.go#L111, and #L233.
    • Code at v0.9.0 for the ASIP: handler.go#L346-L356.
  • Related: REQ-86, REQ-87, REQ-91, F-95, Q-33, E5, ADR 0042.
    • locations, equal to resource
    • actions, equal to the scope
    • attribute_identifiers, with 1 to 50 unique https URIs

    Notes: the list is a design choice. It is one RFC 9396 authorization_details of the provisional type https://gbo.example/authorization-details/authentic-source-attributes. It has these fields:

    Only parties that know that type can use the binding. A QTSP that implements only ETSI connects without a list. In the demo, AZSP_REQUIRE_AUTHORIZATION_DETAILS=true makes the list mandatory. Whether the Netherlands imposes the binding is Q-33. ETSI does not provide the binding (E5).

docs.title: REQ-112: The ASIP offers the clause 6.1 interface
docs.text:
The ASIP MUST offer the interface of ETSI TS 119 478 clause 6.1: verify and retrieve over HTTP, with authorization according to OAuth 2.0. Until Q-64 decides otherwise, the ASIP does not offer the interface of clause 6.2 (ISO 15000).

  • Status: draft
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • ETSI TS 119 478 REQ-ASIP-4.3-04. The ASIP chooses clause 6.1, clause 6.2, or both.
    • Annex IV of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1735. For verify, it designates clause 6.1.1, or 6.2.3, or both.
    • The section on agreements and standards ("Afspraken en standaarden") of PSA S11. It names ETSI TS 119 478 V1.1.1 for the setup of the ASI provider ("ETSI TS 119 478 V1.1.1 voor de inrichting van de ASI-provider").
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the ASIP. Interface agreement.
  • Evidence: PR #499, PR #540, PR #574. The demo ASIP offers only clause 6.1 (asi-route.md#L98). The conformance matrix marks clause 6.2 as a group that is not applicable (etsi-ts-119478.yaml#L9-L11). It marks REQ-ASIP-4.3-04 as passed (#L38-L42).
  • Related: F-80, Q-64, ADR 0037.
  • Notes: this requirement is a choice within REQ-ASIP-4.3-04. The profile records it. Q-64 asks whether clause 6.2 becomes necessary later, also for deferred responses.

docs.title: REQ-113: Fuzzy matching only on free text, with documented rules
docs.text:
An ASIP that supports fuzzy matching (REQ-ASIP-6.1.1.1-10) MUST apply it only to free text, such as names and address lines. It MUST NOT apply it to dates, codes, and numbers. It MUST publish the rules that it applies. A QTSP then knows when it can get MatchWithVariation.

Case Outcome A name that differs only in case, diacritics, hyphens, or white space MatchWithVariation (code) A date or code that differs only in this way, for example 1990-01-01 and 1990 01 01 NoMatch. For dates, the demo does this since v0.9.0 (code). For codes, see the notes.
  • Status: draft
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design. The source is ETSI TS 119 478 REQ-ASIP-6.1.1.1-10. It leaves fuzzy matching free. It names differences in transliteration, spaces, hyphens, and compounding "and similar orthographic variations". These differences fit text and do not fit a date or a code. ETSI prescribes no rules, and this requirement makes that stricter.
  • Addressee: interface agreement: every ASIP that offers fuzzy matching.
  • Evidence: PR #499. Code and tests:
    • Historical code: the rules are documented (README asi-provider#L143) and built (match.go#L110-L131). The test is in handler_test.go#L119-L136. At that commit, the demo normalized every string (match.go#L44-L48).
    • Code at v0.9.0: since step 5 of ICTU/GBO-demo#592 (PR #624), a string with a format in the value schema matches exactly or not. An example is the birth date (match.go#L27-L54, asi-attributes.json). The rules are in the README asi-provider#L158. The test is in service_test.go#L330-L348.
  • Related: REQ-84, REQ-85, Q-38, Q-70 (normalization for each kind of value), ADR 0039.
  • Notes:
    • The value schema of an attribute marks what free text is. The source metadata define this (ICTU/GBO-demo#592: "fuzzy matching follows the type", through value_schema). In v0.9.0, the marker is the JSON Schema format.
    • The demo still normalizes a code without a format. Nationality nl against NL gives MatchWithVariation. A postal code in another way of writing also gives MatchWithVariation. For codes, demo v0.9.0 does not meet the requirement.
    • The rules of the demo itself (ICAO Doc 9303, diacritics, hyphens, white space, case) are not a requirement.

docs.title: REQ-114: A request on behalf of another person gets 501
docs.text:
Until Q-65 decides otherwise, the ASIP MUST NOT support verify and retrieve requests on behalf of another subject (mandate). It MUST answer them with 501, without asking the source anything.

Case Outcome Verify with mandate 501, and the ASIP does not ask the source (code) Retrieve with mandate 501, and the ASIP does not ask the source (code) Malformed request with mandate 400 comes first (code)
  • Status: draft
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design. The source is ETSI TS 119 478 REQ-ASIP-6.1.1.1-12, which leaves support of mandate free. The 501 then follows from REQ-ASIP-6.1.1.1-13. ETSI leaves the content of mandate outside the specification (NOTE 3).
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the ASIP. Interface agreement.
  • Evidence: PR #499, PR #542. Code and tests:
    • Historical code: the demo refuses before it asks the source (service.go#L107-L109, #L140-L142), with 501 (handler.go#L364-L365). The test is in handler_test.go#L190-L203. The test for the order is in service_test.go#L90.
    • Code at v0.9.0: service.go#L133-L135, #L205-L207, and handler.go#L373-L374. The test is in handler_test.go#L186-L199.
  • Related: REQ-112, PSA S04 (representation), Q-65.
  • Notes: this requirement is a choice within REQ-ASIP-6.1.1.1-12. The profile records it. Q-65 asks whether representation becomes necessary later, and where the evidence then comes from.

docs.title: REQ-115: The ASIP verifies attribute fragments
docs.text:
The ASIP MUST support the verification of attribute fragments (REQ-ASIP-6.1.1.1-07, -08). The contract of every data service MUST describe which JSONPath expressions (RFC 9535) the ASIP accepts for a fragment.

Case Outcome Fragment with an expression from the supported subset Match, MatchWithVariation, or NoMatch (code) Expression that selects nothing in the source value Unknown (code) Expression outside the subset 400 (code). There is no decision whether this must be 400 or 501.
  • Status: draft
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design. ETSI TS 119 478 leaves fragments free (REQ-ASIP-6.1.1.1-08-01). If the ASIP does not support fragments, it gives 501 (REQ-ASIP-6.1.1.1-09). With fragments, a QTSP can have one part of an attribute verified without sending the rest. An example is the town of an address.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the ASIP. Interface agreement.
  • Evidence: ICTU/GBO-demo#608 is not built in demo v0.9.0. The built part comes from PR #499. Code and tests:
    • Historical code: the demo supports a subset of JSONPath (match.go#L149-L210, service.go#L211-L233). The tests are in handler_test.go#L169-L188 and service_test.go#L82-L87.
    • Code at v0.9.0: the subset is in match.go#L176-L187, and the fragment check is in service.go#L290-L317. The test is in handler_test.go#L165-L184.
    • The description in the contract is not built in demo v0.9.0. The subset is only in the README asi-provider#L160.
  • Related: REQ-112, REQ-113.
  • Notes:
    • The choice of subset is a choice for the contract and is no requirement.
    • The demo answers an expression outside its subset with 400 (service.go#L220-L221). There is no decision whether an expression that the ASIP does not support gives 400 or 501.
    • In v0.9.0, a fragment can point to a member that the source description does not provide, or provides as a constant. That fragment gets Unknown, and the ASIP does not ask the source (service.go#L140-L161).

docs.title: Removed numbers
docs.text:
These requirement numbers are no longer in use:

  • REQ-96: merged into REQ-91 (the request page names the source).
  • REQ-98: removed. The content of rule ASI0001 follows from REQ-48, REQ-74, REQ-97, REQ-79, and REQ-17.
  • REQ-104: removed. The QTSP identifies the citizen itself, as a duty of the QTSP under ETSI and eIDAS (REQ-88). See also F-93 and Q-40.
  • REQ-105: removed. The QTSP issues an attestation only to the citizen that it identified, as a duty of the QTSP under ETSI and eIDAS (REQ-88).

docs.title: Authorization and data access requirements
docs.text:
These requirements cover how GBO Basis decides on a request. They cover the PEP, the PDP and the rules, the enforcement of the query, and the data that the source returns. They also cover how the policy itself is managed. For the design, see Authorization in GBO Basis.

This page has the following parts:

  • PEP, PDP and PIP
  • Query enforcement requirements
  • Data minimization requirements
  • Policy management guidelines

docs.title: PEP, PDP and PIP
docs.text: The requirements on this page cover the authorization of one request at a source. They apply to the PEP, the PDP of the source, and the information sources (PIP) that the PDP consults. The requirements are generic: they apply to DvTP, EUDI issuance, and the ASI route. Admission covers the admission of a party before any request. Query enforcement covers the decision per field of a query.

docs.title: Rule set in the demo
docs.text:
The demo (v0.9.0) uses the FSC Inway as the PEP and OpenFTV with OPA as the PDP. The reference policy is plain Rego under policies/gbo/. Each rule declares its regime and the FSC services that it applies to (REQ-74, REQ-97). Each rule also states its own reasons to deny (REQ-48). The reference policy has five rules:

Rule Regime FSC service What it grants DVT0001 consent bri income declaration fields under a consent LVG0001 consent lvg ownership check at the LVG source EUD0001 PID bri income declaration to the wallet EUD0002 PID brp death certificate to the wallet ASI0001 PID brp BRP fields for the ASIP ### REQ-04: The source delivers only after a positive decision by its PDP

Every request to a source MUST pass a PEP that consults the PDP of the source. The PEP MUST let the request through only after a positive decision. What is behind the PEP (source gateway, source service) MUST NOT be reachable for a consumer by another route. If no decision comes, the request MUST be denied.

  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design: PSA S05 and FR-26 criteria 1 and 3. Under S05, every data request passes a PEP-PDP chain. A PEP denies by default if decision information is missing or not trusted ("iedere gegevensvraag doorloopt een PEP-PDP-keten", "een PEP weigert standaard bij ontbrekende of onbetrouwbare beslisinformatie").
  • Addressee: interface agreement. The requirement applies to every source that connects through GBO. REQ-81 works it out for the source gateway that GBO delivers.
  • Evidence: every Inway sends every request as an AuthZEN question to the PDP (fsc-infra/docker-compose.yml#L769-L775, #L957-L959, PR #60). The source gateways are only on a network with the Inways (docker-compose.yml#L829-L836, PR #469). No test exists.
  • Related: REQ-81, REQ-21, REQ-42, F-35, ADR 0002, ADR 0033.
  • Notes: design choice: the FSC Inway is the PEP, with the PDP as AuthZEN endpoint. There is no separate PEP service. The isolation of the gateway exists only in compose. In Kubernetes, the isolation needs a NetworkPolicy or an equivalent control.

docs.title: REQ-06: A denial carries a machine-readable reason: coarse for the consumer, full for the operator
docs.text:
The PDP MUST give a machine-readable reason for every denial. The consumer MUST get only a code that tells that the request was denied and in which class. That code MUST NOT reveal which field was denied, whether a field exists, or which check failed. For the operator of the source, the record MUST show which rules decided on each denied field, and with which reasons. The most fundamental reason MUST come first. A fault on the side of the source MUST appear to the consumer as a normal access denial.

Case Outcome Field is outside the rule consumer: FIELD_NOT_PERMITTED. Operator: per field the rule and the reason, for example YEAR_NOT_COVERED. Query cannot be verified consumer: COVERAGE_UNVERIFIABLE with a subcode. For INVALID_QUERY, the consumer gets FIELD_NOT_PERMITTED. Register unreachable, rule cannot be evaluated consumer: ACCESS_DENIED. Operator: PIP_UNAVAILABLE or CONFIG_ERROR with trace.
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design: PSA S05, where the log records the policy version, the relevant context, and the decision ("logging legt de beleidsversie, relevante context en beslissing vast"), PSA S09, and P-12. The consumer codes follow the FTV GraphQL profile for AuthZEN ("Decision and Error Transport", "Security Considerations").
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the reference engine of the PDP. Interface agreement: the consumer codes.
  • Evidence: PR #488 gives this evidence:
    • The consumer code is in engine.rego#L95-L118.
    • The detail per field is in #L56-L68.
    • The order is in #L321-L344.
    • The tests are engine_test.rego#L11 and #L29.
    • If a rule cannot be evaluated, the field is denied (engine.rego#L18-L23) with CONFIG_ERROR / RULE_NOT_EVALUABLE (#L77-L79). The test is engine_test.rego#L784-L791.
  • Related: REQ-32, REQ-71, REQ-74, F-72.
  • Notes: in demo v0.9.0, the detail per field reaches only the console decision log of the engine (observability). The ADL records only the consumer code (authz.rego#L42-L51). Design choice: the order is first the proof, then the state of the consent, then the question, then the caller.
