docs.title: REQ-18: The PDP decides on facts that it established itself, and never on what the consumer declares
docs.text:
The PDP MUST decide on facts that it verified itself or fetched from a trusted source. The PDP MUST take the caller and the service from the transport token that the source signed. It MUST take the consent from a proof whose signature and status the PDP checks itself. It MUST take the admission from the register.

What the consumer sends (header, body, query argument) MUST state only what is asked. It MUST NOT carry a decision without that own check. The PDP MUST ignore decision information that arrives in the question as a ready-made fact.

Case Outcome Consent record sent in the question, no token ignored. The PID regime applies, and the placeholder names nobody: PID_NOT_PRESENT. Register gives no status denied: CONSENT_STATUS_UNAVAILABLE
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design: PSA S05, FR-16 criterion 1, and FR-17 criterion 1. Under S05, the PDP can consult relevant information sources. A PEP denies by default if decision information is missing or not trusted ("de PDP kan relevante informatiebronnen raadplegen", "een PEP weigert standaard bij ontbrekende of onbetrouwbare beslisinformatie").
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the reference PDP (mapper and policy).
  • Evidence: the PDP ignores a consent that is sent in the question (dvtp_helper.rego#L6-L9, test engine_test.rego#L54). The policy checks the token and the status itself (consent.rego#L169-L186, #L270-L280, PR #371). The service and the caller come from the token (ftvgraphql.go#L30-L33, lib.rego#L55-L72). Since PR #580, a declared scope header does not count.
  • Related: REQ-68, REQ-61, REQ-79, REQ-74, REQ-45, F-32, ADR 0032.
  • Notes: in demo v0.9.0, the BSN in the PID regime is a statement of the adapter. The PID is not verified (ICTU/GBO-demo#133, REQ-45). The fetched consent is not in the question. For that reason, the PDP adds it to its answer, for the decision record (engine.rego#L25-L29).

docs.title: REQ-42: The authorization request follows an open PEP-PDP profile, and the PEP passes the request on unchanged
docs.text:
The question from PEP to PDP MUST follow the AuthZEN NLGov profile. In that profile, the caller is the subject, the request is the action and the resource, and the transport context is the context. The PEP MUST pass the request on unchanged (for GraphQL: the raw body). The PEP MUST NOT interpret or add to the request. The PDP side decides which data the request asks for.

  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design: PSA S05, with the agreement on the AuthZEN NLGov profile. S05 asks for a standard vocabulary for subject, action, resource, and context. The interface and the policy do not depend on a product ("gestandaardiseerd vocabulaire voor subject, actie, resource en context", "de interface en het beleid zijn productonafhankelijk").
  • Addressee: interface agreement: PEP to PDP. GBO-delivered component: the mapper on the PDP side.
  • Evidence: the Inway sends the body (fsc-infra/docker-compose.yml#L773-L775). The mapper reads the question and does not change it (ftvgraphql.go#L11-L13, #L89-L103). The changes are in PR #482 and PR #484.
  • Related: REQ-04, REQ-17, REQ-18, Q-16, ADR 0002.
  • Notes: design choice: for GraphQL, the demo follows the FTV GraphQL profile for AuthZEN. The profile work continues upstream. The Inway sends the body only with Content-Type: application/json. Without a body, the mapper fails closed.

docs.title: REQ-44: A channel adapter translates protocol, and the decision on source data lies with the PDP of the source
docs.text:
A channel adapter that GBO delivers MUST do only protocol translation and pass the request on. It MUST NOT decide which data of the source a party gets. It MUST NOT fetch or add decision information (consent, admission, designation) itself. It MUST NOT carry knowledge of a source or use case in code. Checks that belong to the channel protocol itself (wallet session, access token of the channel) stay with the channel.

A channel adapter MUST query the source through the source access that the source offers for all GBO interaction patterns. It MUST NOT ask a source for a channel-specific interface (koppelvlak).

  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: derived. The requirement serves P-10 and PSA S05. If the adapter takes part in the decision, the policy of the source does not alone decide what a party gets. The single interface follows from the design: PSA S07 and P-06 and P-08. Under S07, a bronhouder uses one logical interface for all GBO interaction patterns ("een bronhouder gebruikt voor de GBO-interactiepatronen één logisch interface").
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: channel adapters (in demo v0.9.0, the EUDI adapter).
  • Evidence: the query and the mapping come from the source metadata, with no source-specific query (eudi-adapter/main.go#L16-L21, PR #219). The adapter does not fetch consent. The PDP judges (#L10-L14). No test exists.
  • Related: REQ-64, REQ-45, F-31, Q-17.
  • Notes: the adapter takes the BSN from the PID disclosure and does not check the signature (#L23-L24). That gap falls under REQ-45 and is no decision of the adapter. This requirement and REQ-64 cover the removed REQ-51.

docs.title: REQ-48: Every rule checks actor and scope itself, and a request passes only if no check denies
docs.text:
Every rule of the PDP MUST check the actor and the scope of the request itself, in every regime. The actor MUST NOT follow only from the existence of an FSC contract or connection. The scope (fields and filters such as tax years) MUST NOT be taken from what an adapter or consumer declares. A field MUST be allowed only if a rule about it has no reason to deny on any check. The request MUST be allowed only if every requested field is allowed. A policy set MUST enforce with a test that every rule has its own actor check.

Case Outcome Consent given to another party denied: CONSENT_ACTOR_MISMATCH Year outside the consent, or no year filter denied: YEAR_NOT_COVERED PID regime, caller is not a designated issuer denied: ACTOR_NOT_ALLOWED PID regime, year outside the rule denied: YEAR_NOT_ALLOWED ASI rule, caller is not the ASIP denied: ACTOR_NOT_ALLOWED Integrator without a mandate for this rule denied: INTEGRATOR_NOT_REGISTERED One field denied, the rest allowed the whole request denied
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design: PSA S05 (a check against identity, service, legal basis (grondslag), and data scope, with the acting and the represented party, and allow or deny per field), D-11, FR-16 criteria 2 and 3, and FR-17 criteria 2 and 3.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the reference engine and the rules of the PDP.
  • Evidence: the actor-check test is not built: ICTU/GBO-demo#604. PR #507 and PR #464 built these parts:
    • all fields (engine.rego#L36-L41), the first rule without a reason (#L290-L293), and the mandate (#L246-L267)
    • DVT0001 (dvt0001.rego#L59-L68, #L82-L96)
    • EUD0001 (eud0001.rego#L45-L75, eudi_helper.rego#L13-L24)
    • the tests dvt0001_test.rego#L84, eud0001_test.rego#L65, and engine_test.rego#L315
    • the years, tested with a literal list, a schema default, null, and a variable in dvt0001_test.rego#L162-L202
    • the denial of a field without a decision, which is not left out (PR #519, engine.rego#L18-L23, tested in engine_test.rego#L775-L791)
    • a consent without scopes, which covers no year (dvt0001_test.rego#L183-L187)
  • Related: REQ-97, REQ-74, REQ-106, F-56, ADR 0034.
  • Notes:
    • Contract proposals are co-signed without a check of the grant content (F-56). This requirement is the compensating control. A rule without its own actor check, or an actor list derived from the contract, reopens that decision.
    • In demo v0.9.0, designated issuers and allowed years are fixed in the rules. With more parties or years, they belong in a register (REQ-61).
    • The test that checks every rule for its own actor check does not exist (#604).

docs.title: REQ-74: The authorization regime follows from the evidence a request carries
docs.text:
The regime under which the PDP judges a request MUST follow from the proof that the request carries. It MUST NOT follow from a property that only names the regime (no header, contract property, or claim). Only the rules of that regime MAY judge the request, so the deny reason comes from that regime. If a request carries more than one consent proof, it MUST be denied. If the absence of proof opens a regime, the actors of that regime MUST be disjoint from the actors under another regime. A test MUST enforce this for every environment in which the policy runs.

Case Outcome Consent token present, valid or not consent regime. Only DVT0001 and LVG0001 judge. No consent token PID regime. Only EUD0001, EUD0002, and ASI0001 judge. Two consent tokens denied: CONSENT_CONTEXT_INVALID
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: derived. The requirement serves P-01 and PSA S05. A consumer that can name its regime chooses the legal basis that it is judged on.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the reference engine and the source gateway. Interface agreement: which proof opens which regime.
  • Evidence: PR #363, PR #486, and PR #371 give this evidence:
    • The regime and the active rules are in engine.rego#L173-L181.
    • The check for two tokens is in consent.rego#L44-L62.
    • The tests are engine_test.rego#L227-L238 and consent_test.rego#L438. The disjointness test is engine_test.rego#L366-L376.
    • The source gateway acts on the same proof (bron-sidecar/main.go#L185-L188).
  • Related: REQ-18, REQ-48, REQ-06, REQ-79, REQ-45, F-70, Q-15, ADR 0031.
  • Notes:
    • The PID regime has no positive proof, only the absence of a consent token (ICTU/GBO-demo#133). For that reason, the last two sentences of the requirement are necessary.
    • The disjointness test knows only the local consumers. For the simulation, it gives no guarantee.
    • With positive PID evidence (REQ-45), these two sentences lapse.
    • Grants carry no properties. PR #363 removed flow, and PR #475 removed subject_id_type.

docs.title: REQ-97: Every rule names the FSC services it applies to
docs.text:
A rule of the PDP MUST name the FSC services that it applies to. The PDP MUST count a rule only on a request for one of those services. The service in the transport token that the source signed decides this. A rule MUST NOT allow fields on another service that happen to have the same key (Type.field). This prohibition also applies to a root field alone. A policy set MUST enforce with a test that every rule names its services.

  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: derived. The requirement serves PSA S07 and PSA S05. Under S07, every data request refers to exactly one service ("iedere gegevensvraag verwijst eenduidig naar een dienst"). A field key is unique only within one schema. Without a service binding, a rule for one source gives access to another source.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the reference engine and the rules of the PDP.
  • Evidence: ICTU/GBO-demo#525 and PR #527 give this evidence:
    • The service binding is in engine.rego#L183-L192.
    • The service comes from the token (ftvgraphql.go#L30-L33).
    • engine_test.rego#L471-L480 tests a root field alone.
    • #L497-L501 tests that every rule names its services.
  • Related: REQ-17, REQ-48, REQ-74, F-90.
  • Notes: a PDP that serves one source with one schema does not have the collision. The requirement stays for a PDP that serves more services, as in the demo.

docs.title: Removed numbers
docs.text:
These numbers are removed or merged into another requirement:

  • REQ-05 (several independent authorization axes): merged into REQ-48.
  • REQ-07 (policy as code, apart from the services): removed.
  • REQ-33 (sector grant check at token issuance, Manager role): removed.
  • REQ-34 (token binding at service call, Inway role): removed.
  • REQ-36 (untrusted catalog index for scope-dependent requests): removed.
  • REQ-43 (access basis from validated component identity): removed.
  • REQ-47 (plural organization permissions on one service): removed.
  • REQ-49 (FSC Inway forwards the body unchanged, no token-derived fields): removed.
  • REQ-50 (trust classification of transport context by header prefix): merged into REQ-18.
  • REQ-52 (AuthZEN endpoint directly behind the FSC Inway): removed. ADR 0002 records the decision.
  • REQ-53 (data transformation after authorization in a gateway): removed. For more information, see REQ-20, REQ-21, F-30, and F-37.
  • REQ-56 (dispatch per contract by grant properties): removed. REQ-74 partly replaces it.
  • REQ-70 (grant properties in a Group extension): removed.

docs.title: Query enforcement requirements
docs.text: The query enforcement requirement covers how the PDP decides on a GraphQL query: field by field, against the schema that the source runs. The requirement is generic. It applies to DvTP, EUDI issuance, and the ASI route. The PEP passes the query on unchanged (REQ-42). The PDP side parses it according to the FTV GraphQL profile for AuthZEN.

docs.title: REQ-17: The PDP decides on every field that the source runs, and denies an uncertain field list
docs.text:
The PDP MUST determine the requested fields as the source will run them, against the schema of the called service. The PDP MUST decide on each field separately. The PDP MUST deny a field for which no rule applies. If it is not certain that the field list is complete and correct, the PDP MUST deny the whole request.

The schema on which the PDP decides MUST have the same definition in every type, field, and argument as the schema that the source runs. The PDP MUST NOT add annotations other than those that the profile allows, such as authorization directives. A difference MUST be found before the PDP or the source goes into use with that difference.

The source gateway that GBO delivers MUST refuse a request that is not in the form that the PDP judges. Thus the source runs nothing that the PDP did not decide. The PDP MUST be able to allow only a read query. The PDP MUST deny a request that changes data or opens a subscription, also if a rule covers its fields.

Case Outcome Query cannot be parsed or is not valid against the schema denied: COVERAGE_UNVERIFIABLE / INVALID_QUERY. The consumer sees FIELD_NOT_PERMITTED Schema differs from the pinned schema of the service denied: CONFIG_ERROR / SCHEMA_MISMATCH A field without a rule (also introspection) denied: NO_APPLICABLE_RULE. The whole request is denied Source runs a schema that differs from the schema of the PDP (other type, extra argument or default, other member or enum value) not taken into use: the check fails and names the element Request reaches the source gateway in another form than the PDP judges (other path, a method other than POST, query string, other media type, Content-Encoding or Upgrade) refused by the gateway, nothing decrypted (code) Mutation or subscription denied: OPERATION_NOT_SUPPORTED. The consumer sees that code (code) Request without a data field (only __typename) denied: NO_DATA_FIELDS. The consumer sees that code (code) Every field allowed by a rule allowed
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • PSA S05. Under S05, the decision can allow or deny separate data or fields. A PEP denies by default if decision information is missing or not trusted ("de beslissing kan afzonderlijke gegevens of velden toestaan of weigeren", "een PEP weigert standaard bij ontbrekende of onbetrouwbare beslisinformatie").
    • The additional requirements for the source access API in the design principles. A consumer can only run data requests that are allowed in advance ("een afnemer kan alleen vooraf toegestane gegevensvragen uitvoeren").
    • P-02 and D-11.
    • FTV GraphQL profile for AuthZEN, "Transport subset" (guarantee H1) and "Ownership and drift" (guarantee H3).
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered components: the request mapper and the reference policy of the PDP, and the source gateway.
  • Evidence: PR #480, PR #482. Code and tests:
    • The deny on an uncertain list is in engine.rego#L129-L138. The closed world for each field is in #L282-L284. The tests are in engine_test.rego#L117-L130, #L172-L186, and mapper_test.go#L181-L182.
    • The subcodes of the mapper for an uncertain list are in mapper.go#L27-L43, tested in mapper_test.go#L19 (transport) and #L60 (body). Only a query operation passes (mapper.go#L193-L195).
    • Schema equality: PR #495, PR #496. The comparison is in drift.go#L13-L18, tested in drift_test.go#L49. CI enforces it (ci.yml#L184-L195).
    • Transport form at the source gateway: bron-sidecar/transport.go#L9-L52.
  • Related: REQ-08, REQ-42, REQ-97, F-90, Q-14, Q-16.
  • Notes:
    • Design choice: the PEP (FSC Inway) passes the body on without parsing. The PDP parses it according to the FTV GraphQL profile. Thus no PEP needs to know GraphQL.
    • The consumer does not learn which field was denied, or whether an unknown field exists. Thus the consumer cannot probe the schema.
    • In the demo, policy and sources are in one repository. So one check covers both sides of schema equality.
    • The FTV GraphQL profile ("Ownership and drift") runs the check in two places:
      • In the pipeline of the policy bundle, before the rollout of a bundle.
      • In the pipeline of the source, before a schema change goes live. For a source with its own release cycle, this part belongs to the bronhouder.

docs.title: Removed numbers
docs.text:
• REQ-25 (consumer-facing schema carries no BSN field names): removed. See REQ-79 and REQ-17.
  • REQ-26 (PEP translates between consumer schema and source schema): removed. See REQ-79 and REQ-17.
  • REQ-27 (PDP enforces identity binding by AST argument inspection): removed. See REQ-79 and REQ-17.

docs.title: Data minimization requirements
docs.text: The data minimization requirements apply to the source access. A request selects fields, and a GBO component does not store source data. The requirements are generic. They apply to DvTP, EUDI issuance, and the ASI route. The rule that consent covers a whole data set applies only to DvTP. That rule is REQ-10 on the consent page.

docs.title: REQ-08: Source access delivers only the fields that the request selects
docs.text:
The source access MUST support selective data requests. A request MUST be able to state for each field which data it asks for, and the source MUST deliver only those fields.

  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • PSA S07. Under S07, the API supports selective data requests that are registered in advance ("de API ondersteunt vooraf geregistreerde, selectieve gegevensvragen").
    • D-09 and the additional requirements for the source access API in the design principles.
    • P-02.
  • Addressee: interface agreement: the source access API.
  • Evidence: the sources in the demo offer GraphQL (source mock, graphql-server/main.go#L307). The PDP decides for each selected field (REQ-17).
  • Related: REQ-17, REQ-92, Q-16, ADR 0001.
  • Notes:
    • Design choice: GraphQL, as the PSA proposes. The API profile is not approved.
    • Selection alone does not minimize, because the consumer can select everything. The limit comes from REQ-17.
    • The demo reads "registered in advance" as the fields that a rule covers. It does not read it as a list of fixed queries.

docs.title: REQ-11: A GBO component fetches source data from the source for each request and does not store it
docs.text:
A GBO-delivered component that processes source data MUST fetch that data from the source for each request. It MUST NOT store the data after it handles that request.

  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design. D-05 and P-08. Under D-05, GBO makes no permanent data warehouse ("GBO maakt geen structureel gegevensmagazijn").
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: channel adapters, ASIP, and translation layer.
  • Evidence: the EUDI adapter calls the source through FSC for every issuance (eudi-adapter/main.go#L407-L422). The ASIP reads the BRP through FSC (PR #527). No test shows that nothing is stored.
  • Related: REQ-46, REQ-92.
  • Notes:
    • The adapter stores source metadata (registration, freshness). It does not store source data.
    • D-05 allows temporary storage if it is necessary and lawful, with a recorded retention period. Such an exception then goes here as a note.
    • Nobody checked whether the issuance server (nl-wallet, no GBO component) keeps attributes between the fetch and the issuance.

docs.title: Removed numbers
docs.text: • REQ-09 (fields limited to a catalog set for each scope): merged into REQ-17.

docs.title: Policy management guidelines
docs.text: The guidelines (RL-NN) cover the management side of the authorization function: how a source manages its policy and rolls it out. They are generic and apply to every source, whatever the route (DvTP, EUDI, ASI). They are guidelines for bronhouders and are no system requirements. The design is in PSA S06.

docs.title: Why the items are guidelines and not requirements
docs.text:
The policy administration point (PAP) and the PDP are at the source. The PDP is behind the FSC Inway of the bronhouder. The management function (OpenFTV Manager) serves exactly that PDP. The demo runs all of this in one compose stack. That is a demo artifact and makes no statement about the architecture.

So all policy management is in the domain of the bronhouder:

  • The policy engine is a product that the source chooses. The demo uses OpenFTV, but that is a demo choice and is no rule.
  • The policy itself belongs to the source (P-10).
  • The management and deployment process around the policy is an internal matter of the source.

A GBO MUST on these points is a requirement on the installation of another party. Nobody can enforce it, and it conflicts with the federated direction of Q-02. For that reason, each item is a guideline, written as SHOULD, with the reason and the evidence. A bronhouder can use a guideline as advice, or as a selection criterion for an engine choice. A guideline is no testable requirement.

The promotion rule is this: a guideline becomes a requirement (REQ) only when GBO delivers the management function itself (a reference implementation or a shared facility). Then it is a requirement on a GBO artifact and moves to a requirements page. In this design, policy management stays with each source (Q-21, answered, ADR 0021). Bundle signing (ICTU/GBO-demo#426) is not planned inside one organization. Each guideline names the extra condition that makes it a requirement.

The requirements on GBO components are on other pages: REQ-59 (policy version in the decision record) and REQ-60 (minimization when the chain builds the PDP input).

Terminology: the OpenFTV Manager on this page is the PAP and PIP half of the authorization function. It is a different component from the FSC Manager (contracts and token issuance). Always name which Manager you mean.

docs.title: RL-01: Deliver policy as a versioned bundle instead of baking it into the PDP
docs.text:
A source SHOULD deliver its access policy to the PDP as an identified, versioned bundle, with version control as the source of the content. The PDP SHOULD be able to check the origin and integrity of that bundle. A policy baked into the PDP image, or mounted as a volume, makes every change a rebuild or restart. It also makes the active version hard to trace.

  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design. PSA S06. Under S06, policy is machine-readable and versioned. The recipient can check the authenticity and integrity of published policy sets ("beleid is machineleesbaar, versieerbaar", "de ontvanger kan de authenticiteit en integriteit van gepubliceerde beleidssets controleren").
  • Addressee: guideline for bronhouders.
  • Evidence: a bundle with a version (gbo-pdp.yaml#L11-L17). If PDP_BUNDLE_MANAGER is set, the PDP fetches the bundle (docker-compose.yml#L145-L149), as in make demo-manager.
  • Related: REQ-59, F-09, Q-21, ADR 0021.
  • Notes: in the default stack, the demo bakes the policy into the PDP image. Only make demo-manager delivers a bundle. Signing is missing and not planned (#426). Inside one organization, integrity belongs to the configuration of that organization.
  • Promotion rule: if bundles come from outside the own organization, signing becomes a system requirement.

docs.title: RL-02: Authorize the management API with its own policy set and deny on an empty store
docs.text:
The management API of a policy engine (write policy, publish, attributes) SHOULD be authorized with its own policy set, apart from the policy that decides on data requests. An empty or unreadable management policy store SHOULD lead to a denial and SHOULD NOT give open access.

  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: derived. The guideline serves D-11. If management runs through the decision policy, the outcome is undefined, or the decision policy must open the management API.
  • Addressee: guideline for bronhouders, and a selection criterion for an engine choice.
  • Evidence: an own Cedar store that fails closed (docker-compose.yml#L254-L269, admin.cedar).
  • Related: F-51, ADR 0021.
  • Notes: the engine in use switches authorization off while the policy store is empty. This happens after a fresh install, after a failed migration, or with an empty volume. Check this behavior for every engine choice. The PDP itself does not follow this guideline: the decision policy covers its management endpoints. For that reason, the PDP fetches bundles and does not receive them (gbo-pdp.yaml#L18-L32).
  • Promotion rule: the general promotion rule.

docs.title: RL-03: Separate writing from publishing, and publish with a non-personal, short-lived identity
docs.text:
Policy management SHOULD have read, write, and publish as separate rights. The API SHOULD enforce these rights. Enforcement in the user interface alone is not enough. Publication from version control SHOULD use a non-personal identity and a short-lived token. It SHOULD NOT use a shared administrator account or a long-lived key.

  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design. D-11 and PSA S06 (owner, approver). Under D-11, management rights are limited, temporary, and granted in a way that can be shown ("beheerrechten zijn beperkt, tijdelijk en aantoonbaar toegekend").
  • Addressee: guideline for bronhouders.
  • Evidence: roles (realm-gbo.json#L11-L19), a deployment identity with a short-lived token (README.md#L20-L31), and enforcement in the API (admin.cedar).
  • Related: REQ-59, Q-21.
  • Notes: the demo keeps the roles in a local realm at the facility, and the roles are not federated. The source decides who fills the roles, and through which IdP. The management interface reads rights from a top-level roles claim, which is a token form of the supplier.
  • Promotion rule: the general promotion rule.

docs.title: RL-04: Withdraw policy instead of deleting it, and reconcile the deployed set with version control
docs.text:
A source SHOULD withdraw policy that no longer applies, instead of deleting it. A withdrawal takes the policy out of the active bundle and keeps the record and the history. The publication process SHOULD reconcile the deployed set with version control at every publication. Thus what disappears from version control also disappears from the active set.

  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design. PSA S06. S06 asks for a change history, an emergency procedure, and a rollback procedure ("wijzigingshistorie", "een spoedprocedure en terugrolprocedure zijn beschikbaar").
  • Addressee: guideline for bronhouders.
  • Evidence: seed-openftv-manager.py#L116 (retire_stale).
  • Related: REQ-59, F-52.
  • Notes: the store is cumulative. Without reconciliation, a renamed rule stays in the bundle (F-52). A store that keeps withdrawn policy is a precondition for REQ-59.
  • Promotion rule: the general promotion rule.

docs.title: RL-05: Validate a bundle before activation, and fall back visibly to the last valid set
docs.text:
A bundle SHOULD be validated as a whole before publication: it compiles, it has no duplicate names, and the policy tests pass. The publisher SHOULD get feedback. A PDP that receives an invalid bundle, or cannot fetch a bundle, SHOULD continue to decide on the last valid set. It SHOULD report which version is active, and that a newer version did not load.

  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design. PSA S06. Under S06, tests validate changes before publication. On a failure, the components fall back in a controlled way ("tests valideren wijzigingen vóór publicatie", "bij storingen vallen zij gecontroleerd terug").
  • Addressee: guideline for bronhouders.
  • Evidence: make policy-check runs before every start (Makefile#L92, PR #372, duplicate names in PR #510). CI runs opa check and opa test (ci.yml#L130). Visible fallback: not built.
  • Related: REQ-59, F-52, Q-21.
  • Notes: one bad rule gives no denial. It gives a failure on all requests (F-52). The engine in use reports a module that does not compile as loaded, and continues to decide on the previous policy (#151). A PDP can report healthy without ever receiving a bundle (PR #337).
  • Promotion rule: if more policy owners share one bundle or one PDP, an error of one owner must not stop the other. Then this guideline becomes a system requirement (Q-21).

docs.title: Consent requirements (DvTP)
docs.text:
These requirements cover the consent of the citizen in the DvTP channel. They cover the consent proof and its lifecycle, and the start of a request. They also cover the roles of portal and register, access and revocation by the citizen, and the data model of the register. For the design, see consent facility (toestemmingsvoorziening).

This page has the following parts:

  • Consent proof and use
  • Consent lifecycle requirements
  • Consent initiation and return requirements
  • Role split between consent register (toestemmingsregister) and consent portal (toestemmingsportaal) (S01/S02)
  • Citizen access and revocation requirements
  • Consent register data model

docs.title: Consent proof and use
docs.text:
In the DvTP route (Delen van gegevens via Toestemming met Private dienstverleners), a citizen gives consent to a private service provider (dienstverlener) to get data about the citizen from a source. The requirements on this page cover three topics:

  • what a consent covers
  • what the citizen sees and confirms
  • how the authorization chain checks a consent at every request

The consent portal is the portal UI inside MijnOverheid plus the consent portal backend. It records the choice of the citizen. The consent register stores the consent and issues a signed consent proof. The consumer sends that proof with each request. The PDP of the source checks the proof itself, and asks the register for the current status over FSC (ADR 0032). If an integrator connects, the consent binds the represented party (ADR 0034).

The related topic pages are consent lifecycle, consent register data model, role split S01/S02, initiation and return, citizen access and revocation, and pseudonymization.

Evidence links to gbo-demo point at tag v0.9.0. The linked files did not change between the review commit 819f3eb and v0.9.0.

docs.title: REQ-10: Consent covers a whole data set, and the citizen does not pick fields within a set
docs.text:
A consent MUST apply to one or more indivisible data sets (scopes). It MUST NOT apply to separate fields. The citizen MUST NOT be able to exclude fields within a set.

Under a consent for a set, the PDP MUST allow exactly the fields that the service fixes for that set. The PDP MUST NOT allow more fields. The PDP MUST NOT allow only a part of them because of a field choice in the consent. If a request asks fields of a set without consent, the PDP MUST deny it.

Case Outcome Consent for the set, and the request asks fields of that set allowed (code) The request also asks a field that is not part of the set that field denied: NO_APPLICABLE_RULE (code) Consent only for another set denied: SCOPE_NOT_ALLOWED, or YEAR_NOT_COVERED for another tax year (code) The citizen switches a set off no consent for that set. The citizen cannot switch off a part of a set (code)
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • FR-10 criteria 1 and 2, and FR-38 criteria 4 and 5.
    • PSA S01 (data scope: "gegevensscope").
    • GO, pattern C (a specific data set: "een specifieke gegevensset").
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the portal UI, the consent register, and the reference policy.
  • Evidence: PR #511, PR #580. Code and tests:
    • The proof carries only scopes (consent_token.go#L70-L80).
    • The fields of the set are in dvt0001.rego#L27-L45. The set check is in #L61-L96.
    • The tests are in engine_test.rego#L210-L220, #L265-L270, and #L288-L294.
    • The UI has one toggle per set in ScopeToggle.tsx#L9-L25.
    • PR #509: a consent for another question does not open the root field either (dvt0001_test.rego#L91-L102).
  • Related: REQ-08, REQ-12, REQ-121, F-03, F-17, Q-03, Q-45.
  • Notes: in the demo, the rule fixes which fields belong to a set. The portal UI fixes this again, separately. This information belongs in the service catalog (dienstencatalogus) (ICTU/GBO-demo#382). Whether the design enforces a minimal mandatory set is open: Q-45. In demo v0.9.0, the register and the proof accept a field list per scope (consented_fields) that no component reads.

docs.title: REQ-12: A consent is bound to one consumer, one service, and a named data scope
docs.text:
Every consent MUST be bound to one consumer (OIN), one service with its purpose, and at least one named data set. The portal MUST NOT offer consent for a request without a purpose or a data set. The consent register MUST NOT record a consent without a consumer, a service, or a data set. If a consent has no data set or no purpose, the consent portal backend MUST refuse it with CONSENT_SCOPE_MISSING. The UI then offers no button.

Case Outcome Consumer, purpose, and at least one known set recorded (code) No consumer not recorded. The register refuses (code: HTTP 400 dienstverlener_oin is required) No set chosen button disabled. The backend refuses: CONSENT_SCOPE_MISSING (not built in the backend in demo v0.9.0) No purpose refused: CONSENT_SCOPE_MISSING (the demo fills in hypotheek (mortgage), which deviates) A set that the portal does not know no consent question. The citizen sees the message unknown request (shown as "Onbekend verzoek") (code)
  • Status: draft
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • FR-09 criteria 1 and 2.
    • PSA S01 (a consent record holds at least the consumer, service, purpose, and data scope: "een toestemmingsrecord bevat minimaal … afnemer, dienst, doel, gegevensscope").
    • PSA F2 (consent is free, specific, and informed: "toestemming is vrij, specifiek, geïnformeerd …").
    • GO, pattern C (a specific purpose, consumer, and data set: "een specifiek doel, een specifieke afnemer en een specifieke gegevensset").
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the portal UI, the consent portal backend, and the consent register.
  • Evidence: the work to build is ICTU/GBO-demo#601. Code and tests:
    • The consumer is mandatory in main.go#L417-L420.
    • The UI shows no button without a set in PortaalConsent.tsx#L164-L171.
    • The unknown set is in #L63-L75.
    • A part is not built: the backend and the register do not check the set and the purpose.
  • Related: REQ-10, REQ-37, REQ-68, REQ-106, REQ-111, Q-46, Q-49, Q-69.
  • Notes:
    • The purpose is in the record but not in the proof, so the PDP does not check it.
    • In the demo, the service follows only from the set. The service catalog adds a service identifier (ICTU/GBO-demo#382).
    • FR-09 criterion 2 also names the integrator in the record. This point is open in Q-46.
    • Q-69 asks whether the proof must bind the purpose, so that the PDP checks it (FR-17 criterion 1).

docs.title: REQ-14: After revocation, the chain denies every later request on that consent
docs.text:
After the citizen revoked a consent, the authorization chain MUST deny every later request on that consent. This also applies to a proof that was valid before the revocation. The deny MUST work without any action by the consumer and without a message to the consumer.

Case Outcome Consent revoked, and a request with the proof denied: CONSENT_WITHDRAWN (code) The same proof before and after the revocation first allowed, then denied. The proof itself does not change (code)
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • FR-23 criterion 3, FR-24, FR-17 criterion 4, and FR-11 criterion 3.
    • PSA S01 (the registration supports revocation, and the authorization checks the status at the time of the data request: "de registratie ondersteunt … intrekking", and "de autorisatie controleert de actuele status op het moment van de gegevensvraag").
    • PSA S02 (the consent register handles a revocation without undue delay: "het toestemmingsregister verwerkt een intrekking zonder onnodige vertraging").
    • GO (revocation has direct effect: "Intrekking heeft direct effect").
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the consent register and the reference policy.
  • Evidence: PR #371, PR #390. Code and tests:
    • The revocation is in main.go#L585-L610.
    • The status check in the policy is in consent.rego#L270-L280.
    • The tests are in consent_test.rego#L197-L205 and status_test.go#L23-L48.
  • Related: REQ-38, REQ-68, REQ-75, REQ-109, Q-42, Q-48.
  • Notes: design choices:
    • A revocation changes only the status in the register. The record stays, and the citizen sees it as revoked (shown as "Ingetrokken").
    • The revocation does not touch the proof, the FSC contract, or sessions at the consumer. The consumer gets no message.
    • The deny follows because the PDP asks the status at every request (REQ-68). REQ-75 sets how fast this must work, and whether another mechanism is allowed.
    • The chain does not recall data that the consumer got before the revocation (FR-24). For that data, the portal refers the citizen to the consumer (FR-25, REQ-120).
    • The register does not record when the citizen revoked the consent: Q-48.

docs.title: REQ-68: The PDP decides only on a consent whose origin, binding, and current status it establishes itself
docs.text:
The consent proof of a request MUST bind at least these items: the citizen, the granted sets, the consumer, the authorization service, and the validity. The proof MUST bind the citizen as a value per receiving party (REQ-80). The consumer is the party to whom the citizen gave the consent. The authorization service is the service for which the proof is meant.

Before it allows, the PDP MUST establish itself that the register issued the proof, and that the proof is unchanged. It MUST establish that the binding is complete. It MUST establish that the consumer is the party on whose behalf the request is made. It MUST also establish the current status of the consent.

If the PDP cannot establish one of these points, it MUST deny. The sets, the citizen, and the consumer on which the PDP decides MUST come from that established proof.

Case Outcome Valid proof, consent active, consumer matches allowed (code) Signature does not verify, unknown key, or another algorithm denied: CONSENT_SIGNATURE_INVALID (code) The PDP cannot get the verification keys denied: CONSENT_KEYS_UNAVAILABLE. The consumer sees ACCESS_DENIED (code) Another issuer, another audience, another type, or a mandatory claim is missing denied: CONSENT_CONTEXT_INVALID (code) Consent given to another consumer denied: CONSENT_ACTOR_MISMATCH (code) The register does not know the consent denied: CONSENT_NOT_FOUND (code) The PDP cannot establish the status (time-out, error, unexpected answer) denied: CONSENT_STATUS_UNAVAILABLE. The consumer sees ACCESS_DENIED (code)
  • Status: draft
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • PSA S05 (the PDP can consult relevant information sources, such as the consent register, and a PEP denies by default if decision information is missing or untrusted: "de PDP kan relevante informatiebronnen raadplegen … toestemmingsregister", and "een PEP weigert standaard bij ontbrekende of onbetrouwbare beslisinformatie").
    • PSA S01 (the authorization checks the status at the time of the data request: "de autorisatie controleert de actuele status op het moment van de gegevensvraag").
    • FR-17 criterion 1, and FR-26 criteria 1 and 3.
    • P-01.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the consent register (issuer) and the reference policy (verifier). Interface agreement: the form of the proof between consumer and source.
  • Evidence: PR #238, PR #371, PR #390, PR #469, PR #477. Code and tests:
    • The issuance is in consent_token.go#L130-L152.
    • The verification is in consent.rego#L109-L186.
    • The status check is in #L270-L280.
    • The other checks are in dvt0001.rego#L49-L59.
    • The tests are in consent_test.rego#L172-L193, #L291-L343, #L380-L424, and dvt0001_test.rego#L84-L87.
  • Related: REQ-14, REQ-18, REQ-19, REQ-74, REQ-75, REQ-76, REQ-79, REQ-80, REQ-82, REQ-106, F-61, F-72, F-78, Q-44, Q-55, Q-68, ADR 0032.
  • Notes: ADR 0032 records the design choice. The proof is a token that the register signs (gbo-consent+jwt, ES256). The consumer sends it with each request. The demo handles the token as follows:
    • The Rego policy verifies the token itself. The request mapper only maps GraphQL.
    • The claims are consent_id, encrypted_subject, scopes, scope_entries, dienstverlener_oin, and valid_until, plus iss, aud, iat, nbf, exp, and jti.
    • The policy allows 30 s clock skew.
    • The policy keeps the verification keys (JWKS) in a cache for five minutes. On an unknown key ID, it gets them again at once, without a fallback to old keys.
    • The policy asks the status at every request, without a cache.
    • The policy compares the consumer with the represented party. For an integrator, see REQ-106. Q-68 asks whether the FSC Peer ID can count as the OIN.
    • The status is not in the PDP input. For this reason, the PDP puts the consent that it got in its answer (F-72).
    • The proof carries no version (F-78).
    • Q-55 covers the key location and rotation.
    • A pseudonym for the service provider itself is not built (ICTU/GBO-demo#478).

docs.title: REQ-75: Consent status is available within a set propagation time, availability, and latency
docs.text:
The consent register MUST deliver the current status of a consent within a set maximum propagation time. The propagation time runs from the revocation by the citizen to the first deny in the chain. The register MUST also meet a set availability and a set latency per query. If the status cannot be established in time, the chain MUST deny (REQ-68). The mechanism (query per request, status list, or push) MAY be chosen freely, as long as it meets the set values. If a mechanism has a propagation time of more than zero, it MUST record that time.

  • Status: draft
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • PSA S01 (the authorization checks the status at the time of the data request: "de autorisatie controleert de actuele status op het moment van de gegevensvraag").
    • PSA S02 (without undue delay: "zonder onnodige vertraging").
    • PSA S05 (rules for error handling, time-outs, and fail-safe behavior: "regels voor foutafhandeling, time-outs en fail-safe gedrag").
    • GO (revocation has direct effect: "Intrekking heeft direct effect").
    • FR-11 criterion 3, and FR-17 criterion 4.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the consent register and the status check in the reference policy.
  • Evidence: PR #371, PR #390. Code and tests:
    • The query per request is in consent.rego#L190-L200 and #L268-L280.
    • The tests are in consent_test.rego#L202-L214 and #L303-L314.
    • The values are not set.
  • Related: REQ-14, REQ-68, REQ-76, F-61, F-68, Q-05, Q-24, Q-47.
  • Notes:
    • The management organization sets the values with the owner of the register. The volumes are unknown (Q-47).
    • The demo asks per request, so the propagation time is zero in practice. The demo queries with a 2 s time-out.
    • PR #390 measured the query over FSC once: p50 14.5 ms, maximum 82 ms, and about 290 ms for the first query after a start.
    • The mechanism also affects the audit. With a status call per request, the LDV records of the register show which sources one processing touched (FR-31, F-68). A status list removes that information.

docs.title: REQ-76: The register gives consent status only to an authenticated, authorized PDP, over FSC, and records who asked
docs.text:
The consent register MUST give the status of a consent only to an authenticated, authorized component. That component is the PDP of a source that offers the service for which the consent applies. The query MUST go over FSC.

The register MUST record the verified identity of the caller in its processing log (REQ-72). Along the same path, only the status of the register MUST be reachable.

Case Outcome PDP peer with a contract asks the status status delivered. The peer is the processor in the LDV record (code) Query without an FSC peer denied: HTTP 401 (code) Another path than the status through the status service (detail, list, revoke) denied (code) Peer with a contract, but not the PDP of a source of that service denied. Not built in demo v0.9.0: the demo delivers the status (code)
  • Status: draft
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • PSA S01 (only the citizen and authorized components have access to consent, through a standardized PIP interface for queries: "alleen de burger en bevoegde componenten hebben toegang tot toestemming", and "gestandaardiseerd PIP-koppelvlak voor raadpleging").
    • PSA S05 (connection of PIP sources: "aansluiting van PIP-bronnen").
    • GO (FSC as the connectivity standard).
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the consent register. Interface agreement: the status service over FSC.
  • Evidence: PR #390. Code and tests:
    • The status service is in status.go#L43-L99.
    • The query through the Outway is in consent.rego#L39.
    • The tests are in status_test.go#L13-L96, ldv_test.go#L204-L207, and consent_test.rego#L216-L219.
    • The limit to the PDP of a source of the service is not built (ICTU/GBO-demo#382).
  • Related: REQ-39, REQ-46, REQ-68, REQ-72, REQ-75, F-68, Q-23, Q-58.
  • Notes:
    • In the demo, the PDP queries through its own Outway (peer …0800) and the Inway of the register (peer …0700, service consent-status).
    • The register serves the status on its own listener, which serves nothing else. In demo v0.9.0, the portal-facing listener does not answer status calls.
    • The Manager of the register signs a contract only for peers admitted in the admission register (toelatingsregister): the PDP peer. Thus in the demo, the FSC contract is the authorization.
    • The register can check which source belongs to which service only with the catalog.
    • The status service trusts the Fsc-Authorization header that the Inway passes on. For this reason, the status service must be reachable only through that Inway. In the demo, a component can also reach it directly on the compose network.
    • Every query over FSC is a separate transaction. This counts in the choice of mechanism under REQ-75.

docs.title: REQ-106: An integrator acts only with a registered mandate, and the consent binds the represented party
docs.text:
If an integrator calls on behalf of a service provider, the authorization decision MUST check the consent against the represented party. It MUST NOT check the consent against the party that makes the connection.

The connecting party MUST have a registered mandate for that service provider and that use. If there is no mandate, the request MUST be denied. A mandate MUST have a validity. Outside that validity, a request MUST be denied as if there is no mandate.

A contract in which a party connects on behalf of another party MAY come into force only if that representation is registered.

Case Outcome Consent for service provider X, and integrator registered for X and this rule allowed Consent given to another service provider denied: CONSENT_ACTOR_MISMATCH Integrator registered only for another rule denied: INTEGRATOR_NOT_REGISTERED Integrator suspended denied: INTEGRATOR_NOT_REGISTERED Mandate not in force at that time, or expired denied: INTEGRATOR_NOT_REGISTERED (proposal: not built) The admission register delivers no data denied: INTEGRATOR_REGISTER_UNAVAILABLE Consent given to the integrator itself instead of the service provider denied: CONSENT_ACTOR_MISMATCH No registration of the representation contract stays proposed: DELEGATION_NOT_REGISTERED Service provider suspended, for a delegated contract contract stays proposed: PARTY_NOT_ACTIVE The service provider calls itself, with or without an integrator in the chain allowed, unchanged
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • FR-18, and FR-37 criteria 3 and 4.
    • PSA S05 (if an actor acts on behalf of another party, the authorization decision uses both the acting actor and the represented party, with the role, scope, and validity of the authority: "als een actor namens een andere partij handelt, gebruikt de autorisatiebeslissing zowel de handelende actor als de vertegenwoordigde partij", and "rol, reikwijdte en geldigheid van de bevoegdheid").
    • PSA S04 (a technical intermediary for transport or connectivity only gets no authority from that role to act on behalf of another party: "een technische intermediair voor alleen transport of connectiviteit krijgt door die rol geen bevoegdheid om namens een andere partij te handelen"). The representation context holds the role or capacity, the scope, and the validity ("rol of hoedanigheid, reikwijdte en geldigheid").
    • Tightened: the requirement also applies when the contract comes into force.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the reference policy for requests and contracts, and the admission register with the mandates. Interface agreement: the FSC delegation (DelegatedServiceConnectionGrant). Nothing changes for the consent components, because the proof already binds the service provider (REQ-68).
  • Evidence: ICTU/GBO-demo#379, PR #464. The demo builds this as an opt-in path (make demo-integrator, documented in integrator.md). Code and tests:
    • The represented party is in lib.rego#L55-L72.
    • The mandate is in engine.rego#L246-L267.
    • The contract is in autosign.rego#L119-L139.
    • The tests are in engine_test.rego#L613-L721, dvt0001_test.rego#L113-L126, and autosign_test.rego#L171-L203.
  • Related: REQ-61, REQ-68, REQ-110, AV-06, F-56, F-73, Q-12, Q-46, Q-68, ADR 0034.
  • Notes:
    • The represented party is the FSC delegator. If there is no delegator, it is the subject ID of the caller.
    • The mandates are in the admission register and reach the PDP as acts_for.
    • Q-46 asks whether the integrator also belongs in the proof, or whether the mandate in the register is sufficient.
    • The design does not enforce the processor side of FR-18 (processor agreement, no lasting storage) technically. That side is in AV-06.
    • For a contract, the policy sees only the pair, and not who represents whom. At every request, the policy does check the direction.
    • An integrator is always a processor (AV-06), so its role needs no separate check.

docs.title: REQ-107: Consent can be given only after confirmation that the citizen saw the information
docs.text:
The UI of the consent portal MUST make the action "give consent" available only after the citizen confirmed that they saw the information shown. The confirmation mechanism MUST be accessible according to WCAG 2.1 AA. If a request to give consent has no confirmation, the consent portal backend MUST refuse it, before any processing.

Case Outcome Not confirmed button disabled Confirmed, and at least one scope chosen button active, consent recorded Confirmation undone again button disabled again Request to the backend without confirmation, for example directly on the API refused: CONFIRMATION_MISSING. No record, and no activation or transformation at BSNk Keyboard or screen reader only confirming and giving work
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • FR-08 criteria 1 to 3.
    • FR-09 (dependency: store only after the confirmation of FR-08).
    • PSA F2 (consent is free, specific, informed, unambiguous, and provable: "toestemming is vrij, specifiek, geïnformeerd, ondubbelzinnig en aantoonbaar").
    • PSA S02 (the interaction meets accessibility requirements: "de interactie voldoet aan toegankelijkheidseisen").
    • Tightened: FR-08 asks to block the button in the UI. This requirement also lets the backend enforce it.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the portal UI inside MijnOverheid and the consent portal backend.
  • Evidence: not built: ICTU/GBO-demo#598. The demo has no confirmation. When the citizen chooses one scope, the button becomes active (PortaalConsent.tsx#L164-L171).
  • Related: REQ-12, REQ-24, Q-49, Q-51.
  • Notes:
    • The requirement chooses no mechanism. FR-08 gives a checkbox, or mandatory scrolling with a confirm button, as examples.
    • A separate field with the moment of confirmation is not necessary. The backend refuses without confirmation, so every recorded consent is confirmed.
    • Whether the register must record which information the citizen saw is open: Q-51.
    • The confirmation comes from the client, as a field in the request. The check catches a client that skips the step (a UI error, another client). It does not catch a caller that sends the field itself.
    • The design accepts this gap. The identity comes from the login (REQ-24), so only the citizen can forge the field, and only for their own consent.

docs.title: REQ-117: Before choosing, the citizen sees in plain language who asks what, for what, and for how long
docs.text:
Before the choice, the portal UI MUST show the name of the consumer, the service with its purpose, and the validity period. Per data set, it MUST show the data elements that the consumer gets, and whether the set is mandatory or optional. Per element, it MUST show the bronhouder that supplies it, without the values.

The portal UI MUST show that the consumer is an admitted participant. This statement MUST be based on the admission that the consent portal backend establishes in the register (REQ-111). The portal UI MUST state that the route is voluntary, and which equivalent alternative exists.

The portal UI MUST NOT offer as a choice the form in which a source recognizes the citizen (BSN or pseudonym). That form follows from the authorization of the source (REQ-82).

The texts MUST be at language level B1. The legal description MUST stay available. The description of sets and elements MUST come from the service description that the consent facility knows. It MUST NOT come from the request of the consumer.

Case Outcome Request for known sets consumer, purpose, valid until, and per set the title and description in B1 (code) Data elements per set per set the elements, without values (proposal: the demo shows only title and description) A set with elements of more than one bronhouder per element the bronhouder (proposal: not built) Admitted, active consumer the screen states that the consumer is admitted (proposal: not built) Mandatory and optional sets the screen shows a mandatory set as mandatory, and the citizen cannot switch it off (proposal) Voluntariness and alternative stated on the screen (proposal: not built) The citizen refuses back to the consumer with status=denied, and no consent (code)
  • Status: draft
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • FR-05 criteria 1 to 5, FR-07 criteria 1 and 2, FR-30 criterion 3, and FR-38 criterion 1.
    • PSA S02 (the citizen sees in plain language the consumer, service, purpose, data scope, duration, and consequences. The setup offers an equivalent alternative if law or policy requires it. The interface does not present these as a real choice: "de burger ziet in begrijpelijke taal de afnemer, dienst, doel, gegevensscope, duur en gevolgen", "de inrichting biedt een gelijkwaardig alternatief als wetgeving of beleid dat vereist", and "de interface presenteert deze niet als inhoudelijke keuze").
    • PSA F2 (consent is free, specific, and informed: "toestemming is vrij, specifiek, geïnformeerd …").
    • P-13.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the portal UI inside MijnOverheid. The consent portal backend delivers name and purpose from the registration (REQ-111).
  • Evidence: partly built. Code and tests:
    • The screen is in PortaalConsent.tsx#L115-L149. The refusal is in #L100-L106.
    • The UI shows one set per card in ScopeToggle.tsx#L9-L25.
    • The descriptions are in scopeGroups.ts#L8-L30.
    • No test covers what the screen shows.
    • Not built: the elements per set, mandatory or optional, and the voluntariness and alternative.
  • Related: REQ-10, REQ-12, REQ-19, REQ-37, REQ-82, REQ-107, REQ-111, REQ-121, REQ-122, F-98, Q-13, Q-45, Q-76.
  • Notes:
    • Design choice in the demo: the UI fixes the sets and descriptions. The elements are in the data (fields), but the UI does not show them.
    • In the demo, the validity period comes from the request.
    • Who sets the period, and whether the citizen must be able to change it (FR-05 criterion 5, FR-11 criterion 1), is open: Q-13.
    • Whether the period can differ per source is open: Q-76.
    • FR-05 does not work out which "gevolgen" (consequences, S02) the citizen sees.
    • Supervision of voluntariness is an open decision of S02.
    • S02 also calls pseudonymization transparent to the citizen ("transparant voor de burger"). The GBO team asked the PSA authors whether that means invisible or explained (F-98).
    • A public list of admitted participants (FR-30 criterion 3, also for others: "ook voor anderen") is a task of the management organization.

docs.title: REQ-118: If a service excludes delegation, an authorized representative cannot give consent for it
docs.text:
This requirement applies to a service whose description excludes delegation. For such a service, the portal UI MUST NOT show a consent screen to a citizen who logged in on behalf of another person. If a consent is given under such a login, the consent portal backend MUST refuse it with DELEGATION_NOT_ALLOWED, before any processing. The citizen MUST then get a clear message that no representative can give consent for this service. A citizen who logged in with their own means MUST be admitted.

Whether a service excludes delegation MUST come from the service description that the consent facility knows. It MUST NOT come from the request of the consumer.

In two cases, the consent facility MUST refuse with DELEGATION_NOT_ALLOWED (fail-closed). In the first case, it cannot establish whether the login is on behalf of another person. In the second case, the login is on behalf of another person, and the service description does not state whether the service excludes delegation.

Case Outcome Service excludes delegation, and login on behalf of another person no consent screen, and a message to the representative. The backend refuses: DELEGATION_NOT_ALLOWED. No consent, and no activation or transformation at BSNk Service excludes delegation, and the citizen logs in for themselves consent screen Service allows delegation, and login with a valid authorization consent screen. Q-73 asks whose consent it then is The consent facility cannot establish whether the login is on behalf of another person refused: DELEGATION_NOT_ALLOWED, and no consent screen The service does not state whether it excludes delegation, and login on behalf of another person refused: DELEGATION_NOT_ALLOWED, and no consent screen The service does not state whether it excludes delegation, and the citizen logs in for themselves consent screen
  • Status: draft
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • FR-02 criteria 2, 3, and 5, with the dependency on FR-32. The setting per service follows from the legal basis (grondslag).
    • PSA S05 (if an actor acts on behalf of another party, the authorization decision uses both the acting actor and the represented party: "als een actor namens een andere partij handelt, gebruikt de autorisatiebeslissing zowel de handelende actor als de vertegenwoordigde partij").
    • Tightened: FR-02 asks to block access to the screen. This requirement also lets the backend enforce it. The backend also refuses if the login or the service does not establish it.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the portal UI inside MijnOverheid and the consent portal backend. MijnOverheid delivers whether the login is on behalf of another person (Q-61 sub-question 7). The management organization records the setting per service in the catalog.
  • Evidence: not built. The demo has no authorization (machtiging).
  • Related: REQ-24, REQ-40, REQ-119, REQ-121, Q-44, Q-61, Q-73.
  • Notes: if MijnOverheid already blocks earlier (Q-61 sub-question 7), the refusal in the backend is still necessary for a client that skips the step. REQ-119 and Q-44 cover whether the citizen returns after the message, and with which outcome.

docs.title: REQ-121: Screen, initiation check, and reference policy follow the same data-set description
docs.text:
The portal UI, the consent portal backend, and the reference policy MUST take the data sets from the same description of the service. Per set, that description holds the data elements with their bronhouder. It also holds whether the set is mandatory or optional, and the consumers that are allowed to ask for the set.

An administrator MUST be able to add or change a set without a code change in the portal UI or the consent portal backend.

Case Outcome An administrator adds a set to a service set usable in initiation and screen, without a new release of UI or backend (proposal) The reference policy allows under a set a field that the description does not name, or misses one a test of the policy set fails (proposal) The screen shows for a set an element that the description does not name a test fails (proposal)
  • Status: draft
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • FR-32 description and criterion 1, and FR-38 criterion 1.
    • FR-21 (description: the same elements as when the citizen gave consent).
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the portal UI, the consent portal backend, and the reference policy. The content of the description is a task of the management organization (Q-62).
  • Evidence: not built: ICTU/GBO-demo#382.
  • Related: REQ-10, REQ-37, REQ-38, REQ-64, REQ-117, F-74, F-98, Q-21, Q-45, Q-62, Q-69.
  • Notes:
    • In the demo, the sets are in the UI (scopeGroups.ts#L35-L43), and the fields are separately in the rule.
    • A source with its own policy (Q-21) is bound to REQ-10. This requirement does not bind it.
    • Q-45 asks whether the design enforces mandatory and optional sets.
    • FR-39 criterion 5 puts the link from catalog to scopes in a central policy. Under the decision on Q-21, the link belongs in the service description (F-98).

docs.title: REQ-122: The citizen gets a confirmation of their choice
docs.text:
After the citizen gave, refused, or revoked consent, the consent facility MUST give the citizen a confirmation of that choice. After giving, the confirmation MUST name the consumer, the service with its purpose, and the granted data sets. It MUST also name the valid-until moment. It MUST name these items as they are recorded.

After a revocation, the confirmation MUST name which consent is revoked. A confirmation MUST follow only a choice that is recorded. If recording fails, the citizen MUST be told so and see no confirmation.

Case Outcome Consent given and recorded confirmation with consumer, service, purpose, sets, and valid until. Then the return (REQ-119) The citizen refuses confirmation that no consent was given. Return with the outcome refusal Consent revoked confirmation of the revocation (FR-23, step C-10a) Recording or revoking fails error message. No confirmation, and no return as successful
  • Status: draft
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • PSA S02 (the citizen gets a confirmation of the choice made: "de burger ontvangt een bevestiging van de gemaakte keuze").
    • FR-23 with step C-10a, and FR-14.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the portal UI inside MijnOverheid and the consent portal backend.
  • Evidence: not checked.
  • Related: REQ-107, REQ-109, REQ-117, REQ-119, REQ-120, Q-43, Q-44, Q-61.
  • Notes:
    • The requirement chooses no form. The possible forms are these:
      • a screen before the return
      • a message in MijnOverheid
      • an entry in the overview to which the citizen can go directly
      • a combination of these forms
    • FR-14 asks for an automatic return. A screen before the return must fit with that (Q-61 sub-question 2).
    • Q-43 asks whether the register records a refusal. The confirmation to the citizen is separate from that question.

docs.title: Removed numbers
docs.text:
• REQ-13 (status check per request against the consent register as PIP): removed. The successors are REQ-68 and REQ-18.
  • REQ-15 (no BSN in the consumer request): merged into REQ-79.

docs.title: Consent lifecycle requirements
docs.text:
A consent has a limited validity. The lifecycle requirement covers the validity of a consent and its repeated use within that validity. The statuses that a citizen sees and revocation are in citizen access and revocation and REQ-14. These statuses are active (shown as "Actief"), expired (shown as "Verlopen"), and revoked.

In the demo, the consent register sets an absolute valid-until moment when it records the consent. It writes that moment into the consent proof as both valid_until and the expiry time exp. The PDP checks it at every request. A consumer can use a consent again and again within its validity. Single use is not built (SL-01b is blocked). Who sets the validity period is open again (Q-13).

docs.title: REQ-19: A consent has a finite validity, and after that the PDP denies
docs.text:
Every consent MUST have a finite valid-until moment. The PDP MUST check that moment at every request and deny a request after that moment. Within the validity, the consent MUST be usable repeatedly. If the valid-until moment is missing or cannot be read, the PDP MUST deny.

Case Outcome Within the validity allowed (code) Second request within the validity allowed (design FR-11 criterion 2, code: no reuse check) After the valid-until moment, within 30 s clock skew denied: CONSENT_EXPIRED (code) More than 30 s after the valid-until moment denied: CONSENT_TOKEN_EXPIRED (code) Valid-until missing, or different from the expiry time of the proof denied: CONSENT_CONTEXT_INVALID (code)
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design. FR-11 criteria 2 and 3, FR-17 criteria 1 and 4, and PSA S01 (the validity period, and the registration supports expiry: "geldigheidsduur", "de registratie ondersteunt … verloop").
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the consent register (sets the moment) and the reference policy (checks it).
  • Evidence: PR #238, PR #371. Code and tests:
    • The moment is in main.go#L421-L424 and consent_token.go#L142.
    • The check is in dvtp_helper.rego#L46-L48 and consent.rego#L124.
    • The tests are in consent_test.rego#L347-L358, #L400-L402, and dvt0001_test.rego#L76-L78.
  • Related: REQ-68, REQ-117, F-04, F-11, Q-04, Q-13, Q-42, Q-76.
  • Notes:
    • FR-11 criterion 1 lets the default period for each service come from the catalog. It also lets the citizen change the period within bounds. It is open whether the citizen must be able to do that (Q-13). This requirement does not demand it.
    • Q-76 asks whether the validity can differ for each source.
    • In the demo, the consumer chooses the period with validity_seconds. The default is one year, with no upper bound (ICTU/GBO-demo#382 point 5, ICTU/GBO-demo#380).
    • Design choice: the expiry time of the proof is the valid-until moment, with 30 s clock skew. So expiry gives two reason codes, depending on the moment: CONSENT_EXPIRED within the skew, and CONSENT_TOKEN_EXPIRED after it. The design accepts that.
    • FR-11 criterion 2 also asks to record when a consumer first fetched data: Q-42.

docs.title: Consent initiation and return requirements
docs.text:
A consent starts at the consumer. The consumer sends the citizen to the consent portal with a request that names who asks what. After the choice, the portal sends the citizen back to the consumer with the outcome. The requirements cover that request, the data that the portal takes from the registration instead of the request, and the return.

In the demo, the consumer sends the context as query parameters: consumer OIN, scopes, purpose, and return address. The portal keeps the context in the browser session during the mock login. It refuses a scope that it cannot describe, and shows only the requested scopes. On success, the proof goes back in the URL fragment. On refusal, the return carries status=denied. In demo v0.9.0, the consent portal backend does not check the request (ICTU/GBO-demo#427).

docs.title: REQ-37: A consent request names the consumer, the service, the requested data sets, and the return address
docs.text:
A request of a consumer for consent MUST name at least the consumer, the service, the requested data sets, and the return address. If an integrator acts on behalf of the consumer, the request MUST also name the integrator. These data MUST still be available after the citizen logged in. If an item is missing, the citizen MUST NOT see a consent screen. The same applies if the request asks for a data set that the consent facility does not know.

The consent portal backend MUST refuse such a request: INITIATION_INCOMPLETE if a mandatory item is missing, UNKNOWN_SCOPE for an unknown data set. A data set can be known to the consent facility, but not belong to that service according to the service description. It can also be known but not recorded for this consumer. In both cases, the consent portal backend MUST refuse the request with SCOPE_NOT_REGISTERED, before the citizen sees a consent screen.

The name and purpose of the consumer MAY be missing. They come from the registration (REQ-111).

Case Outcome Complete request, known data sets after the login, the consent screen with this context at once (from code) One of the mandatory items is missing refused: INITIATION_INCOMPLETE, no consent screen (demo: only the UI, the message no session, shown as "Geen sessie") Unknown data set refused: UNKNOWN_SCOPE, no consent screen (demo: only the UI, the message unknown request, PR #435) Known data set that does not belong to the requested service, or is not recorded for this consumer refused: SCOPE_NOT_REGISTERED, no consent screen (not built) Request on behalf of a consumer through an integrator the request also names the integrator (proposal from FR-12 criterion 2: not built)
  • Status: draft
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • FR-12 criterion 2.
    • FR-13 criterion 1, with its rationale (scope ID and return address).
    • FR-14 criterion 1.
    • FR-10 description (within the legal ceiling of the service catalog: "binnen het wettelijke plafond van de dienstencatalogus").
    • FR-17 criterion 2, FR-32 criterion 2, and FR-38 criterion 5.
  • Addressee: interface agreement: the initiation interface (koppelvlak) between consumer and consent facility. GBO-delivered component: the portal UI inside MijnOverheid, which shows no consent screen.
  • Evidence: partly, only in the UI. Code and tests:
    • The mandatory fields are in useRedirectContext.ts#L29-L41.
    • The refusal is in PortaalConsent.tsx#L49-L75.
    • A test of the unknown data set is in scopeGroups.test.mjs#L16.
    • The consumer mocks build the request in buildPortalUrl.ts#L69-L80.
    • The backend checks nothing. ICTU/GBO-demo#427 adds that check.
  • Related: REQ-10, REQ-106, REQ-111, REQ-121, Q-44, Q-45, Q-60, Q-61.
  • Notes:
    • The form of the request is open: query parameters, a signed request, or a reference to a request sent in advance. How the request survives the login at MijnOverheid is also open: Q-60, Q-61 sub-questions 2 and 4.
    • Name and purpose come from the registration (REQ-111). The demo also demands them in the request.
    • The demo knows the data sets from a fixed list in the UI (scopeGroups.ts#L35-L43) and does not take them from the service catalog.
    • In the demo, the service does not get into the consent. The register receives the purpose as use_case (PortaalConsent.tsx#L82-L87).
    • SCOPE_NOT_REGISTERED is a reason of its own next to UNKNOWN_SCOPE. With it, the consumer can tell "this set does not exist" from "you are not allowed to ask this set for this service".
    • The PDP of the source does not repeat this check. The proof binds only sets that the backend allowed. REQ-10 limits what the PDP allows under a set.

docs.title: REQ-111: What the citizen sees about the consumer, and the return address, come from the registration and not from the request
docs.text:
Before it shows a consent screen, the consent portal backend MUST take the name of the consumer and the purpose from the registration. It MUST check that the consumer is admitted and active for the requested service. It MUST check the return address against the addresses recorded for that consumer in the admission register. The backend MUST refuse a request that fails these checks before the citizen sees a consent screen. The same applies to a request with a name or purpose that differs from the registration.

Case Outcome Active consumer, registered return address consent screen, with name and purpose from the registration Name or purpose in the request differs from the registration refused: INITIATION_MISMATCH Consumer suspended or not admitted refused: PARTY_NOT_ACTIVE Consumer active, but not admitted for this service refused (no decision on the reason), no consent screen (not built) Return address not registered for that consumer refused: RETURN_URL_NOT_REGISTERED, no return to that address
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • FR-14 criterion 1, with its rationale (protection against open redirects).
    • FR-34, FR-12, and FR-16 criterion 2 (is authorized for the requested service and data: "bevoegd is voor de gevraagde dienst en gegevens").
    • PSA S04 (trust anchors and participant status can be checked by machine: "vertrouwensankers en deelnemersstatus zijn machineleesbaar controleerbaar").
    • Tightened: the requirement fixes which data come from the registration. Provable origin of the request is out of scope.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the consent portal backend. Management organization: the return addresses in the admission register.
  • Evidence: not built: ICTU/GBO-demo#427. The portal reads consumer, name, scope, and return address from the URL (useRedirectContext.ts#L29-L38). Only the frontend checks the address, against a fixed list of origins.
  • Related: REQ-37, REQ-61, REQ-110, REQ-117, REQ-119, Q-44, Q-53, Q-59, Q-60, Q-69.
  • Notes:
    • With these checks, a forged request can lead only to a consent to the real consumer, with the right name. The return also goes only to the address of that consumer.
    • It is open whether it must also be provable that the consumer made the request (FR-34 criterion 1): Q-60.
    • The return addresses are in the admission register and not in the service catalog. They belong to the consumer, and the admission is already there (REQ-61).
    • The check for each service needs an admission register that knows, for each consumer, the services for which it is admitted (FR-30, FR-32). REQ-61 records the admission for each bronhouder.
    • Q-69 asks whether the PDP also checks this at the request to the source.

docs.title: REQ-119: After every outcome the citizen returns to the consumer with that outcome
docs.text:
When the consent process ends, the consent facility MUST return the citizen automatically to the registered return address of the consumer (REQ-111). This applies to every outcome, also after a refusal or an error. The return MUST name the outcome. For any outcome other than a given consent, the consent facility MUST NOT record a consent. If the consent facility cannot establish the return address, it MUST NOT return the citizen.

Case Outcome The citizen gives consent back with the outcome success. The proof reaches the consumer as Q-44 decides The citizen refuses back with the outcome refusal (demo: status=denied, code) The consent cannot be recorded (for example no value for a source, REQ-82, or the register does not answer) back with the outcome error, no consent Refused by REQ-118 (delegation) back with an outcome. Refusal or error: Q-44 Consumer or return address cannot be established (REQ-111) no return. What the citizen sees: no decision The citizen closes the window or the session expires no return (Q-43, Q-44)
  • Status: draft
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design. FR-14 criteria 2 and 3. Criterion 2 applies whatever the outcome is, success, refusal, or error ("ongeacht de uitkomst (succes, weigering of fout)").
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the portal UI inside MijnOverheid and the consent portal backend. Interface agreement: the outcome values in the return.
  • Evidence: partly. A refusal returns with status=denied (PortaalConsent.tsx#L100-L106). A success returns with the proof in the URL fragment (PortaalBevestiging.tsx). The cancel button (shown as "Annuleren") does not return (PortaalConsent.tsx#L108). The return after an error is not checked.
  • Related: REQ-37, REQ-82, REQ-111, REQ-117, REQ-118, REQ-122, Q-43, Q-44.
  • Notes:
    • These points are open in Q-44 (partly answered):
      • which outcomes the consumer tells apart, and what they are called
      • how the proof arrives on success: through the browser, or through a code that the consumer exchanges
      • whether the consumer gets the allowed sets back separately
    • "Aborted" is not an outcome.

docs.title: Role split between consent register and consent portal (S01/S02)
docs.text:
The PSA splits the consent function into two capabilities: S01 consent registration (the consent register) and S02 consent portal (the consent portal: the portal UI inside MijnOverheid and the consent portal backend). The requirements for this split keep the BSN out of the register, and fix where the citizen identity comes from.

In the demo, the consent portal backend receives the BSN from the validated portal token. It derives a reference to the citizen (an HMAC of the BSN). On the first consent, it asks BSNk for values. It sends only the reference and the encrypted values to the register. The register stores the polymorphic values under the reference. It is open whether register and backend stay two systems, and which of them is the BSNk participant (Q-49, ADR 0040, proposed).
