docs.title: REQ-23: The consent register gets no BSN, not even temporarily
docs.text:
A request to the consent register MUST NOT contain a BSN. The same applies to every answer of the register and to every data item that it stores, also temporarily while it handles a request.

  • Status: draft
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • PSA S01 (the register holds no BSN if a pseudonymous identification is enough: "het register bevat geen BSN als een pseudonieme identificatie volstaat").
    • PSA S03 (only components and organizations with a valid legal basis process the BSN: "alleen componenten en organisaties met een geldige grondslag verwerken het BSN").
    • FR-35 criterion 1.
    • Tightened: the BSN is also not in a request or an answer, so that the BSN stays limited to one component.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the consent register, and the consent portal backend that calls it.
  • Evidence: PR #148, PR #469. Code and tests:
    • A test of the creation of a consent and of keeping the polymorphic values is in portal_test.go#L348.
    • The adapter to the register has no method that takes a BSN (register.go#L1-L10).
    • The stored model has no BSN (main.go#L33-L46).
    • Overview and revocation send only the reference or the consent ID (register.go#L60-L63). There is no test of its own for that.
  • Related: REQ-20, REQ-39, REQ-69, Q-49, Q-56.
  • Notes:
    • The register knows the citizen under a reference that the consent portal backend derives from the BSN. Under that reference, the register keeps the polymorphic values of the first activation (REQ-69). It receives the encrypted values for each party only to sign the proof.
    • It is open who makes the reference from the BSN. The demo does it in the backend. The working assumption (route D) puts it in the register.
    • If the design follows the working assumption, or if register and backend become one system, this requirement does not apply in this form: Q-49. The requirement applies to the register as long as it is a component of its own.

docs.title: REQ-24: The citizen identity comes from the authentication service assertion at the required assurance level and not from client input
docs.text:
The consent portal backend MUST take the identity of the citizen from the validated assertion of the authentication service. The backend MUST NOT use a BSN that the client sends as input as the identity. The consent portal backend MUST accept only an assertion that states the assurance level of the authentication. The assertion can state a level lower than the set minimum, or no level. If so, the backend MUST show no personal data and no consent options. It MUST also record or revoke nothing.

Case Outcome Assertion at the minimum level or higher identity accepted Assertion at a level lower than the minimum, or without a level refused (no decision on the reason). Nothing shown, recorded, or revoked (proposal: not built)
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • FR-01 criterion 2 (at the minimum assurance level that the government requires: "op het door de overheid vereiste minimale betrouwbaarheidsniveau").
    • P-05.
    • PSA S02 (the authentication has a suitable assurance level: "de authenticatie heeft een passend betrouwbaarheidsniveau").
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the consent portal backend.
  • Evidence: PR #148. Code and tests:
    • The backend takes the BSN from the validated token, and refuses a request without one (portalhttp.go#L138-L147).
    • The creation of a consent sends a token and no BSN (portalClient.ts#L20-L25).
    • No automated test covers the refusal.
  • Related: REQ-38, REQ-40, REQ-107, REQ-118, BSNK-04, Q-50, Q-59.
  • Notes:
    • The demo simulates the login. With a mock login, the backend signs a token with the BSN itself and also validates it (auth.go#L12-L24). That says nothing about the assurance level.
    • It is not known whether a token of the authentication service is available inside MijnOverheid. So the requirement prescribes no token. It prescribes only that the identity comes from the validated assertion and not from client input.
    • The working assumption is that MijnOverheid passes on the BSN after the login (BSNk preconditions). How MijnOverheid does that decides how the backend checks this requirement: Q-50.
    • The government sets the minimum level (FR-01 criterion 2), and GBO does not. Whether the MijnOverheid assertion states the level belongs to Q-50.
    • BSNk also requires a login at the requested level before a transformation (BSNK-04).

docs.title: Removed numbers
docs.text:
• REQ-22 (the pseudonymization action belongs in S02): removed, pending Q-49, watch item for ADR 0040.
  • REQ-35 (citizen ownership check on revocation): merged into REQ-40.

docs.title: Citizen access and revocation requirements
docs.text:
A citizen can see the consents that they gave and revoke them in the consent portal inside MijnOverheid (FR-20, FR-22, FR-23). The requirements for this function cover these topics:

  • the overview of consents
  • the components that can reach the register for the overview
  • ownership
  • export
  • revocation
  • the notice about the rights of the citizen at the consumer

In the demo, the consent portal backend derives the reference to the citizen (an HMAC of the BSN) from the validated portal token. The backend asks the register for the consents under that reference. It shows them as active, expired, or revoked. On a revocation, the backend checks ownership and asks the register to set the status to revoked. The record stays.

Viewing and revoking do not call BSNk. The authorization chain denies the next request on a revoked consent with CONSENT_WITHDRAWN (REQ-14). The status names follow F-97. The status retrieved (shown as "Opgehaald") waits for Q-42.

docs.title: REQ-38: A logged-in citizen can view consents with status and revoke them
docs.text:
The consent portal backend MUST let a citizen with a verified identity (REQ-24) view their consents and revoke a consent. The overview MUST order the consents by the moment of granting. It MUST hold the active consents, and the recently expired or revoked consents. For each consent, the overview MUST show the consumer, the purpose, the data sets, the validity, and the status. The data sets MUST show the same data elements as the consent screen showed before, without values.

If the citizen has no verified identity, the backend MUST show nothing and change nothing. The status MUST follow from the register and the validity, on the same grounds on which the authorization chain denies.

Case Outcome Logged in, overview the own consents, each with the status active, expired, or revoked (from code) Validity passed expired (from code) Revoked, also if the validity passed later revoked (from code) Logged in, revoke an own active consent revoked (from code) Detail of a consent for each set, the same data elements as on the consent screen, without values (proposal: not built) Not logged in, or invalid assertion refused, nothing shown or changed (from code: HTTP 401)
  • Status: draft
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • FR-20: the description (a chronological overview: "een chronologisch overzicht") and criteria 1 and 2.
    • FR-21: criterion 3 and the description (the same data elements as shown when the citizen gave consent, without the actual values: "dezelfde data-elementen als getoond tijdens het geven van de toestemming, zonder de feitelijke waarden").
    • FR-22 criteria 1 and 2, FR-23 criterion 2, and FR-01 criterion 3.
    • PSA S02 (the provision of a view and revocation function: "inzage- en intrekkingsfunctie").
    • P-13.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the consent portal backend. The portal UI inside MijnOverheid shows the result.
  • Evidence: PR #148, PR #469. Code and tests:
    • The routes are in portalhttp.go#L322-L357.
    • The refusal without an assertion is in #L138-L147. No test covers this refusal.
    • The status is in consent.go#L135-L146, tested in portal_test.go#L276.
  • Related: REQ-24, REQ-40, REQ-108, REQ-109, REQ-111, REQ-117, REQ-120, REQ-121, F-19, Q-25, Q-42, Q-53, Q-61, Q-63.
  • Notes:
    • The status retrieved follows after Q-42. The processings for each consent (FR-20 criterion 2) follow after Q-25.
    • The length of "recently" depends on the retention period: Q-63.
    • The form of the link between the UI inside MijnOverheid and the backend is open: Q-61 sub-question 1.
    • Design choice: the demo has no separate route for one consent. The UI filters the overview.
    • In the demo, the name of the consumer comes from a fixed list in the UI (onderwerpMap.ts#L14-L21). As on the consent screen, the name must come from the registration.
    • Q-53 asks whether the overview shows a consent of a suspended consumer differently from active.

docs.title: REQ-39: Only the consent backend can create, query, and revoke the consents of a citizen in the register
docs.text:
The consent register MUST allow only the consent portal backend to create, query, and revoke the consents of a citizen. The register MUST also allow only that backend to read and keep the values that the register keeps for that citizen. A portal UI, a citizen, or another component MUST NOT be able to call the register for these actions directly.

Case Outcome The consent portal backend creates, queries, or revokes allowed The portal UI or the browser calls the register directly not reachable (proposal, reachable in the demo) The PDP of a source asks for the status only through the entry for the status (REQ-76), no other actions (from code)
  • Status: draft
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design. PSA S01 (only the citizen and authorized components have access to consent, and the provision of an interface for the consent portal: "alleen de burger en bevoegde componenten hebben toegang tot toestemming", "interface voor het toestemmingsportaal"). Tightened: the citizen has access only through the consent portal backend, because only that backend checks ownership (REQ-40).
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the consent register and the deployment that it runs in.
  • Evidence: partly. Code and tests:
    • The UI talks only to the backend (nginx.conf#L7-L8, vite.config.ts#L12-L17).
    • The status query has its own entry that serves nothing else (status.go#L13-L26, PR #390).
    • Not enforced: the register publishes a host port, allows every origin, and does not authenticate (docker-compose.yml#L718-L719, main.go#L301-L305).
  • Related: REQ-23, REQ-40, REQ-76, Q-49, Q-57, Q-58.
  • Notes:
    • It is open whether the register authenticates the backend, or whether network isolation is enough: Q-58.
    • If the register and the backend become one system (Q-49), this limit becomes a boundary inside that system.
    • The public keys for the proof are public and are out of scope here.
    • The register refuses an overview without a citizen reference (main.go#L486-L502). This limits an overview to one citizen, but the register does not check who asks.

docs.title: REQ-40: A citizen sees and revokes only their own consents
docs.text:
At every overview, every view of one consent, and every revocation, the consent portal backend MUST determine the citizen from the verified identity (REQ-24). It MUST show or change only the consents of that citizen. The backend MUST NOT use a reference to a citizen that the request carries. The backend MUST refuse a revocation of the consent of another citizen before the register changes anything. The consent of another citizen and an unknown consent MUST get the same outcome: not found (CONSENT_NOT_FOUND). Then the answer does not reveal whether a consent exists.

Case Outcome Overview only the consents of this citizen (from code) Revoke an own consent revoked (from code) Revoke the consent of another citizen refused: CONSENT_NOT_FOUND (HTTP 404), consent unchanged (demo: 403 consent_not_owned_by_caller) Revoke an unknown consent refused: CONSENT_NOT_FOUND (HTTP 404)
  • Status: draft
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design. PSA S01 (only the citizen and authorized components have access to consent: "alleen de burger en bevoegde componenten hebben toegang tot toestemming"), tightened: the citizen has access only to their own consents. Also FR-20 criterion 1 and FR-23.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the consent portal backend.
  • Evidence: to build: ICTU/GBO-demo#602. The demo has this evidence:
    • PR #238 and PR #469.
    • The overview is in portal.go#L249-L266, tested in portal_test.go#L327.
    • The revocation is in portal.go#L268-L293, tested in portal_test.go#L232, #L250, and #L266.
    • The refusal reason is in portalhttp.go#L167-L169.
  • Related: REQ-24, REQ-38, REQ-39, REQ-109, Q-49, Q-56, ADR 0040.
  • Notes:
    • Design choice: the backend recognizes the citizen by an HMAC of the BSN under its own key (route D, working assumption). The backend asks BSNk nothing for this.
    • A new key makes existing consents impossible to find until a migration of these consents: Q-56.
    • The ownership check is in the backend, because the register does not see who calls. So the register must accept calls only from the backend (REQ-39).
    • The demo has no route for one consent. If such a route comes, the same check applies.

docs.title: REQ-108: The citizen can export the overview of consents
docs.text:
After login, the citizen MUST be able to export the overview of their consents. The export MUST contain the same consents and data as the overview, and MUST NOT contain the BSN or the name of the citizen.

Case Outcome A logged-in citizen exports a file with all consents of the overview (active, and recently expired or revoked): consumer, service, sets, valid until, and status A citizen without consents empty export, no error Not logged in no export Content only consents of this citizen, no BSN, and no name
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design. FR-20 criterion 3, FR-01, PSA S02 (access), and P-13. Tightened: the export contains no BSN or name of the citizen.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the portal UI inside MijnOverheid, and the consent portal backend if it makes the export. The requirement does not fix where the export happens.
  • Evidence: not built. The demo has no export. The demo issue follows after Q-52.
  • Related: REQ-40, Q-25, Q-27, Q-52.
  • Notes: the format follows from Q-52. The processings for each consent (FR-20 criterion 2) belong in the export after a decision on where they come from (Q-25, Q-27). Until that decision, the export contains only the consents.

docs.title: REQ-109: Revocation is possible only for a valid consent
docs.text:
The UI of the consent portal MUST offer the action "revoke" only for a consent with the status active or retrieved. It MUST NOT offer it for expired or revoked. The consent portal backend MUST refuse a revocation of an expired or already revoked consent. It MUST NOT change the status or make a new registration then.

Case Outcome Active button visible, revoked after the citizen approves Retrieved (still valid) button visible, revoked after the citizen approves (to build after Q-42) Expired no button. The backend refuses a direct request: CONSENT_NOT_REVOCABLE. The status stays expired Already revoked no button. The backend refuses a direct request: CONSENT_NOT_REVOCABLE. No new registration The consent of another citizen refused, as in demo v0.9.0 (REQ-40)
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design. FR-23 criterion 1, FR-24 criterion 1, PSA S01 (the registration supports revocation and expiry), and PSA S02. Tightened: the FRs put the button in the UI. This requirement also makes the backend enforce the rule.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the portal UI inside MijnOverheid and the consent portal backend.
  • Evidence: partly. The backend check is in ICTU/GBO-demo#600. The UI shows the button only for the status active (MijnToestemmingenDetail.tsx#L127). The backend checks only ownership. It sets an expired or revoked consent to REVOKED again, with a new LDV record (portal.go#L269, main.go#L282).
  • Related: REQ-14, REQ-40, F-97, Q-42.
  • Notes: the statuses active, retrieved, expired, and revoked have the screen names that F-97 chose: "Actief", "Opgehaald", "Verlopen", and "Ingetrokken". Their form on screen follows the text guideline. The backend refuses a second revocation and does not accept it silently. So a double click gets a message.

docs.title: REQ-120: For every consent and after every revocation, the portal points the citizen to their rights at the consumer
docs.text:
The portal UI MUST show a notice in the detail view of every consent and after every revocation. The notice MUST state that data already given to the consumer stays with the consumer. It MUST state that the citizen can use their GDPR rights there, such as erasure. It MUST also give the contact details of the consumer for that purpose. The consent portal backend MUST take those contact details from the registration of the consumer and not from the request of the consumer.

Case Outcome The citizen opens the detail view of a consent text about GDPR rights, with the contact details from the registration (proposal: not built) The citizen revokes a consent the message after the revocation states that data already given stays with the consumer, with the contact details (proposal: not built) No data fetched yet under the consent the notice still shows. The requirement does not depend on Q-42 Consumer without registered contact details does not occur for an admitted consumer: no admission without these details (AV-14)
  • Status: draft
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design. FR-25 criteria 1 and 2, FR-23, and FR-24 (description: data already delivered falls under the GDPR responsibility of the consumer). Tightened: FR-25 applies the notice only to the case in which revocation is no longer possible. According to FR-24, that case does not exist (F-98). So the notice is always in the detail view and after a revocation.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the portal UI inside MijnOverheid and the consent portal backend. The management organization records the contact details at admission.
  • Evidence: not built.
  • Related: REQ-14, REQ-38, REQ-109, REQ-111, REQ-122, AV-14, F-98, Q-62.
  • Notes: sub-question 2 of Q-62 covers where the contact details are kept and how they reach the portal.

docs.title: Removed numbers
docs.text: • REQ-41 (revocation is a change of the consent record, with no token invalidation and no change at the consumer): merged into REQ-14.

docs.title: Consent register data model
docs.text:
The consent register must keep certain data for production. The data model follows from the requirements. It is no requirement with its own number: every data item refers to the requirement or functional requirement that it follows from. Where an open question decides the model, the table marks an open place.

The model says what the register knows. It does not say in which tables or which product. It is open whether the register and the consent portal backend (S01 and S02) are one system or two: Q-49.

State: November 2, 2026. Demo: the schema of the demo (postgres_store.go#L15-L60) covers the core. Where the schema deviates, the item says so. The compose default runs the register in memory.

The PostgreSQL store is optional (SL-12 is planned). With a persistent store, the register needs a fixed signing key (CONSENT_SIGNING_KEY_PATH), so that proofs stay valid after a restart (Q-55).

docs.title: Citizen
docs.text:
The register keeps two data items about the citizen:

Data item Content Basis Reference to the citizen An HMAC of the BSN under a secret key of the portal, with the key version in it. No BSN. REQ-20, route D Polymorphic values PI and PP of the first activation, under the reference. Once for each citizen. After that, only transformation. REQ-69

The register does not keep the BSN. It also does not keep the encrypted identity (VI) and the encrypted pseudonym (VP) for each receiving party. It signs those into the proof and forgets them (REQ-69, REQ-80).

docs.title: Consent
docs.text:
The register keeps these data items for each consent:

Data item Content Basis Consent ID Own ID of the register. It is in the proof and is the key for the status query. REQ-68 Citizen The reference to the citizen. REQ-20 Consumer OIN of the service provider to whom the citizen gave the consent. For an integrator, the represented party. REQ-12, REQ-106 Use case The service from the catalog for which the consent applies. REQ-12, FR-32 Scope per source For each source: the scope and the fields for which the citizen gave consent. One representation. A flat list of scopes can be derived from it. REQ-12 Created Moment of granting. FR-22 Valid until Absolute moment. The register keeps only the result. Where the period comes from (a default period for each service, bounds, and whether the citizen changes it) is open: Q-13. FR-05, FR-11, FR-32, REQ-19 Status Active or revoked. An expired consent follows from "valid until". FR-22, FR-24, REQ-68

The demo deviates from this model in three places:

  • Scopes are in the schema twice: as a flat list and as scope per source. Production needs only the scope per source.
  • The consumer chooses the validity period (validity_seconds). The default is one year, and the citizen cannot change anything: ICTU/GBO-demo#380.
  • The purpose comes from the redirect of the consumer. The register stores it as use_case, default hypotheek.

docs.title: Log of processings
docs.text: Every change produces an LDV record (REQ-72). The demo writes that record through an outbox in the same transaction as the change. So there is no consent without a log record. That is a choice of the demo and is no requirement.

docs.title: Open places
docs.text:
Open questions decide these places in the model:

Place What the model needs when the question is answered Question Retrieved Whether and when a consumer used a consent, and how the register learns that. Q-42 Validity period Whether the register records only the result, or also the default period and a change by the citizen. Q-13 Validity per source One valid-until for each consent, as in demo v0.9.0, or a valid-until for each source within the consent. Q-76 Change Whether a consent can change. If so, whether the record changes or a new record replaces the old one. Q-77 Authorized representative In whose name a consent given by a representative is, and whether the register records the representative with it. Q-73 Refusal A record of the refusal, a count for each consumer, or nothing in the register. Q-43 Mandatory set Whether the register records for each consent which fields were mandatory, or whether this comes from the catalog. Q-45 Integrator With option (a), a field for the integrator with the consent. With option (b), nothing in the register: the mandate is in the admission register. Q-46 Volumes Size and load. This decides storage and indexes, and does not change the data. Q-47 Moment of revocation A field with the consent, or only in the LDV log. Q-48 Proof of the interaction PSA S01 asks for it in the record. The record that the citizen saw the information follows from REQ-107. It is open whether the register records the version of the information shown. Q-51 Retention periods How long expired and revoked consents, PI and PP, and references stay. Q-63 Storage durability Which durability and recovery requirements apply to the register storage. Q-54 S01 and S02 Whether the polymorphic values and the consents are with one participant. A polymorphic value does not leave the party that requested it (BSNK-03). Q-49

docs.title: EUDI issuance requirements
docs.text:
These requirements apply only to the issuance of attestations to the EUDI wallet (the PuB-EAA route). The citizen discloses a PID from the wallet. The nl-wallet issuance server verifies the disclosure and calls the GBO EUDI adapter. The adapter queries the source over FSC through the generic PEP-PDP chain. Then the issuance server issues the attestation under the certificate set of the bronhouder.

This route exposed a generic basis. The generic pages hold that basis:

  • the regime from evidence (REQ-74)
  • the thin channel adapter (REQ-44)
  • the source-owned description (REQ-64)

The requirements on this page cover only what is specific to the wallet. ADR 0018, ADR 0017, and ADR 0028 record the design. The runtime view is in EUDI issuance.

Evidence links to gbo-demo point at tag v0.9.0.

docs.title: REQ-45: The source is queried only about the citizen from a verified PID disclosure
docs.text:
The GBO issuance facility MUST take the subject of a source query for an attestation only from a verified PID disclosure. A verified PID disclosure has a signature that was checked against a trust list of PID providers. The facility MUST be able to show that this disclosure belongs to this request. A request without such a disclosure MUST NOT reach the source. A request with a shared attestation that is not a PID MUST NOT reach the source. A request that does not provably come from the verifying party MUST NOT reach the source either.

The trust list for that check MUST hold only the anchors of PID providers.

Case Outcome Verified PID disclosure, provably for this request source queried with the BSN from the PID (proposal, binding not built) Disclosure without a BSN refused before the source with HTTP 400 (from the code) Shared attestation is not a PID refused (proposal, reason open) Request not provably from the verifying runtime refused (proposal and not built: the adapter route has no caller authentication) Signature invalid or provider not on the list no request to the adapter (the issuance server verifies, without an independent test)
  • Status: draft
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design: ARF v3.0.0 Annex 2 OIA_12 (a relying party validates the PID signature with a trust anchor from the LoTE of PID providers) and OIA_14 (LoTE per ETSI TS 119 602). The other source is PSA S11 ("issuance, verification and retrieval use suitable authentication, authorization and logging", "agreements arrange binding to citizen and wallet").
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the EUDI adapter and the issuance configuration that GBO generates. The issuance server is part of nl-wallet. What the issuance server verifies is a product property. This requirement does not cover it.
  • Evidence: not built: ICTU/GBO-demo#133. Demo v0.9.0 has this state:
    • The adapter trusts the BSN (main.go#L23-L26). It refuses a disclosure without a BSN in #L249-L253.
    • The route POST /attestations/{sourceID}/{typeID} (source_release_runtime.go#L69) runs on a plain listener without caller authentication (main.go#L700).
    • Issuance asks only for the BSN from the PID (issuance_config.go#L162).
    • The trust list is in issuance_server.toml.example#L3-L9. The code in issuance_release.go#L120-L121 adds the issuer CA of every source to it.
  • Related: REQ-44, REQ-57, REQ-60, REQ-74, F-70, F-83, Q-18, ADR 0018, ADR 0031, ADR 0043.
  • Notes:
    • The issuance server verifies the PID disclosure. For that reason SL-25 (PID verification in the adapter) was dropped.
    • The gap is in the callback. The signature check is in place. Any caller that reaches the adapter URL can post a body with any BSN. The adapter then calls the source over FSC as the designated issuer peer, so the PDP allows the request. The adapter returns the projected claims without any wallet involvement.
    • Two solutions meet the requirement: the adapter verifies the SD-JWT itself, or the verifying runtime delivers signed evidence and authenticates the callback. Both solutions also need the binding of the disclosure to the request.
    • With this requirement, the PID becomes positive evidence for the PID regime. In demo v0.9.0, that regime is "no consent token" plus a list of designated issuers (eudi_helper.rego#L13-L30, F-70).
    • In demo v0.9.0, the trust list also holds the GBO development CA and the issuer CAs of the sources. A PID verification must trust only PID providers. How fresh the list must be is open (Q-18, sub-question 4). Which list anchors PuB-EAA providers is open as well (Q-30).
    • Checking the revocation status of the PID is a SHOULD (VCR_13).
    • The reference QTSP authenticates its callback with a secret path over CA-pinned HTTPS (qtsp_issuance.go#L134-L142). The source route does not.
    • The BSN from the PID stays in the PDP input and is in both decision logs. REQ-60 is not met for EUDI (ADR 0043).

docs.title: REQ-57: An attestation about someone other than the requester follows an agreed relation from the verified requester
docs.text:
An attestation can hold data about someone other than the requester. For such an attestation, the chain that GBO delivers MUST query the source only along a relation that the source recorded in its service description. The starting point MUST be the subject from the verified PID (REQ-45). The starting point MUST NOT be a value that the caller chooses. The reference policy MUST deny a query that takes another entry point or asks for fields outside that relation. The service description MUST mark such a relation, with the kind of relation.

Case Outcome Requester with a marriage that ended by the death of the partner certificate with the data of that partner (from the code) Partner died on another date than the dissolution no certificate. The source returns nothing, and the adapter answers HTTP 404 (from the code). Date incomplete (only year and month) certificate (from the code) Entry point without the BSN of a citizen denied: PID_NOT_PRESENT (from the code) Field outside the view denied: FIELD_NOT_PERMITTED (from the code) Entry point with the BSN of someone other than the PID holder the PDP cannot tell the difference, so this case depends on REQ-45 (proposal) Relation not marked in the service description proposal, outcome open
  • Status: draft
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: derived. The requirement serves PSA S11 ("agreements arrange binding to citizen and wallet") and P-02. Without a recorded relation from the requester, anyone with a valid PID can put data about any other person in an attestation. Compare Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1569, Annex II point 2(c) (only the minimum set of attributes).
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the reference policy and the adapter. Interface agreement: the marking of the relation in the service description.
  • Evidence: PR #125, PR #304.
    • The selection at the source is in brp-graphql-server/main.go#L671-L705, tested in main_test.go#L183 and #L190.
    • The closed field list is in eud0002.rego#L33-L51 and the entry point is in #L62-L66, tested in eud0002_test.rego#L42.
    • The subject comes from the PID (source_metadata.go#L272-L273).
    • The marking in the service description is not built.
  • Related: REQ-45, REQ-64, REQ-72, REQ-78, AV-10, AV-11, F-47, Q-14, Q-20.
  • Notes:
    • Design choice: in demo v0.9.0, the relation runs through a view of the source. Filter arguments in the schema, which the policy requires with fixed values, also meet the requirement (ICTU/GBO-demo#425). In the view variant, the PDP does not see the relation and only limits the fields. The source carries the selection. The mechanism to check argument values exists (lib.rego#L30-L41).
    • Representation is outside this requirement. A person who asks on behalf of another falls under Annex II point 2(a) of Implementing Regulation 2025/1569 and a mechanism of its own (PSA B-19).
    • The deceased is not a data subject in the sense of the GDPR. The source logs the requester and the living parents (AV-10).
    • More than one result from the source leads to a refusal (REQ-116).

docs.title: REQ-58: Every bronhouder has its own certificate set for issuance, and missing material fails
docs.text:
The GBO issuance facility MUST keep a certificate set of its own per bronhouder. The set holds a certificate that signs attestations, and an access certificate with which issuance shows itself to the wallet. The facility MUST NOT sign an attestation or a request to the wallet with the set of another bronhouder, in any case. If the set of a source is missing, incomplete, or differs from what is activated, issuance MUST refuse for that source. Issuance MUST NOT fall back to another set.

Case Outcome Source with a complete set of its own issuance under its own issuer and access certificate Set missing source blocked: CERTIFICATE_SET_NOT_FOUND. Other sources continue. Set without OIN or organization name source blocked: CERTIFICATE_SET_INVALID Mounted material differs from the active release no issuance configuration generated Two sources behind one FSC peer each its own set
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design: ARF v3.0.0 Annex 2 Reg_10a (at least one access certificate per registered service), PuBPNot_04 (every PuB-EAA can be authenticated with the trust anchors notified for that provider), and ISSU_73 (signing certificates per ETSI TS 119 412-6 clause 8). The other source is PSA S11 ("the bronhouder stays legally and substantively responsible").
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the reconciler and the generator of the issuance configuration.
  • Evidence: ICTU/GBO-demo#225, PR #237, PR #247, PR #276.
    • The set per source is in issuance_config.go#L159-L180.
    • The blocking is in source-registry/onboarding/service.go#L283-L297, tested in service_test.go#L130, fsc_contract_discovery_test.go#L225, and #L278.
    • The check for differing material is in issuance_release.go#L113-L116, without a test.
  • Related: REQ-64, REQ-67, REQ-77, F-50, F-81, Q-07, Q-17, ADR 0023, ADR 0028.
  • Notes:
    • The set also holds a certificate for the status list (issuance_config.go#L179). Q-17 (#225) covers whether that certificate belongs to the source or to the facility, and who holds the keys. This requirement says which certificates exist. It does not say who keeps them.
    • No procedure exists to rotate and revoke certificates without a wallet update (ICTU/GBO-demo#381, rows 2 and 3).
    • In production, a registered service also needs a registration certificate, and the seal key sits in a QSCD (F-81).
    • In the demo, all sets hang under one development CA (issuance_server.toml.example#L4-L5). This CA is part of the demo configuration.
    • The reference QTSP gets a set of its own, and fails on an incomplete set (qtsp_issuance.go#L109-L131). Missing QTSP material does not block source issuance.

docs.title: REQ-77: An attestation gets the validity and revocation policy of the bronhouder
docs.text:
For each attestation type, the GBO issuance facility MUST apply the validity period that the bronhouder records. The facility MUST NOT apply a value from its own code. An attestation that is valid for more than 24 hours MUST carry a status reference with which it can be revoked. On instruction of the bronhouder, the facility MUST be able to revoke an issued attestation, without an action of the holder.

Case Outcome Validity recorded by the bronhouder issued with that validity (proposal, demo v0.9.0 uses 365 days for every source) Validity longer than 24 hours status reference in the attestation (from the code: status list per type) Source data changed while the attestation is still valid for at least 24 hours revoked (proposal, who signals the change is open) Bronhouder revokes status set to revoked (proposal)
  • Status: draft
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1569, article 4, with these paragraphs:
      • paragraph 1: a written and public policy for validity and revocation
      • paragraph 2: only the provider can revoke
      • paragraph 3: for a validity of more than 24 hours, revoke in at least the listed cases
      • paragraph 5: status information available with integrity and authenticity
    • ARF v3.0.0 Annex 2 VCR_01b (SD-JWT VC: valid for at most 24 hours, or a status list), VCR_11a (Token Status List), and VCR_09 (revoke when an attribute changes)
    • PSA S11 ("agreements arrange … status, revocation and validity")
    • GO ("GBO is legally not a PuB-EAA provider")
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the issuance facility.
  • Evidence: not built: ICTU/GBO-demo#381 (rows 11 and 12), ICTU/GBO-demo#225. In demo v0.9.0, the validity is fixed in issuance_config.go#L166-L168 and qtsp_issuance.go#L152. The status list per type is in issuance_config.go#L179.
  • Related: REQ-58, REQ-64, AV-12, AV-13, F-82, Q-17, Q-18, ADR 0028.
  • Notes:
    • The policy itself (paragraph 1) belongs to the bronhouder as provider. That policy is a candidate connection condition (AV-12) and no requirement on GBO. The facility revokes technically, on instruction of the bronhouder (AV-13). Q-17 covers who holds the key of the status list.
    • GBO only queries. It gets no signal when source data changes (F-82). For each type, the choice is short-lived (less than 24 hours) or long-lived with a change feed and revocation.
    • The issuance server of nl-wallet sets the structure of the status list (random index, herd privacy). That structure is a product property.
    • The other points of the former security baseline are in REQ-58, REQ-45, REQ-44, REQ-64, REQ-60, REQ-72, and REQ-11.

docs.title: REQ-78: Issuance issues nested claims, with selective disclosure per element as the schema prescribes
docs.text:
The attestation schema of the source can define a claim as an object or a list. The GBO issuance facility MUST be able to issue such a claim in that form. It MUST apply the selective disclosure that the schema prescribes for each claim, also for each nested property and each list element. It MUST NOT refuse a schema, or flatten it, because it contains nested claims.

Case Outcome Schema with only single-valued claims issued, with sd per claim (from the code) Schema with an object or a list (for example the parents per person) issued, with disclosure per element (proposal, demo v0.9.0 refuses it at validation)
  • Status: draft
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design: ARF v3.0.0 Annex 2 ARB_30 (the rulebook records for all claims, also nested properties and list elements, whether they MUST, MAY, or MUST NOT be selectively disclosable), PSA S11 ("attestations follow an established attestation rulebook and schema", and the bronhouder records mapping and attestation schema in its GBO configuration), and P-02.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the mapping profile and the generation of Type Metadata in the EUDI adapter.
  • Evidence: not built: ICTU/GBO-demo#381, row 13. Demo v0.9.0 has only single-valued datatypes in profile.go#L117-L121. It sets sd per claim in source_claims.go#L237-L241 (PR #463).
  • Related: REQ-57, REQ-64, F-47, Q-20, ADR 0017.
  • Notes:
    • The rulebook and the source choose whether a certificate models the parents per person. GBO does not make that choice.
    • Each claim in the source description has sd set to always (the default), allowed, or never. GBO carries this value into the generated Type Metadata.
    • Whether NL Wallet shows nested claims and lets the holder share them per element is wallet behavior (#381, row 13). That behavior decides whether the demo can show this requirement end to end. It does not decide whether the requirement applies.

docs.title: REQ-116: An attestation contains only what the source answered, per its mapping, and an answer that does not fit gives no attestation
docs.text:
The GBO issuance facility MUST take every claim of an attestation from the answer of the source. It MUST use the mapping that the bronhouder records in its service description (REQ-64). It MUST NOT round, convert, add, or derive a source value beyond what that mapping prescribes.

An answer does not fit the mapping if a mandatory claim is missing or empty. It also does not fit if a value does not have the recorded type, or if the answer holds more than one result. If the answer does not fit the mapping, the facility MUST NOT issue an attestation. That includes an attestation with only the claims that do fit. An answer without a result MUST end as "not found", distinct from an error.

Case Outcome Answer fits the mapping attestation with exactly the mapped claims. Fields outside the mapping stay out (code). Amount with cents, datatype number value unchanged in the claim and without rounding (code) Mandatory claim missing no attestation: HTTP 502, GBO_SIMPLE_PATH_MISSING in the log (code) Mandatory claim is null, or has another type no attestation: HTTP 502, GBO_SIMPLE_TYPE_MISMATCH in the log (code) More than one result no attestation: HTTP 502, GBO_SIMPLE_RESULT_AMBIGUOUS in the log (code) No result not found: HTTP 404. The processing is still logged (code). Optional claim missing or null claim left out, the rest issued (code)
  • Status: draft
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design: PSA S11 ("the bronhouder stays legally and substantively responsible for the public attributes issued", "if attestation issuance needs a semantic mapping, the bronhouder records in its GBO configuration which mapping … applies"), PSA S10 ("the set-up applies validation rules before delivery"), and P-10. This requirement is stricter than these sources: no partial attestation and no conversion by GBO.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the mapping profile and the issuance runtime of the EUDI adapter. Interface agreement: the mapping profile as part of the service description.
  • Evidence: PR #204.
    • The projection is in profile.go#L126-L169. The runtime is in main.go#L302-L316.
    • The test profile_test.go#L75 uses the cases in cases.json#L82-L145. main_test.go#L582 tests that only mapped claims are issued. main_test.go#L609 tests decimals. ldv_test.go#L505 tests an answer without a result.
  • Related: REQ-64, REQ-78, REQ-101, REQ-124, Q-38, ADR 0017.
  • Notes:
    • Design choice: gbo-simple-v1 only copies, renames, and flattens. Selection, conversion, and conditions are not in it (docs/gbo-simple-v1.md#L5-L19). A source that needs another form delivers it itself. Claims derived from source data are an open decision of PSA S11.
    • In demo v0.9.0, onboarding for EUDI accepts only whole amounts. nl-wallet v0.5 cannot show a non-integer value (source_claims.go#L220-L221, docs/gbo-simple-v1.md#L121). That is a product property.
    • If an error occurs, the consumer sees only 502. The error code is in the adapter log.
    • The ASIP does not use gbo-simple-v1. Its asi capability composes values with pointer, join, const, and each (ADR 0039). The rule "no partial result" holds there too (REQ-101).

docs.title: REQ-124: For every attestation, the versions of the mapping, the source schema, and the attestation schema are traceable
docs.text:
For every issued attestation, the GBO issuance facility MUST make the applied versions traceable. These are the versions of the mapping of the bronhouder, of the source schema, and of the attestation schema. The facility MUST apply only the mapping that the bronhouder recorded for that data service in its GBO configuration (REQ-116). If the bronhouder recorded no mapping, the facility MUST convert nothing.

Case Outcome Mapping recorded and activated converted. The mapping version, the source version, and the target version are traceable at issuance. No mapping recorded nothing converted, and no attestation New mapping version activated later issuances name the new version, and earlier ones name the old version
  • Status: draft
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design: PSA S10 ("mappings to OOTS-EDM and attestation schemas are explicit. They can be traced to the source and target versions used"), PSA S11 (the bronhouder records in its GBO configuration which mapping applies), and D-14.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: issuance (the EUDI adapter).
  • Evidence: REQ-116 gives the evidence that only the mapping of the bronhouder is applied. The traceability of the versions is not checked.
  • Related: REQ-59, REQ-64, REQ-66, REQ-72, REQ-116, Q-79.
  • Notes:
    • Traceability can come from the version of the activated source metadata (REQ-66) in the processing log record (REQ-72). The form is a design choice.
    • This requirement is the counterpart for the mapping of REQ-59 (the policy version in the decision record).
    • S10 asks the same for the mapping to OOTS-EDM. That requirement follows after Q-79.

docs.title: Removed numbers
docs.text:
• REQ-51: removed. REQ-44 (thin channel adapter) and REQ-64 (source-owned description) cover "The adapter does not hard-code use-case parameters".

The list of all removed numbers is on the requirements overview.

docs.title: Logging and audit requirements
docs.text:
These requirements cover the three records of GBO: the decision record (ADL), the processing record (LDV), and the trace that links them. For the design, see Logging, audit and traceability.

This page has the following parts:

  • Decision audit requirements
  • Processing logging requirements
  • Observability requirements

docs.title: Decision audit requirements
docs.text:
The decision audit requirements cover the record of authorization decisions. They set rules for these topics:

  • the Authorization Decision Log (ADL) of Logius
  • the protection of the record
  • the policy version that the record names
  • the personal data that the record can hold

The requirements are generic. They apply to DvTP, EUDI issuance, and the ASI route. Processing logging covers the record of each processing (LDV). Observability covers the trace ID.

docs.title: REQ-32: Audit records are protected, complete, and stored apart from operational logs
docs.text:
Decision records (ADL) and processing log records (LDV) MUST be protected against change and deletion. This protection applies to anyone who does not manage them. They MUST NOT be sampled. They MUST have their own retention period and access, independent of those of operational logs and traces. Operational logs MAY carry the same trace ID, but they are no audit source.

  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • PSA S09: measures protect log data against unauthorized change and deletion, and agreements set retention, access, inspection, and destruction explicitly ("maatregelen beschermen loggegevens tegen ongeautoriseerde wijziging en verwijdering", "afspraken regelen bewaartermijnen, toegang, inzage en vernietiging expliciet").
    • LDV, behavior of the application (no log sampling).
    • P-12.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the logbook and the components that write to it. Interface and audit agreement: the decision record at the source.
  • Evidence:
    • The ADL is in Postgres, apart from the console log in Loki (docker-compose.yml#L117-L125, PR #337).
    • Readers get only SELECT (adl-reader.sql#L17, PR #373).
    • The logbook in the demo has write and read, and no change or delete (handler.go#L49-L53). That logbook is a stand-in for the logbook of the controller (Verantwoordelijke). It is no GBO component.
    • Retention period and tamper resistance at storage level: not built.
  • Related: REQ-71, REQ-72, REQ-123, Q-08, ADR 0036.
  • Notes: retention periods and read access are open in Q-08. Nobody tested whether the writing role of the PDP can change its own records.

docs.title: REQ-59: The decision record names the policy version that decided
docs.text:
Every decision record (REQ-71) MUST carry the identity and version of the policy set that made the decision (adl.core.policies). For every policy set, it MUST be traceable which version became active when. The source decides how it forms that version (bundle ID with version, commit hash, image version).

  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • PSA S09: authorization decisions refer to the applied policy version and to relevant information about the legal basis ("autorisatiebeslissingen verwijzen naar de toegepaste beleidsversie en relevante informatie over de grondslag").
    • ADL adl.core.policies.
    • PSA S06 (start date and change history).
  • Addressee: interface and audit agreement: every PDP that decides on a data request.
  • Evidence: not built, and there is no demo issue for it. The bundle carries a version (gbo-pdp.yaml#L17), but that version does not reach the ADL record (PR #373). Records carry policies: 0.
  • Related: REQ-71, F-53, Q-08, Q-21, RL-01, RL-04.
  • Notes: without this field, nobody can link the history of the policy (who published which version) to a decision. In the default stack, the policy comes from the PDP image. In that case, the version must also be traceable.

docs.title: REQ-60: Logging contains no BSN that the processing does not need
docs.text:
A GBO-delivered component MUST keep the BSN and other directly identifying data out of its operational logs and spans. Some identifying values in the PDP input are not necessary for the decision. A component that builds the PDP input MUST keep such a value out of the input, or replace it before it sends the input. If that fails, the request does not continue. Masking in the decision log MUST NOT be the only safeguard.

Case Outcome Operational log or span no BSN. A data subject (Betrokkene) only as pseudonym or opaque reference PDP input, DvTP no identity: a placeholder, which the source replaces only after the consent Decryption or replacement fails the request does not reach the source PDP input, EUDI and ASI no BSN (not met in demo v0.9.0, see the notes)
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design. PSA S09 (logging holds no more personal data than necessary: "logging bevat niet meer persoonsgegevens dan noodzakelijk") and P-03, P-04.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the GBO components and the chain that builds the PDP input. It is no requirement on the policy engine of the source.
  • Evidence:
    • DvTP: PR #469, tested in substitution_test.go#L76, #L247, and ldv_test.go#L385.
    • Logs and spans in the ASI chain: e2e_test.go#L425 (PR #535) and trace_test.go#L110 (PR #530).
    • For the other components, there is no automatic check.
  • Related: REQ-20, REQ-21, REQ-71, REQ-72, F-54, F-72, Q-08, ADR 0043.
  • Notes:
    • Design choice: leave the value out before the policy engine, instead of masking it inside the engine. From the outside, a masking rule that does not work looks the same as one that works (F-54).
    • In the EUDI channel and the ASI route, the BSN is in the PDP input, and so in the decision record (eudi-adapter/source_metadata.go#L272-L273, asi-provider/internal/graphqlsource/source.go#L94).
    • Demo issue #368 decides how the BSN goes out. If the team chooses masking there, this requirement must change.

docs.title: REQ-71: Every authorization decision is in an ADL-conformant decision record, and that record is the audit source
docs.text:
Every authorization decision on a data request MUST be recorded in a record according to the Logius standard Authorization Decision Log. The record MUST make it possible to replay the decision. It holds the request, the answer, and the policy version (REQ-59). It also holds the answer of every information source consulted during the evaluation (adl.core.information). A reference to that answer can replace the answer. The reference MUST then stay available as long as the record exists.

If the request passes an FSC Inway or Outway, adl.fsc.transaction_id MUST be set. Where more decision logs exist side by side, the ADL record MUST be the designated audit source. Other streams MUST NOT be an audit source.

Case Outcome Allowed or denied one record, with outcome and reason code Evaluation fails also one record Decision depends on the consent status the status answer is in or with the record Request through FSC adl.fsc.transaction_id next to trace_id
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • PSA S09 (Authorization Decision Log to record authorization decisions).
    • GO, reused building blocks (ADL 1.0.0).
    • ADL (adl.core.information, adl.fsc.transaction_id).
    • FR-31 criterion 1.
  • Addressee: interface and audit agreement: the PDP of every source, whatever the product. GBO-delivered component: what GBO delivers to the PDP (request mapping, policy).
  • Evidence: the ADL in Postgres is mandatory (docker-compose.yml#L125, PR #337). The demo reads it as the audit source (PR #373). The demo does not meet these parts:
    • transaction ID and trace behind the Inway (#369)
    • policy version (REQ-59)
    • status answer in the record (F-72)
  • Related: REQ-32, REQ-55, REQ-59, REQ-60, REQ-06, F-41, F-53, F-63, F-72, Q-08, Q-25, ADR 0036.
  • Notes:
    • The detail for each field (which fields were allowed or denied) does not need to be in the record. It follows from a replay, and the ADL prefers a reference to a copy.
    • A reference brings a retention duty for its source (Q-08).
    • The ADL is working version 1.0.0. Pin the version in a conformance claim.
    • The policy fetches the consent status during evaluation. For that reason, a replay from (input, policy, data) needs the status answer in the record.

docs.title: Removed numbers
docs.text: • REQ-31 (persistent, correlatable audit record for each authorization decision): merged into REQ-71.

docs.title: Processing logging requirements
docs.text:
The processing logging requirement covers the record of each processing of personal data. Decision audit covers the decision side (ADL). The requirement on this page covers the processing side. It is generic and applies to DvTP, EUDI issuance, and the ASI route.

The Logius standard Logboek Dataverwerkingen (LDV) asks for a log record for every processing, for each controller. Only trace metadata crosses an organization boundary. The decision of a PDP is no processing. A transformation at the source, such as the decryption by the source gateway, is a processing (F-64).

docs.title: REQ-72: A GBO component that processes personal data writes an LDV log record for each processing at its controller
docs.text:
Every GBO-delivered component that processes data of a data subject MUST write a log record according to Logboek Dataverwerkingen for each action. It MUST write the record to the logbook of the controller of that processing. The trace ID in that record MUST follow from REQ-55. There MUST be a separate log record for each data subject. A further data subject of the same processing hangs as a child under the first.

The field dpl.core.data_subject_id MUST name the data subject in an identifier space of the controller itself, with an explicit data_subject_id_type. It MUST NOT name the data subject with the BSN. The field dpl.core.processing_activity_id MUST refer to a versioned, resolvable processing activity. A component that calls another party during the processing MUST set dpl.read.nextLogbookId to the read API of that party. Only trace metadata crosses an organization boundary.

  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • LDV and its read extension.
    • PSA S09 (LDV as functional frame, and each component records the events that are relevant for its responsibility: "iedere component legt de gebeurtenissen vast die voor zijn verantwoordelijkheid relevant zijn").
    • GO, reused building blocks.
    • FR-31 criterion 1.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: source gateway (bron-sidecar), consent register (toestemmingsregister), consent portal (toestemmingsportaal), EUDI adapter, and ASIP. The logbook and the source application of a bronhouder belong to that bronhouder (P-10).
  • Evidence: ICTU/GBO-demo#302, PR #366, PR #469. Code and tests:
    • The source gateway logs decryption and forwarding (bron-sidecar/ldv_test.go#L309).
    • The EUDI adapter names the holder without a BSN (eudi-adapter/ldv_test.go#L159) and points to the logbook of the source (#L471).
    • Child records: brp-graphql-server/ldv_query.go#L219.
    • Write side: PR #303. A processing that cannot be logged delivers nothing (bron-sidecar/ldv_test.go#L475-L492).
  • Related: REQ-32, REQ-55, REQ-60, REQ-76, AV-02, AV-10, F-64, F-68, F-69, Q-08, Q-25, Q-72, ADR 0026.
  • Notes:
    • The ldv-logboek in the demo is a stand-in for the logbook of the controller, and is no GBO component. It refuses a record with a BSN (validate.go#L148, tested in validate_test.go#L94) or with an activity that does not resolve (validate.go#L119). That is therefore no evidence for this requirement.
    • LDV allows BSN as a type. "Never the BSN" is a stricter rule from S09 and P-04.
    • The register of processing activities is a stand-in for each logbook (register.go#L28). A real register is missing. For GBO components it belongs with the management organization (Q-08).
    • dpl.core.foreign_operation.processor is a URL made from the FSC peer ID or the grant hash. It identifies the caller, but nothing resolves behind it.
    • In demo v0.9.0, the ASIP writes no log records.
    • Design choice: a processing delivers data only after its log record is durable locally (outbox). An outage of the logbook does not stop the chain (graphql-server/main.go#L394-L398, bron-sidecar/main.go#L541-L549).
    • It is open whether GBO components write attributes outside the LDV core: Q-72.

docs.title: Removed numbers
docs.text: • REQ-73 (a consumer sends trace context and records the transaction ID of every source call): removed, replaced by connection condition AV-01.

docs.title: Observability requirements
docs.text: The observability requirement covers the correlation of logs and traces over the chain. Each request has one trace ID, and the components record the FSC transaction ID next to it. The requirement is generic. It applies to DvTP, EUDI issuance, and the ASI route. Decision audit covers the decision record. Processing logging covers the processing record.

docs.title: REQ-55: One trace ID per request across the whole chain, and the transaction ID can be linked to it
docs.text:
Every GBO-delivered component MUST take the trace ID of an incoming request unchanged from W3C Trace Context (traceparent). It MUST record the span of the caller as parent. It MUST send traceparent with every outgoing call. Every record that the component writes about the request (processing log record, operational log record, span) MUST carry that trace ID. The Fsc-Transaction-Id MUST NOT replace an incoming trace. A component that starts or receives an FSC transaction MUST record the transaction ID next to the trace ID.

Case Outcome Request with traceparent trace ID taken over, and the span of the caller is parent. An Fsc-Transaction-Id that comes with it does not change the trace ID Request without traceparent, with Fsc-Transaction-Id the transaction ID MAY be the trace ID Entry component without traceparent that starts a transaction itself MAY choose its trace ID equal to that transaction ID Processing with more than one FSC hop one trace ID, several transaction IDs. The link runs through the records that carry both, and does not depend on equality
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • PSA S09 (each data request gets a request identifier that is usable over the whole chain: "iedere gegevensvraag krijgt een verzoekidentificator die over de hele keten bruikbaar is", and standardized correlation and trace context).
    • LDV trace_id.
    • W3C Trace Context.
    • FR-31 criterion 1 (traceable correlation references across components).
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component.
  • Evidence: PR #366, PR #530. Code and tests:
    • Order of sources for the trace ID: tracecontext.go#L78, tested in tracecontext_test.go#L100 and #L86.
    • Take-over: source gateway bron-sidecar/ldv_test.go#L415, EUDI adapter eudi-adapter/ldv_test.go#L308, and ASIP graphqlsource/trace_test.go#L96.
    • Pass-on: outway.go#L45-L50.
    • Transaction ID on the span behind the Inway: graphql-server/main.go#L385-L387.
    • Trace ID in operational logs: slogctx.go#L15-L24.
    • Parent only within the same trace (PR #329, tracecontext.go#L166-L192, tested in tracecontext_test.go#L146-L170).
    • The PDP passes trace and transaction ID on to the register (PR #305, consent.rego#L190-L200).
  • Related: REQ-71, REQ-72, AV-01, F-16, F-39, F-41, F-67, ADR 0035.
  • Notes:
    • Behind the FSC Inway, the decision record does not meet this requirement. The Inway gives the PDP no traceparent, and gives the transaction ID only as X-Request-Id. So the ADL record gets its own trace and no adl.fsc.transaction_id (F-41, #369). That is behavior of FSC and the policy engine. The fix lies upstream.
    • In demo v0.9.0, the operational logs of the source gateway, the EUDI adapter, and the ASIP do not carry a trace ID.
    • Design choice: logs and traces are joined on identifier equality. The join does not use timestamps.
    • Consent issuance and the later query are separate units of work, with separate traces. The consent_id joins them (F-16).

docs.title: Removed numbers
docs.text:
• REQ-16 (end-to-end traceparent propagation): merged into REQ-55.
  • REQ-28 (logs and traces can be reconstructed by a shared identifier for each request): merged into REQ-55.
  • REQ-29 (no BSN in observability logs): merged into REQ-60.
  • REQ-54 (peer transaction log and portal correlation by Fsc-Transaction-Id): merged into REQ-55.

docs.title: Pseudonymization and BSNk requirements
docs.text:
These requirements cover how the citizen is identified without a BSN for the consumer, and the preconditions that BSNk PP sets for that design. For the design, see Who sees which identifier and Pseudonymization.

This page has the following parts:

  • Pseudonymization and subject identifier requirements
  • BSNk PP preconditions for the DvTP design

docs.title: Pseudonymization and subject identifier requirements
docs.text:
In the consent path, the consumer holds no identifier of the citizen at all. This applies to the BSN and to every other identifier. The requirements on this page cover four topics:

  • what the consent proof carries about the citizen
  • how a request names the subject
  • where the value from the proof becomes a BSN or a source pseudonym
  • what the consent facility (toestemmingsvoorziening) must know to make those values

The design of demo increment SL-51 works in four steps:

  1. At consent time, the consent portal (toestemmingsportaal) backend asks BSNk PP for a value for each receiving source. Every source gets an encrypted pseudonym (VP). Only a source on the BSN Authorization List (Autorisatielijst BSN) also gets an encrypted identity (VI). BSNk transforms only while the citizen is logged in (BSNK-04).
  2. The consent register (toestemmingsregister) signs these values into the proof as encrypted_subject, keyed by the OIN of each source. It does not keep the values. It keeps the polymorphic identity (PI) and the polymorphic pseudonym (PP) of the portal under a reference to the citizen.
  3. The consumer names the subject with a placeholder. It uses consent:identity for a BSN API and consent:pseudonym for an API on the own pseudonym of the source. The PDP sees no identifier of the citizen.
  4. After the allow, the source gateway (bron-sidecar) takes the value for its own OIN. The decryption component of the source reads the value. The gateway checks that the value names its own OIN as recipient. Then the gateway puts the result in the place of the placeholder. There is no BSNk call at query time.

ADR 0032 records the proof and the placeholder. ADR 0033 records the decryption at the gateway. BSNk preconditions lists what BSNk PP imposes.

In the demo, the BSNk mock follows the BSNk interface but does not encrypt. As a result, anyone can read the values. The three demo sources share one OIN and one decryption component.

docs.title: REQ-20: In the consent path the consumer gets no BSN in the proof or in the response
docs.text:
In the consent path, the consumer MUST NOT receive a BSN. The BSN MUST NOT be in the consent proof, in another value from the consent facility, or in the answer of the source. The consumer MUST be able to make a request without knowing an identifier of the citizen. A rule in the consent regime MUST NOT allow a field that returns the BSN. A policy set MUST enforce that with a test per rule.

Case Outcome The consumer reads the consent proof only the consent ID and the scopes. The citizen is in the proof only as values that the sources can read. Under consent, the consumer asks for the BSN field of the source denied with NO_APPLICABLE_RULE. The consumer sees FIELD_NOT_PERMITTED.
  • Status: draft
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design: P-04, PSA S03 ("voorkomen dat onbevoegde afnemers het BSN ontvangen"), GO, building blocks (BSNk PP for all DvTP requests, before a private service provider receives data), and FR-35 criteria 2 and 3.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the consent portal and the consent register (what the proof carries), and the reference policy of the PDP (which fields are allowed under consent). Interface agreement: what the consumer sees.
  • Evidence: to build: ICTU/GBO-demo#604. PR #469 gives this evidence:
    • The consumer reads only the consent ID and the scopes (token.go#L11-L18).
    • The consumer names the subject with a placeholder (kind.go#L39-L54, test consumer_test.go#L84-L99).
    • The portal has values made only for the sources (portal.go#L197-L224, test portal_test.go#L444-L457).
    • Under consent, no rule covers the BSN field (dvt0001.rego#L32-L45 against bd.graphql#L45-L51).
    • No test covers the answer path.
  • Related: REQ-17, REQ-21, REQ-69, REQ-79, REQ-80, F-15, F-30, F-76, Q-01, Q-27.
  • Notes:
    • The requirement applies to the consent path. In the EUDI path, the request carries a BSN that the PDP sees. ICTU/GBO-demo#368 covers how to keep that BSN out of the decision log.
    • P-04 and FR-35 criterion 2 allow a party-specific pseudonym for the consumer. That pseudonym is outside this requirement and not built (ICTU/GBO-demo#478). Its form is Q-01.
    • The consumer holds no identifier. As a result, what the consumer records about "this person" depends on the consent (F-76, Q-27).
    • In demo v0.9.0, the answer path depends only on the closed world of the rules. No test checks, for each rule in the consent regime, that the rule covers no BSN field.

docs.title: REQ-21: The source converts the value from the proof itself, only after a positive decision and without a central party
docs.text:
The source MUST convert the value from the consent proof itself, to the BSN or to its own pseudonym. The conversion MUST take place after a positive decision of its PDP, and MUST NOT take place after a deny. The BSN MUST stay limited to the source and exists there only for the source call. The conversion MUST NOT need a call to BSNk or another central party. If the conversion fails, the request MUST NOT reach the source.

Case Outcome Allowed request with consent:identity one decryption. The source gets the BSN in the place of the placeholder. Allowed request with consent:pseudonym the source gets its own pseudonym. The identity is not read. Request without a subject passes unchanged, and nothing is decrypted Request outside the transport subset of the profile refused, and nothing is decrypted Decryption fails not forwarded, and recorded as a failed processing Decryption cannot be recorded not forwarded
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design:
    • PSA S03 ("de inrichting voert identiteitsvertaling alleen uit voor een toegestane dienst en gegevensvraag"), with the provision "veilige omzetting aan de kant van de bronhouder"
    • FR-35 criterion 3
    • precondition BSNK-04: BSNk transforms only while the citizen is logged in, so it does not transform at query time
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the source gateway and its link with the decryption component of the source.
  • Evidence: PR #469, PR #477, and PR #494 give this evidence:
    • The gateway acts on the proof and substitutes only behind the Inway (main.go#L1-L9, #L232-L259, substitution.go#L149-L211).
    • A component that offers nothing of BSNk decrypts with the own keys of the source (decryption.go#L1-L8, docker-compose.yml#L773-L793, httpapi.go#L34-L53).
    • The tests are ldv_test.go#L182-L221, #L228-L273, #L383-L410, #L494-L510, transport_test.go#L82-L104, and substitution_test.go#L160-L181.
  • Related: REQ-04, REQ-20, REQ-79, REQ-80, REQ-81, F-30, F-37, F-79, ADR 0033.
  • Notes:
    • Design choice: the conversion is in a gateway behind the Inway, and not in a plugin on the Inway. A plugin after the authorization is possible only in an own build of the Inway (ICTU/GBO-demo#364).
    • If the conversion takes place before the PDP, the PDP cannot tell a converted BSN from a BSN that the consumer filled in itself.
    • The gateway acts on the presence of a consent token. A request without a token passes unchanged (the PID regime of the EUDI path).
    • The conversion is "after the decision" only because nothing other than the Inway reaches the gateway (REQ-04, REQ-81, F-79). The gateway does not check the proof itself (substitution.go#L105-L107).
    • In the demo, the sources share one decryption component and one OIN. In production, every source runs its own.

docs.title: REQ-69: The consent register stores the polymorphic values under its own reference and no encrypted values per party
docs.text:
The consent register MUST NOT record more identifying data about the citizen than it needs to manage and show consents. It MAY keep the polymorphic identity and the polymorphic pseudonym of the first activation under its own reference to the citizen. This reference is not a BSN. It MUST NOT keep the encrypted identity and the encrypted pseudonym for a receiving party. Those values travel in the signed proof to that party.

  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design: PSA S01 ("het register bevat geen BSN als een pseudonieme identificatie volstaat"), P-03 and P-04, and FR-35 criterion 1. The design tightens FR-35 criterion 1 and deliberately fills it in differently (see the notes). Precondition: BSNK-03.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the consent register (S01).
  • Evidence: PR #238 and PR #469 give this evidence:
    • The stored model knows only the reference (main.go#L33-L46).
    • The values per party go only into the signed proof (#L449).
    • The register stores PI and PP separately under the reference, and the first pair stays (postgres_store.go#L52-L60, #L122-L129).
    • The reference is in subjectref.go#L11-L25.
    • The tests are polymorphic_test.go#L39, #L85, portal_test.go#L348-L385, and #L389-L419.
  • Related: REQ-20, REQ-23, REQ-68, REQ-80, F-98, Q-01, Q-49, Q-56, Q-57, ADR 0040.
  • Notes:
    • Design choice: the register keeps PI and PP, so the portal activates a citizen once and not at every consent (route D).
    • This choice deliberately deviates from the text of FR-35 criterion 1. That criterion allows the register to record only a party-specific identifier in place of the BSN, and the consent proof ("een partijspecifiek kenmerk ter vervanging van het BSN en het bewijs van toestemming"). The design differs from that text in three ways:
      • The register keeps PI and PP under its own reference.
      • The register keeps no party-specific values.
      • The register does not keep the proof, but signs it.
    • F-98 reports this deviation to the owner of FR-DvTP.
    • A polymorphic value is specific to the party that requested it, and does not leave that party (BSNK-03). Only the encrypted values are specific to a recipient.
    • The portal (S02) requests the values and the register (S01) keeps them. That split fits only if both belong to the same BSNk participant (Q-49).
    • Q-57 covers the protection of the kept PI and PP. Q-56 covers the rotation of the key behind the reference. Q-01 covers whether the recipient-specific pseudonym fits legally.

docs.title: REQ-79: Under a consent the subject comes only from the proof
docs.text:
A request under a consent MUST name the subject with a fixed placeholder. The request MUST NOT carry its own value for the subject. The placeholder states which form the source API takes: the BSN or the own pseudonym of the source. Every rule MUST name the placeholders that its API accepts. The PDP MUST deny a request that has anything other than such a placeholder in the place of the subject.

The placeholder MUST apply only under a proof that the PDP verified itself. Without such a proof, the placeholder stands for nobody. The placeholder MUST come as a variable of the request. If the placeholder is written literally in the query text, the PDP MUST deny.

Case Outcome Verified proof, placeholder that the rule accepts the subject is the citizen of the proof, and the other checks decide Literal BSN under a proof denied with CONSTRAINT_MISMATCH Placeholder literally in the query text denied (in the demo: allowed, and the source finds nobody) Placeholder that the rule does not accept (consent:pseudonym for DVT0001 and LVG0001) denied with CONSTRAINT_MISMATCH Unknown placeholder (consent:subject) denied with CONSTRAINT_MISMATCH Placeholder under a proof that does not verify denied with the reason of the proof, and with CONSTRAINT_MISMATCH Subject only from a schema default denied with CONSTRAINT_MISMATCH Placeholder without a proof PID regime, denied with PID_NOT_PRESENT A literal value under a proof still reaches the source gateway refused, and nothing is decrypted
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: derived. The requirement serves P-01 and PSA S05. If the consumer can fill in the subject itself, the consent of one citizen applies to the data of another citizen. Also design: FR-35 criteria 2 and 3, and P-04 (the consumer does not know the BSN).
  • Addressee: interface agreement: the placeholder in the request. GBO-delivered component: the reference policy of the PDP and the source gateway.
  • Evidence: to build: ICTU/GBO-demo#603. PR #469, PR #476, PR #507, and PR #484 give this evidence:
    • The placeholders are in lib.rego#L43-L53.
    • The placeholders apply only under a verified proof (dvtp_helper.rego#L67-L74).
    • Each rule names its placeholders (dvt0001.rego#L72-L80, lvg0001.rego#L50-L56).
    • The PID regime takes no placeholder (eudi_helper.rego#L32-L39).
    • The consumer sends a placeholder per kind of question (kind.go#L39-L54).
    • The gateway refuses a literal value (substitution.go#L167-L179).
    • The tests are dvt0001_test.rego#L128-L158, lvg0001_test.rego#L52-L55, dvtp_helper_test.rego#L31-L56, engine_test.rego#L272-L285, #L340-L347, eud0001_test.rego#L75-L79, ldv_test.go#L291-L305, and substitution_test.go#L139-L158.
  • Related: REQ-06, REQ-17, REQ-20, REQ-21, REQ-48, REQ-68, REQ-74, F-44, F-77, ADR 0032.
  • Notes:
    • Design choice: the names consent:identity and consent:pseudonym come from the demo.
    • The argument at the source is called bsn, also when a pseudonym goes into it. This fact belongs in the connection documentation for consumers.
    • One placeholder per form means one subject per request. A question about more than one person does not fit this design (F-77, point 2).
    • The gateway substitutes only variables. A placeholder written literally in the query text passes the PDP and is not substituted. The source then finds nobody (F-77, point 3).
    • A separate check (REQ-48) covers that the consent was given to this caller.
    • If the PDP denies, the consumer sees FIELD_NOT_PERMITTED (REQ-06).
    • In demo v0.9.0, the subject variable is not in one place (ICTU/GBO-demo#479).

docs.title: REQ-80: The proof carries a value per party that only that party can read, and the recipient checks that the value is meant for it
docs.text:
The consent proof MUST name the citizen only in values that are made per receiving party. Each value carries the identification of that party and the version of its keys. A recipient MUST decrypt its value itself, with keys that it received in advance. A recipient MUST refuse a value that, according to the value itself, was made for another party. The consent register and the consumer MUST NOT be able to read the values.

Case Outcome Proof without values, or with a party without a pseudonym the register gives no consent. The PDP denies with CONSENT_CONTEXT_INVALID. Proof without a value for this source refused at the source, and nothing is decrypted Value under the OIN of the source, but made for another party refused at the source Identity asked, the source has only a pseudonym refused at the source. The source does not read the pseudonym instead. A source that points to a key directory without keys the gateway does not start
  • Status: ready for review
Source, evidence and notes
  • Source: design: P-04, PSA S03 ("een private afnemer zonder wettelijke BSN-bevoegdheid ontvangt een partijspecifieke identiteit of pseudoniem", "pseudoniemen voor verschillende partijen of contexten zijn niet onderling koppelbaar"), GO, building blocks (BSNk PP for all DvTP requests), and FR-35 criteria 2 and 4. Preconditions: BSNK-03, BSNK-07, BSNK-08, and BSNK-09.
  • Addressee: GBO-delivered component: the portal (has the values made), the register (signs them into the proof), and the source gateway (reads them). Interface agreement: the claim encrypted_subject in the proof.
  • Evidence: PR #466, PR #469, and PR #477 give this evidence:
    • The claim is in consent_token.go#L22-L36 and #L70-L80.
    • The register and the PDP require a pseudonym per party (consent_token.go#L45-L64, consent.rego#L154-L161).
    • The portal has values made per form (portal.go#L197-L224).
    • The source reads with its own keys (decryption.go#L1-L8, #L44-L71) and checks the recipient (substitution.go#L213-L251).
    • The consumer does not read the values (token.go#L11-L18).
    • The tests are substitution_test.go#L110-L137, #L183-L196, #L232-L245, ldv_test.go#L275-L289, main_test.go#L151-L158, and consent_test.rego#L406-L424. The register test is main_test.go#L197.
  • Related: REQ-21, REQ-68, REQ-69, REQ-82, AV-09, F-75, F-78, Q-01, Q-26.
  • Notes:
    • The demo tries out the form and the split of roles. It uses a mock that follows the BSNk interface but does not encrypt.
    • In the demo, anyone can read the values. As a result, the demo does not demonstrate the last sentence of the requirement.
    • The real BSNk needs pre-production access.
    • In the demo, the sources share one OIN, so there is one value per form.
    • Proofs from before SL-51 (with a pi claim) are refused.
    • An own pseudonym for the consumer is not built (ICTU/GBO-demo#478). No demo source takes a pseudonym (ICTU/GBO-demo#474).
    • ICTU/GBO-demo#467 and BSNK-09 cover how a source gets its keys.
    • A source keeps the keys of an older version as long as proofs for that version are valid (decryption.go#L44-L46, AV-09). For more information, see REQ-82.

docs.title: REQ-81: Only the component that enforces the decision reaches the source gateway
docs.text:
The source gateway converts the value from the consent proof to the BSN or to the own pseudonym of the source. The gateway MUST be reachable only for the component that enforces the authorization decision (the PEP of the source). This way, the conversion can take place only after a positive decision.
