docs.title: Admission and activation
docs.text:
Two management-plane scenarios come before the first request:

  1. Contract admission: a party asks for an FSC contract. The FSC Manager of the provider asks the PDP whether that party is admitted.
  2. Source activation: the operator of a GBO component takes a source into use. The component fetches the service description of the source, validates it, and activates it as an immutable release.

Both scenarios carry no citizen data. They share one principle: a valid contract is necessary, but it is not enough. Admission comes from a register and does not follow from the contract (REQ-61). Activation is an explicit management action and does not follow from the contract either (REQ-65).

For the concepts, see Authorization: admission and contract acceptance and Source onboarding. The decisions are ADR-0015 and ADR-0016.

docs.title: Scenario 1: contract admission
docs.text:
A consumer, an integrator, or a GBO component (the issuance facility, the ASIP, the PDP itself) wants to connect to an FSC service of a bronhouder. The party creates a contract proposal in its own FSC Manager. The FSC Manager of the provider does not sign on a flag. It sends every proposal to the OpenFTV PDP as an AuthZEN evaluation and signs only on allow (fsc-infra/docker-compose.yml#L701-L702). The FSC Managers of the BRP peer and the consent register (toestemmingsregister) peer use the same policy (#L892-L893, #L1079-L1080).

sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(241,239,232) Administrator actor ADM as Register administrator end box rgb(237,233,254) Admission register participant REG as Admission register<br/>(dvtp-onboarding-register) end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis participant PDP as OpenFTV PDP<br/>(autosign.rego) participant CM as FSC Manager<br/>of the consumer participant PM as FSC Manager<br/>of the provider end box rgb(237,233,254) Records participant ADL as ADL<br/>(postgres-ftv) end ADM->>REG: Admit party: Peer ID, name, active, admitted sources loop Every 5 s (PIP pull) PDP->>REG: GET /internal/openftv/participants REG-->>PDP: Participants with acts_for end CM->>CM: POST /v1/contracts (grant), signed by the consumer CM->>PM: Contract proposal (FSC, mTLS) PM->>PDP: AuthZEN evaluation<br/>context.doelbinding = auto_sign_contract PDP->>PDP: Eight ordered checks on the register data PDP->>ADL: Decision record alt Allow PDP-->>PM: decision true, rule FSC_AUTOSIGN_ADMITTED_PARTY PM->>PM: Countersign PM-->>CM: Signature: the contract becomes valid else Deny PDP-->>PM: decision false, reason_admin.code Note over PM: The proposal stays proposed.<br/>No signature, no rejection. end

docs.title: Data per hop
docs.text:
Each hop of contract admission carries the following data:

# From → to Interface Data Notes 1 Administrator → register Register UI (localhost:9415), CSRF-protected forms FSC Peer ID (20 characters), display name, active, Peer IDs of the admitted bronhouders The register has no accounts. Anyone who reaches the UI locally is administrator (README). Integrations (acts_for) and technical participants are part of the deployment configuration. The UI does not manage them 2 to 3 PDP → register GET /internal/openftv/participants (handler.go#L63), interval 5 s, timeout 2 s data.entities.dvtp_participant, keyed by Peer ID: name, active, allowed_source_peer_ids, acts_for (dvtp-onboarding.yaml) The pull uses a network that only the register and the PDP share. Every entry carries acts_for. If the party acts for nobody, acts_for is empty. As a result, a withdrawn mandate replaces the old entity 4 Consumer → own FSC Manager POST /v1/contracts, internal API, mTLS (seed-bri-connection-hv.sh#L113-L135) Contract content: grant (type and service), validity, the peers FSC grants carry no properties (ADR-0031) 5 Consumer Manager → provider Manager FSC Manager interface, mTLS with the organization certificate (demo CA) Signed contract proposal The contract hash identifies the proposal. A new submission is a new proposal with a new hash 6 Provider Manager → PDP AuthZEN, https://openftv-pdp:8443/authzen/v1, the Manager pins the PDP CA subject (self_peer_id, peer_ids), action autosign_contract, resource (contract hash, grant_types), context.doelbinding = auto_sign_contract (autosign.rego#L12-L15) The input has no service name and no delegation direction. The PDP judges who connects. It does not judge to which service (F-56) 7 to 8 PDP Package doelbinding.auto_sign_contract, separate from the request policy (REQ-62) Decision record in the ADL, next to the request decisions The purpose limitation (doelbinding) selects the package. A renamed package resolves to nothing (autosign.rego#L8-L10) 9 to 11 PDP → provider Manager → consumer Manager AuthZEN response, then FSC signature Allow: FSC_AUTOSIGN_ADMITTED_PARTY, counterparties, source Peer ID. Deny: first failing code, counterparties, grant types (autosign.rego#L184-L202) The response holds only Peer IDs and no personal data

docs.title: Ordered refusal codes
docs.text:
The policy runs eight checks in a fixed order. The first check that fails names the refusal (autosign.rego#L165-L175). Each check defaults to false, so malformed input leads to a refusal instead of an undefined check. The policy refuses a contract for one of eight reasons, in this order:

# Code Refuses when Tests (v0.9.0) 1 NOT_AN_AUTOSIGN_REQUEST The action is not autosign_contract, the resource is not a contract, or attributes are missing autosign_test.rego#L223, #L230, #L239 2 GRANT_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED The grants are not all type 2 (service connection) and not all type 3 (delegated service connection): a publication, a mix, or no grant #L149, #L205, #L209, #L213 3 NO_COUNTERPARTY The contract names no party other than the provider #L219 4 ADMISSION_REGISTER_UNAVAILABLE The PIP pull supplied no register #L86, #L91 5 PARTY_NOT_IN_REGISTRY A counterparty is not in the register. This also applies when the register is empty #L130, #L96, #L190 6 PARTY_NOT_ACTIVE A counterparty is suspended (active is not true) #L138, #L185, #L195 7 SOURCE_NOT_ALLOWED A counterparty is not admitted for the Peer ID of this source #L109, #L113 8 DELEGATION_NOT_REGISTERED The contract has a delegated grant, but no integration between the two counterparties is registered #L176, #L180, #L201

The tests #L74, #L117, and #L171 cover the allow paths. If the policy refuses one party among several, it refuses the whole contract (#L143).

A refusal leaves the proposal at proposed. The party can correct its admission and submit again. The new submission gets a new assessment (REQ-63). This behavior is product behavior of the FSC Manager. No automated test covers it. If a setup configures an automatic refusal, the setup breaks the requirement.

docs.title: Delegated grant (integrator)
docs.text:
An integrator connects on behalf of a consumer (the represented party). The integrator uses one contract that holds a delegated service connection grant (type 3). The contract has three signatures (seed-bri-delegation-int.sh#L1-L17):

sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis: FSC and PDP participant IM as FSC Manager<br/>of the integrator participant DM as FSC Manager<br/>of the represented party participant PM as FSC Manager<br/>of the provider participant PDP as OpenFTV PDP end IM->>IM: Create contract: delegated grant,<br/>integrator, represented party, service IM->>DM: Contract proposal DM->>DM: Accept (operator action) IM->>PM: Contract proposal PM->>PDP: AuthZEN evaluation, grant_types [3] Note over PDP: Checks 1–7 for both counterparties,<br/>then check 8: one acts_for the other PDP-->>PM: Allow, or DELEGATION_NOT_REGISTERED PM-->>IM: Countersignature: contract valid

Each hop of the delegated grant carries the following data:

# Data Notes 1 to 2 Delegated grant with the Peer IDs of the integrator, the represented party, and the provider The FSC Manager of the represented party has no autosign. In the demo, the seed script accepts on its behalf. The script does what the operator does in the Controller UI (#L147-L167) 4 to 6 peer_ids with the two counterparties, grant_types [3] The integrator must be admitted in its own right. A mandate does not replace the admission of either party

The contract check admits the pair of counterparties. It does not check the direction (autosign.rego#L119-L139). The input does not say which party delegates. The check refuses a third counterparty. A contract that is signed the wrong way round passes this check, but the request policy denies it on every call.

At request time, the provider Manager puts the represented party in the act claim of the access token. The engine then requires a mandate for the represented party and for the granting rule (engine.rego#L246-L267, ADR-0034). The engine decides as follows:

Situation at request time Code Tests (v0.9.0) Registered integrator, mandate for the represented party and the rule allow engine_test.rego#L613 No mandate for the represented party or the rule INTEGRATOR_NOT_REGISTERED #L621 The integrator is suspended INTEGRATOR_NOT_REGISTERED #L706 The register is missing from the PDP data INTEGRATOR_REGISTER_UNAVAILABLE in the trace, request code PIP_UNAVAILABLE. The consumer sees ACCESS_DENIED #L631

The register attaches the mandates to the entry of the integrator (service_test.go#L245). The consent binds the represented party. It does not bind the integrator (REQ-106). For the DvTP query with an integrator, see DvTP query.

docs.title: Register missing against register empty
docs.text:
The PDP data can be in two states that look the same but have a different meaning (autosign.rego#L43-L59, PR #579):

PDP data Meaning Code No data.entities, or no dvtp_participant document The PIP pull supplied no register: an outage or a wrong mapping ADMISSION_REGISTER_UNAVAILABLE dvtp_participant is {} The register is available and admits nobody PARTY_NOT_IN_REGISTRY

Both states lead to a refusal. The two codes tell the operator whether the pull or the admission needs a repair. The readiness script of the demo waits for the first successful pull before it seeds contracts (wait-openftv-admission.sh).

The OpenFTV pull adds and replaces entities. If an entity disappears from a later response, the pull does not remove it. For this reason, the register deactivates a participant and never deletes it. A deleted record leaves the old admission in the PDP (REQ-61).

docs.title: Main observations
docs.text:
Contract admission in gbo-demo v0.9.0 has these properties and gaps:

  • Admission is register data (F-55). No policy rule holds the admission. Adding, suspending, or withdrawing a party changes register data. The PDP sees the change within one pull interval of 5 s, without a policy change or a restart.
  • Contract and request rules are separate (REQ-62). The two rule sets share no rules and no reason codes. They do share one policy set and one availability object. As a result, one broken module stops both (F-52).
  • A suspended consumer keeps its access. A suspension stops only new contracts. At request time, the policy checks the status of an integrator. It does not check the status of a direct consumer. A suspended consumer with an existing contract can still request data, also with a valid consent (REQ-110, Q-53).
  • Changes are not traceable. The register has no accounts and no change log (REQ-123). The task to run the register is assigned to the management organization (Q-22). It is open who builds the facility (Q-74).
  • The register key is the FSC Peer ID. It is open whether policy can read the Peer ID as the OIN of the consumer (Q-68).

docs.title: Scenario 2: source activation
docs.text:
For each source, the issuance facility and the ASIP need to know the data service, the query, the mapping, and the offer. The source publishes that description itself (REQ-64, F-57). The source reconciler of the EUDI adapter fetches the description, validates it, and writes it to the Source Registry. The runtime readers read only activated releases.

First, the metadata contract and the data contract of the source must be valid. They pass contract admission like every other contract, because the issuance facility is a technical participant in the admission register (toelatingsregister).

sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(241,239,232) Operator actor OP as Operator end box rgb(237,233,254) Certificates participant CS as Certificate store end box rgb(255,237,213) Issuance facility participant REC as Source reconciler end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis: FSC participant FM as FSC Manager<br/>of the issuance facility participant OUT as FSC Outway<br/>of the issuance facility end box rgb(221,235,247) Source participant SRC as Source<br/>(Inway, PDP, /.well-known/gbo) end box rgb(237,233,254) Source Registry participant SR as Source Registry<br/>(PostgreSQL) end box rgb(255,237,213) EUDI channel participant AD as EUDI adapter participant ASIP as ASIP participant ISS as Issuance server end OP->>REC: Add sources/configured/{source_id} OP->>CS: Place the certificate set of source_id REC->>CS: Load the certificate set Note over REC: OIN from serialNumber,<br/>name from O REC->>FM: List contracts (internal API, mTLS) FM-->>REC: Valid grants with grant hashes alt Transport fsc REC->>OUT: GET /.well-known/gbo<br/>Fsc-Grant-Hash, If-None-Match OUT->>SRC: FSC request Note over SRC: PDP rule SOURCE_METADATA_FSC SRC-->>REC: 200 document + ETag, or 304 else Transport file REC->>REC: Read the document from --metadata-dir end REC->>REC: Validate, and bind to the data contract REC->>SR: Write candidate, state rollout_required alt Demo: --auto-promote REC->>SR: Promote: immutable release + active_release_id else Production: explicit promotion OP->>SR: Promote, or activate-source-release --release-id end loop Every 5 s AD->>SR: Read the active release (reader role) AD->>AD: Swap the in-memory snapshot end loop Every 5 s ASIP->>SR: Read the active release (reader role) end OP->>ISS: make eudi-config: write issuance_server.toml, restart

docs.title: Data per hop
docs.text:
Each hop of source activation carries the following data:

# From → to Interface Data Notes 1 Operator → reconciler One file per source in sources/configured/ (source_configuration.go#L16-L28) source_id (file name), transport per leg, metadata locator, provider_peer_id The file holds no OIN and no organization name. Those values come from the certificate 2 to 4 Operator → store → reconciler Public certificate store (--certificate-store=public-filesystem) Issuer, reader and status-list leaf certificates of the source The reconciler gets only public leaves. Only the issuance init container gets the private keys (REQ-58) 5 to 6 Reconciler → FSC Manager Internal Manager API, mTLS (docker-compose.yml#L1846-L1865) Contract snapshot: per provider Peer ID and service, the grant hash A contract without a source file activates nothing 7 to 9 Reconciler → Outway → source GET /.well-known/gbo with Fsc-Grant-Hash and If-None-Match Source metadata document (gbo-source-metadata-v1, version 1.0 or 1.1), ETag The PDP of the source allows only known peers, on the metadata services, on exactly this path (authz.rego#L14-L36). The document is public and holds no citizen data. A 304 extends only the freshness 10 Reconciler Validation (service.go#L399-L416) Schema, source_oin against the certificate, version, validity window, one read operation, mapping, offers, claims, the asi capability The data service that the document names must have a valid data contract 11 Reconciler → registry Writer role Candidate per source, with state The registry refuses private key material 12 Reconciler or operator → registry One database transaction (store.go#L300-L390) Release (identified by the SHA-256 of its content) and the singleton active_release_id A release never changes. Automatic promotion is off by default (reconcile_command.go#L197). Compose turns it on 13 to 14 Adapter → registry Reader role, every 5 s (source_release_runtime.go#L59-L63) Source snapshots, Type Metadata, offer catalog The adapter loads the full material only when the release ID changes 15 ASIP → registry Reader role, ASIP_SOURCE_REGISTRY_REFRESH = 5 s (asi-provider/main.go#L101) Per data service: query, attribute mapping, legal name of the authentic source, discovery records 16 Operator → issuance server Init container writes issuance_server.toml Offers, disclosure, certificates, trust anchors The issuance server reads its configuration only at start, so a new release needs a controlled restart

For the document structure, the transports, and the release readers, see Source onboarding.

docs.title: Failure per source
docs.text:
A source that fails gets the state stale or blocked. The other sources keep their state (REQ-66). For the reason codes, see service.go#L141-L152. Source activation handles each failure as follows:

Trigger Result Tests (v0.9.0) Valid metadata contract, no source file Nothing is activated fsc_contract_discovery_test.go#L143, #L89 Certificate set missing That source gets blocked: CERTIFICATE_SET_NOT_FOUND. The reconciler checks this before any network call. The other sources continue #L172, #L278, service_test.go#L130 Certificate without OIN or organization name blocked: CERTIFICATE_SET_INVALID code (service.go#L283-L297) FSC Manager unreachable FSC sources get FSC_MANAGER_UNAVAILABLE, and the candidate stays within grace. Sources without FSC continue service_test.go#L159, #L319, fsc_contract_discovery_test.go#L599 Source file, no metadata contract blocked: METADATA_CONTRACT_NOT_FOUND #L201 Fetch fails, previous candidate within grace stale. Issuance continues on the previous version #L549, #L519 Fetch fails, no candidate, or file missing blocked: METADATA_FETCH_FAILED #L851 Document invalid: schema error, OIN differs from the certificate, more or less than one read operation, or valid for less than one hour METADATA_INVALID. The last complete candidate stays main_test.go#L628 asi capability invalid, or a document with only asi The whole source gets METADATA_INVALID asi_onboarding_test.go#L152 GBO attribute catalogue unreadable Only sources with asi are refused asi_onboarding_test.go#L227 No contract for the data service in the document DATA_CONTRACT_NOT_FOUND service_test.go#L295 Lower version, or the same version with other content Not activated none, code only (source_registry_backend.go#L163-L175, #610) Registry write fails blocked: ACTIVATION_FAILED code (service.go#L418-L421) Promotion fails The previous release stays active store_test.go#L94 One configured source without a valid version No new release for any source. The active release stays (deviation, #606) registry_test.go#L91 Operator rolls back to a stored release The stored release becomes active. Automatic promotion keeps the rollback until new content arrives registry_test.go#L116, store_test.go#L147, source_registry_command_test.go#L47 Rollback to a release the adapter cannot load Refused. The pointer does not change source_registry_command_test.go#L72 Active version of a source past grace Issuance for that source answers HTTP 503. The offer list /eudi-offers.json answers 503 for all sources (deviation, #606) code only (main.go#L221-L225) Adapter refresh fails The previous complete snapshot stays in use source_release_runtime_test.go#L125, #L89 ASIP reads the release The ASIP reads per data service from the active release asi_onboarding_test.go#L323

docs.title: Main observations
docs.text:
Source activation in gbo-demo v0.9.0 has these properties and gaps:

  • A valid contract is not activation (F-58). The source file is the management action. Transport and mandate are two decisions with two owners. Two parts are not built: the rule for who can take the action, and the way GBO records the admission decision. These parts are PSA B-09 in the decision register and REQ-123.
  • The source owns its description (F-57). GBO validates and activates the description. Its origin is the authenticated FSC transport plus the OIN from the certificate. The document itself has no signature. The file transport is a visible, temporary exception for a source without an endpoint. The demo does not record the agreement of the bronhouder (F-71, AV-08).
  • Releases have a full lifecycle (F-59). The lifecycle has validation before activation, bounded staleness, atomic promotion, and rollback. Policy bundles do not have this lifecycle. For a comparison, see Policy distribution.
  • Isolation is incomplete. One failing source freezes new releases for all sources, and the offer list fails for all sources at the same time (#606).
  • DvTP is not covered. For DvTP, the GBO rules hold the offer of a source. A publication of the source does not hold it (REQ-64). The question of how a source connects to the ASIP is partly answered (Q-38).

docs.title: ASI verification: a QTSP verifies or retrieves an attribute
docs.text:
A qualified trust service provider (QTSP) asks the Authentic Source Interface Provider (ASIP) to verify or retrieve attributes of a citizen at the authentic source. This exchange follows eIDAS Article 45e and ETSI TS 119 478, clause 6.1 (ADR-0037, GO: ASI provider). The citizen approves each request by logging in at the authorization server of the ASIP.

The ASI route in gbo-demo v0.9.0 has four runs:

  1. Discovery and registration
  2. Authorization and login
  3. Verify through the chain
  4. Test statement to the wallet

For the concepts, see these pages:

  • The components and the trust boundary: Level 2: ASI chain.
  • The profile per ETSI clause: ASI requirements.
  • The trust roles: ASI trust roles.
  • The source description: The asi capability.
  • What is real, stub, or interpretation in the demo: docs/asi-route.md.

The demo runs one data service, brp, for the authentic source rvig (BRP mock). Its base URL is /brp/authsrc-api (ADR-0038, dataservices.json). The QTSP is the reference QTSP of the demo. It is not a real QTSP. The route runs only in the local stack (make demo-asi).

docs.title: Discovery and registration
docs.text:
A QTSP finds the data service for an attribute without addresses in its configuration (REQ-99, REQ-100). The QTSP registers once per authorization server (REQ-88).

sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(241,239,232) External roles participant Q as QTSP<br/>(qtsp-reference) participant DIP as Discover Interface<br/>(asi-discovery-stub) end box rgb(255,237,213) ASI provider participant ASIP as ASIP<br/>(asi-provider) participant AS as Authorization server<br/>(asi-authorization-server) end box rgb(237,233,254) Register participant REG as Register of relying parties<br/>(stub file) end Q->>DIP: GET /retrieve, queryType dataServices,<br/>attributeIdentifier, conformsTo DIP->>ASIP: GET /brp/dataservices ASIP-->>DIP: dataService records of the active description DIP-->>Q: Records: endpointURI, endpointDescription,<br/>provider, country Q->>Q: One data service for all attributes? Q->>ASIP: GET /brp/openapi.json ASIP-->>Q: Contract: servers, x-oauth-authorization-server Q->>AS: GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server AS-->>Q: Metadata: issuer, endpoints, jwks_uri Q->>Q: Metadata URL belongs to the issuer? Q->>AS: POST /register: redirect_uris, scope,<br/>software_statement with x5c and registryURI AS->>AS: Chain to a trust anchor, certificate valid,<br/>organizationIdentifier, iss, iat, exp AS->>REG: Look up registryURI REG-->>AS: Identifiers, entitlements, legal name AS-->>Q: 201: client_id, jwks with the certificate key Note over AS,REG: Every hour, for each registered client AS->>REG: Look up registryURI again AS->>AS: No QEAA_Provider: deactivate.<br/>Register unreachable: keep active.

Each hop of discovery and registration carries the following data:

# From → To Data Notes 1 to 4 QTSP → Discover Interface → ASIP In: an attribute identifier. Out: one record per attribute and data service No personal data travels. The stub holds no records. It reads them per query from the ASIP and checks them against the ETSI schema (directory.go#L35-L40). The ASIP lists the attributes of the active source description. If no description is active, the ASIP answers 503 (handler.go#L139-L165). 5 QTSP (internal) The records A token is for one data service. If no data service provides all attributes, the QTSP stops before the authorization server (qtsp.go#L124-L162, F-89). 6 to 7 QTSP → ASIP The contract (ETSI Annex B OpenAPI) servers must equal the endpointURI. x-oauth-authorization-server is a GBO extension: ETSI requires the reference but gives no field (F-91, Q-39, E1). 8 to 10 QTSP → authorization server RFC 8414 metadata The QTSP checks that the metadata URL is the RFC 8414 location for the issuer (qtsp.go#L190-L214). 11 to 12 QTSP → authorization server RFC 7591 request with a software statement, sealed with the QTSP certificate (x5c, registryURI) No personal data travels. The certificate must chain to a trust anchor and carry an organizationIdentifier. In the demo, the certificate comes from the development reader CA. It is not an access certificate per ETSI TS 119 411-8 (F-85). 13 to 15 Authorization server ↔ register registryURI. Out: identifiers, entitlements, legal name The entry must carry QEAA_Provider and the organizationIdentifier of the certificate (registration.go#L199-L215). It is open which identifier links the two (Q-35). The client key is the certificate key. The authorization server keeps clients in memory. 16 to 17 Authorization server ↔ register The same lookup The re-check runs every AZSP_ENTITLEMENT_RECHECK_INTERVAL (1 h) (REQ-89, registration.go#L221-L245). If the register is unreachable, the client stays active (Q-34). Tokens already issued stay valid (Q-41).

docs.title: Authorization and login
docs.text:
The citizen starts at the QTSP and logs in there first. The QTSP then sends the browser to the authorization server. One request page shows who asks what at which source (REQ-91). The citizen approves by logging in, or refuses (REQ-90). The diagram shows three alternatives: the cross-device wallet login, the DigiD mock, and a refusal.

sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(221,235,247) Citizen actor C as Citizen<br/>(browser) end box rgb(241,239,232) QTSP participant Q as QTSP end box rgb(255,237,213) ASI provider participant AS as Authorization server participant V as Wallet verifier<br/>(nl-wallet) end box rgb(241,239,232) Wallet participant W as NL Wallet<br/>(phone) end C->>Q: Log in at the QTSP: NL Wallet without BSN,<br/>or test data C->>Q: POST /start: product and values Q-->>C: 302 to /authorize: code, PKCE S256, state,<br/>scope, resource, authorization_details C->>AS: GET /authorize AS-->>C: Request page and transaction cookie C->>AS: POST /authorize/decision alt NL Wallet, cross-device AS->>V: POST /disclosure/sessions: asi-login,<br/>PID with five claims V-->>AS: session_token, kept with the transaction AS-->>C: Wallet page with QR code, refreshes itself W->>V: Fetch the request, signed with the<br/>reader certificate of asi-login W->>V: Presentation: PID as SD-JWT VC V->>V: Issuer signature, trusted issuer,<br/>wallet binding C->>AS: GET /authorize/wallet: status DONE AS->>V: GET disclosed attributes, API key V-->>AS: bsn, family_name, given_name,<br/>birthdate, nationalities else DigiD mock AS-->>C: DigiD mock page C->>AS: POST /authorize/digid: BSN as password else Refuse AS-->>C: 302 to redirect_uri: error access_denied end AS-->>C: 302 to redirect_uri: code and state C->>Q: GET /callback: code, state Q->>AS: POST /token: code, code_verifier,<br/>client_assertion, DPoP proof AS-->>Q: Access token, at+jwt, 10 min

Each hop of authorization and login carries the following data:

# From → To Data Notes 1 Citizen → QTSP name, birth date, nationalities (no BSN) The QTSP uses use case qtsp-login on the same verifier, with its own reader certificate. This shared verifier is a demo shortcut. The test-data login is a stub. The QTSP keeps the login in memory for 30 minutes. 2 to 3 Citizen → QTSP → browser The product and the values to check (address) The redirect carries PKCE S256, state, the operation as scope, resource = the endpointURI, and authorization_details with the attribute identifiers (REQ-103, ADR-0042). The values stay at the QTSP. 4 to 5 Browser → authorization server The authorization request. Out: the request page If resource does not name exactly one data service, the answer is invalid_target (REQ-95). The page names the QTSP by its legal name from the register, the operation, the source, and the attributes. The transaction lives 5 minutes and is used once. A cookie binds the transaction to the browser. 6 Browser → authorization server The choice: wallet, digid, or deny The choice of a means starts the approval. The code comes only after a successful login. 7 to 9 Authorization server → verifier → browser DCQL: urn:eudi:pid:nl:1 with bsn, family_name, given_name, birthdate, nationalities The authorization server keeps the session with the transaction and never takes one from the browser (provision.go#L33-L49). 10 to 12 Wallet ↔ verifier PID with the BSN The reader certificate names the authorization server. It does not name the QTSP. Any phone can scan the QR code (F-93). The verifier verifies the issuer signature, the trusted issuer, and the wallet binding. The trusted issuers come from a fixed list. They do not come from a trusted list (REQ-102, Q-36). 13 to 15 Authorization server ↔ verifier BSN, names, birth date, nationalities Only a PID of the right type with a BSN identifies the citizen. The NL PID has no place of birth (F-94). 16 to 17 Browser → DigiD mock BSN The DigiD mock is a stub. It checks only for nine digits and gives only the BSN (F-88). 18 Authorization server → browser error=access_denied No login takes place, and the source gets no request. 19 to 20 Browser → QTSP code, state The code is single use and valid for 60 s. Before the QTSP asks for a token, it checks its session and state. 21 QTSP → authorization server POST /token: code, code_verifier, private_key_jwt client assertion, DPoP proof From each pair of mechanisms that ETSI offers, the demo uses one: private_key_jwt and DPoP. The demo uses no mTLS and no PAR (F-84, Q-66). 22 Authorization server → QTSP RFC 9068 access token, ES256: aud = data service, scope, authorization_details, cnf.jkt, opaque sub, BSN claim, acr/amr, PID claims (wallet only) The QTSP can read the BSN in the token (F-86, E7, #595). The token carries the means used (REQ-86, tokens.go#L53-L85).

docs.title: Same-device wallet login
docs.text:
If the browser and the wallet are on one phone, a button opens the wallet. The wallet returns the browser with a nonce (#548, PR #573). This flow needs an HTTPS issuer, because nl-wallet accepts only an HTTPS return URL. Over local HTTP, the button is disabled, and only the QR code works. A run on a real phone waits for the simulation environment (#596, #594).

sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(221,235,247) Citizen actor C as Citizen<br/>(browser on the phone) end box rgb(255,237,213) ASI provider participant AS as Authorization server participant V as Wallet verifier end box rgb(241,239,232) Wallet participant W as NL Wallet<br/>(same phone) end C->>AS: POST /authorize/decision: wallet AS->>V: POST /disclosure/sessions with a return<br/>template to /authorize/wallet/return V-->>AS: session_token, kept with the transaction AS-->>C: Button Open NL Wallet and QR code C->>W: Universal link opens the wallet W->>V: Fetch the request, presentation W-->>C: Back to the website: return URL with nonce C->>AS: GET /authorize/wallet/return:<br/>transaction, session_token, nonce AS->>AS: Session of this transaction<br/>in this browser? AS->>V: GET disclosed attributes with the nonce V-->>AS: PID, only for the right nonce AS-->>C: 302 to redirect_uri: code and state

These hops carry the data that is specific to the same-device login:

# From → To Data Notes 2 Authorization server → verifier The return template The verifier returns only after a same-device session (session_type_return_url = "same_device", only for asi-login). 7 to 9 Wallet → browser → authorization server transaction, session_token, nonce The authorization server refuses another browser or another session before it calls the verifier. The browser also comes back after a refusal in the wallet (identification.go#L322-L356). 10 to 11 Authorization server ↔ verifier nonce. Out: PID with the BSN The nonce binds the disclosure to the browser that the wallet returned. Another phone cannot finish this session (F-93).

docs.title: Verify through the chain
docs.text:
The QTSP calls the ASIP with the token. The ASIP verifies the token, takes the BSN from it, and calls the source once, through its own FSC Outway. The generic GBO chain starts behind the ASIP (F-87).

sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(241,239,232) QTSP participant Q as QTSP end box rgb(255,237,213) ASI provider participant ASIP as ASIP<br/>(data service brp) participant AS as Authorization server end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis participant OW as asip-outway<br/>(peer …1200) participant IW as bd-inway<br/>(PEP, peer …0200) participant PDP as OpenFTV PDP<br/>(ASI0001) participant GW as Source gateway<br/>(brp-sidecar) end box rgb(221,235,247) Source participant SRC as BRP mock<br/>(brp-graphql-server) end Q->>ASIP: POST /brp/authsrc-api/verify: DPoP token,<br/>DPoP proof, traceparent, attributes ASIP->>AS: Metadata and JWKS, once, cached AS-->>ASIP: Signing keys ASIP->>ASIP: Token, proof and scope.<br/>BSN from the token. ASIP->>ASIP: Contract schema, approved attributes,<br/>mandate, attributes described ASIP->>ASIP: One query from the active<br/>description, only the needed fields ASIP->>OW: POST /brp/graphql: query, BSN as variable,<br/>Fsc-Transaction-Id, traceparent OW->>IW: mTLS, Fsc-Authorization, same body IW->>PDP: POST /authzen/v1/evaluation with the body PDP-->>IW: Allow per field, ADL record IW->>GW: Query GW->>SRC: Query unchanged, no consent token SRC-->>ASIP: Fields of the person, or no person ASIP->>ASIP: Build the attributes and compare ASIP-->>Q: 200: attributeVerificationResults,<br/>X-JWS-Signature Q->>Q: Seal valid? Else not accepted.

Each hop of the verification carries the following data:

# From → To Data Notes 1 QTSP → ASIP Authorization: DPoP <token>, DPoP proof with ath, attribute values to check The values are personal data that the QTSP already has. insufficient_scope and every other token error give 401, as ETSI lists. 2 to 3 ASIP → authorization server jwks_uri from the metadata If the kid is unknown, the ASIP fetches the keys again. If the keys are not available, the ASIP answers 503 (REQ-87). 4 ASIP (internal) Token, proof. Out: the BSN The ASIP first verifies the token: signature, issuer, aud, expiry, DPoP binding and replay, and scope (handler.go#L222-L258). The BSN comes only from the token. No log line holds the BSN. 5 ASIP (internal) The request Schema against the contract: 400. Attributes outside authorization_details: 401. mandate: 501. An attribute the source does not describe: 404 (handler.go#L260-L356, service.go#L129-L139). 6 ASIP (internal) The asi description from the active release The ASIP reads the active release every 5 s with the reader role. It derives one query with only the fields of the requested attributes (REQ-92, ADR-0039). 7 ASIP → asip-outway POST /brp/graphql (grant link /brp): {query, variables: {bsn}} with the BSN, Fsc-Transaction-Id, traceparent One FSC transaction per request. The span names the source, the transaction ID and the attribute identifiers, never the BSN or a value (source.go#L75-L104, REQ-55). 8 asip-outway → bd-inway FSC, mTLS, with the body and the BSN The hop uses the contract of the ASIP peer …1200 for service brp on …0200 (FSC peers). 9 to 10 bd-inway ↔ PDP AuthZEN: actor …1200, service brp, the query with the BSN ASI0001 grants the ASIP peer the BRP fields behind the attributes, on brp only. It does not check the token or the QTSP (asi0001.rego#L1-L72, REQ-97). The PDP never sees the QTSP or the citizen. The ADL holds the BSN (REQ-60, ADR-0043). 11 to 12 bd-inway → gateway → BRP mock The judged query If the query has no consent token, the gateway passes it through. The BRP logs its own processing. In demo v0.9.0, the ASIP writes no LDV records. 13 BRP mock → ASIP fields of the person, or null The answer goes back through the same FSC chain. 14 ASIP (internal) Fields. Out: a result per attribute pointer, join, const, and each build the attribute from the fields. The result is Match, MatchWithVariation, NoMatch, or Unknown. Unknown means only that the source holds no value (REQ-84). Fuzzy matching applies only to strings without a format (REQ-113). 15 ASIP → QTSP results, provider, authenticSource (legal name from the description), header X-JWS-Signature A verify response holds no source value (REQ-85). One authentic source per response (REQ-94). The seal is a detached JWS, ES256, with x5c, over the exact body. The ASIP does not seal errors (REQ-83, ADR-0041, handler.go#L402-L417). 16 QTSP (internal) The seal The chain must lead to QTSP_SEAL_TRUST_ANCHORS. If it does not, the QTSP does not accept the result.

The retrieve operation runs the same way at POST /brp/authsrc-api/retrieve with scope retrieve. The request names attribute identifiers, without values. The sealed 200 carries the values of every requested attribute. If the source holds no value for one of them, the answer is 404. Retrieve gives no partial result (REQ-101).

docs.title: Test statement to the wallet
docs.text:
After an accepted result, the reference QTSP issues a test statement to the wallet of the citizen who logged in at the QTSP. The QTSP uses the central issuance server of the EUDI route, with its own use case and its own certificates (qtsp_issuance.go#L19-L27, EUDI issuance).

sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(221,235,247) Citizen actor C as Citizen<br/>(browser) end box rgb(241,239,232) QTSP participant Q as QTSP end box rgb(255,237,213) EUDI participant IS as Issuance server<br/>(nl-wallet) end box rgb(241,239,232) Wallet participant W as NL Wallet<br/>(phone) end Q->>Q: Accepted result: pending statement<br/>with the login identity Q-->>C: Result page with a QR code<br/>for use case qtsp-attestation W->>IS: Fetch the request, signed with<br/>the reader certificate of the QTSP W->>IS: PID: family_name, given_name,<br/>birthdate, nationalities, no BSN IS->>Q: Callback over internal HTTPS,<br/>secret path, the shared attributes Q->>Q: Same as the login identity? Q-->>IS: Statement: subject, outcome per attribute,<br/>source, date, test and not qualified IS-->>W: SD-JWT VC over OpenID4VCI, signed<br/>with the issuer certificate of the QTSP

Each hop of the test statement carries the following data:

# From → To Data Notes 1 to 2 QTSP → browser The result and a fixed link per use case This hop occurs only after Match, MatchWithVariation, or a retrieved value. The pending statement lives 10 minutes in memory and is used once. A later request of the same citizen replaces it. 3 to 4 Wallet → issuance server PID without the BSN A QTSP is not allowed to process the BSN. 5 Issuance server → QTSP name, birth date, nationalities The QTSP gets no session, only the shared attributes. The callback uses a secret path over CA-pinned HTTPS, without client authentication (qtsp_issuance.go#L134-L152). 6 QTSP (internal) The identity The link to the login uses only these personal data. This link is a demo binding and does not check a unique identity (F-93). 7 to 8 QTSP → issuance server → wallet statement The statement is valid for 30 days, has attestation_qualification = "EAA", and carries a clear test marking. It is not a QEAA. For MatchWithVariation, the statement records the value that the QTSP sent. It does not record a source value.

docs.title: Error paths
docs.text:
The ASI route has the following error paths:

Trigger Outcome Pinned by (v0.9.0) No data service provides all requested attributes The QTSP stops before the authorization server. Request API: 422. api_e2e_test.go#L201 No active source description Records, verify, and retrieve answer 503. The contract stays published. source_test.go#L168, graphqlsource/source_test.go#L148 Software statement invalid: signature, chain, expiry, or no organizationIdentifier invalid_software_statement registration_test.go#L105 No QEAA_Provider, or the identifier is not in the register entry unapproved_software_statement (REQ-88) registration_test.go#L152 Register unreachable at registration 503 temporarily_unavailable registration_test.go#L324 Entitlement withdrawn in the register The next re-check deactivates the client: invalid_client. Issued tokens stay valid for up to 10 min (Q-41). registration_test.go#L224, #L276 Register unreachable at re-check The client stays active (demo choice, Q-34) registration_test.go#L306 Unknown client or redirect_uri Error page, no redirect handler_test.go#L211 resource missing or not exactly one data service invalid_target (REQ-95) handler_test.go#L153 The citizen refuses access_denied, without login login_test.go#L61 DigiD mock: BSN is not nine digits The page stays open with an error login_test.go#L110 Wallet declines or the session expires Back to the request page. The transaction stays. wallet_test.go#L205 Verifier unreachable, also after DONE 503 page. The transaction stays for the DigiD mock. wallet_test.go#L299 Same-device return in another browser or for another session Refused before the authorization server calls the verifier wallet_test.go#L123, #L148 Same-device return without the right nonce Back to the request page with a message wallet_test.go#L177 Wrong code_verifier, or a code that is used twice, expired, or of another client invalid_grant handler_test.go#L239, #L246 Client assertion missing, wrong, or replayed invalid_client handler_test.go#L293, #L347 No valid DPoP proof at the token endpoint invalid_dpop_proof handler_test.go#L374 No token, an invalid token, or a DPoP proof that is missing, invalid, or replayed 401 with WWW-Authenticate: DPoP token_test.go#L46-L216 Scope does not cover the operation 401 insufficient_scope token_test.go#L217 Attribute outside the approved authorization_details 401 insufficient_scope (REQ-103) token_test.go#L233 Token for another data service 401 (REQ-95) dataservices_test.go#L16 Keys of the authorization server not available 503 token_test.go#L289 Body not valid against the contract 400, after the token check and before other checks handler_test.go#L220, token_test.go#L262 mandate present 501 (REQ-114) handler_test.go#L186, #L194 Attribute the source does not describe, also one of another data service 404. The ASIP does not call the source. handler_test.go#L151, #L157 Source holds no value, or the BSN is unknown to the source Unknown (REQ-84) handler_test.go#L140, token_test.go#L254 Retrieve, and the source holds no value for one attribute 404, no partial result (REQ-101) handler_test.go#L291 Chain unreachable, or the Outway answers 5xx 503, never Unknown (REQ-93) graphqlsource/source_test.go#L157, source_test.go#L141 PDP deny (the Inway answers 401), GraphQL errors, or an answer of another shape 500, never Unknown The same tests PDP: the caller is not the ASIP peer ACTOR_NOT_ALLOWED asi0001_test.rego#L29 PDP: a consent token, or no BSN in the root argument PID_NOT_PRESENT asi0001_test.rego#L37-L49 PDP: another service than brp, or another BRP field Rule not bound, or the field falls to the closed world asi0001_test.rego#L56-L61 Seal from an unknown anchor The QTSP does not accept the result e2e_test.go#L285 Test statement: NoMatch or Unknown No pending statement issuance_test.go#L97 Test statement: another PID, or a statement that is expired or used Empty document list, nothing issued issuance_test.go#L53, callback_test.go#L38

The conformance matrix gives each ETSI requirement ID a status and named tests. At v0.9.0, the matrix has 55 passed, 4 stub, 21 not applicable, and 1 failing. If an ID or a test is missing, a CI job fails (etsi-ts-119478.yaml, ci.yml#L72-L73).

docs.title: Main observations
docs.text:
The ASI route in gbo-demo v0.9.0 has these properties and gaps:

  • The QTSP is outside FSC. Its admission is a certificate and a register entitlement at the authorization server. The source and the PDP see only the ASIP peer …1200. The ASIP passes nothing about the QTSP into the chain (F-87, Trust boundary).
  • Two logins, no link. The citizen logs in at the QTSP and at the authorization server. Nothing proves that it is the same person. In the cross-device route, another phone can scan the QR code (F-93, Q-40, E6).
  • The BSN travels in two places where it is not needed. The QTSP can read the BSN in the token (F-86, #595). The PDP input and the ADL also hold the BSN (REQ-60, ADR-0043).
  • Approval is a login, not a consent. The citizen approves one request. The demo stores no approval, and the citizen cannot revoke one (REQ-90, Wallet approval is not a legal basis).
  • One token per source. A QTSP that needs attributes of two sources authorizes twice. The citizen sees each source by name (ADR-0038, F-89, E3).
  • Per-attribute binding is optional. If the request has no authorization_details, the token binds only per operation, as in ETSI. A configuration option makes the detail required (ADR-0042, F-95, Q-33).
  • No value with a variation. MatchWithVariation returns no value. The conformance matrix records that row as failing (F-92, Q-29, E2).
  • The seal format is a GBO choice. ETSI defines no seal format (Q-32, E4). The demo seals with a development certificate.
  • Identification data is incomplete. The NL PID has no place of birth. The DigiD mock gives only the BSN (F-88, F-94, Q-36).

docs.title: Not built in demo v0.9.0
docs.text:
Demo v0.9.0 does not build these parts of the ASI route:

  • A resource list from the source descriptions. The authorization server takes its resource list from AZSP_RESOURCES. The rest of the asi capability is built (#592, Q-38).
  • A deployment in the simulation environment, and a connection of an external QTSP (#594).
  • Protection of the BSN in the access token (#595, F-86).
  • A same-device wallet login on a real phone. It is built and tested, and waits for #594 (#596).
  • iss in the authorization response, RFC 9207 (F-96, E9). The effect of a withdrawn entitlement on issued tokens (Q-41, E10).
  • LDV records by the ASIP and the authorization server (REQ-72).
  • Clause 6.2 (ISO 15000) and deferred answers (REQ-112, Q-64). Requests on behalf of another person (Q-65).
  • A production register, access certificates per ETSI TS 119 411-8, real DigiD, and a qualified seal certificate (F-80, F-85, Q-28, Q-37).
  • Registration of the data services in the Discover Interface (Q-31, Q-67).

docs.title: Design-level scenarios
docs.text:
The scenarios on this page have no implementation in gbo-demo v0.9.0. Each section gives the intended sequence, the behavior of v0.9.0 for such a request, and the open points. The first two scenarios go through the same chain as every built data-plane scenario, in this order:

  1. the Outway,
  2. the Inway of the source, as PEP,
  3. the PDP of the source,
  4. the source gateway,
  5. the source API.

The third scenario uses no GBO runtime.

docs.title: Gov-to-Gov
docs.text:
A government consumer reads source data under a legal basis (grondslag). The request has no consent and no pseudonymization, because both parties can process the BSN. The design makes two decisions:

  • The regime follows from the evidence that the request carries. A Gov-to-Gov regime needs its own positive evidence. It cannot be a third regime that the PDP selects because something is absent (ADR-0031, F-70).
  • The PDP evaluates the legal basis locally from policy data, with no PIP call (ADR-0004).

Demo v0.9.0 has no rule set, no evidence format, and no legal-basis data. This gap is risk R3 in Risks and technical debt.

sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(241,239,232) Consumer participant GOV as Government consumer<br/>backend end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis participant OUT as FSC Outway<br/>of the consumer participant MGR as FSC Manager<br/>of the provider participant IN as FSC Inway (PEP) participant PDP as PDP of the source participant GW as Source gateway end box rgb(221,235,247) Source participant API as Source API end GOV->>OUT: GraphQL query, subject = BSN,<br/>legal-basis evidence (form open) OUT->>MGR: Access token request (mTLS, grant hash) MGR-->>OUT: Access token, no grant properties OUT->>IN: mTLS + access token + body IN->>PDP: AuthZEN evaluation (raw body) Note over PDP: Regime from the legal-basis evidence.<br/>Legal basis from policy data, no PIP call.<br/>Per-field rules as in every regime. PDP-->>IN: Allow or deny IN->>GW: Forward (no consent token: pass-through) GW->>API: Query with the BSN API-->>GOV: Requested fields (through Inway and Outway)

docs.title: Data per hop
docs.text:
Each hop of the Gov-to-Gov request carries the following data:

# From → to Data Notes 1 Consumer → Outway Query and variables, the BSN as subject, the legal-basis evidence The form of the evidence is open. ADR-0031 rules out declarations, such as a header, a grant property, or a default 2 to 3 Outway ↔ provider Manager FSC token The contract first passes contract admission 4 to 7 Inway → PDP → Inway PDP input with the BSN The BSN is in the PDP input and in the decision logs, as in the EUDI and ASI routes of demo v0.9.0 (REQ-60, ADR-0043) 8 to 10 Inway → gateway → source Query with the BSN, then the requested fields The gateway passes a request without a consent token through (ADR-0033). Each controller logs its own processing (ADR-0026)

docs.title: What v0.9.0 does
docs.text:
Demo v0.9.0 handles a Gov-to-Gov request as follows:

Request Result Evidence Government peer without an admission for the source Contract refused: PARTY_NOT_IN_REGISTRY or SOURCE_NOT_ALLOWED Admission Admitted peer, no consent token, a real BSN as subject PID regime, denied: ACTOR_NOT_ALLOWED (not a designated issuer) engine_test.rego#L351 Service without a rule for the field denied: NO_APPLICABLE_RULE engine.rego#L282

The chain fails closed. Until a rule set with its own evidence exists, a government consumer gets no data.

docs.title: Open points
docs.text:
The Gov-to-Gov design has these open points:

  • It is open what form the positive evidence for the legal basis has, and who issues it (REQ-74).
  • It is open where the legal-basis data lives (which consumer, which service, which legal basis, which fields), and who maintains it. ADR-0004 puts it in policy data.
  • The PID actor lists must stay disjoint from the consumers of other regimes. If a Gov-to-Gov consumer omits its evidence, it must not enter the PID regime (F-70).

docs.title: SDG-OOTS
docs.text:
A competent authority in another member state requests evidence about a citizen or company through the Once-Only Technical System. The design is an OOTS adapter at the GBO edge (ADR-0020, PSA S08). eDelivery AS4 exists only at the edge. The bronhouder sees a normal FSC request through the standard PEP-PDP chain. It is open who builds the adapter (Q-79).

sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(241,239,232) External participant ER as Evidence requester<br/>(other member state) participant EU as OOTS common services<br/>(discovery) participant AP as Dutch access point<br/>(AS4) end box rgb(255,237,213) OOTS participant OA as OOTS adapter<br/>(OOTS-EDM to GraphQL) end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis participant OUT as FSC Outway<br/>of the adapter participant IN as FSC Inway (PEP) participant PDP as PDP of the source end box rgb(221,235,247) Source participant API as Source API end ER->>EU: Find the evidence type and the provider ER->>AP: AS4 message: OOTS-EDM evidence request AP->>OA: Evidence request OA->>OA: Map the evidence type to a source query OA->>OUT: GraphQL query over FSC OUT->>IN: mTLS + access token + body IN->>PDP: AuthZEN evaluation Note over PDP: Regime and evidence for OOTS<br/>not designed PDP-->>IN: Allow or deny IN->>API: Query (through the source gateway) API-->>OA: Source data (through Inway and Outway) OA->>OA: Map to OOTS-EDM evidence OA->>AP: Evidence response AP->>ER: AS4 message: evidence

The OOTS process steps around the request, such as the identification of the user and the preview, stay with the Basisinrichting OOTS. The diagram does not show them.

docs.title: Data per hop
docs.text:
Each hop of the OOTS request carries the following data:

# From → to Data Notes 1 to 3 Requester → access point → adapter OOTS-EDM evidence request in an AS4 message: evidence type, the subject, the requester Transport, discovery, and the European process stay with the Basisinrichting OOTS (Q-79) 4 Adapter Evidence type → source query The mapping depends on the canonical semantic models (ADR-0024) 5 to 10 Adapter → source GraphQL query and FSC token, then source data The same chain as every FSC consumer. The adapter translates the protocol. The decision stays with the PDP of the source (REQ-44, REQ-46) 11 to 13 Adapter → requester OOTS-EDM evidence The mapping version must be traceable, as for issuance (REQ-124)

docs.title: What v0.9.0 does
docs.text: The demo does not touch OOTS. It has no adapter, no access point, and no rule for OOTS. If an adapter peer sends a request without a consent token, the request enters the PID regime and fails the actor check, as in Gov-to-Gov. The gap is risk R2 in Risks and technical debt.

docs.title: Open points
docs.text:
The OOTS design has these open points:

  • It is open who builds the adapter: GBO, or the OOTS-V operator with the GBO interface (Q-79). OOTS-V is the part of the Basisinrichting OOTS that receives evidence requests.
  • The regime and the evidence for an OOTS request are open (REQ-74, ADR-0031). If an OOTS request has no evidence of its own, the PDP denies it.
  • The requirements register has no OOTS requirement.

docs.title: Relying-party presentation
docs.text:
The citizen presents a wallet attestation from GBO to a relying party over OpenID4VP, with selective disclosure. No GBO decision component and no source take part at presentation time. This is the purpose of an issuance-based route. The data are fixed at issuance, and the source carries no presentation load. For the issuance itself, see EUDI issuance.

docs.title: Data per hop
docs.text:
Each hop of the presentation carries the following data:

# From → to Data Notes 1 to 3 Relying party → wallet → citizen Reader certificate of the relying party, the requested claims The approval in the wallet is no legal basis for the relying party (F-83) 4 Wallet → relying party Selected claims of the attestation, signed by the issuer, with key binding The wallet sends only the claims that the citizen selects 5 Relying party → trust list Trust anchor of the PuB-EAA issuer It is open which list applies: a List of Trusted Entities or the trusted lists (Q-30) 7 to 8 Relying party → issuance facility Status list per attestation type, Type Metadata Static publications. The relying party fetches the whole list, so the issuer does not learn which attestation the relying party checks. No PDP, no FSC, and no source take part

docs.title: What v0.9.0 does
docs.text:
For this scenario, demo v0.9.0 has these limits:

  • The demo has no relying party for GBO attestations. The ASI wallet verifier asks only for the PID (asi-wallet-verifier/README.md).
  • Trust uses the development CA chain. The test wallet and the demo verifiers trust the development issuer CA.
  • Every attestation is valid for 365 days. A status list exists per type, but revocation on instruction of the bronhouder is not built (REQ-77).

docs.title: Open points
docs.text:
The relying-party scenario has these open points:

  • The trust list for PuB-EAA providers (Q-30) and the designation of the Dutch PuB-EAA issuer (Q-28) are open. In production, the relying party verifies the seal of the bronhouder as PuB-EAA provider. GBO operates the technical facility (ADR-0028). ADR-0023 proposes the EUDI certificate roles.
  • Freshness. The attestation shows the source data at issuance. GBO only reads the source on request. If the data change, GBO gets no signal. Long-lived attestations need a change feed and revocation (F-82).

docs.title: DvTP: the citizen views and revokes consents
docs.text:
A logged-in citizen opens the page My consents (shown as "Mijn toestemmingen") in the consent portal (toestemmingsportaal). The portal shows the consents of the citizen with their status, and the citizen revokes one consent. The portal finds the consents through its own reference to the citizen, without a BSNk call. A revocation takes effect at the next request of the consumer.

For the concepts, see Revocation and Citizen recognition: route D. For the components, see Level 2: consent chain. For the requirements, see Citizen access.

docs.title: Main observations
docs.text:
The citizen-access flow in gbo-demo v0.9.0 has these properties and gaps:

  • The server derives the reference. The portal derives subject_ref from the BSN in the signed portal token. As a result, a citizen cannot list or revoke the consents of another citizen (REQ-40, TestListIsolatesByCitizen).
  • Viewing and revoking need no BSNk. The reference is an HMAC that the portal computes itself (route D, ADR-0040, proposed). A new key gives every citizen a new reference. Migration to a new key is not built (Q-56). It is open whether the register and the portal backend are one system (Q-49).
  • Revocation keeps the record. The status becomes REVOKED and the record stays. The effect reaches the consumer at its next request, through the online status lookup (REQ-14, DvTP query). The demo has no status cache, so the propagation time is one request. The norm for the propagation time is open (REQ-75, Q-47).
  • Every step is a logged processing. The portal logs each derivation of the reference with its reason. The register logs each read and the revocation under subject_ref. No record holds a BSN (TestNoBSNInAnyRecordedProcessing, Logging).
  • The demo does not meet all requirements. A revocation of the consent of another citizen gives 403, where REQ-40 asks for 404. The demo accepts a second revocation (REQ-109). The demo has no export (REQ-108), no rights notice (REQ-120), no "retrieved" status (Q-42), and no revocation time (Q-48).
  • The register trusts its caller. The register serves list, read, and revoke to every caller on its network. Only network placement limits this to the portal backend (REQ-39, Q-58).

docs.title: DvTP: the citizen gives consent
docs.text:
In DvTP, the consumer is a private service provider (dienstverlener). A citizen at the consumer goes to the consent portal (toestemmingsportaal), logs in, and gives consent for one or more data sets. The result is a consent record in the consent register (toestemmingsregister) and a signed consent proof. The proof goes back to the consumer. The consumer uses the proof in DvTP query.

For the concepts, see Consent and Pseudonymization. For the components, see Level 2: consent chain. The main decisions are ADR-0032 (the consent proof) and ADR-0040 (route D, proposed).

docs.title: Main observations
docs.text:
The consent flow in gbo-demo v0.9.0 has these properties and gaps:

  • The BSN boundary. The BSN occurs only in these places:

    • the browser and the portal token (hops 3 to 5),
    • the portal backend (hop 8),
    • BSNk, at the first consent (hop 11).

    The register and the consumer never see the BSN (REQ-20, REQ-23). The BSN in the browser is a demo shortcut.

  • One activation per citizen. At every later consent, the portal finds PI and PP under its own reference. Then the portal only transforms (TestASecondConsentOnlyTransforms). A new SUBJECT_REF_KEY gives every citizen a new reference. Migration to a new key is not built in demo v0.9.0 (Q-56).

  • No consumer identifier in the proof. The proof carries values that only the sources can read. The consumer does not recognize the citizen across consents (F-76). A VP for the consumer itself is not built in demo v0.9.0 (#478).
  • The proof freezes at consent. BSNk makes the values only while the citizen is present. As a result, the parties, the key versions, and the proof form are fixed for the whole validity (F-78, The proof freezes at consent). The portal configuration (CONSENT_SOURCES) names the sources. No catalogue supplies them (REQ-82).
  • BSNk recognition is open. Only a recognized party can activate and transform (BSNK-01). It is open whether the consent facility (toestemmingsvoorziening) can be a recognized party. It is also open whether the register and the portal backend are one BSNk participant (F-75, Q-26, Q-49).
  • The initiation is not provable. The consumer name, the purpose, and the return address come unsigned from the redirect URL (REQ-37, REQ-111, #427). The record holds the purpose as use_case. The proof does not hold the purpose (REQ-12, Q-69).

  • Some portal duties are not built. Demo v0.9.0 does not have these portal duties:

    • a step in which the citizen states that they saw the information (REQ-107),
    • a plain-language summary to the norm of REQ-117,
    • a separate confirmation of the choice to the citizen (REQ-122).

    It is open whether the portal must prove what the citizen saw (Q-51).

docs.title: DvTP: the consumer queries a source under consent
docs.text:
A consumer (afnemer) asks a source for data about a citizen who gave consent. The consumer sends a GraphQL query and the consent proof through FSC. The PDP of the source decides before any data reaches the source. After an allow, the source fills in the citizen. Besides the direct call, the flow has two variants: a call by an integrator, and a call by the Installatie Register to LVG.

For the concepts, see Authorization, Consent, and Pseudonymization. For the components, see Level 2: authorization chain and Level 2: bronhouder. The main decisions are ADR-0031, ADR-0032, and ADR-0033.

The precondition is that the consumer has an FSC contract with the source. The Manager of the source signed the contract after a positive admission decision of the same PDP (REQ-61, REQ-62). For that scenario, see Admission and activation.

docs.title: Data per hop
docs.text:
The tags (for example Medium and Low) are the data classes of What travels where. The hop numbers refer to the steps of the sequence:

# From → to Endpoint In Out Data and notes 1 Consumer backend → HV Outway POST /bri/graphql Body {query, variables} with variables.bsn = "consent:identity". Headers X-GBO-Consent-Token, Fsc-Transaction-Id, and traceparent — Plain GraphQL, no envelope. The placeholder names the citizen (REQ-79). The consumer reads only consent_id and scopes from the proof (token.go#L32-L52). It sends the proof unchanged (AV-05, outway.go#L34-L51). The year filter travels inside the query (kind.go#L75-L95) 2 HV Outway → BD Manager Token request Grant hash of the bri contract — The Manager of the providing peer issues the access token 3 BD Manager → HV Outway — — Access token (certificate-bound JWT) Medium. The token carries sub, service_name, grant_hash, and service_peer_id. It has no grant properties, so flow and subject_id_type are not in it (REQ-74) 4 HV Outway → BD Inway FSC transport Body 1:1, Fsc-Authorization, X-GBO-Consent-Token, and Fsc-Transaction-Id — FSC native transport over mTLS (ADR-0003) 5 BD Inway → PDP POST /authzen/v1/evaluation subject (HV peer, token attributes), action.properties.body, resource, and context.headers — The AuthZEN plugin of the Inway is the PEP. It passes the request unchanged (REQ-42). The Inway sends no traceparent. It correlates with X-Request-ID = Fsc-Transaction-Id (ftv-graphql-profile.md#L105-L106) 6 PDP (internal) Mapper, then policy AuthZEN request FTV field list The mapper only maps (Query mapping). The policy reads the token from the headers and selects the regime (engine.rego#L173-L181, Regime selection) 7 PDP → register GET /.well-known/jwks.json — — Direct, without FSC. Only if the cache is empty or older than 300 seconds, or if the kid is unknown 8 Register → PDP — — ES256 public keys Low. No stale-key fallback 9 PDP (internal) Proof verification X-GBO-Consent-Token consent_id, scopes, dienstverlener_oin, and valid_until The policy verifies the proof. The mapper does not (REQ-68, REQ-18, consent.rego#L174-L186). The policy does not read encrypted_subject. It only requires a pseudonym per party 10 PDP → PDP Outway GET /consent-status/consents/{id}/status consent_id, traceparent, and Fsc-Transaction-Id — Medium: consent_id. Per evaluation, no cache, 2-second timeout, and raise_error: false (consent.rego#L194-L200) 11 PDP Outway → Register Inway FSC service consent-status Same as hop 10 — From the PDP peer …0800 to the register peer …0700 (FSC peers, REQ-76) 12 Register Inway → register Status listener, port 4012 consent_id — The listener serves only the status. If the request has no FSC peer, the listener answers 401. The register logs the lookup with the calling peer as processor 13 Register → PDP — — {status} or 404 Only the status is online. The content of the consent comes from the proof (F-61) 14 PDP (internal) Rules Resolved consent, field list, and subject Decision per field DVT0001 binds the fields of service bri. It checks actor binding, placeholder, scope, years, and fields (REQ-48, REQ-97, dvt0001.rego#L72-L80). The PDP input holds no BSN and no pseudonym 15 PDP → BD Inway AuthZEN decision — decision: true, granted fields The engine adds the resolved consent to its response for the console log (engine.rego#L25-L29). The ADL records the request and the decision (ADR-0036) 16 BD Inway → bron-sidecar POST /graphql Body 1:1, X-GBO-Consent-Token, and Fsc-Authorization — The Inway forwards only after the allow. Only the source Inways reach the source gateway (REQ-81, Network isolation) 17 Source gateway (internal) Substitution Proof, body VI for OWN_PEER_OIN If the request carries a consent token, the source gateway takes the subject from that token. The source gateway does not verify the token again (substitution.go#L105-L107) 18 Source gateway → decryption component POST /signed-encrypted-identity VI, own decryption keys, and scheme keys — For consent:pseudonym, the source gateway sends the VP to /signed-encrypted-pseudonym. No BSNk call in the query path (REQ-21, BSNK-09) 19 Decryption component → source gateway — — BSN, recipient OIN BSN, inside the source boundary. In the demo, the three sources share one decryption component and one OIN 20 Source gateway (internal) Recipient check and substitution BSN, recipient Body with the BSN The value must name the own OIN as recipient (REQ-80, substitution.go#L213-L232). The source gateway logs the decryption in the LDV logbook of the source 21 Source gateway → source POST /graphql variables.bsn = BSN — BSN only at the source. The query and operationName stay the same 22 Source → source gateway — — {data} Only the selected fields (REQ-08). The source gateway logs the forward 23 to 25 Source gateway → BD Inway → HV Outway → consumer — — {data} No BSN in the response. The consumer logs its processing under the consent_id (F-76, Q-27)

docs.title: Variant: an integrator calls for the consumer
docs.text:
An integrator is a software party that calls the source for a consumer under FSC delegation (ADR-0034, integrator.md). The demo runs this variant opt-in with make demo-integrator. The consent stays a consent to the consumer (Hypotheek-BV, peer …0300).

sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(241,239,232) Integrator participant INT as integrator-backend end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis participant IO as Integrator Outway participant BDM as BD Manager participant BDI as BD Inway (PEP) participant PDP as OpenFTV PDP end box rgb(237,233,254) Admission register participant REG as Admission register end REG-->>PDP: acts_for of the integrator (PIP pull, every 5 s) INT->>IO: POST /bri/graphql with the proof of Hypotheek-BV IO->>BDM: Request an access token for the delegated grant BDM-->>IO: Access token, sub = integrator, act.sub = Hypotheek-BV IO->>BDI: Body, headers and token BDI->>PDP: AuthZEN, subject.id = integrator,<br/>outway_delegator_peer_id = Hypotheek-BV PDP->>PDP: Proof names Hypotheek-BV?<br/>Integrator active and mandated for Hypotheek-BV in DVT0001? PDP-->>BDI: Allow or deny Note over BDI: After an allow, hops 16 to 25 of the main sequence follow

The integrator variant differs from the direct call in these hops:

# What differs from the direct call 1 The admission register (dvtp-onboarding-register) supplies integrations as acts_for on the entry of the integrator. A mandate names the represented party and the rules (REQ-106, AV-06) 2 integrator-backend is the consumer backend behind the own Outway of the integrator (peer …1100). The proof is the proof that the portal gave to Hypotheek-BV 3 to 4 The contract is a DelegatedServiceConnectionGrant between the integrator, Hypotheek-BV, and the source. The OpenFSC Manager puts the delegator in act.sub. This is the reverse of RFC 8693 (integrator.md#L61-L67) 6 The Inway maps the delegator to subject.attributes.outway_delegator_peer_id. The policy reads that field and does not read the claim 7 The consent binds the represented party. This is the delegator, or else subject.id (lib.rego#L62-L72). Every delegated call also needs a mandate for that party and the granting rule (engine.rego#L253-L266)

At the source, the source gateway and the source log the integrator as foreignOperation.processor. The LDV record has no field for "on behalf of". The FSC transaction log of the source records both peers (integrator.md#L132-L152). It is open whether the proof must name the integrator (Q-46).

docs.title: Variant: the Installatie Register asks LVG about ownership
docs.text:
The LVG pilot uses the same consent pattern with a different consumer and a different source (lvg-ir.md). The Installatie Register (IR) asks the national buildings facility (LVG) whether a building unit belongs to the citizen. The citizen gives two consents:

  • One consent to IR in the consent portal (toestemmingsportaal), with scope lvg:vbo:eigendom. This consent is in GBO.
  • One consent to the installer inside IR. This consent is not in GBO.
sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(221,235,247) Citizen actor B as Citizen end box rgb(241,239,232) IR participant K as keyper-mock (IR) participant IRB as ir-backend end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis participant IRO as IR Outway participant BDI as BD Inway (PEP) participant PDP as OpenFTV PDP participant LS as lvg-sidecar end box rgb(221,235,247) Source participant LVG as lvg-graphql-server end Note over K: Holds the proof of the consent<br/>citizen to IR, scope lvg:vbo:eigendom B->>K: Approve the installer (IR consent, outside GBO) K->>IRB: Ownership check for a vboId, with the proof IRB->>IRO: POST /lvg/graphql<br/>vbo(bsn = consent:identity, vboId) IRO->>BDI: FSC, service lvg on peer …0200 BDI->>PDP: AuthZEN evaluation PDP->>PDP: LVG0001 with the consent checks of DVT0001,<br/>scope pinned to lvg:vbo:eigendom PDP-->>BDI: Allow BDI->>LS: Body and proof unchanged LS->>LS: Decrypt the VI, replace the placeholder with the BSN LS->>LVG: vbo(bsn, vboId) LVG-->>IRB: vboId or null, back through LS, BDI and IRO IRB-->>K: Ownership confirmed or not

The LVG variant differs from the direct call in these hops:

# What differs from the direct call 2 to 3 ir-backend is the consumer backend with QUERY_KIND=lvg (kind.go#L47-L53). The query is vbo(bsn: $bsn, vboId: $vboId) { vboId } with the placeholder in $bsn 4 IR has its own peer …1000, so the actor binding tells IR apart from Hypotheek-BV. LVG is a logical source behind bd-inway on the shared provider peer 5 to 6 Hops 6 to 14 of the main sequence apply: proof verification and the online status lookup. If a consent does not have the LVG scope, LVG0001 denies with SCOPE_NOT_ALLOWED 9 lvg-sidecar logs lvg-identiteit-ontsleuteling and lvg-bronquery-doorgifte in the LVG logbook. lvg-graphql-server logs lvg-vbo-eigendom, also for null 11 to 12 Three outcomes are possible: the vboId (the citizen is the owner), null (not the owner), or a deny (no valid consent). Only if the citizen is the owner does IR record the access of the installer (lvg-ir.md#L64-L70)

IR keeps the proof. At every access of an installer, IR asks again under the same consent. After a revocation, the next question fails (lvg-ir.md#L60-L62, Repeated use). With one consent, IR can ask about any vboId. The pilot must answer whether the vboId belongs in the consent (lvg-ir.md#L113-L114).

docs.title: Error paths
docs.text:
A deny carries two layers of reason (Reason codes, REQ-06):

  • Consumer code: the PDP puts this code in reason_user, and the ADL stores it. It never names the field or the failed check.
  • Administrator codes: these codes are per field. They reach only the OPA console decision log. For a server fault, the request code is PIP_UNAVAILABLE, and the trace keeps the cause.

In demo v0.9.0, the FSC Inway removes the consumer code. The Inway reads reasonUser, but the PDP sends reason_user (ftv-graphql-profile.md#L93-L96). As a result, the consumer gets a deny without a code. The consumer backend then shows UNAVAILABLE to the citizen (denial.go#L12-L56).

On every PDP deny, no request reaches the source gateway or the source. If one field has more than one reason, the administrator code is the first reason in a fixed order (engine.rego#L321-L339). The error paths have these triggers and codes:

Trigger Consumer code Administrator code Pinned by (v0.9.0) The citizen revoked the consent FIELD_NOT_PERMITTED CONSENT_WITHDRAWN consent_test.rego#L197-L207, dvt0001_test.rego#L72 valid_until passed, within the 30-second skew FIELD_NOT_PERMITTED CONSENT_EXPIRED dvt0001_test.rego#L76 exp passed by more than 30 seconds FIELD_NOT_PERMITTED CONSENT_TOKEN_EXPIRED consent_test.rego#L347 Forged or tampered proof, unknown kid, an algorithm other than ES256, no signature, or no JWT FIELD_NOT_PERMITTED CONSENT_SIGNATURE_INVALID consent_test.rego#L318-L345, scenario use-bogus-consent-deny The request has two tokens. Or the token has a wrong type, issuer, or audience, or misses a claim. The code CONSENT_SCOPE_MISMATCH does not exist. A consent without a matching scope gives SCOPE_NOT_ALLOWED. A year outside the consent gives YEAR_NOT_COVERED.

docs.title: Observations
docs.text:
The DvTP run in demo v0.9.0 shows these facts:

  • The evidence selects the regime. A consent token, verified or not, puts the request in the consent regime. If the request has no consent token, only PID-regime rules apply. No header, grant property, or default decides the regime (REQ-74, ADR-0031). The PID regime starts when a proof is absent. As a result, its actor lists must stay disjoint from consent consumers (F-70).
  • The legal basis travels as a proof, and the status stays online. The PDP verifies the proof locally. It asks only for the status, per request and fail-closed (REQ-68, F-61). As a result, every DvTP request depends on the register (REQ-75, Q-05). The status answer is not in the PDP input, so the ADL cannot replay the decision (F-72).
  • The subject comes from the proof. The consumer names the citizen only with a placeholder (REQ-79, Subject binding). The PDP does not check who the subject is. It checks only that the subject comes from the proof. One request is about one citizen (F-77).
  • The rule "after the decision" depends on network isolation. The source gateway does not verify the token again. A consumer holds real proofs, so a second verification gives no protection. Only the source Inways reach the source gateway (REQ-81, F-79, ADR-0033). In Kubernetes, this isolation needs a NetworkPolicy (Deployment units and network zones).
  • BSNk is not in the query path. The source reads its own value with its own keys (REQ-21, BSNK-04). A source keeps older keys while proofs for that key version are valid (AV-09). In demo v0.9.0, no demo rule accepts consent:pseudonym, because no demo source takes a pseudonym (#474).
  • The PDP gives a clean deny instead of an HTTP error. For an unknown consent or an unreachable register, the PDP makes a policy decision with a reason in the decision record. The consumer does not get an upstream error (F-24).
  • The records correlate. The consumer sends traceparent and Fsc-Transaction-Id (REQ-55, AV-01, ADR-0035). The Inway does not pass traceparent to the PDP. The policy puts both on the status lookup. For how the records join, see Logging.
  • A suspended consumer keeps access. A consumer with an existing contract can still send queries, also with a valid consent (REQ-110, Q-53).

docs.title: EUDI issuance: the PuB-EAA route
docs.text:
A citizen scans a QR code, shares the PID from the NL Wallet, and gets an attestation with data from an authentic source. The bronhouder is the PuB-EAA provider. GBO operates the technical issuance facility (ADR-0028, PSA S11). The decision for this route is ADR-0018.

One issuance in gbo-demo v0.9.0 has hops, data on each hop, and error paths. The following sections give these details and do not explain the concepts again. For the concepts, see these pages:

  • The components: Level 2: EUDI chain.
  • The regime: Regime selection.
  • The source description and its release: Source onboarding.
  • The certificates: EUDI trust roles.
  • The BSN in this route: Exception: the BSN in the EUDI and ASI routes.

docs.title: Before the first QR code
docs.text:
The route runs only from an active source release. For each source, the release holds these items:

  • The offers.
  • The GraphQL query and its parameters.
  • The claims.
  • The display texts.
  • A reference to the certificate set.

GBO generates the issuance configuration and the Type Metadata from the release (REQ-64, ADR-0016, ADR-0017). A valid FSC contract does not activate a source (REQ-65). For that run, see Admission and activation. If no release is active, no offer exists and the portal shows no QR code.

The demo has two attestation types:

Type Source (source_id) FSC service Rule Offers Subject of the data Income statement (inkomensverklaring) belastingdienst bri EUD0001 Year (jaar) 2024 and 2025 The PID holder Death certificate (akte van overlijden) rvig brp EUD0002 One, without parameters The deceased partner of the PID holder (related-person attestation)

The offers come from the source documents (BD, BRP). In the default demo, both sources are on the Belastingdienst peer …0200 (FSC peers).

docs.text:
The sequence shows the income statement for 2024, cross-device.
