docs.title: Data per hop
docs.text:
The table marks personal data in bold. The hop numbers refer to the steps of the sequence:

# From → To Endpoint Data Notes 1 to 2 Portal → adapter GET /eudi-offers.json (through the portal proxy) Per offer: key, label, source_id, type_id, and parameters No personal data. The adapter serves the offers of the active release (source_release_runtime.go#L95-L104, nginx.conf#L43-L49). 3 to 4 Citizen ↔ portal — In: the chosen offer. Out: a universal link with request_uri The portal builds the link in the browser (eudi.ts#L42-L51). The QR code is public, so any person can scan it. This is the only initiation route in the demo. 5 to 7 Wallet ↔ issuance server POST /disclosure/<offer>/request_uri The disclosure request The request asks for one PID claim, bsn (issuance_config.go#L162). The reader certificate of the source names the issuer and the purpose (REQ-58). 8 to 10 Wallet → issuance server OpenID4VP PID with the BSN The issuance server checks the presentation against issuer_trust_anchors (issuance_server.toml.example#L3-L9). That list also holds non-PID anchors (REQ-45). The approval in the wallet is no legal basis (F-83). 11 Issuance server → adapter POST /attestations/{sourceID}/{typeID}?<offer parameters> Disclosed attributes, urn:eudi:pid:nl:1 with the BSN Public HTTPS (an ISRG-rooted certificate, through a tunnel). The route has no caller authentication (source_release_runtime.go#L69-L81, #133). For more information, see The callback gap. 12 Adapter (internal) Active release In: path and body. Out: the BSN The binding of sourceID and typeID must exist in the active release. The adapter takes the BSN from the PID and does not check a signature (main.go#L143-L162, #L23-L26). 13 Adapter → logbook LDV write Record dataverwerking.pid-bsn-extractie The record names the data subject by a pseudonym that is local to the logbook. It does not hold the BSN. If the logbook does not acknowledge the record, the adapter does not call the source (main.go#L256-L262, ldv_issuance.go#L101-L147, REQ-72). 14 Adapter (internal) Query plan In: the offer parameters and the query of the release. Out: {query, variables: {bsn, jaar}} The parameters must match a published offer exactly (source_metadata.go#L272-L298). The adapter has no query or mapping of its own (REQ-44). 15 Adapter → edi-outway POST {outway}/graphql {query, variables} with the BSN, and the headers Fsc-Grant-Hash, Fsc-Transaction-Id, and traceparent The adapter checks that the source document names the contracted service (main.go#L466-L503). No X-GBO-Scope and no flow. The txlog and the trace carry the transaction ID. The ADL record behind the Inway gets its own trace and no transaction ID (#369, REQ-55, ADR-0035). 16 to 17 edi-outway ↔ edi-manager FSC access token In: the grant hash. Out: a certificate-bound token The Outway caches the token. The grant carries no properties. 18 edi-outway → bd-inway FSC, mTLS Body 1:1 with the BSN Every channel goes through FSC with a valid certificate (REQ-46). 19 bd-inway → PDP POST /authzen/v1/evaluation AuthZEN envelope: Outway peer …0100, service bri, and the body with the BSN The Inway is the PEP. The mapper parses the GraphQL and does not call BSNk (Regime selection). 20 PDP → bd-inway AuthZEN response Allow or deny, per field The request has no consent token, so the PID regime applies. EUD0001 checks the designated issuer, the BSN in the root argument, and allowed_years (eud0001.rego#L45-L75, REQ-74, REQ-97). The PDP writes the BSN to the ADL and the console decision log (REQ-60). 21 to 22 bd-inway → gateway → source POST /graphql The judged query with the BSN The request has no consent token, so the gateway passes it through unchanged (Level 2: bronhouder). The source logs its own processing. 23 Source → adapter GraphQL response Income data for the year Back through the same FSC chain, 1:1. 24 Adapter (internal) gbo-simple-v1 In: the response at result_pointer. Out: flat claims Exactly one result gives claims. Zero results is no_data. Any error gives no attestation (REQ-116). Only scalar claims (REQ-78). 25 Adapter → logbook LDV write Record dataverwerking.attestatie-samenstellen The record names the number of claims without their values. It points at the logbook of the source. The adapter writes it for every outcome after the call to the source. If the logbook does not acknowledge the record, the adapter withholds the answer (main.go#L283-L292). 26 Adapter → issuance server Response to hop 11 [{attestation_type: <VCT>, attributes, format: "dc+sd-jwt", id}] with the claims The VCT is the URL of the generated Type Metadata (main.go#L319-L334). 27 to 28 Issuance server → wallet OpenID4VCI Attestation (SD-JWT VC) Signed with the issuer certificate of the source. Valid 365 days, with one status list per type (issuance_config.go#L166-L180, REQ-77). The wallet shows the issuer from the certificate.

docs.title: Public endpoints of the adapter
docs.text:
The adapter serves three routes on one listener (source_release_runtime.go#L59-L106):

Route Caller Content When the release is not available GET /eudi-offers.json Developer portal, consumer frontends The offer catalog 503 for all sources, also when only one source is past its grace period GET /types/{sourceID}/{typeID}/v{version} Wallet, relying parties The SD-JWT VC Type Metadata that GBO generates from the claims. Its URL is the VCT. 503 POST /attestations/{sourceID}/{typeID} Issuance server The attestation callback 503

The issuance server installs the same Type Metadata bytes and computes vct#integrity over them. A change to the claims or the display needs a different type_version (type_metadata.go#L17-L40, The eudi capability).

docs.title: The callback gap
docs.text:
The issuance server checks the PID. The adapter does not know that the request comes from the issuance server. No mechanism binds the BSN in hop 11 to a checked disclosure (REQ-45, Q-18, #133). The demo uses this gap itself. The developer portal has a playground that posts a typed BSN to the adapter (EudiQrPanel.tsx#L36-L51, nginx.conf#L36-L42).

sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(241,239,232) Caller participant X as Any caller<br/>that reaches the adapter end box rgb(255,237,213) EUDI participant AD as EUDI adapter end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis participant OW as edi-outway<br/>(designated issuer) participant PDP as PDP<br/>(EUD0001) end box rgb(221,235,247) Source participant SRC as Source end X->>AD: POST /attestations/belastingdienst/inkomensverklaring?jaar=2024<br/>body with any BSN, no wallet AD->>OW: Query with that BSN OW->>PDP: Actor …0100, no consent token PDP-->>OW: Allow: designated issuer, BSN present SRC-->>AD: Income data of that person AD-->>X: Claims, without any wallet

The data on each hop of this gap is as follows:

# Data Notes 1 Any BSN No caller authentication, and no proof of a checked disclosure. 2 to 4 BSN The request has no consent token, so it enters the PID regime. The only gate of this regime is the list of designated issuers (F-70, eudi_helper.rego#L13-L30). 5 to 6 Income data The caller gets the projected claims.

SL-25 removed the PID check from the adapter, because the issuance server checks the PID. The issuance server checks the signature, so the gap is in the callback. REQ-45 names two fixes:

  • The adapter checks the SD-JWT itself.
  • The issuance server authenticates the callback and delivers signed evidence.

Both fixes need the binding of the disclosure to the request. The reference QTSP callback on the same issuance server uses a secret path over CA-pinned HTTPS (qtsp_issuance.go#L134-L152, ASI verification).

docs.title: Error paths
docs.text:
The consumer of the adapter is the issuance server. The issuance server gets only the HTTP status. The details are in the adapter log (stage). For a PDP deny, the details are also in the ADL.

The FSC Inway removes the reason of a deny (ftv-graphql-profile.md#L93-L95). In every error path, no attestation reaches the wallet. The error paths have these triggers and outcomes:

Trigger Outcome Pinned by (v0.9.0) The release is past its grace period for one source GET /eudi-offers.json gives 503 for every source. The portal shows no QR code. source_release_runtime.go#L95-L100 The adapter cannot load a release 503 source activations unavailable source_release_runtime.go#L70-L74 sourceID or typeID not in the active release 404 source_release_runtime.go#L75-L79 Source metadata missing, expired, or past the stale grace (15 min fresh, 1 h grace) 503 source metadata unavailable, for this source only (REQ-66) main.go#L221-L225, source_metadata_cache.go#L10-L14 Body unreadable, or no disclosed attestation in it 400 main.go#L234-L246 PID without a BSN 400 no BSN in disclosed PID. The adapter logs nothing and does not call the source. main.go#L249-L253, ldv_test.go#L402 The logbook does not acknowledge the LDV record of hop 13 500. The adapter does not call the source. main.go#L256-L262, ldv_test.go#L354 Offer parameters outside the published offer (for example jaar=2023) 400 invalid attestation parameters main.go#L263-L268, main_test.go#L434 PDP deny: the caller is not a designated issuer ACTOR_NOT_ALLOWED in the ADL. The adapter answers 502. eud0001_test.rego#L65, eud0002_test.rego#L36 PDP deny: no BSN, or a placeholder, in the root argument PID_NOT_PRESENT. The adapter answers 502. eud0001_test.rego#L71-L80, eud0002_test.rego#L42 PDP deny: the request carries a consent token PID_NOT_PRESENT. The adapter answers 502. eud0001_test.rego#L83 PDP deny: a year outside allowed_years, or no year filter YEAR_NOT_ALLOWED. The adapter answers 502. eud0001_test.rego#L39-L58 PDP deny: a field outside the rule (closed world) FIELD_NOT_PERMITTED or NO_APPLICABLE_RULE. The adapter answers 502. engine.rego#L282, Rule model Chain unreachable, non-200 answer, or GraphQL errors 502 source request failed. The adapter does not pass on the upstream body. The assembly record has status ERROR. main.go#L294-L300, main_test.go#L444, ldv_test.go#L267 Result does not fit the claims: GBO_SIMPLE_PATH_MISSING, GBO_SIMPLE_TYPE_MISMATCH, GBO_SIMPLE_RESULT_TYPE 502 source response could not be projected. No partial attestation. The code is only in the adapter log. main.go#L302-L308, profile.go#L33-L37, cases.json#L96-L125 More than one result 502 with GBO_SIMPLE_RESULT_AMBIGUOUS cases.json#L89-L93 No result (no_data) 404 source has no data for this subject and parameters. The adapter still writes the assembly record, with zero claims. main.go#L310-L315, cases.json#L82-L86, ldv_test.go#L505 The logbook does not acknowledge the LDV record of hop 25 500. The adapter withholds the attestation. main.go#L284-L292 Missing or incomplete certificate set of a source The issuance facility blocks the source (CERTIFICATE_SET_NOT_FOUND, CERTIFICATE_SET_INVALID). Other sources continue to work. REQ-58, A certificate set per source A caller posts a body with any BSN directly to the adapter Allowed in demo v0.9.0. The source answers, and the caller gets the claims. Not built: #133, REQ-45

docs.title: Related-person attestation: death certificate
docs.text:
The death certificate holds data about the deceased partner of the citizen who shares the PID. The subject of the claims differs from the person who discloses the PID (F-47, REQ-57, SL-43). The run is the same as the run in the preceding sections, with these differences per hop:

# Difference 11 POST /attestations/rvig/akte-van-overlijden, without parameters. 14 to 15 The query is akteVanOverlijden(bsn: $bsn) with the BSN of the PID holder, on service brp. 19 to 20 EUD0002 decides. It grants a closed list of output fields and checks the BSN in the root argument. It has no year check (eud0002.rego#L20-L66). 21 to 22 The gateway is brp-sidecar, and the source is brp-graphql-server. 22 to 23 The source resolves the relation itself. It selects the marriage that ended by the death of the partner. If the partner died on a different date than the dissolution, the source returns nothing. Then the adapter answers 404 (main_test.go#L183). 25 The deceased is not a data subject under the GDPR. The source logs the requester and the living parents (AV-10).

The PDP sees only the flat output of the source view. It does not see the relation. The relation depends on the source and on the subject from the PID. Because of the callback gap, a caller can ask for the death certificate for any BSN.

The preferred design puts the relation in filter arguments of the published schema. The policy then requires these arguments with fixed values (#425, Q-14). In demo v0.9.0, the source description does not mark the relation.

docs.title: Observations
docs.text:
The run of an issuance in demo v0.9.0 shows these facts:

  • The regime follows from the evidence. A request without a consent token goes into the PID regime. That regime has no positive evidence of its own. Its only gate is the list of designated issuers. This list must stay disjoint from the consent consumers (REQ-74, F-70, ADR-0031). A test pins the disjointness only for the seeded consumers (engine_test.rego#L366-L376).
  • The PID check and the source query have no link. The issuance server checks the PID. The adapter callback has no authentication (REQ-45, Q-18). The PID trust list also trusts the GBO development CA and the issuer CA of every source.
  • The BSN is in the decision logs. The adapter puts the plain BSN in the query variables. As a result, the BSN is in the PDP input, the ADL, and the console decision log (REQ-60, F-54, ADR-0043, #368). The LDV records of the adapter hold no BSN.
  • The offer and the policy are independent limits. The source offers 2024 and 2025. EUD0001 allows 2024 and 2025. A request for 2023 fails at the adapter (no offer). The PDP also denies it (YEAR_NOT_ALLOWED). Publication by a source does not authorize the published data (F-74).
  • The adapter holds no knowledge of a source. The query, the parameters, the claims, the display, and the Type Metadata come from the release (REQ-64, F-57). The source decides through its own PDP (REQ-44).
  • No partial attestation exists. Any projection error gives 502 and no attestation (REQ-116). The issuance server sees no reason code.
  • The validity is fixed. Every source attestation is valid 365 days. GBO has no change feed from the source. As a result, GBO cannot revoke an attestation when the source data changes (REQ-77, F-82).
  • Correlation works, with one gap. The adapter sends one Fsc-Transaction-Id and a traceparent. The txlog, the LDV records of the adapter and the source, and the trace share them. The ADL record behind the Inway has its own trace and no transaction ID (#369) (REQ-55, Reading a chain).

docs.title: Not built in demo v0.9.0
docs.text:
Demo v0.9.0 does not have these items:

  • An authenticated callback, and the binding of the disclosure to the source query (#133, REQ-45).
  • A PID trust list with PID-provider anchors only.
  • The BSN out of the PDP input (#368, ADR-0043, proposed).
  • Validity and revocation per type, set by the bronhouder, with revocation on instruction or on a change in the source (REQ-77, AV-12, AV-13).
  • Nested claims (REQ-78), and traceability of the mapping version per attestation (REQ-124).
  • The relation as filter arguments, and its marking in the source description (#425, REQ-57).

  • The regulatory frame for PuB-EAA issuance (F-81, Q-28). This frame has these parts:

    • Designation.
    • A registration certificate.
    • A qualified seal in a QSCD.
    • Conformity with ETSI TS 119 471 and TS 119 472-3.

    The trust list for PuB-EAA providers is open (Q-30). Key custody is open (Q-17).

  • A second initiation route next to the QR code in the developer portal.

  • Cross-route items from the ASI work (ASI verification):
    • The BRP document also publishes the asi capability. An error in asi refuses the whole source, and this includes its EUDI issuance (#592, source-onboarding.md#L400-L401).
    • The issuance server also issues the test statement of the reference QTSP. That use case runs only in the local stack. A deployment in the simulation environment is #594.
    • #595 (BSN in the ASI token) and #596 (same-device wallet login on a phone) concern only the ASI route.

docs.title: Policy distribution
docs.text:
Policy distribution is a management-plane scenario. Policy travels in this scenario, and no citizen data travels. The management plane decides who changes the rules. The decision plane decides who gets which data. The two planes are separate (F-51).

The scenario takes place at the bronhouder. The PDP is behind the FSC Inway of the bronhouder, and the OpenFTV Manager serves exactly that PDP. Policy management stays with each bronhouder (Q-21, ADR-0021). In the demo, everything runs in one compose stack. This setup is a demo artifact and makes no statement about the architecture.

For the concept, see Policy lifecycle.

Two components have the name Manager. The OpenFTV Manager manages policy (PAP). The FSC Manager manages contracts and issues access tokens. This page covers only the OpenFTV Manager.

docs.title: Two modes
docs.text:
The PDP gets its policy in one of two modes:

Mode Where the PDP gets its policy Started by Mount (default) The PDP image carries policies/ (Dockerfile#L62-L67). Compose bind-mounts ./policies over that copy (docker-compose.yml#L157). The PDP hot-reloads at each edit every make demo* target Bundle (opt-in) The PDP pulls bundle gbo-pdp from the OpenFTV Manager at start, because PDP_BUNDLE_MANAGER is set (docker-compose.yml#L145-L149) make demo-manager, then make manager-seed after each change (Makefile#L151-L177)

The demo runs OpenFTV release v0.1.0. The PDP builds from the tag with the FTV GraphQL mapper patched in. The Manager and its management interface are the published v0.1.0 images (docker-compose.yml#L245). If the three versions differ, or if the version is not a release tag, CI fails (ci.yml#L355-L373).

docs.title: Scenario 1: mount mode (default)

sequenceDiagram autonumber box rgb(241,239,232) Author actor DEV as Policy author end box rgb(237,233,254) Version control participant GIT as policies/ in version control end box rgb(241,239,232) Build participant MK as make policy-check end box rgb(220,252,231) GBO Basis participant PDP as OpenFTV PDP end box rgb(237,233,254) Records participant ADL as ADL (postgres-ftv) end DEV->>GIT: Edit a .rego file DEV->>MK: Any make target that starts the PDP MK->>GIT: Refuse non-Rego files and duplicate file names MK->>MK: opa check policies MK-->>DEV: Pass, or stop before the PDP starts PDP->>GIT: Load /policies (bind mount), recursive Note over PDP: Hot reload on every edit PDP->>ADL: Decision records

Each hop in mount mode carries the following data:

# From → to Data Notes 1 Author → version control Rego source with tests next to the rules Version control is the source of the content 2 to 5 make → policies/ File list, compile result policy-check runs before every target that starts the PDP (Makefile#L92-L106). make policy-test adds opa fmt --diff and opa test (#L115-L117) 6 to 7 PDP → mount Every file under /policies as a Rego module (PDP_POLICIES_LANGUAGE=rego, PDP_POLICIES_STORE_RECURSE=true) The reload log line policy added/replaced does not prove that the new rules decide (#151) 8 PDP → ADL Decision records The PDP does not start without the ADL database (docker-compose.yml#L117-L125)

MGR->>PG: Store the policy and the audit trail     SEED->>MGR: GET /v1/policies: which policy left version control?     SEED->>MGR: PUT /v1/policy/{id}, tag gbo-retired     Note over SEED,PDP: make demo-manager and make manager-seed restart the PDP     PDP->>MGR: GET /v1/bundle/gbo-pdp (internal port 9443)     MGR->>MGR: Cedar: pdp-bundle.cedar permits GET on this path     MGR-->>PDP: Gzipped bundle {version, policies with tag gbo-authz, data}     PDP->>PDP: Compile the whole set and activate it     PDP->>PG: Decision records to the ADL (ftv_adl)

docs.title: Data per hop
docs.text:
Each hop in bundle mode carries the following data:

# From → to Interface Data Notes 1 to 2 Seed → Keycloak POST /realms/gbo/protocol/openid-connect/token (seed-openftv-manager.py#L83-L113) Client openftv-manager-ui, user deployment, password from FTV_MANAGER_DEPLOY_PASSWORD Publishing token: non-personal deployment identity, role admin, token lifespan 1800 s, and no long-lived API key (RL-03) 3 Seed → version control File system policies/**/*.rego without tests, repo-relative path Version control is canonical for the content. The Manager is the distribution mechanism (RL-01) 4 to 6 Seed → Manager → Postgres POST /v1/policy/{id}, on conflict PUT (#L171-L211) Rego source, title, tag gbo-authz id is uuid5 of the repo-relative path, so a new run updates the policy instead of making a duplicate. The Manager has no file store: policy enters only through the API, the same path as the management interface 7 to 8 Seed → Manager GET /v1/policies, then PUT /v1/policy/{id} (#L116-L168) Policies with gbo-authz that are not in version control get tag gbo-retired and title prefix RETIRED Reconciliation (RL-04). DELETE fails upstream on a foreign key to the audit trail, so the script retires policies and never deletes them 9 to 11 PDP → Manager GET /v1/bundle/gbo-pdp on the internal port (gbo-pdp.yaml) Gzipped bundle: version, the policies with tag gbo-authz, design-time data The PDP pulls the bundle. The Manager has no push targets (targets: []). The PDP presents no identity. pdp-bundle.cedar permits only can_read on this one path (RL-02) 12 PDP — The active policy set The PDP compiles the set as a whole. If one package is duplicated, every request fails (F-52, RL-05) 13 PDP → Postgres ADL Decision records for data requests and contract proposals The ADL is the authoritative record (ADR-0036). The ADL records no policy version (REQ-59). The ADL can hold OINs. In the EUDI and ASI routes, it can also hold the BSN (REQ-60)

docs.text:
The Ports column gives each port as host:container. The host ports are the compose defaults. Policy distribution uses the following components:

docs.title: Main observations
docs.text:
Policy distribution in gbo-demo v0.9.0 has these properties and gaps:

  • Two planes, two policy sets. Cedar policies authorize the Manager API. These policies are separate from the Rego decision policy. On the PDP side, this separation is missing. The PDP guards its own management endpoints with the decision policy. As a result, push works only if that policy opens up. The demo pulls instead (F-51, RL-02).
  • Write and publish are not separate. The realm defines author, but no Cedar policy in v0.9.0 grants it an action. Only admin writes and publishes. The deployment identity is that non-personal admin (RL-03).
  • Version control is canonical. The PAP distributes the policy. Manual API changes are possible. As a result, reconciliation at every publication is the only guard against drift (RL-04).
  • The policy set fails as a whole. The policy set is one availability object. If one rule is faulty, the whole set fails, and every request gets HTTP 500 instead of a deny. Since SL-45, the same set also holds the contract policy (policies/fsc/). As a result, one broken module stops the data exchange and also the admission of new participants (F-52, REQ-62).
  • No signing, by decision. The bundle has an ID and a version, but no signature. A bundle gets a signature only when it crosses an organization boundary. Inside one organization, signing is not planned (#426, closed as not planned, F-09, ADR-0021).
  • Source metadata has a fuller lifecycle. Source releases get validation before activation, atomic promotion of immutable releases, and rollback (REQ-66, Source activation). The policy bundle has none of these steps. For this reason, RL-05 is a backlog item and more than a wish (F-59).
  • Read access to the ADL is open. Read access to the decision log is an authorization question. The auditor role reads the ADL through the management interface. The ADL can hold OINs, and in the EUDI and ASI routes also the BSN. It is open who can read the ADL (Q-08, F-53).

docs.title: Traceability
docs.text:
• Requirements: RL-01, RL-02, RL-03, RL-04, RL-05, REQ-59, REQ-60, REQ-62, REQ-66
  • Findings: F-09 (open), F-51 (open), F-52 (open), F-53 (resolved in demo), F-59 (closed)
  • Open questions: Q-21 (answered), Q-02 (answered), Q-08 (open)
  • Demo increments: SL-44 (done), SL-45 (done)

docs.title: How to trace
docs.text:
This TO is the reference for what GBO builds, the reasons for it, and the points that are open. From any kind of information in the TO, you can follow the chain to the other kinds. The TO connects five kinds of information:

Kind ID Question it answers Where Architecture decision ADR-NNNN What did the GBO team choose, and which alternatives did it refuse? Decision log Requirement REQ-NN, RL-NN, AV-NN, BSNK-NN What must the result do, and how does a test check it? Requirements Demo increment SL-NN Which demo work proved it, and with which PRs? Demo increments Finding F-NN What did the demo build show about the design? Open findings, closed findings Open question Q-NN What must another forum decide, and what does the TO assume until then? Open questions, answered questions

Two more pages support the chain:

  • The design to demo matrix takes each element of the GO, the PSA, FR-DvTP v0.9, and the EUDI regulation. For each element, it records whether the demo covers it.
  • Standards feedback lists the open points in ETSI TS 119 478 (E1 to E10) that the ASI route found.

docs.title: The chain
docs.text:
graph LR ADR[Architecture decision<br/>ADR-NNNN] -->|serves| REQ[Requirement<br/>REQ / RL / AV / BSNK] REQ -->|proved by| SL[Demo increment<br/>SL-NN + demo PRs] SL -->|exposed| F[Finding<br/>F-NN] F -->|lands in| REQ F -->|lands in| ADR F -->|needs a decision| Q[Open question<br/>Q-NN] Q -->|blocks| ADR ARC[arc42 section<br/>building blocks, runtime, concepts] -->|explains| ADR ARC -->|explains| SL %% GBO diagram palette: the same colors as the Globaal Ontwerp classDef basis fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#16A34A,color:#0F172A classDef dvtp fill:#FEDCD8,stroke:#E28F80,color:#1E293B classDef eudi fill:#FFEDD5,stroke:#EA580C,color:#0F172A classDef source fill:#DDEBF7,stroke:#6F94B8,color:#1E293B classDef ext fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#444441 classDef store fill:#EDE9FE,stroke:#7C3AED,color:#1E1B4B classDef mock fill:#F3F4F6,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef planned fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#9CA3AF,color:#6B7280,stroke-dasharray:6 4 classDef zoom stroke-width:3px class ADR,REQ,SL,F,Q store class ARC ext

Each kind of item in the chain carries these links:

  • A decision serves one or more requirements. An accepted decision has evidence in the demo. A proposed decision waits for an open question.
  • A requirement names its source, its addressee, and its evidence in the demo. The source is the GO, the PSA, FR-DvTP, or the demo itself.
  • A demo increment is a bounded piece of demo work. It names its demo PRs and the requirements, findings, and questions that it produced.
  • A finding names its trigger, what it showed, and where it landed: a requirement, a decision, a risk, or an open question.
  • An open question names the forum that must answer it. It also names the working assumption that the demo and this TO use until then.

Every arc42 page and every ADR ends with a Traceability section. That section lists the IDs that the page explains or depends on.

docs.title: Start points
docs.text:
The first step depends on where you start:

You start at Do this A part of the demo Find the component in the building block view or the flow in the runtime view. Its Traceability section names the decisions, requirements, and increments. A demo increment Open its entry in Demo increments. Explained in links the TO section. Produced links the requirements, findings, and questions. An open finding Open its entry in Findings. Read the summary first. The block Evidence, impact and proposal links the requirement, decision, or question. Coverage lists every page that cites the finding. An open question Open its entry in Open questions. The summary gives the question and the working assumption. The block below it names the forum that decides. Coverage lists the decisions that the question blocks. A decision Read the ADR. Coverage shows its full chain in one row. A requirement Open it from the list of all requirements. Evidence links the demo test or code. Coverage lists the pages that explain the requirement.

docs.title: Example: the consumer has no citizen identifier
docs.text:
The chain for this example has six steps:

  1. The runtime page DvTP query shows that the consumer sends a placeholder. After the allow, the source gateway puts the source's own value in place of the placeholder.
  2. The decision is ADR-0033, with the consent proof in ADR-0032.
  3. The decision serves REQ-21, REQ-79, and REQ-80.
  4. The demo work is increment SL-51, with its demo PRs.
  5. Three findings are open against the decision:
    • F-76: what the consumer records about "this person".
    • F-77: the PDP checks that the subject comes from the proof. The PDP does not check who the subject is.
    • F-79: "after the decision" holds only if nothing but the Inway reaches the gateway.
  6. One decision waits: who is the BSNk participant (Q-49)? The proposed ADR-0040 records the working assumption (route D).

docs.title: Baseline and maintenance
docs.text:
• Demo baseline: gbo-demo v0.9.0 (November 2, 2026). Links to demo code use this tag. A few historical evidence links pin an earlier demo commit.
  • Status of the registers: November 2, 2026. On that date, 34 findings and 61 open questions are open or partly answered.
  • Numbers: numbers are never reused. A withdrawn or removed requirement keeps its line in the list of removed numbers.
  • When the demo changes: make these four updates:
    1. Update the requirement Evidence.
    2. Add or close findings.
    3. Update the increment.
    4. Update the Traceability section of the pages that explain the change.
  • Generated page: scripts/gen_traceability.py generates Coverage. CI runs the script with --check. The script fails in two cases:
    • A page links an ID that no register defines.
    • No TO page or decision cites an open finding or an open question.

docs.title: Answered questions
docs.text: These questions have an answer, or they are closed. Each entry gives the answer and where it landed. The questions that are still open are on Open questions.

docs.title: Q-02: Central authorization server or distributed PDP (per bronhouder)?
docs.text:
• Status: answered
  • Question: Does one central PDP decide for all sources, or does each bronhouder run its own PDP?
  • Answer: Decentral, at the bronhouder. The GO table of provisions places the source access API, the PEP, PDP, and PAP, and the FSC Inway at the bronhouder. If responsibilities and availability are assured, PSA S05 allows a PDP per bronhouder or a shared PDP. B-04 allows several variants under one PEP-PDP interface. The B-04 owners (bronhouders, FDS/GDI) set the conditions for a shared PDP. GBO does not set them.
  • Landed in: ADR 0004, REQ-04. As a shortcut, the demo runs one shared PDP behind both Inways. SL-44 shows that each source can run its own PDP with bundle distribution.

docs.title: Q-03: Atomic consent or field level: what is lawful and understandable?
docs.text:
• Status: answered
  • Question: Does the citizen consent per field, or per indivisible data set (gegevensset)?
  • Answer: Per data set. In the GO, consent applies to a specific purpose, consumer, and data set. FR-10 (FR-DvTP v0.9) puts consent at set level, with "1 scope = 1 record". The citizen switches an optional set on or off as a whole. The demo portal switches per scope and conforms. FR-10 also adds a fixed minimal mandatory set, which is Q-45 and issue #382.
  • Landed in: REQ-10, F-03.

docs.title: Q-04: Is consent single-use or repeatable within a validity period?
docs.text:
• Status: answered
  • Question: Is a consent valid for one retrieval, or can the consumer use it again until it expires?
  • Answer: Repeatable. In FR-11 (FR-DvTP v0.9), every consent has a configurable validity period. Within that period, the consumer can use the consent again. Single use is no longer an option.
  • Landed in: REQ-19, F-04. The question who sets the period is Q-13.

docs.title: Q-05: Who is authoritative for revocation and expiry, and what is the propagation SLA?
docs.text:
• Status: answered
  • Question: Which party is authoritative for revocation and expiry? How much time can a revocation take to reach the decision?
  • Answer: The central consent register (toestemmingsregister) is authoritative (GO, B-06). Revocation has direct effect. The authorization chain calls the register as PIP when the data request arrives (PSA S01, S02 "without undue delay", FR-11 v0.9 "real-time"). The demo conforms: the PDP calls for the status per request, without a cache (PR #371). The proof travels signed, but its status stays online (F-61).
  • Landed in: REQ-68, ADR 0032. The figures (propagation time, availability, latency) are a design requirement in REQ-75.

docs.title: Q-06: Authentication means for private parties: eHerkenning, PKI certificate, or both?
docs.text:
• Status: answered
  • Question: With which means does a private party authenticate: eHerkenning, a PKI certificate, or both?
  • Answer: Both, with separate roles.
    • FR-03 (FR-DvTP v0.9): people use eHerkenning, at onboarding and for management.
    • FR-33 and FR-34: systems use an organization identification means from a recognized issuer, linked to OIN or KvK.
    • PSA S04: organizations and systems use recognized identifiers and certificates.
    • The demo conforms for systems. The legal identity comes from the validated certificate (F-60).
    • The origin of source metadata fetched outside FSC is a design matter and no question for the PSA (F-71).
  • Landed in: REQ-67, REQ-64, ADR 0023. The identifier and the issuer are Q-07.

docs.title: Q-07: PKIoverheid scope as trust anchor (also EUDI Access CA?)
docs.text:
• Status: answered
  • Question: Is PKIoverheid the one trust anchor for both FDS and EUDI, including the EUDI Access CA?
  • Answer: The question is answered or no longer applies, as follows:
    • On the FDS side, systems authenticate with PKIoverheid certificates (GO, PSA S04).
    • The seal on an attestation follows the eIDAS framework. It uses a qualified seal certificate from a QTSP, checked against the EU trusted lists (F-66).
    • Access certificates (ETSI TS 119 411-8) only authenticate a provider or relying party to the wallet. They do not sign attestations.
    • GO and PSA no longer pursue one infrastructure for FDS and EUDI.
    • Issuer and reader certificates are a set per source. The reason is that the legal identity and the display name depend on the signing certificate (issue #225).
    • The Access CA is a dependency on the Dutch EUDI governance.
    • The open key and seal question moved to Q-17.
  • Landed in: REQ-58, F-66, ADR 0023. For a private consumer, the choice is OIN or KvK. The GO names the OIN. The link between the identifiers is an open decision in S04.

docs.title: Q-09: How does the FSC grant (org permission) relate to consent (legal basis)? Can one be missing?
docs.text:
• Status: answered
  • Question: Are organization permission (the FSC grant) and legal basis (consent) separate checks, and must both always be present?

  • Answer: Yes, there are two separate, cumulative checks:

    • Admission: PSA S04 ("participation requires a prior admission decision") and FR-16 (FR-DvTP v0.9).
    • Legal basis: PSA S05, FR-17, and the GO.

    The demo conforms (SL-05, SL-45). The governance part is Q-22 and B-09.

  • Landed in: REQ-61, REQ-62, REQ-74.

docs.title: Q-10: Which functions must really be central, and which are decentral at each bronhouder?
docs.text:
• Status: answered
  • Question: Which provisions run centrally, and which run at each bronhouder?
  • Answer: The GO table of provisions gives the answer:
    • The PEP, PDP, and PAP and the source access are decentral, at the bronhouder.
    • The consent facility (toestemmingsvoorziening) is central and mandatory for DvTP ("needs a statutory basis").
    • BSNk PP is mandatory for DvTP (Logius).
    • PuB-EAA issuance, the ASI provider, and the OOTS adapter are optional central connection provisions.
    • Operators "still to be decided" fall under B-17 and B-06.
    • Funding is outside this analysis.
  • Landed in: ADR 0004, Q-02. In the demo, the register and BSNk are central, which conforms. The PDP is shared as a shortcut. The demo removed sector-pip (issue #378).

docs.title: Q-11: Transformation between source schema and canonical model: where and how?
docs.text:
• Status: answered
  • Question: Where and how is a source schema transformed to a canonical model?
  • Answer: There is no central canonical model.
    • GO F4 gives a shared concept framework (NL-SBB, MIM, RDF/SKOS, DCAT-AP-NL) and "the canonical data models of bronhouders".
    • In PSA S10, mappings are explicit and traceable. Bronhouders and domains own their models.
    • For EUDI, the source supplies its own mapping (F-57).
    • For OOTS, there is an optional shared mapping facility (GO, B-12).
    • Ownership of the semantics falls under B-11.
    • One point is open for a check. S10 requires that every data service refers to a managed schema and concept framework. That includes the service description of the source (/.well-known/gbo).
  • Landed in: ADR 0024, REQ-64, F-57.

docs.title: Q-12: Role of integrators: pass-through, and can they see data?
docs.text:
• Status: answered
  • Question: Is an integrator only a pass-through, and can it see the data?
  • Answer:
    • FR-DvTP v0.9 removes FR-06. The citizen gets no information about the integrator.
    • FR-18: the integrator is a processor for the service provider (dienstverlener). It can view and edit data as far as the assignment needs. It does so under a processing agreement and without persistent storage.
    • FR-37: the integrator has its own onboarding and its own organization identification means. It also has a registration in the service catalog (dienstencatalogus) per service provider and use case.
    • For more information, see PSA S04, S05, and B-19.
    • The consequence for the actor binding of consent was F-73. The demo tested it with FSC delegation (issue #379).
  • Landed in: REQ-106, AV-06, ADR 0034. Follow-up: Q-46.

docs.title: Q-15: How does the Manager decide which access-basis path applies to a (consumer x scope) combination?
docs.text:
• Status: answered
  • Question: Which mechanism selects the access-basis path (consent or legal basis) for a request?
  • Answer: The premise ("the Manager selects the path") lapsed.
    • The regime follows from the evidence that the request carries. A consent token opens the consent regime. Without a consent token, the PID regime applies (PR #363).
    • The GO and PSA S05 check the legal basis in policy.
    • An admission question remains: who is on the actor list of the PID regime? That is a register fact (Q-22).
    • Positive PID evidence is F-70, issue #133, and Q-18.
    • Grants carry no properties any more. The demo removed subject_id_type (issue #473).
  • Landed in: REQ-74, ADR 0031 (supersedes ADR 0030), F-70.

docs.title: Q-16: AuthZEN/OpenFTV conformity: which profile does GBO follow, and is GBO at the working-group table?
docs.text:
• Status: answered
  • Question: Which PEP-PDP profile does GBO follow, and does GBO take part in the OpenFTV working group?
  • Answer:
    • GBO takes part in the OpenFTV working group and prepares a proposal for a GraphQL profile (B-02, issue #331).
    • The conformity level is the NLGov AuthZEN profile (GO, PSA S05).
    • The demo conforms on the wire protocol through OpenFTV v0.1.0 (PR #337). In demo v0.9.0, only the GraphQL mapping is patched.
    • The profile variant and the choice "purist or pragmatic" belong in the proposal.
    • The mapping of DvTP fields onto AuthZEN is the open S05 decision on the definitive GBO profile. Q-14 is input for it.
    • The standardization route for grant properties lapsed (PR #363, issue #364).
  • Landed in: REQ-42, ADR 0002.

docs.title: Q-19: Where do adapter parameters come from? Boundary of the thin adapter and catalog coupling
docs.text:
• Status: answered
  • Question: Where do the query parameters that a channel adapter sends to a source come from?
  • Answer: From the source, for both branches.
    • EUDI: the source publishes the query, the declared parameters, the mapping, the attestation schema, and the offer in /.well-known/gbo. GBO validates and activates them (SL-46, PR #224). The adapter has no use-case knowledge. The demo removed the use-case catalog on the GBO side.
    • DvTP: FR-32 (FR-DvTP v0.9) sets up a statutory service catalog with the legal ceiling per use case. The operator of the DvTP service makes the catalog with the sector representative and manages it. The catalog links data sets to service providers and marks each set mandatory, optional, or minimal.
    • B-03: content management is federated, and findability is central. For more information, see PSA S07.
    • The consequence is F-74: DvTP takes the scope from the demand side, and EUDI takes it from the supply side (issue #382).
  • Landed in: REQ-64, REQ-44, ADR 0016, ADR 0008.

docs.title: Q-20: SD-JWT VC claim shape for related-person data: flat display strings or structured objects?
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Question: Does an attestation carry related-person data (for example, the parents on a death certificate) as flat display strings or as structured claims?
  • Answer: The question became a schema choice per attestation type. It is no longer a system question.
    • In PSA S11, attestations follow an agreed attestation rulebook and schema.
    • The GO has attestation schemas per use case.
    • The schema comes from the source (REQ-64).
    • ARF ARB_30 lets the rulebook state the selective disclosure of nested properties and list elements. Each one MUST, MAY, or MUST NOT be selectively disclosable. Issuance must be able to follow the rulebook.
    • Issue #381, row 13, tests nested claims in the NL Wallet.
  • Landed in: REQ-78, F-47.

docs.title: Q-21: Who can manage and publish the policy of a bronhouder, and how is that authority set federatively?
docs.text:
• Status: answered
  • Question: Who sets the authorization policy for DvTP: a central Policy Authority (FR-39) or the bronhouder (GO)? Who can manage and publish it?
  • Answer: Policy management stays with each bronhouder.
    • PAP and PDP are at the bronhouder, as the GO says (issue #426, closed as not planned, October 28, 2026).
    • The policy guidelines stay guidelines. They do not become requirements.
    • Publication control is a norm in PSA S06. It covers the owner, the approver, the effective date, the change history, tests before publication, and an emergency and rollback procedure.
    • The text of FR-39 (central Policy Authority, signed bundles) is outdated. FR-DvTP needs a change to this text.
    • Authority over policy lies with competent public parties (B-05).
  • Landed in: ADR 0021 (rewritten: "Policy management and distribution per bronhouder"), RL-01 to RL-05, F-09, F-51, F-52.

docs.title: Q-22: Who runs the admission register, on which grounds, and what legal protection has a refused party?
docs.text:
• Status: answered
  • Question: The question has four parts:
    1. Who keeps the admission register (toelatingsregister)?
    2. On which grounds does a party get admission?
    3. What legal protection does a refused party get?
    4. At which granularity is admission given?
  • Answer:
    • Register: the operator of the DvTP service keeps the register (FR-30, FR-DvTP v0.9). The system framework (FDS gatekeeper, draft) follows from B-09.
    • Grounds: PSA P-16 ("objective, proportionate and verifiable; the permitted service, legal basis and data request are registered in advance") and FR-30 (selection criteria, connection conditions).
    • Granularity: per service (P-16, FR-32), through the catalog and the consent registration (issue #382).
    • Legal protection: procedural, at the management organization and B-09. The technical part is REQ-63.
    • The actor list of the PID regime is a register fact. It must stay disjoint from the DvTP consumers (REQ-74, F-70).
    • Demo gap: FR-30 criterion 3 (status "trusted" visible to the citizen) is missing.
  • Landed in: REQ-61, REQ-62, REQ-63, candidate connection conditions, F-55, F-56, ADR 0015.

docs.title: Q-23: Through which interface does a source get the consent status, and how does the register know who asks?
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Question: The PDP of a source calls the register for the consent status across an organization boundary. Over which interface does it do this, and how does the register authenticate the caller?
  • Answer: PSA S01 sets the norm: only the citizen and authorized components have access to consent. The interface and the caller identity are a design decision for the GBO team, as builders of the register. The GO gives FSC as the direction. In demo v0.9.0, the status query goes over FSC. Thus the register records the verified FSC peer as the processor in LDV (issue #383). The trade-off between a query per request and a status list is at REQ-75.
  • Landed in: REQ-76, REQ-75, ADR 0032.

docs.title: Q-24: Must a private consumer record its processing according to LDV?
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Question: Must a private consumer, which LDV does not bind, record its processing so that a reader can follow a chain from its start?
  • Answer: The minimum is normative: the consumer sends W3C Trace Context and records the transaction ID. In PSA S09, every data request gets a request identifier that is usable across the whole chain. Full LDV at the private consumer is a candidate connection condition. FR-31 (FR-DvTP v0.9) puts the chain audit at the service. The LDV records of the status queries at the register form that chain-wide index. This is true only while the PDP calls for the status per request (REQ-75, F-68).
  • Landed in: AV-01 (minimum), AV-02 (full LDV, candidate), F-68.

docs.title: Coverage
docs.text: The script scripts/gen_traceability.py makes this page from the registers and from the Traceability section of every page. Do not edit this page by hand. After you change a register entry or a Traceability section, run python3 scripts/gen_traceability.py.

docs.title: Not explained
docs.text: Every open finding and every open question is cited by at least one TO page or decision.

docs.title: Closed findings
docs.text: These findings are closed, resolved in the demo, superseded, or no longer apply. Each entry says where the outcome landed: a requirement, a decision, or a page of this TO. The open findings are on Findings.

docs.title: F-02: Central PDP as an implicit choice
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: one policy engine served every request. So the demo implied a central PDP, while PDP placement was an open design question.
  • Outcome: Q-02 set the direction: federated by default, with a PDP per bronhouder, and a central adapter variant as fallback. In demo v0.9.0, the PDP sits behind the Inway of each source.
  • Landed in: ADR-0004, Q-02.
  • Evidence: docker-compose.yml

docs.title: F-03: The UI offered per-field selection against FR-10 (atomicity)
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: the citizen was able to switch single fields on and off. FR-10 asks for an indivisible data set.
  • Outcome: since SL-13, policy decides per data set. Since SL-06a, the portal chooses per scope. FR-10 v0.9 has no partial consent, and Q-03 is answered. Demo issue #382 covers the fixed minimal set.
  • Landed in: REQ-10.
  • Evidence: ScopeToggle.tsx

docs.title: F-04: No consent lifecycle: no TTL, no single use, no status model
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: a consent was only active or revoked. The demo did not enforce validity or use.
  • Outcome: the PDP checks validity per request (SL-01a, SL-47). FR-11 v0.9 drops single use: a consent is reusable within its validity (Q-04). Demo issue #389 covers the "retrieved" status. F-19 holds the design question.
  • Landed in: REQ-19, ADR-0032.
  • Evidence: policies/gbo/consent.rego#L124

docs.title: F-06: The source trusted the PEP without a check and had no fourth validation point (FR-26)
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: the source accepted every request from a shared PEP and did no check of its own.
  • Outcome: the shared PEP no longer exists. Every request passes the Inway of the source. The Inway asks the PDP of the source over AuthZEN. This design matches the GO, PSA S05, and criterion 1 of FR-26 v0.9. One point stays open for the FR authors: the FR-26 dependency still names a "central authorization component" (FR-17). That dependency conflicts with the GO.
  • Landed in: REQ-04, ADR-0004.
  • Evidence: demo issue #88 (PEP service removed)

docs.title: F-07: Only OTel tracing, with no LDV and no non-repudiable decision log
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: traceability was technical and short-lived. There was no processing log, no persistent decision log, and no citizen log.
  • Outcome: SL-10 built the correlation layer, and SL-04 persisted decision logs. LDV per system came with demo issue #302 and PR #366. In PR #373, the ADL became the audit source. Protection and retention are norms in PSA S09 and are open in Q-08. F-68 and Q-25 cover citizen access.
  • Landed in: REQ-55, REQ-71, REQ-72, REQ-32, ADR-0026, ADR-0036.

docs.title: F-08: No mTLS or certificate-bound token on FSC
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: the old FSC mock identified organizations with an HMAC JWT and an OIN lookup, without mTLS.
  • Outcome: the outcome has five parts:
    • Transport runs on OpenFSC, with mTLS between Outway and Inway and with contract-bound authorization (SL-39, SL-42).
    • The legal identity comes from the certificate (F-60).
    • Q-07 answers the question of the PKIoverheid anchor.
    • No source asks for a certificate-bound token (RFC 8705). FR-34 v0.9 asks for a binding only outside the secure connection.
    • The review found a further gap: nothing proves that the browser initiation comes from the service provider (dienstverlener) (FR-34, criterion 1). Demo issue #427, REQ-111, and Q-60 record this gap.
  • Landed in: REQ-46, REQ-67, ADR-0003, ADR-0023.

docs.title: F-09: No policy lifecycle: hot reload without bundle, signing or versioning
docs.text:
• Type: design gap
  • Status: closed (November 2, 2026: ADR-0021 records the signing rule)
  • Trigger: the first demo mounted Rego files as a volume and reloaded them. SL-44 (PR #208) built most of the lifecycle.
  • Observation: the state of the policy lifecycle in demo v0.9.0 is as follows:
    • Built: git stays canonical. Policy goes out as an identified, versioned bundle. The PDP decides from the bundle with an empty policy directory (RL-01). RL-02 and RL-03 cover management authorization and role separation. RL-04 and RL-05 cover retire-not-delete and validation.
    • Not built: bundle signing. Nobody can verify the origin of a bundle.
    • The default demo configuration mounts ./policies into the PDP (docker-compose.yml#L157). Bundle pull is opt-in through make demo-manager (gbo-pdp.yaml).
    • Demo issue #426 (signing) closed as not planned on October 28, 2026. Q-21 keeps policy management at each source, so PAP and PDP are in one organization.
  • Why it matters: PSA S06 asks that a party can check the authenticity and integrity of policy sets. Criteria 1 and 2 of FR-39 v0.9 ask for sealed bundles. The GO names signed policy bundles. If another party than the policy owner runs a PDP, that PDP cannot check the origin of a bundle without a signature.
  • Proposal: record in ADR-0021 that signing is a requirement for a bundle that crosses an organization boundary. Inside one organization, signing is not planned. Validation with fallback stays with F-52. The FR-39 text about a central policy authority is outdated (Q-21) and goes back to the FR-DvTP authors. When ADR-0021 records the rule, close this finding.
  • Related: F-51, F-52, F-59, RL-01 to RL-05, Q-21, ADR-0021.

docs.title: F-11: The demo lets the consumer set the validity period
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: the consumer sends validity_seconds. FR-05 names the citizen as the party that sets the period.
  • Outcome: FR-05 and FR-11 v0.9 put the default per service in the catalog. The citizen can adjust the period within bounds. Demo issue #380 covers the demo deviation: a default of one year and no upper bound. Q-13 holds the question whether the citizen must adjust the period. That question reopened on November 2, 2026.
  • Landed in: REQ-19, Q-13.
  • Evidence: consent-register/main.go#L403

docs.title: F-14: The scope header is an untrusted catalog index, not a token claim
docs.text:
• Status: resolved in demo
  • Point: X-GBO-Scope selected the policy context but was not proof of anything.
  • Outcome: the header stayed untrusted, and policy checked the scope separately (demo issue #101). Since demo issue #483, the DvTP flow does not send the header. The PDP checks the requested scope against the verified consent.
  • Landed in: REQ-48, REQ-18.
  • Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#L379

docs.title: F-15: REQ-20 was worded BSN-only
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: the claim was that the DigiD token and the pseudonym must not reach the consumer either. By that claim, REQ-20 was too narrow.
  • Outcome: the GO and PSA S03 say that the service provider never gets the BSN. It gets only a party-specific pseudonym. So REQ-20 is correct. In demo v0.9.0, the return redirect carries the signed consent proof. Q-01 covers the form of the pseudonym.
  • Landed in: REQ-20, REQ-80.

docs.title: F-16: No single trace across consent issuance and the DvTP query
docs.text:
• Status: closed (observation, no action)
  • Point: consent issuance and a later query have separate traces.
  • Outcome: the two are separate units of work, often hours or days apart. One trace for both conflicts with OTel semantics. The audit axis between them is consent_id. The decision record carries consent_id next to the trace ID.
  • Landed in: REQ-55, REQ-71, ADR-0035.

docs.title: F-17: Scope descriptions in the consent portal are hard-coded
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: the portal shows hard-coded scope texts, separate from what policy enforces. The DvTP scopes are spread over policy, a generated field map, and scopeGroups.ts.
  • Outcome: demo issue #382 holds the finishing work (DvTP catalog per FR-32). F-74 holds the design.
  • Landed in: REQ-121.
  • Evidence: ScopeToggle.tsx#L1 (reads scopeGroups)

docs.title: F-18: DvTP initiation is redirect-only and does not cover an asynchronous invitation
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: FR-DvTP covers only a redirect while the citizen is present.
  • Outcome: an asynchronous invitation is out of scope. FR-DvTP v0.9 knows only redirect initiation (FR-12 to FR-14). The GO and the PSA have no invitation route. Reusable consent within its validity covers retrieval without the citizen present (Q-04, demo issue #380). An invitation is a MijnOverheid function. The topic comes back only with a concrete use case.
  • Landed in: REQ-37.

docs.title: F-20: The integrator role in DvTP needed PSA elaboration
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: the portal showed an empty integrator field. A small fix to that field implied at least eight design choices, among them end-to-end encryption (old FR-18).
  • Outcome: FR-06 is dropped, and Q-12 is answered. FR-18 v0.9 makes the integrator a processor that can see the data. FR-37 v0.9 covers its onboarding. The integrator connects under FSC delegation. F-73 holds the remaining gap (demo issue #379). The integrator field is removed from the portal.
  • Landed in: REQ-106, AV-06, ADR-0034.

docs.title: F-21: The catalog role split between FDS and GBO was not explicit
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: the PSA named no GBO component that consumes the catalog (a "catalog broker").
  • Outcome: GBO has no catalog broker. PSA B-03 sets federated content management with a common profile for findability (PSA open decisions). S07 and S10 agree. The source owns its service description (F-57). The DvTP catalog follows F-74.
  • Landed in: REQ-64, ADR-0016.

docs.title: F-22: The catalog runtime pattern for the PDP was undecided
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: catalog data had two possible routes to the PDP: as a bundle, or per request as a PIP fetch.
  • Outcome: policy goes out as a sealed bundle (FR-39 v0.9, PSA S06). The PDP consults the catalog and the registers as PIPs (PSA S05). Source metadata is pulled, validated, and activated atomically. F-09 and F-52 hold the open points.
  • Landed in: REQ-64, REQ-66.

docs.title: F-23: Rich catalog or rich policy
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: several demo increments moved content (allowlists, templates, and constraints) from policy code to catalog data, without a PSA choice.
  • Outcome: PSA S10 says that the catalog does not duplicate authorization policy. Policy runs through S06, and the catalog is federated (B-03). The source owns the rich description (F-57). GBO carries only the validation profile.
  • Landed in: ADR-0016.

docs.title: F-24: An unknown consent gave an HTTP error instead of a clean deny
docs.text:
• Status: resolved in demo
  • Point: the old PEP turned "consent not found" into HTTP 400, and the consumer saw upstream_error.
  • Outcome: SL-47 (PR #238) built the fix: policy builds the consent context. An unknown consent gives exists: false and the decision CONSENT_NOT_FOUND. An unreachable register gives status_available: false and a clean deny. Both are policy decisions with a reason code in the decision record.
  • Landed in: REQ-06, ADR-0032.
  • Evidence: policies/gbo/consent.rego#L273-L280

docs.title: F-25: PEP schema translation was regex-based and DvTP-specific
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: the PEP rewrote the query with regular expressions that worked only for DvTP.
  • Outcome: the PEP service no longer exists. The PDP maps the query by its AST. After the decision, the source gateway replaces the subject.
  • Landed in: REQ-21, ADR-0033.
  • Evidence: services/openftv-pdp/mapper/ftvgraphql.go

docs.title: F-26: Trace-driven UI coloring in the developer portal was fragile
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: the portal colored the chain from Jaeger and Loki data with complex timing logic.
  • Outcome: this finding concerns demo tooling only and is not a design finding. The proposed event stream is built and replaces the Jaeger polling.
  • Evidence: useChainEvents.ts

docs.title: F-27: AuthZEN envelope adopted, but not the RFC0052-GBO wire shape
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: the PEP sent the query as a resource attribute. AuthZEN 1.0 puts the query in action properties.
  • Outcome: the FSC Inway with OpenFTV v0.1.0 (PR #337) is AuthZEN-conformant (Q-16). Demo issue #331 takes a GraphQL profile upstream (PSA B-02).
  • Landed in: REQ-42, ADR-0002.

docs.title: F-28: The tech lead agreed to the generic GBO chain
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: in the architects' meeting, the position was that there is no separate EUDI authorization chain.
  • Outcome: the tech lead agreed to the direction. There is one generic PEP and one generic PDP, and policies decide the behavior. Channels differ in access basis, policies, metadata, and identifier handling. All channels use the same components. The adapter stays thin. The demo showed this design in F-31, and REQ-74 holds the regime choice.
  • Landed in: ADR-0004, ADR-0031.

docs.title: F-29: consentId in the query was DvTP-specific
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: the consent belongs in policy and evidence. The business query does not carry it. This point revises the removed REQ-25 to REQ-27.
  • Outcome: SL-47 (PR #238) built it: the proof travels in the X-GBO-Consent-Token header. Since SL-51, the query names the subject by a placeholder. The subject comes only from the proof.
  • Landed in: REQ-79, REQ-17, ADR-0032.
  • Evidence: dienstverlener-backend/outway/outway_test.go#L60-L66

docs.title: F-30: De-pseudonymization belongs at the source, and the GBO core stays BSN-free (DvTP path)
docs.text:
• Status: resolved in demo
  • Point: the conversion to a BSN must happen at the source, and the source uses its own keys for it. The conversion must not happen in the PEP or the PDP.
  • Outcome: SL-22 and demo issue #88 built this rule. Since SL-51, the source gateway decrypts its own value from the proof after the allow, without BSNk at query time. This rule holds only for DvTP. The EUDI and ASI routes carry the BSN from the PID (F-54).
  • Landed in: REQ-21, REQ-20, ADR-0033 (supersedes ADR-0011).
  • Evidence: services/bron-sidecar/

docs.title: F-31: Generic chain shown: two front doors through one PEP and one PDP
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: SL-20 sent EUDI issuance through the same chain as the DvTP query.
  • Outcome: the demo proved the point. PEP and PDP stay generic. Rules and evidence carry the channel difference. The adapter only translates the protocol. Q-17 holds the remaining governance points (issuer model, adapter ownership).
  • Landed in: ADR-0004, ADR-0031.

docs.title: F-32: Access basis from a self-declared flow field was an interim solution
docs.text:
• Status: resolved in demo
  • Point: the consumer declared the flow, so a caller was able to try to skip the consent check.
  • Outcome: demo issue #88 first moved flow to a grant property (F-43). Since PR #363, the regime follows from the evidence that a request carries (F-70). No consumer claim drives dispatch.
  • Landed in: REQ-74, ADR-0031.

docs.title: F-34: Placement of per-request context in transport is a choice
docs.text:
• Status: resolved in demo
  • Point: context in the request body mixed values that the consumer declared with values that the transport validated.
  • Outcome: SL-31 made the body pure GraphQL and put the context in headers with a trust prefix. The old FSC mock is gone. The rule stays: the PDP decides only on facts that it establishes itself. Consumer declarations do not count as facts.
  • Landed in: REQ-18 (absorbs the removed REQ-49 and REQ-50).

docs.title: F-35: The FSC Inway has a built-in AuthZEN plugin, so the PEP service doubled the PEP role
docs.text:
• Status: resolved in demo
  • Point: in the FSC model, the Inway is the PEP. A separate PEP service was a duplicate.
  • Outcome: SL-40 removed the EUDI branch of the PEP service. Demo issue #88 removed the service. DvTP and EUDI share one AuthZEN path to the PDP. Transformation after the decision happens at the source (F-30, F-37).
  • Landed in: REQ-04, REQ-42, ADR-0002.

docs.title: F-36: A sector grant is not a native FSC concept
docs.text:
• Status: resolved in demo
  • Point: FSC grants are per service and per peer. A sector grant needs a contract per peer or a policy attribute.
  • Outcome: the demo did not continue the sector branch. The removed REQ-33 and REQ-34 carried it. Admission comes from the admission register (toelatingsregister) and the contract decision of the PDP (F-55). Demo issue #378 removed sector-pip.
  • Landed in: REQ-61, ADR-0022 (history).
  • Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#L779-L786

docs.title: F-37: Transformation after authorization is a gateway task, not a policy task
docs.text:
• Status: resolved in demo
  • Point: a BSN must not enter the AuthZEN envelope. So the DvTP pipeline cannot move into the PDP.
  • Outcome: demo issue #88 moved the transformation to the source gateway. After that change, the envelope on the DvTP path carries only a placeholder. The EUDI and ASI routes do not meet the rule "no BSN in the authorization envelope" (F-54).
  • Landed in: REQ-20, REQ-81, ADR-0033.

docs.title: F-38: The rich catalog extended to routing and policy lookup
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: the EUDI adapter kept its own use-case catalog with FSC routing, next to the policy-side mapping.
  • Outcome: the use-case catalog is gone. Routing comes from contract discovery and source metadata (SL-46, F-57). F-74 holds the DvTP remainder.
  • Landed in: REQ-64, ADR-0016.

docs.title: F-39: FSC v2.4.0 has no OTel instrumentation, so trace context breaks at FSC hops
docs.text:
• Status: resolved in demo
  • Point: traces broke after the move to real FSC.
  • Outcome: Outway and Inway forward headers unchanged, so traceparent reaches the source. The only break is the AuthZEN hop (F-41). The chain follows W3C Trace Context. The ADL records the FSC transaction ID next to the trace context (F-67).
  • Landed in: REQ-55, ADR-0035 (supersedes ADR-0019).

docs.title: F-40: fsc-logging defines a transaction log and Fsc-Transaction-Id correlation
docs.text:
• Status: resolved in demo
  • Point: the Logius draft fsc-logging gives a shape for per-peer transaction logs. So GBO does not have to invent one.
  • Outcome: SL-38 showed the shape: the developer portal reads the transaction log of each peer. The fsc-logging draft is one of three related logging standards (F-63).
  • Landed in: REQ-55, AV-01, ADR-0035.
  • Evidence: dev-portal-backend/fsctxlog.go

docs.title: F-41: FSC plugins use context.Background() for downstream calls
docs.text:
• Status: resolved in demo (ADL side not met)
  • Point: the trace context is lost at the AuthZEN hop.
  • Outcome: the Inway sends only X-Request-Id to the PDP. The original headers are nested in context.headers. OpenFTV v0.1.0 reads neither of these values there. The ADL record behind the Inway has its own trace and no transaction ID. The developer portal finds the record through the stored request headers. The fix is upstream in OpenFSC (demo issue #369).
  • Landed in: REQ-55, ADR-0035.
  • Evidence: dev-portal-backend/adl.go#L48-L68

docs.title: F-42: Two routes to the FSC transaction log
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: the log API exists inside the organization and on the peer-facing Manager. The demo uses the internal API.
  • Outcome: the internal route is a demo shortcut. The open PSA S09 decisions on access and aggregation, and Q-08, decide who can read the logs in production.
  • Evidence: dev-portal-backend/fsctxlog.go

docs.title: F-43: Grant properties as a trusted dispatch signal per contract
docs.text:
• Status: superseded
  • Point: move flow and subject_id_type from an untrusted header into signed FSC grant properties.
  • Outcome: the first build used an additional-claims service (PR #55, ADR-0014). PR #284 then built the property route (F-62). PR #363 removed flow, because the regime follows from the evidence (F-70). Demo issue #473 removed subject_id_type.
  • Landed in: ADR-0030 (superseded by ADR-0031).
  • Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#L787-L790

docs.title: F-44: Where does the PI live, and how does policy bind to the subject?
docs.text:
• Status: resolved in demo
  • Point: the register stored the PI to let the PDP look up consent by PI.
  • Outcome: after SL-47 (PR #238), the PI is not in the register. The register keeps a portal-scoped subject reference. The subject travels in a signed, audience-bound proof. Policy binds to the subject in that proof. No lookup by PI exists. Since SL-51, the proof carries an encrypted value per party.
  • Landed in: REQ-68, REQ-69, REQ-80, ADR-0032.

docs.title: F-45: Grant-link configuration only through a Controller UI form
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: FSC v2.4.0 has no REST endpoint for Outway grant links. The demo writes the grant links with SQL.
  • Outcome: accepted as a demo shortcut. A REST endpoint is a candidate feature request to the FSC maintainers, together with F-46.
  • Evidence: fsc-infra/scripts/seed-bri-contract.sh

docs.title: F-46: Service endpoint update only through the Controller UI or database
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: to change a service endpoint by REST, FSC v2.4.0 needs a delete and a re-create.
  • Outcome: accepted as a demo shortcut. In demo v0.9.0, the seed sets the endpoint. A REST call for this change is a candidate feature request, together with F-45.

docs.title: F-49: A flow-name suffix as the PDP source-profile discriminator was ad hoc
docs.text:
• Status: premise lapsed
  • Point: the PDP chose the source schema by a suffix on the flow name.
  • Outcome: SL-48 (PR #236) removed the suffix. Later, the flow itself went too (F-70). In demo v0.9.0, rules name the FSC services that they apply to (F-90). The general question of schema selection went to a design spike, demo issue #137.
  • Landed in: REQ-97, ADR-0031.

docs.title: F-50: Attestation issuer and purpose statement are bound to the signing certificate
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: a fallback to another source's certificates made the wallet show the wrong issuer and purpose (PR #125).
  • Outcome: built. Every bronhouder has its own certificate set. Missing material causes a hard failure. Q-17 and demo issue #225 cover key management and the status list.
  • Landed in: REQ-58, ADR-0018.

docs.title: F-53: Two decision logs side by side and no designated audit source
docs.text:
• Status: resolved in demo
  • Point: the same decision landed in the ADL (Postgres) and in the console log of the engine (Loki). Neither log was named the audit source.
  • Outcome: SL-50: the ADL implements the Logius Authorization Decision Log standard. The ADL is the audit source. The console log is observability. PR #373 makes the developer portal read the ADL. The per-field detail stays in the console log only (F-72). The governance decision on this choice runs with Q-08.
  • Landed in: REQ-71, ADR-0036.

docs.title: F-55: Admission is a registration instead of a policy rule, and the automatic "no" stays reversible
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: admission was a hard-coded list in Rego, so every change was a policy release.
  • Outcome: SL-45 (PR #228, PR #239) added an admission register. The PDP reads it as a PIP. The contract decision has its own rule set. A refused proposal stays pending, and a terminal refusal is a separate act. This design matches PSA S04 and S05. Q-22 answers the governance question.
  • Landed in: REQ-61, REQ-62, REQ-63, ADR-0015.
  • Evidence: policies/fsc/autosign.rego#L170-L171

docs.title: F-56: The contract payload is thin: the decider sees who, not what
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: the FSC Manager sends only the hash, the grant types, and the peer IDs to the contract decision. As a result, admission per service is not possible. Admission is per bronhouder.
  • Outcome: accepted on purpose (decision of September 2, 2026). Every regime authorizes the actor and the basis per request (REQ-48). Since PR #363, no grant property authorizes anything. Admission per service runs through the catalog and the consent (Q-22, demo issue #382). Demo issue #240 lists the triggers to reopen this point.
  • Landed in: REQ-61, ADR-0015.

docs.title: F-58: A valid transport contract does not take a source into use
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: the first version found sources implicitly. A valid FSC contract was enough to fetch metadata and to publish products.
  • Outcome: SL-46 (PR #237) added explicit source configurations, a visible blocked status per source, and automatic promotion that is off by default. Transport and mandate are two separate decisions. This design matches PSA S04 and S07.
  • Landed in: REQ-65, ADR-0016.

docs.title: F-59: Source releases have the lifecycle that policy bundles lack
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: source metadata has validation before activation, bounded staleness, isolation, atomic promotion, and rollback. Policy bundles have none of these.
  • Outcome: REQ-66 and PSA S06 state the requirement in generic form. The policy side follows F-52 and Q-21. Signing (demo issue #426) closed as not planned (F-09).
  • Landed in: REQ-66, ADR-0016, ADR-0021.

docs.title: F-60: Three identity carriers, with the certificate authoritative for the legal identity
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: the demo used one field for the FSC Peer ID and the OIN. In the simulation, these values differ.
  • Outcome: SL-49: since PR #242, the demo uses two fields. Since PR #247, the OIN and the organization name come from the validated issuer certificate. This follows the GO (PKIoverheid) and PSA S04. Q-06 and Q-07 are answered. The link between OIN, KvK, and eIDAS identifiers is an open S04 decision outside the GBO build.
  • Landed in: REQ-67, ADR-0023.

docs.title: F-61: The legal basis travels as proof, the status stays online: a deliberate asymmetry in freshness
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: the consent proof is a signed, audience-bound artifact. The PDP verifies the proof locally. On every request, the PDP fetches the consent status online. The PDP can cache keys, but it cannot cache a status. If the status is unknown, the PDP denies.
  • Outcome: "status online, fail-closed" is the norm (GO, PSA S01, FR-11 v0.9). Since PR #371, the policy itself verifies the proof and fetches the status. Keys stay in the cache for five minutes, with no stale fallback. REQ-75 gives the numbers. To replay a decision, the record must hold the status answer (see F-72).
  • Landed in: REQ-68, REQ-75, Q-05, ADR-0032.
  • Evidence: policies/gbo/consent.rego#L25

docs.title: F-62: The additional-claims service is a version-compatibility workaround, and the contract-properties route is open again
docs.text:
• Status: resolved in demo
  • Point: the source Manager injected the regime claims into the FSC token from a manual JSON file (add hook). The reason was a simulation peer on OpenFSC v1.44. That version cannot co-sign contract properties. FSC standardizes grant.data.properties: the properties are in the grant hash and in the prp claim of the token. OpenFSC supports them since v2.0.0.
  • Outcome: PR #284 moved the properties into the co-signed contract and removed the additional-claims-service. PR #363 then removed flow as a property, because the regime follows from the proof (F-70). PR #475 removed subject_id_type. REQ-56 and REQ-70 are removed. Q-15 answers how contracts carry the correct properties.
  • Landed in: REQ-74, ADR-0031 (supersedes ADR-0030).

docs.title: F-63: Logius has three related logging standards, and the demo decision log implements one of them
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: Logius keeps a family of log standards with the same OTel record shape: LDV (processing), ADL (authorization decisions), and FSC-Logging (transport). The OpenFTV decision log already implements the ADL.
  • Outcome: the family is the norm under PSA S09. ADL 1.0.0 is published. A PDP decision is not a processing in LDV terms, so it goes to the ADL. Since PR #373, the ADL is the audit source of the demo. This answered F-53. REQ-59 and F-72 hold the open conformance points.
  • Landed in: REQ-71, REQ-72, ADR-0036, ADR-0026.
  • Evidence: OBSERVABILITY.md#L61-L64

docs.title: F-64: The LDV gap is at the processing instead of the decision, and the source gateway transformation is itself a processing
docs.text:
• Status: resolved in demo
  • Point: no component wrote LDV records. In LDV terms, these are all processings: the source query, de-pseudonymization at the source, register operations, and attestation building. Each controller (Verantwoordelijke) must log its own processings in its own logbook.
  • Outcome: built in demo issue #302 and corrected in PR #366. The build has trace context, one logbook per system, and a pseudonym per controller. In demo v0.9.0, the register of processing activities is a stand-in (Q-08).
  • Landed in: REQ-72, ADR-0026.
  • Evidence: services/ldv-logboek, docs/ldv/README.md

docs.title: F-65: dataSubjectId and the read extension fit the GBO pseudonym model and settle how citizen access works
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: LDV puts the data subject in dpl.core.data_subject_id. LDV recommends a pseudonym, with an explicit type field. The read extension builds a chain from the starting application through nextLogbookId.
  • Outcome: this supports REQ-60: a pseudonym in the log is the recommended form. With recipient-specific pseudonyms, access across organizations can search only on the trace ID. A search on the subject is not possible. The consent portal (toestemmingsportaal) cannot read the whole chain through nextLogbookId in DvTP, because GBO does not start the chain (F-68). Citizen access goes per controller (GDPR art. 15). Each controller logs under its own pseudonym (F-69).
  • Landed in: REQ-60, REQ-72, Q-01, Q-08, ADR-0026.

docs.title: F-66: Erratum: the PuB-EAA seal and the Access CA were confused with PKIoverheid
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: an earlier analysis said that PuB-EAAs are sealed with "PKIoverheid or the EUDI Access CA". That statement is wrong.
  • Outcome: a PuB-EAA carries a qualified seal from a certificate that a QTSP issued (Regulation (EU) 2024/1183, Annex VII). Relying parties check the seal against the QTSP trust anchor or the PuB-EAA Provider LoTE (ETSI TS 119 602). An Access CA issues access certificates only for authentication to the wallet (ETSI TS 119 411-8). An Access CA never signs attestations. PKIoverheid is the Dutch PKI for mTLS and FSC. "PKIoverheid as Dutch Access CA" is an open recommendation, not a fact.
  • Landed in: Q-07, REQ-58, REQ-67, ADR-0023, ADR-0028.

docs.title: F-67: A trace ID equal to Fsc-Transaction-Id conflicts with LDV and the ADL
docs.text:
• Status: resolved in demo
  • Point: REQ-55 made the trace ID equal to the FSC transaction ID. LDV and the ADL take the trace ID unchanged from traceparent. FSC-Logging makes a transaction ID unique per transaction. The equality breaks in three cases:
    • A caller brings its own traceparent.
    • One processing queries several sources.
    • The request takes an extra FSC hop, for example the consent status lookup.
  • Outcome: PR #366: every component reads traceparent first. Each component records the transaction ID next to the trace ID (ADL adl.fsc.transaction_id). The transaction ID is a fallback only at an entry point without traceparent. REQ-55 is revised.
  • Landed in: REQ-55, ADR-0035 (supersedes ADR-0019).
  • Evidence: services/ldv-client/tracecontext.go#L25

docs.title: F-69: A pseudonym that travels across the chain lands in the logbooks of two controllers
docs.text:
• Status: resolved in demo
  • Point: the source gateway logged the PI that it received from the consumer. The same PI was then in the consumer logbook and in the source logbook. A reader with access to both logbooks can join them on the person as well as on the trace.
  • Outcome: REQ-72 states that each controller logs under a pseudonym from its own pseudonym space. A controller never logs under an identifier that the caller sends. The demo fixed this in demo issue #367 through PR #366. Since SL-51, the cause is gone. No pseudonym travels: the consumer sends a placeholder (F-76).
  • Landed in: REQ-72, ADR-0026.

docs.title: F-73: The actor binding of consent assumes that the consumer calls itself, and an integrator breaks that assumption
docs.text:
• Status: closed
  • Point: the consent proof binds the consumer to the transport caller. FR-18 and FR-37 v0.9 let an integrator call as a processor for the service provider, with its own identity. In that case, the binding fails, or it needs an exception that empties it.
